Good yogurt, nice flavor selection. I mixed the chocolate with the banana-yummy! Cute pink and green color scheme. I think children would especially love the decor.

I'm a huge fan of all things Bongo Java -- I think Fido is the best coffee shop I've ever been to -- so I was excited that they were going to open a coffee shop around the corner from where I live.  I went today for the first time, and it is wonderful.  It is a clean, good looking space, and, of course, the selection of coffee and tea is fantastic.   The menu is broad enough to make anyone happy, although I do hope they will eventually have daily specials, something that makes the food at Fido heads above a typical coffee shop.  (Perhaps they already have them and I was just there at an in between time when they weren't offered.)

The staff could not have been friendlier. Thanks for opening this great place in an area that sorely needed a great coffee shop.   There's plenty of parking, and lot of outlets to plug in your computer.

WOW. I just had an amazing breakfast at Ohana Cafe. Real Hawaiian food amazing. I went with the macadamia nut pancakes with turkey bacon and red potatoes. It was absolutely delicious and the best part is it's only 10 minutes from where I live. The owner and staff are so pleasant and helpful on explaining the various dishes on the menu. I'm so impressed it's almost dinner time. So it's back there for a real Hawaiian burger or their famous loco moco. Aloha

Might very well be the best beer fridge in town. And a wine selection that's pretty decent,  too. Stopped by on Saturday on the mini golf course set up by several of the Midtown merchants. Weather was a little chilly.

Went to happy hour tonight and was able to try out their awesome new drink menu - all of mine were fantastic! I especially recommend the Hibiscus one! Also, as always, the sushi was delicious!

The service at this location is by far the best - Samantha is probably the nicest person ever and extremely knowledgable and helpful! Plus the rest of the staff was extremely friendly and helpful as well!

I will definitely be back regularly :)

I realize I've already reviewed this place twice, but it honestly deserves a third. Here's why...

My girlfriend and I had planned to come into town for Satchmo Summer Fest, thanks to a crazy cheap hotel deal I had emailed to me by Bookit. The goal was to get there the Thursday before the festival. American Airlines, however, had other plans for us. Long story short, we finally arrived in New Orleans over 12 hours later than our original itinerary called for.

The next day, once we finally started moving about, we stopped into Bourbon Heat to get a few drinks and to cool off. After telling the bartender Nic our story, he went above and beyond to make sure we were taken care of. This is the kind of personal attention that not only kept us coming back every day of the trip, but will also keep me coming back every day of every future trip. I love this place!

Learned a lot through the yelp event here today! Feeding TB is doing wonderful things for our community and is helping hundreds of thousands of food insecure families. Volunteering here was a fun way to give back and I would recommend it for anyone. We sorted through canned and packaged goods/beverages, and contributed to over 12,000 meals in 1/2 day. Shifts weren't too long or too short and they had a mandatory 15 min break after 2 hrs. The staff were really caring and great at instructions! This is an easy and effective way to give back, and perfect for large groups including school, work, family, and church organizations. I'm happy to have learned more about them and their impact, especially being a yelp member and being mindful of food equity!

Best service over ever had dealing with locksmiths. I've been really distracted lately and locked my keys in my truck 2 days in a row. Jeromi Noel from Alpine lock and key came both times to to unlock my truck. Very professional and awesome service. Thank you for helping me. Highly recommend this service when you are in a bind like I was.

The best upcoming brunch spot in Nashville! Food was great. The drinks are worth it, strong and delicious! Matt and Rachel took great care of us at the bar. Service was unbeatable. Clean, friendly and fun environment. Perfect for a date, family or solo. It's a must go to!
My husband and I decided to try this place out for our dinner date and lets just say we were mind blown. The wonton soup was AMAZING and the pad Thai was just a s good!! We will definitely return!!

I'm torn between giving a 3 star or 4 star. Brewery wise, I gotta give it a four, the beers here were definitely awesome! My personal favourite was definitely the Raspberry Hefeweizen. I'm a beer guy and all of the ones I tried (the tap beers) were great, but if I were to come back I definitely would get the Raspberry Hefeweizen first.

Unfortunately the food did not live up to the taste of the beer. I got a Pork Schnitzel (basically a porkchop / pork steak) and it was overcooked. The sauce was good but the meat was harder / tougher than I'm assuming it was supposed to be. If I come back I'm definitely trying something else because that was not very good.

What a great place to stay! Super friendly staff!
Pets stay free! The place is very well kept and in a great location. We were only in town for the weekend and were able to get around in a moments notice.
Overall great place

Wonderful! Highly recommend. From the drinks to the truffle Mac and cheese, everything I tried was wonderful. Especially the fish tacos. Smoky and wonderful with just the right amount of spice and crunch.

We hosted a party here for clients and had a buffet style set up! All went extremely well. I have also been here for lunch. I had the fish sand which on one occasion, oysters on another. Awesome place and is a routine place for me.
So good!! Those are all the words you need. It's kind of hidden in the international market, (which is it's own interesting place) with other stores and food vendors.

Food Truck Friday was divine featuring Heart Food Truck. The food was delicious, eclectic and affordable. They do parties, private events and you may see them at your next venue.

The Sill Works is special, unique an has private parties and tours.

Nachos: 

TGI Friday's obviously doesn't understand what nachos are. Ten chips arranged neatly in a circle on a plate with stuff melted onto them, which makes them soggy? These are NOT nachos. I had them in London, England first, and thought it was just the British flaking out about nachos, being less familiar with Mexican food and all. Then I realized these are actually what TGIF serves world-wide. Fail.

Atmosphere: 

I don't really like it here. It's sort of generic and the staff uniorms make them all look like sad clowns.

Service: 

Probably average at this TGIF, though one time in England they had half the restaurant empty and refused to seat us because they had "no room". We tried to point out that half the place was empty, but they just insisted "Well, we're full, you'll have to wait 45 minutes". No explanation. We left and went to Outback instead.
The bison burger is awesome! Also the deep fried veggie appetizer is yummy. Parking is hard to deal with, and there is a lot of bar traffic from Shea's.
We have a couple of favorites that we keep ordering and as such have not sampled everything here, but it is superior coffee and the only kind we French Press at home.
This is a great store! No hassle returns and they always have great sales going on. Not to mention, great customer service. I've never had a bad experience here!

The freshest fruits & vegetables, choice meats, fragrant herbs & spices. If you expect all if this when you dine-out then prepare to have your expectations fulfilled at Sandra Rice & Noodles. We dined here recently with the Yelp Int'l Supper Club and in my opinion every dish was a culinary masterpiece. This place is fantastic and the owner & chef, who also served us, has the most pleasant & amusing personality and takes great pride in her restaurant and her food. As she should. She also is very accomodating to anyone's particular tastes and mentioned more than once that she will cook anything that is not on the menu per request as long as she knows the dish or the ingredients and of course if the ingredients are available. I really enjoyed the several course delectable feast that was served to our group.  There were Spring Rolls filled with fresh crisp veggies and Vietnamese sausage, refreshing Papaya Salad, Sweet & Sour Soup which had a mildly spicy broth and chunks of pineapple & other vegetables, steaming bowls of fragrant Jasmine Rice, Pan Fried Tilapia (complete with bones & head attached) flavored with lemongrass & chiles, bone-in Beef Short Ribs cut into medium sized chunks and resting in a platter of meaty broth, and various dishes of sweet rice pudding for dessert - one had corn in it (yum!) and another had chunks of lychee. The owner again was so gracious and even served an exotic fruit (the name escapes me) native of Vietnam that was odd-looking but fun to eat and tasted similar to lychee. They have a sizable menu and their prices are incredibly reasonable. I know I'll be boldly & confidently recommending this place a lot.

One of the myriad choices for food in this great mecca inside an old train terminal. We went based on a reco from the concierge at Westin hotel.

We walked around for 30 or more minutes before we decided to give this one a try. Ordered two sandwiches, off the craved menu, pork loin and beef brisket. Added hot peppers, cheese and rabe to Pork and hot peppers and cheese to beef.

The bread and jus makes it great and the meat is very tasty. The beef seemed to be hot as well as the peppers and after half of the sandwich I was in full sweat and my mouth was on fire.

Traded my other half to the better half to get her pork loin.

Bill with two sandwiches and one drink was $28. Both were great but I would tone down the beef one the next time out.

Immediately went to Bassett's for a palette cleansing ice cream cone. ;0)

Will return.

Yesterday at 9 am, my [former] front door ringer buzzed. The movers were early and I was not ready for them. This month has been a whirlwind of unexpected sickness, Philly permits, boxes, phone calls, pangs of sadness at the thought of leaving my home-state, and plenty of chocolate binging.

"You're early. I wasn't expecting you until 9:30." Blink and stare. Blink. Spazzy expression.

Somehow, it got done. The move. It was probably the easiest part of the entire month of May. The boxes I hadn't yet taped were piled onto the truck last. The movers were nothing short of professional but also were incredibly personable. They were great!

Bobby Adams, the owner, will make sure the job gets done. I must have called and texted him five times (or more..) in the week leading up to the move due to an issue with getting my temporary no parking permit for the street in Philly. He was completely compassionate and reassuring. Sure enough, I got the permit and it worked out.

Now the unpacking is underway, which isn't *as tough* as the packing portion! Big thanks to Adams Moving Services for getting my stuff across state lines safely and efficiently!

Do NOT go here for coloring. Absolutely horrible experience!!!! The staff is friendly, however my stylist lacked knowledge in coloring leaving me spotted dark, roots showing and about 10 different shades of orange. Not only did I get a bad dye job, I now have my hair breaking off due to damage from the foils. Sat there for 3 hours for foils, paid over $100 for orange hair that I now have to get fixed.

I came here for a quick cut 2 weeks ago.
My hair is medium-length and is a little wavy - I had asked May to give me a trim 'with layers'.
I'm not sure how she interpreted it bcos only the front part of my hair had layers (that too minimal), and the back was just straight one-length.
I was really not satisfied with what I got.
Its super cheap and washes and blowdries, yes thats why I'm giving the third star. The blowdry was also completely straight and didn't feel special at all.
Not going back again!

Not Just Full of Baloney 

Piece of Meat is a place that can turn the most mundane type meats into a gourmet meal. Take for instant, in your grammar school day, when mom made you a baloney sandwich. You know doubt enjoyed it, but was it a gourmet sandwich? Who in the world would have labeled such a sandwich gourmet? Far from it, right? 
Well forget about what you remember about baloney. This place takes this sandwich to another level, and not because this is the only sandwich they make either. But what would one expect with accolades like: Best new restaurant 2019 from Food and Wine magazine. And there are several more comments like the latter from other notable sources. My review is on the baloney sandwich called NOT TURKEY AND THE WOLF'S BOLOGNA, a compilation of owner chef Leighann Smith's thick sliced Bologna, provolone cheese, BBQ sauce, fried onions, lettuce, mayo, on an onion bun. I caught sight of this place watching the morning news when I saw partner owner chef Dan Jackson assemble this sandwich for the news station channel WVUE Fox 8, New Orleans. I love baloney but this is not the normal stuff. They make their own version of the famous sausage. It was wonderfully delighting to eat. I'll be back to try their other items on their unusual menu.

I had my sister in from Chicago. I made reservations there was miscommunication we were sat immediately. We were sat in a quiet room (conversation was great). Alicia was our server very friendly, attentive, and spot on. The key West Chowder delish. Coconut shrimp tasty
Entree - the salmon and the Duck excellent 
Drinks were huge accurate Martini's yum
Over all the dinner was great the ambience refreshing, definitely a return visit in the future

Came in today on a Saturday at 11:30 am and was so surprised and amazed when walking in. Pizza by the slice $2 and was hot and fresh.  Many other appetizers and salads to add on.   Staff was great and was attentive, they come on by to check on you and how things are going.  Best part is that seating isn't cramped and can have a conversation with your party and not have to whisper or hear the next booth's conversation.  Will definitely be coming back.
Best spicy chicken tenders and great fries! Grandkids loved the food and atmosphere. Will be back!

I've lived at Trellis at the Lakes (formerly Camden Lakes) for 2 years and it has been a great experience. The reviews that reference the transition from Camden to Trellis are unfair and unrealistic. If you know anything about business you know transitions take time. The leasing staff now is better than the Camden staff and the maintenance team is and always has been great.

My fiance and I have been wanting to try Epice for a long time now so we decided to stop in on a random Wednesday night and we are so glad we did!  We started off the meal with the  Al-Raheb, roasted eggplant puree, which was light and packed with flavor.  The pomegranate seeds were a great touch.  It's definitely only enough for 2 people to share, but it was a nice precursor to our meal.  As for the entrees, I had a hard time deciding what to get (which is not unusual for me), but I finally opted for the Mishwe, tenderloin brochette and my fiance ordered the Lahm.  Before our entrees came, we had a little peasant salad but it was ratherforgettable (and overly acidic).  A few sprinkles of some kind of cheese would have helped balance out the salad, or maybe I just really love cheese and want to incorporate it any way I can.  

After the salads we indulged in our delectable entrees.  Oh my goodness I cannot say enough about how delicious they were.  My Mishwe was melt-in-your-mouth tender and the cilantro roasted potatoes that were served alongside the meat were super tasty as well.  I was able to steal a bite (or two) of my fiance's lahm and it was fantastic and bursting with favor.  Everything was perfectly cooked, seasoned, and presented.  The service was top-notch and the ambiance was perfect- not stuffy or pretentious, but I could tell that this place wants to focus the attention on the food and its authenticity and not let the diner get distracted by anything else.  

Because of our wonderful experience, Epice quickly became one of our favorite places in Nashville and we can't wait to go back!

We went here for the first time and we're not disappointed. Food was excellent (Specifically the lamb burger was phenomenal. Just wish burgers were a little bigger). The desserts were out of this world and creative, and the service was perfect. This is a great place to go solo or with a great group of friends.

If you are up to fatty, high carb food this is the place to go. A relic from the eighties. But sometimes I feel the urge to go there... By the way: it is not a café. It's rather a burger and omelette place with ketchup on the table and a railway station atmosphere.

Okay, so I met the wonderful gals who founded dog town while working at Cutter's Mill Pet store. They handed out cards, and I was going on vacation in a month so I decided to see what they had to offer. Their facility was GORGEOUS. they have an indoor dog park, and separate play areas for dogs of different sizes if that's a concern. The K9 Grass they have cleans and drains itself, and my dogs always seem HAPPY to go there! The staff cares about the dogs and their owners, and they sure know how to make my dogs happy when we leave!
They also introduced us to our current groomer, which is a plus; great recommendations and very knowledgeable.  Prices are great for the area, even if I cant afford doggie day care on a daily basis. Boarding includes doggie day care, play time and much more. 


hidden gem in colmar, can't wait to visit again!

Jessica is fabulous!!! She is so down to earth and willing to go the extra mile. When I arrived in SB for the wedding weekend, she followed up with every last little detail and never rushed any meeting we had together or forgot any of our concerns. She is extremely outgoing and friendly, but professional and hustles!! We always felt taken care of and reassured with her in our corner. More than that, she is extremely creative in her designs and set up our reception space beautifully. The day went off without a hitch and I know it was because of her. Jessica is the type of planner to stay up with you all night until everything is perfect. 4 stars, for sure!
I have never had food poisoning this bad before. I don't know what happened but shortly after eating here I began vomiting, and won't be going back.

Made a reservation on a Saturday at 8:30 pm but when we got there, no one was at hostess stand, just a sign saying please go forward to be seated. Great, however this sign was at a corner where you could go right or left. Went right into the dining area but couldn't see or hear a soul, so went back and went left. There was a group eating off a buffet and a woman doing some kind of lounge singing. We saw no employees so had to ask the singer if anyone worked there. She pointed at a man who promptly ignored us. So guess what, we were out of there. Went down the street to Charlie Gitto's and had a great meal

I stopped in here tonight after working late. I made it in the door about 3minutes minutes after they closed. They had already closed down the kitchen and looked like they were about to lock up. To my surprise they fired up the kitchen and made my to go order! Talk about going the extra mile! And the food? I ordered  spicy shrimp fried rice, broccoli beef, and sesame chicken and it was delicious. My girl friend and I will be telling all of our friends how nice these guys were to us and how good the food was. Thanks panda house!
Amazing Italian. Pasta, pizza, salad, and bread with dips. It's a great restaurant, and is worth the chunk of dough.

Love the casa grande on Robb but think I like this location even more. It's not as busy and the lounge is larger but food and drinks are the same-excellent at both locations. Tiana the bartender makes a wonderful margarita and provided great service.

Tracey consistently solves problems with surprising efficiency. Her common sense mixed with her legal expertise got me through negotiations with great results and much less stress than I had experienced with two other lawyers in Santa Barbara. I recommend her without any reservations at all if I get the opportunity. Thanks, Tracey!

I'd give this joint 2 1/2 stars if I could but since I can't and I'm feeling unusually generous, I'll give them three. Their draft selection doesn't suck  (and they have La Chouffe) which automatically bumps them up a notch.  Also, they have more than one Irish whiskey, another plus.Their menu is massive and all over the place.  It's an 'Irish Pub' (or at least America's idea of an Irish pub) but they serve burritos.  Color me confused.  However, their burgers are awesome, not the usual pub frozen patties.  I can't stand that.  The bar is a massive, old school, solid wood dealie. 

Moriarty's is not a place I'd think of going of an evening but if I'm in the hood and craving a burger and brew and don't want to cross Broad Street to get to the Good Dog, I'll do it.

This place is on point! Definitely a hidden gem and definitely a popular joint!

Staff: Super friendly

Food: Mind blowingly good and true to its southern roots

Atmosphere: Like you just got back from your Uncle Bubbas cabin out on the lake. Love the cozy fishing decor!

Their sweet tea is amazing and if you're not that southern you can opt for a half sweet half unsweetened tea.

Ribs were fall off the bone tender. They have sauce on the table for you to add to your BBQ and it's a must.

Chicken and waffles had all my friends silent. Nobody was talking because everything was delicious!

Honorable mentions: Catfish, Mac and Cheese, fried Okra and greens. The sides stole the show.
The catfish po boy is amazing. It was flavorful. The catfish was cooked well. I'd eat here everyday if I could.

Great atmosphere for brunch outside!!  Food is not bad, but the service is horrible!!!  Consistently horrible!!!!  I don't think they are sufficiently staffed.  All the servers are so nice but just seem chaotic and always seems to take very long.  And when I use the word very, I use it with extra emphasis.   Breakfast took approx 2 hours!!!!!!  Menus alone took about 15-20 min to get.  Just a heads up if you want to enjoy the outside, bring your own water, drinks because it will take a long long long time for anything!

Commander's Palace is not trendy. It is not trying to be cool and definitely not trying to be like a restaurant you could find in Los Angeles or New York City and that is why I LOVE it. This is a restaurant that is uniquely New Orleans. 

They have carpeted floors, balloons decorating the tables, chef hats for special celebrations, and they will wrap up your leftovers like an aluminum swan. They are old school in the best way possible. 

Apart from the atmosphere, the food is wonderful. Order anything on the menu and you will love it. I have never eaten anything I didn't like at Commander's and the entire experience is unforgettable. My advice to you--ask to sit in the Garden Room and order the Strawberry Shortcake for dessert. You won't be disappointed.

This office is quick and does extensive checks not only for vision, but for cancers,astigmatism,etc. You also have the option to to have your eyes dialated (Insurance covers this) or pay a small fee to not have them dialated and they use a high tech machine instead. I don't need glasses, but they have a nice selection of designers frames for sunglasses. They fitted me for them and sent them off so they would got me perfect. I live about 20 m away,so the doctor meet me at a gas station near my home when my glasses came in. The best service I've ever had from a doctors office! I drive 20 m every yr to come here fort check up. So worth it, even though I probably pass 10 other optometrist on the way!

The black & tan was excellent but I should have remembered I was at a pub and not a Mexican restaurant the fish tacos at $10.25 we're not that great I should have gone for the bangers and mash or fish & chips.   I had a great time as I always do here but I just need to remember, when in Rome.....

LOVE this place. Cozy, friendly staff, and very reasonable prices for the quality.  Is it the best sushi I've ever had? Not quite, but it IS excellent for the very decent price.  Oh, and try the gyoza or the crab rangoon...my favorites!!
Good Mexican food! Don't need to say anything else...

*WARNING* I wish I could give zero stars.  I used them for a bathroom remodel.  In the beginning it seems as though they have it all together.  You're in the showroom going over your dreamy ideas and plans with a well dressed employee who seems to care about you and the hard earned money you're putting into your exciting remodel.....   eventually a crew shows up here and there to make a mess, miss critical details in the plans, not show up, delay, delay, delay.....   So many excuses.  My master bath remodel took THREE times the amount of time they told me it would.  Part of their pitch was that they do not hire subcontractors... absolutely NOT true.  It's taken me over a year to write this review because I was afraid I'd be too harsh but my goodness, I'm still so angry at their lack of care or concern for their customers time and money.  I don't think there was a single employee that come over to work on the project that didn't complain or tell me horror stories about what was going on with other projects at the time.  Their office staff is wonderful at calling and keeping up with payments though.  You can only count on that!  Shameful

We used Priceline to find a reasonable place to stay on New Year's Eve, and got a non-smoking room here for $140 including tax.

A tourist class hotel with basic amenities, but no Bible in the room, which we found curious.  Instead were a few fact books and one on the history of Philadelphia, which was a helpful addition.

Check-in/out is self service, but the staff was friendly and helpful when we had problems with both.  Very clean, with a modern-conservative decor.    When we needed a cab, the staff let us know when one was available.   

There are fill-your-own purified water bottle dispensers next to the elevators, which was a nice touch, particularly when you're dehydrated from the cold (or heat).

Parking was around the corner, $33.  A cab to South Street: $8.  CVS & H&M within 1 block, so you're set in the event you have a headache or lost your luggage and need some disposable clothing.

Amazing bbq! Meat just falls off the ribs. Ribs are juicy and tender, perfect! Fries are nice and crispy, cornbread is soft and fluffy. Service is excellent, personal and friendly. We will definitely be back again.

Hey I knew there would be a wait.  20 minutes out in the cold was bearable.  Getting to the register and being told, "sorry we are out of white meat". WTF tell the folks in line.  Ordered the chicken strips, slaw, Mac and cheese and southern grits.  Waited another 20 minutes. Sorry nothing was great, or best ever.

2.5 Stars

I come to this DD because it is conveniently located on the correct side of the road for me to stop at on my way into work. Since they don't offer soy milk, my drink options are limited to hot coffee or iced coffee.  Most of my experience with this particular DD is just with the drive-thru.

So, at the drive-thru - sometimes they hear your order correctly, sometimes they don't.  Sometimes you get exactly what you ordered, sometimes you don't.  Sometimes they tell you the price once you order, sometimes they don't.  

They seem to cycle through help quickly, since I have different people greeting me every month.  They always seem to be short of help - I have been here when the drive-thru line is long, and when I pull up it looks like there are just two workers trying to take care of everything.  Very frequently there are cars pulled out of line, waiting for their order to be filled.

Fortunately - the coffee is consistently good.  Tip - don't forget to buy your pumpkin K-cups-they are awesome!

Well, I was in a hurry to get a pedicure three days ago and went here. I had the manicurist remove my calluses, he used what looked like a cheese grater...he went so deep that I wasn't able to wear shoes since I went! My pedicure was fine but the pain wasn't! I called them that night and I believe that I spoke with the owner. He informed me that sometimes they have to "go that deep to do a proper job". I've had dozens of pedicures and have NEVER had this happen. 
These photos are what my foot looks like now, three days after going...ouch!

Had for take out. For mains had the teriyaki chicken and the beef ribs. The chicken dishes was quite tasty. Come with rice, glass noodles, tofu slices and the spicy cabbage side (which I don't like). I recommend this dish. The ribs were not great though. They were tough and didn't have a good taste. Came with the same sides as the chicken.

Michael's is a roadside diner on Street Road, Bensalem, PA. It has a counter with spinner seats and a fairly large dining room. It serves three squares a day with professional servers who have been there for decades. 

I stopped by for breakfast this week and took a stool facing the dessert cooler and ordered coffee with a Country Omelet, hash browns and rye toast. The java was industrial strength, as desired. The three egger was okay with an overload of green pepper along with onion and diced potatoes. The hash browns were a bit of overkill given their cousins in the eggs, and would have tasted better if they replaced the spuds inside the shell, as they had far more flavor and texture than those puny chunks used as filler. Overall, the opus was a tad dry, detracting from what might have been a contender had it been moister and had better balanced ingredients. 

Liked the rye toast. 

Service was fine. Access into the building was ADA compliant with ramp and wide front door. Didn't check the bathrooms. 

Michael's was decent, but nothing to distinguish it from the other culinary attractions along this stretch of Street Road.

Love having this little gem two blocks from my house! I used to kind of only walk to Buen Gusto, but this is my new favorite spot. Everything I've tried is perfect and it's fun sitting outside with the unobstructed riviera view. The pink neon piggy sign puts a smile on my face on my drive home from work!
Must get the hash browns. Everything is delicious. Peach pancakes and chocolate sin pancakes are amazing.

Don't be fooled by the other "Nick's Roast Beef!" Go to the one in the hood!! it is the BEST! I was fresh off a plane from California, so hungry and ready to eat some hearty South Philly food, so when my lil sis said we were going to Nick's, I was stoked!!! 

Best Ever Roast Beef!!! (excluding my uncle's deli, c'mon it's family!)

As a Tampa native, living just a few blocks from here,I grew up visiting Alessi bakery and have seen it go through many changes. Today I went to pick up some pastries for my grandpa for father's day. It had been about a year since I had visited and couldn't believe how run down and uninviting it looked! The last time I went cakes, fresh sandwiches and more filled the counters and coolers, inviting you to want to sample it all. Today it was sparse, dimly lit and almost looked like it wasn't even open! The pastry counter appeared dirty and rundown, and just didn't make me feel like I wanted to purchase anything. I ended up leaving with a few things for him, but I doubt I'll go back until I hear about some updates/changes. Even the outside sitting area was full of trash, and appeared very run down. What happened Alessi?? If you haven't been here in a while, check it out. I can't be the only one who's noticing these changes.

Wow what a nice find ! Driving by it didn't look like much but do yourself a favor and don't judge the book by the cover! I've eaten here at least 6 times in the last few months and have never been disappointed. Maybe a different lunch menu would be nice? Try them out, you'll be a fan too!

Cute little coffee shop. Don't expect to really be able to sit inside because it's very small. 
I ordered a "Mexican vanilla latte" which they might as well just put vanilla latte on the menu because when the barista announced the drink I asked if it's the Mexican vanilla latte and she rudely responded saying "we only have one type of vanilla". Which I found rude because on the menu it clearly says Mexican vanilla latte and I would feel bad if I took someone else's drink so I just wanted to make sure with her that it was the right drink. 

The latte was very good. The espresso was so smooth and the vanilla was subtle. It was a good combination.

I went here with my boyfriend and our two friends for a double date. We were going to go to Abyssinia, which is basically right next door, but we thought we'd give this place a shot since we had never been here before.

Overall, kind of disappointing. I don't want to bash them for the more than obvious language barrier, but it really did make ordering very difficult. The menu seemed easy to understand but they never really explained what the "veggie sides" were. When we asked, it was just really hard to get a clear answer. 

Also, it seemed like they were operating out of a home, which was just weird to me. That may not be the case, but that was the vibe we all got from it. Just a little weirded out that it wasn't a commercial kitchen.

Pros: friendly service, reasonable prices, good food
Cons: strange atmosphere, confusing menu, strong language barrier

TLDR; just go to Abyssinia next door for better food and service.

I've had watch batteries replaced here, and a small diamond in my engagement ring replaced.  They are very reasonably priced and quick to do the job.  They even offered for me to bring my ring back every couple months to make sure all the diamonds were secure, and to have it cleaned for free, even though it wasn't sold by them.  Very nice people, and I highly recommend them.

What's not to like about Gulf Shores? It's always busy, great location, it's clean and everything is good. Creole(?) cuisine isn't my first love but the menu is huge, so there's likely something for everyone. Harry, the owner, is super friendly and engaging--clearly, it's a labor of love. We started with the crab cakes (great!) and finished with the citrus Mahi Mahi. Loved it! Service was excellent.

My cousin and I stopped by here for a drink and I really liked it. It was my first time here been wanting to come for so long and finally got the chance. The waitress was so sweet and patient. Our order came out pretty quick. We went during afternoon time on a Sunday and it wasn't crowded or anything. There were enough seats. I will definitely be coming back.

Celebrated my daughter's grad school graduation at lunch the other day. Everything was perfect. We were greeted as we entered the restaurant, our waiter was attentive but not invasive. The food was excellent. Two in our party got lunch combos, the short rib toast, and the chef plate which was a softshell crab sandwich. Two others ordered the chicken entrée and the graduate ordered the salmon entree. Everyone believed they had ordered the best thing. The tuna tartare appetizer was amazing but for us  the octopus appetizer was the star of the show. I don't usually do reviews but I had to come on here and review this restaurant because our experience was amazing can't say enough about it. Beautiful decor , professional staff, And excellent food. If you're thinking about going there stop thinking about it and just go

Fun times at the dueling piano bar and wow those hurricanes are strong. They're reasonably priced too, and it's not to hard to find a seat. We had a great time and came back twice in only four nights. Definitely a must visit place on any trip to New Orleans!

The food is good.  The location is great. 
Try  the Hong Kong Style Pan Fried Noodles. 
After you eat, take a walk on State street

Only stay at this location if you're broke and can't afford anything else in the area. It absolutely sucked from many aspects. The one star is solemnly for the fact that you can tell these rooms have recently been remolded and the beds are okay... but our toilet was broken, there was no cable, and the floors hadn't been cleaned. When my parents took showers, their feet became black from walking on the floors which is gross. Also, we asked for a non smoking room- yet our room reeked of cigarette smoke:(  In addition, there was no WiFi, and we tried calling the front desk on our first night and no one answered after 15 minutes of trying. The mini fridge also froze all of our food and drinks we put in there, maybe it was just the setting it was on, but overall staying here was not enjoyable.  Plus, this side of downtown makes sense for the cheaper prices because of how rundown it seems.

I have never had alterations done before so I did a quick Google search and this was the closest to me.  I brought the owner 2 suits, one $4,000 Giorgio Armani and another cheapo that I wanted to have tailored for less formal occassions.  The results were fantastic!  The Armani was expertly threaded and you couldn't tell that it didn't come from the factory already tailored.  What surprised me was that the cheap suit looked just as good as the Armani after he worked his magic!  I'll be back again soon.

My friend is Vegan, and this is one of her most frequented local restaurants. I ordered the Chicken a la Renee for $8.99 with mashed potatoes, green beans, and a salad. It's a great price for a place where you can actually get veggies! And, I had left overs. The garlic mash potatoes are more like homemade mashed potatoes. The veggie burger is legit too. We sat outside. That is a nice option to have, if you dislike chilly air conditioning. The server was very helpful. Meal payment is made inside at the register. There is plenty of parking.

They were attempting to repair a LG Studio series gas range. Top of the line according to manufacturer. They replaced a circuit board which cost over $300.

After replacing the board the issue still was prevalent. They contacted the manufacturer and it was then deemed that TWO more circuit boards need to be replaced. Another $700 and we still don't know if the issue will be solved. 

This being the case we went out and bought a competitor brand gas range. As we will have invested over $1000 and who knows what's will fail next.

Why didn't they just deem the range a "dog" and have the manufacturer supply a reconditioned range. But who knows the reconditioned range may be worse off. Or maybe a mouse may have been inside.

Maybe the manufacturer wants all items fixed no matter what the costs. But when you are spending almost as much as the items cost in the beginning there has to be a cut off point!

This newer coffee shop is a great place to meet friends or just hang out. The atmosphere is beautiful and especially great if you want to snap a photo or just enjoy pretty surroundings. The first time I was here I wasn't crazy about my drink (a chai latte that was way more latte than chai) but I decided to give it a second chance and I am glad I did. The cafe miel I had was very tasty. This spot has quickly become a staple in the Fountain Square area and I recommend checking it out if you are nearr
The Chinese food is great here!! The silver legacy has other restaurants worth visiting.

Really enjoyed dinner here this week with two friends.  With the courteous and on-point assistance of our waiter, we elected to share plates: shrimp hushpuppies, watermelon and tomato salad, curried veggies with rice, short rib.  The hushpuppies were AMAZING - crispy on the outside, soft and savory inside.  (At least) three tomato varieties were on the fresh and tasty salad. The curried vegetables were very good; I don't love short rib in general so I can't offer an honest opinion there. We couldn't decide on one of the many tempting desserts so we chose the butterscotch pot de creme and the berry mess.  Both were delectable, but the butterscotch was really special!!  So creamy but not heavy.  I love sorbet so the berry mess was quite a treat, too.  The decor is lovely - modern but comfortable.  Our waiter was helpful and attentive.  We all enjoyed this dining experience.

Great sandwiches and pizza is okay. Wings are cooked great,however almost every time we ask for Hot or xtra Hit they place us on hold and have to check to see if they have enough Hot Sauce.  Not sure why they can't have a large jar of Hot sauce ready for folks ordering wings like every other pizza shop I've ordered wings from before. So unfortunately we sometimes go elsewhere for that reason. #lostrevenue

I could not be happier with this place. I just feel like they've done so much for me. Like they could have taken advantage of me, but they didn't. I bought a Toyota Prius last month and I love it. JT was my sales rep, he is relatable and funny. He seems to genuinely care. And Christian in finance did to, even when I was being difficult  and they kept having to repeat things. Lol I'll be getting all my services done here.
Thanks guys!

We took my mom here for her birthday and it was so so. The waitress would not stop hovering and didn't say much when she did. It was odd. The food tasted fine but they didn't do anything to celebrate my moms birthday- I would have thought they would have sang. If the old lady was the owner- she was not very nice.

It's easy to find really awesome food in this city, but Sara's is definitely my favorite so far.  If you're not sure what you feel like eating, this is a really great choice.  Their menu includes everything from indian dishes like shrimp vindaloo to muscovy grilled duck breast (both are awesome).  It's a classy place with a nice, quiet atmosphere.  Oh yeah... and the staff were extremely friendly on both occassions.  5 stars.

This was a great Italian dining experience.  Our group had the back room where we were very well taken care of by the serving staff.  Our group of 8 shared two orders of toasted ravioli, calamari, and two orders of rice balls for apps.  Many of us ordered from their daily specials, but my scallops were each about the size of the palm of my hand!  Beautifully cooked and paired with root vegetables and gnocchi drizzled with brown butter sauce.  I live on the coast and I don't think I've ever had better scallops. They left enough room for dessert and I enjoyed a wonderful carrot cake.  We were there for about two hours and the back room privacy and attention from the staff made it a truly wonderful evening.

I keep ordering from Chubby's hoping that each time will be the time I get a good cheesesteak. That and the fact that they except credit cards.  Maybe its my fault I got to stop ordering hoagie cheesesteaks that come with lettuce tomato.  Each time its different: Sometimes I wondered if they forgot the cheese, or why there was so little meat or why meat was not even hot. Then I figured out the reason why there sandwich sucks, is because the lettuce and tomato are underneath the meat taking up too much space in the bread and also makes the meat cold.   I notice that there is alway a small amount of meat on the grill when they are making sandwiches. Is this because they are not busy or they are just cheap with the meat?  I don't know what it is, all I know is I am going to Delassandro's across the street from now on.  Even if I have to pay a surcharge at the ATM to get cash...its worth it.

Went post-Drake concert. service was awful--hookahs were subpar, nothing special. They use 33mm coals as their default coal type, which doesn't last very long when 4 people are smoking. Food was overpriced for what it was. Asked servers for water multiple times (upwards of 4 times) over the course of our 2hr stay, to no avail. It was very hard to get any waiter's attention, despite there being multiple waiters for a small seating space. We have definitely had muuuch better experiences elsewhere for the same price. would not recommend this spot.

Frozen asparagus in the asparagus salad, and a delicious sounding ubaruta margarita that was less than sub par. Too sweet, not anything like it sounds on the menu. Bartender might not know what muddled means. Overall, 10 Barrell has gone way too main stream.... Where hipsters go to drowned. Nice waiter tho, he was cool with giving us dirty plates because i said it was ok.

The food, drinks, and service were pretty good, but then they brought out the molasses factory foster... this was literally the best thing I have ever eaten. Fried plantains, pain perdue, vanilla ice cream, with cinnamon  I will return for that by itself.

My family loves to frequent Peacemaker! Such a cool, rustic interior and delicious food. The seafood is all to rave about, but let me tell you-the sides are just as good! First, we always get the hush puppies and they're gone in a flash. May just be me, but I never see hush puppies offered on menus anymore, and the ones here are to die for. Additionally, I love a good French fry, and these are top notch. Oh and the lobster mac...I would eat this for my meal! So freaking delicious. I think it's new to the menu, and if it is, whoever added it made a smart choice. It is $14 for a very small dish, but it is so good. Like I said, I wish it was an entree because I would totally order it. Keep up the good work, Peacemaker!
The food was good, nothing too fancy. The prices were a bit steep for average food. The waitress was good. It's going through remodeling right now but I think will look good again when it's done.

The absolute best! There facilities are very nice and very clean. All the people that work there are great! Dr Felix Bopp is excellent at HRT Pellets. The care and concern he has for each patient is second to none. I have had the pellet procedure at other locations and this one is the best. They are also very accommodating when it comes to scheduling and getting in to see the Doctor. A++

Went to grab a burger. The bartender, Amanda is awesome.  Great service. A little disappointed in the basic burger I ordered. Asked for medium and it was well done. Had good flavor though and was satisfying. Fun atmosphere.

Love, love, love the Dollar General and I don't care who knows it! I ended up here on Sunday when I tried to go to my neighborhood hardware store only to find it closes early on Sunday. This place has EVERYTHING. 

Items in our bags by the end of the trip:
(2) humane "no-kill" mousetraps
(1) package Atomic Fireball candy
(1) package Bit O' Honey candy
(1) liquid measuring cup
(2) rolls of tape
(1) notebook of paper
Total: Under $10

This is my new go-to spot for laundry detergeant, a new laundry basket, old-time candy, paper goods, writing supplies - really anything I can think of and would normally travel to Target for (or to South Street Market across the street).

I even got a surly check-out! Now I know that doesn't sound exciting but after reading all the reviews I was excited to see that the place lived up to everything that was written here. Yay for yelper accuracy!

When we stopped here for  breakfast we had no idea what wonderful surprises awaited us. The doh nut is something everyone NEEDS to try, it the king of all breakfast sandwiches. Its basically a bacon/egg/cheese sandwich but the bun is kronuts!!  Hubby had a grilled cheese with Muenster & it was also cooked to perfection. 

Decor is super cute (outdoor area looks fun too) and staff are very friendly. Can't wait to work my way through the whole menu!

Such a cool atmosphere and unlike anything I've ever been to. You walk into the wine and cheese shop, select a bottle (or 2!) and then select whatever cheeses and meats you so choose from a refrigerator. Once you have your items, you bring it to the counter to pay, they take your cheeses and meats, and deliver it to your outside (or upstairs inside in our case due to the rain!) and it's like magic. It comes back a beautiful cheese board with nuts and spreads and a delicious loaf of sliced artisan bread! Highly recommended! They also have a menu t order from the kitchen if you really need more, but two of us were full after our platter and wine!

This is my favorite place to eat in Reno. All you can eat sushi with the best rolls I've had is a great combination, particularly the basil salmon and ceviche rolls. The chefs are professional and the prices are very reasonable. Have a seat at the bar and dig in!

I got to say this little place is one of the last throw back bars in Manayunk.  I was on a bar crawl with this bar number three in the crawl.  The first two place's we stopped at were the Terrace Tavern & The Old Eagle which are located just 5 min. away.  I was happy to see that they had PBR on tap and I'm sure it was because they were not running a special.   It was my turn to buy the round and using my Jedi mind tricks I got off quite easy as 2 PBR's, a Coors Light, A Lager & a Twisted Tea came to just $14.00,  you just got to love that.  The bar is not real big and some of the highlights are the jukebox and the shuffle bowl.  They also have a few video games and that's about it. We had a great time, so that what counts the most as the bartender is quite nice and made you feel welcome.  They have your basic bar menu and the selection of beer is mostly domestic but hey it fits right in here as the prices are right.  The next two bars are Dawson Street and T. Hogan's so this made for a nice crawl as they are all only 5 to ten minutes apart walking.

I was here the other day, and I had a really fabulous experience.

A number of Anthropologists helped me, but Kristen is the only name I recall.  Because my memory sucks.  They were all super friendly, hospitable, and incredibly helpful.

The selection here is plentiful -- it's even better than at the Christiana and Evesham locations.  Lots of beautiful garments to look at.

I walked out with some really cute finds.  The prices are a little steep, but the materials feel wonderful, and the construction is good, too.

The home décor area is also a lot of fun to play around in.   The Anthro aesthetic seems to be a mix of Bohemian and eclectic.  It's pretty, but I prefer a more zen, Spartan, and contemporary vibe.  It's still fun to get lost in a sea of beautiful knickknacks though.

Absolutely loved the restaurant from the minute my Lyft pulled up to the building. Ordered the fried chicken egg Benedict and it literally melted into my mouth. I also ordered the morning margarita and it was amazing. Not only were the drinks and food were superb, but the scenery outside was truly comforting. Will definitely be coming back here on my next trip to the Big Easy!!
I ate there last night. I sat outside and it was really nice to be on South Street. The food was very good!

I had a nice breakfast here a chili cheese omlette I won't say it's the best I ever had but it was good. The portions were plenty. I found the combination of of slaw and beans along with the hash browns interesting. The service was good. I will return I want to try the biscuits and gravy I think not many places do it well but have high hopes for this place.

Art dogs has to be the most friendly business in Midtown. The collection of inventory on hand is amazing. There is no cheap junk here. Everything is tip top quality. And the staff is uber knowledgable. They've done a great job of mixing business with pleasure. I highly recommend stopping by to enjoy the atmosphere if you are in the area.
We love Dickeys however this location had a smaller menu.  Didn't see the deep fried pickles that I love.  The service was great and the establishment was clean.

I guess it should be called "China Wing" as it only occupies a small wing of the massive West Edmonton Mall. The place heavily decorated to fit the theme and definitely stands out from the rest of the mall. 

The main attraction is the T&T Supermarket, which is pretty much the only reason why I come to China Town. T&T pretty much has every Asian grocery you can think of. There are also a few other restaurants in China Town that are worth a stop. 

There used to be a great little import shop but I guess it closed down. I used to buy imported Japanese video games there every once in a while.

So this is within the new Tampa Midtown buildings, and is situated on top of ALoft hotels. Absolutely beautiful interior with some great aesthetics for some beautiful photos! Outside dining has a bar and multiple tables. However, the roof does share space with the hotel pool so you will hear chatter/noise from that area. 

The menu lacked options for the entrees (believe there are 6/7 options max) and were quite pricy. There's quite a few appetizers to chose from. The pricing on the appetizer is decent and normal for the area, but the entrees are a bit more. Remember you're paying more for the location and the views than the food. 

I ordered the tostones and they were simply awful. They was old, stale, chewy, and had no flavor. The guacamole and the crema were the most flavorful thing on the plate. When we asked the waitress if these were made fresh we were told "we can have some made fresh for you." It's disappointing to know they're serving old/stale food and wouldn't answer the question directly. My friend ordered the poke bowl appetizer, but it didn't come with rice. Though I don't believe the menu says it does, but if you're expecting it they don't have it. I ended up going with the Cuban and I would definitely say it's lackluster. I wanted so much to like the food but I honestly was so disappointed and joked with my friends that going to Shake Shack would have been more fulfilling of a meal.

Initially upon our arrival we were told we wouldn't have a table until closing but we waited around for about half an hour taking some photos. Then we checked in and they said it'd be about 30ish more minutes and a table opened up. However, we walked the outdoor dining and there was plenty of seating open outside so I'm not sure if it was a staffing issue or something else. Once we got seated our waitress wasn't the most personable and was kind of rude up front. It was through dinner the waitress tried to be a bit more personal with us, but it felt stilted. 

If I was to return, I'd eat elsewhere and go back here to have drinks and chit chat with my friends. That's just me personally and I hope others have much better experience than I did!

We just moved to the area and hadn't had a chance to check out bakeries.  A friend had a chicken pot pie and an assortment of cupcakes from Mix.  Wow!  Truly the best pot pie I have ever eaten.  The crust was absolutely perfect and I can't wait to try their sweet pies.  The cupcakes were delicious as well and the presentation was wonderful.

What is this place and why doesn't my city have one!  Rice paper burritos?  What!!  Yes yes yes!  The spice, the flavor, and the cost is RIGHT!  Loved this place and plan to return every time I'm in STL for work. Thank you for the inventive menu and FLAVORS!

My stylist, Kathy Brown, is a miracle worker! She takes the time to really understand what you want. She is also patient enough to teach you how to style the new cut on your own! Wonderful place, amazing hair stylists!

Not bad -- I ended up spending a fair amount of time here on my last trip because my companions like to gamble. Good selection of games though I did not see many new slots. 

I was not impressed with the wine selection on tap. The ONLY wines you can buy by the glass here are the house red and house white, which in my opinion tasted really awful. (To each their own though!) They didn't even have red at several of the bars I tried. The only way you can get around this is to drink at the steakhouse bar, which adjoins the casino and has an amazing beer/wine/liquor selection. The bartender there is a mensch too! 

The beer selection is slightly better but nothing to write home about either. I'm sure they want their visitors to stick with hard liquor to keep the cash flowing, but not everyone is into that and it would be nice to have better options for us beer and wine drinkers.

Great food! Started with the Caesar salad it was delicious- crisp and just the right amount of dressing. Hubby had the lobster bisque, it was ok but fishy tasting which I guess makes sense :) Next I had the tuna appetizer, it was fatty but the sauce was very tasty. Hubby had the petite filer which he loved. It was cooked just how he asked. We shared the mushrooms and lobster Mac n cheese- phenomenal! It however was my moms bday which we called in a reservation for and let everyone including waited know and they didn't do anything special.. No silly song, cocktail or dessert. Bummer
Really cool find in Clayton. Had the pasta toscano and small house salad for lunch and took half the pasta home. Pizza looked very good to at the other tables.

Wow. This place has crazy good dogs. Have tried a variety of meat and vegetarian dogs, and i might like the veggie dogs even more. Chicken are also very good if you want to stay abbot more healthy than beef and pork. 

I love the themes dogs, particularly the international ones. The samosa one was interesting and flavorful  - all the authentic Indian spices in real samosas but may not appeal to everyone. The latke dog tasted great as well. I had such a hard time trying just 2 of them!

Unbelievable how good the food is and how helpful the staff is on helping you choose what to eat. You can not go wrong eating anything there. The take out is great and it even reheats well the next day.

SHUTDOWN...they went out of business,unless of course they decided to take a month long vacation lol I talked to Marcos pizza next door and they said they shutdown. It's a shame since I enjoyed their food:(

Amazing!
No idea what I ordered, but it tastes so good! It definitely has some potatoes in it.
Very nice new restaurant. All of the sushi is delicious. The service is awesome. I've been three times and will continue to go.

Service was good what I would expect from a more expensive seafood restaurant I was underwhelmed by my portion I happen to have gone during devour downtown and it was my first dining experience there.  I started off ordering the jumbo shrimp cocktail which was very gotten it was served with an extra side of horseradish which I always prefer.  When it came to my entrée I had ordered Mahi Mahi  the fish looked like it was more like tilapia.  Our server never followed up to see how we were enjoying our meals otherwise I would've sent it back for a different option.  For how much we spent at the restaurant I expected my meal to be wonderful needless to say I won't be returning to this restaurant

This is probably the best sushi in south jersey. I eat a lot if sushi when i go to LA and this is as goid as many of those restaurants and a lot mire fairly priced. The fish is always moist and has a fresh shimmer. They have a large menu of creative dishes.

The meal we had at Cavan was the best that we've had in New Orleans. Our waiter, Rhett, provided excellent service and was very friendly and knowledgeable about the dishes. He described the dishes as they were coming out and was so informative, as well.
Chef, Nathan Richard, creates dishes with a uniquely artistic quality that, even in New Orleans, is so refreshing to find. Chef Richard started us with oysters with caviar. They were the exact right amount of salty and slight sweetness. We also shared a Charcuterie board with various smoked meats and soft cheeses. We could have just eaten that as our main dish, it was so good. The dish included among other things a very tasty pimento cheese. 
We also recommend the alligator soup (the alligator was so tender!) and the chicken and sausage gumbo, which was the perfect balance of seasoning without being too spicy and overpowering as it so often is.
We also shared the salmon poke tacos.They were made with big cubes of very tasty salmon and again, was not overly seasoned. The tacos were another dish that we could have eaten by itself, it was just so good!
But if you have to limit yourself to only 2 dishes for the night, it would have to be the 14 oz. blackened pork chop served with sweet potato salad and cane syrup mustard and also the millet risotto. Besides being a beautiful dish, the pork chop was the biggest we had ever seen and it was cooked to tender perfection. The risotto will be the best tasting risotto you have ever had with a perfect creamy texture.
We give Cavan, Chef Nathan and our waiter, Rhett, five stars. We will definitely be going back again every time we visit New Orleans. And it'll be the number one restaurant we will recommend to our friends!

I've been to Yamitsuki a few times and I always leave satisfied! They have a lot of menu options including cocktails and sake. I absolutely LOVE ramen so I can confidently say that it's not the best ramen I've had but it's really good! Yamitsuki is not my top choice for ramen but it's definitely in my top 5!

They also serve sushi here as well!
Love the nuoc mia more than anything cause I only get them at Vietnam so I'm happy to have it now

I left a message with Progress Plumbing around 10am on a Saturday morning regarding a leaky valve in my basement. Chip promptly called me back about 15 minutes later and gave me a fair quote on fixing the problem. He showed up shortly thereafter and proceeded to fix the leak. During this time he explained what he was doing and why he needed to do it. He seemed very honest and trustworthy so I'll definitely be calling him again if I'm in need of plumbing services.

I actually really like the crabby cafe. As a resident you get 10% off your bill. They have an excellent beer menu. Offer great deals during the week such as $6 mussel Monday's (my personal fav) or 50 cent wings on Thursdays. They have awesome buffalo shrimp which I pretty much have to get each time I go there. Great for watching sports as well. They're open pretty much always which is another plus. They were one of the only places that were open around me during the blizzard a couple weeks back.

I love this place, the  food is all ways good and hot. I am a big fan of the burger, just make sure u get it medium well, anything over that and it will be a bit dry. The chicken is crisp but dont expect those large chicken breast that you see in some places.  These chickens look like they are yard chickens! Anyone raised in the country knows what a yard chicken is and yard chicken = yummy! Do expect a line.  The seating it limited.  The wait staff is nice and very quick with the drink refills.  The one problem is the bathrooms.  They are small, outside and don't expect any hand towels.  That being said I dont go to a joint like coop's to use the bathroom. Its all about the food!
Yes it's slow. And it's also the post office. The clerks are friendly and helpful, and only a little bit smug. That's an A- for the USPS.

Mehhhhhhhhhh...Whole Foods is MUCH better. And you can actually move a shopping cart through that place. Trader Joe's is too small and didnt offer anything that I had needed on my shopping list. Only go if you are not buying anything specific. 

Upside is the quality of their items and the employees are very good.
I just ordered on door dash and got the smallest crab legs I have ever seen. Barely any meat in them. I feel like I just got punked lol!

First time here and 5. Excellent service. Great menu -followed by exceptional food. Beautiful views and ambience.  They had a sports like bar area -and dining area separate   Outside seating and party rooms up front. 
We started with grilled wings   They were perfectly grilled,not burnt and had a little kick.  Served with choice of sauce. Then 
 I had the crab cake salad -excellent-flavorful all crabmeat over spring mix with mango roasted peppers and carrot wings.  ribbons. Tim had the short rib sandwich which he loved.   He's hard to please too!  
I will definitely recommend this gem -this hidden gem-to all the people I know who love good food -good service and excellent choices of menu items.

Met a friend there last week after work and it was delicious!  I had been there before and it was convenient to order and take home but now they added a full bar and redid the menu. So good! Very colorful and flavorful sushi. Definitely recommend.

I actually came here for a family reunion, one portion of the restaurant was rented out. It was a course meal style, similar to Asian weddings but the course meal we ate was shorter with different selections of foods. 

Seafood soup 
Squid salad
Fried squid and eggrolls with fish sauce 
Fried rice 
Fried noodles and seafood 
Beef and Chinese broccoli

Everything was mediocre except for fried squid. They were crunchy and had a nice mild salt and pepper seasoning. Other than that, I don't recall anything else being good. 

The fish sauce was super sour and weird so don't dip your eggrolls in them FYI. I most likely will not come back.

This is a typical Chinese take out/delivery joint. However, the dishes we ordered were above par. There was plenty of shrimp in the house mei fun, the fried rice that came with the combo had veggies and lots of pork.

This place was amazing. We went here for our Anniversary and the Service and Food were great !!! The waiter was very good at knowing the cuts of meat and explaining the ingredients of the salads and the deserts. I would recommend this place and go on an empty stomach as it is a lot of food.
Absolutely delicious. Our only complaint is they weren't open for dinner on Sunday :)  Loved it!

Four of us went to dinner tonight and will definitely be going back again.
The cheesy biscuits were awesome and just enough for us to share. The two gals had the mini yorkies and the flavor was great.  Decided that it was sort of heavy for a meal and maybe we should have shared one order and had a bowl of chowder each to go with it.  The two guys had the lamb shank special and thought it was a delicious meal.  We had sticky toffee pudding and white chocolate cheesecake that we shared for dessert and both were excellent.  Our server, Sarah, was very friendly and knowledgeable.  The host for the restaurant was extremely authentic.   We watched him greet and seat all customers in a very friendly manner.  He was excellent at handling everyone and was fun to have greeting us.  Many interesting things on the menu.

The first time I went to the "Trop" I saw my Yankees play and win. I was expecting Tropicana Field to be a dump, but it was in very good condition. The place was really clean with plenty of shops and a huge open atrium that reminded me of a mall back home. The concourses are dated and reminded me of the Metrodome in Minnesota. Then I saw the playing field and thought to myself, this is definitely different. After getting used to the strange atmosphere of the place it really started growing on me. The bullpen pavilions are a great place to hang with friends and mingle with the ball players. The real problem with the Trop is the area its built in. St. Petersburg is like American's retirement village. Its like a ghost town most of the time. They should really move the team up north closer to the Tampa Bay downtown to improve attendance in my opinion.
Friendly staff, good portion size, average prices and easy parking. The store is a bit dated on the interior but overall for what it is there is really no complaints.

Nature's food patch is really great. I recently made a diet change and went full on paleo! The folks at nature's food patch could not have been more helpful in helping me figure out what was complaint and what was not. 

Coconut aminos? They got it. 

Ghee? done. 

They also have a really amazing produce section and an incredible salad bar/hot bar. 

It is more expensive than publix, yes, but you get what you pay more. I'm OK paying a little more for groceries to have really great quality.

Jimmys crows nest is a rooftop bar overlooking Clearwater beach. The view is great and the music is pretty good. The drinks however are not great, overtly sweet, made with cheap ingredients and served in plastic cups. Not the cleanest place, either. It's fine if you wanna hangout with a good view for a while.
All you need to know about Geno's is across the street at Pat's.  No comparison; Pat's is the best.  Do yourself a favor and head across the street....
Absolutely marvelous first visit  great sandwich I turn to brother man from the fourth floor , only I want is a sandmich lol ggggggrrrreeaat!!!

Flavorful, well seasoned & prepared food and at great value! Friends recommended this new Taqueria located on historic Main Street St. Charles in the former J. Notto's bakery location. I've been once for lunch alone and once for dinner with a group of friends and had a great experience during both visits. It's very small, but very good. They take care with the preparation of their proteins & they have chorizo, steak, chicken, fish, shrimp, coconut shrimp, avocado & bean tacos, burritos, enchiladas con mole, taco salad, Nachos, etc. Tacos are small authentic street taco style served in double corn tortillas. I highly recommend them. Their prices are low & tortilla chips are fresh made and are very thin and crispy reminiscent of Chevy's chips, but better. Their fresh salsa and guacamole are also very good. It's so refreshing to have a local Mexican option that serves fresh, healthy Mexican food and not just the same old processed cheese sauce doused American-Mexican that we are served at countless places with different names but almost identical menus. I plan to be a regular here, not only for the food, but also due to their customer service. You can tell this place is a labor of love. Congrats Lil Gio's, I think you'll be around for a long time to come!

We just had so much fun on a 4 hour excursion on 3 Rooker Charters! If you are anywhere near Clearwater Florida and like to be on the water then give this a try. Captain John is great. He is very knowledgeable about the area and the sea life around you. We went snorkeling, beachcombing, ate a nice lunch of burgers, that he grilled for us, with fresh fruit and veggies. The highlight for us was the dolphins. A small pod followed along with us for a time and then they started jumping the boat wake. They played along with us for probably half an hour. It was amazing and so much fun. He has a few other activities like tubing, etc., if you prefer. Check them out at 3rookercharters.com.

Agreed: people disagree about a mess 'a things. The leading culinary "bone of contention" (pun intended) is our beloved Barbecue. Or is it BBQ? or Bar-B-Cue? or Bar-B-Que or Bar-B-Q? I mean, people can't even agree on how to spell it, let alone how to cook it.

So having now traversed the continental states by plane hundreds of times and by car 7 times, I declare the following: Man, you can get some good 'Que' a lot of places across these wide-open spaces. And peoples' preferences are highly influenced by their home region. For the longest time I thought Carolina-style, vinegar-based barbecue was the be-all, end-all for barbecue. To me Texas rode herd on the best beef, and Memphis has wet and dry rubs....and...Kansas ...well, enough rambling. 

How about Martin's Bar-B-Que Joint?

The long lines and filled tables should tell you something. It's darn good!

Started with some smoky, spicy, dry-rubbed Spare Ribs. Heavy on the rub and smoke; you can temper that with sauce if you like. Almost had a jerky-like quality to the dark tips.

Next - tender, very juicy, fall-off-the-bone Baby Back Ribs; wet sauce topped these bad babes. Ummm good. Suck dem' bones, lick d'ose fingers.

Brisket - just moist enough, but with a bit of "tooth" to the meat, again smoked to perfection and a hint of pepper. 

Smoked sausages - so very smoky (as they should be) with a peppery tongue tease and "glow" for the back of your palate - all wrapped in a great natural casing with a "snap." 

One little disappointment - the pulled pork was just so-so. Tender and moist, but had very little character except to say it was like eating plain pork roast at Grandma's Sunday dinner table.

Biggest surprise of the meal was (all kidding aside) Cornbread Hoe-Cake; not sweet, but savory with a wonderful piquant, black pepper dominance to the flavor. Great palate cleanser between bites. 

Baked beans were good, but I fell short on really deciphering their seasonings - other than onion. Taste and see for yourself.

So which is the best? Probably the one you have in your hand, dripping sauce on the computer as you read this. 

Que-up! I'll see you at Martin's Joint soon.

Sweet Soul is my least favorite Ciccio Restaurant Group. Like other people, I am addicted to Fresh Kitchen & like Green Lemon. There's nothing I enjoy more than supporting local businesses, which is why I was so disappointed that they didn't have Matcha at the St. Pete location compared to the S. Tampa location, only Charcoal (Vanilla). Also, I have a sweet tooth and the Charcoal was insanely sweet that it became unpleasant after a few bites...I have been eyeing their Matcha soft serve for the longest time - the main reason I invited a friend was to give that flavor a try. My friend said the same thing, the Charcoal was too sugary atop her Matcha Waffle Cone. The redeeming factor was addition of dragonfruit, coconut chia pudding, raspberries, granola, Goji berries & honey drizzle. 

They have spacious seating outdoors, parking is tight & employees were nice.

Welcome to St. Pete - so glad you are here, but pleaasse do us a favor & add Matcha soft serve as an option, too!

My boyfriend and I were visiting for the weekend and we missed our kitties at home. We saw a card for cat therapy in our hotel's littler card menagerie and decided to check them out! We got there when they opened at 11 AM on a Saturday and were luckily able to fill the last 2 slots for that hour. We paid $14 each because it was a Saturday, but prices vary by day. I recommend booking ahead to guarantee a spot, because we saw multiple groups turned away after. It was quiet and clean with kitties galore, lounging, playing, snoozing, hiding. They were all well behaved and so precious. I love that they adopt all these cats out, but I also think it's a great concept for people who can't have pets to go snuggle for an hour. I think it's a great way to socialize these kitties before they find their forever home! Thanks, Cat Therapy!

This would be 3.5 stars.  The service was pretty good.  The burger was okay - better than fast food places, but not as good as the Counter burger chain.  We got the original burger, and the fries were kind of soggy.  I would come back again though, to try a different flavor and see if that might be a better experience.

Excellent brunch place for those who don't want to spend a whole lot of money.

They have your typical offerings, omelette station, prime rib, seafood bar, bacon, eggs,  etc.

It's relatively inexpensive, about $20 a person, because it doesn't have bottomless mimosas. However the price does include either two  mimosas or two Bloody Mary's. So I will call this a good place for those who aren't exactly thrilled about the all you can eat and bottomless mimosa places and the price that comes with those type of restaurants.
My favorite Starbucks in the city.  Great chaise lounges in the back that are perfect for snuggling on with a good book on a cold day.
Had the cheeseburger pizza and my daughter had the chicken bacon crunch i was so sad when they were gone. Need to stop by and grab a pie to take back to Florida.

SO SO happy this finally opened in Broad Ripple! They did a fantastic job with the exterior and interior of the building. I would definitely just hang out at the bar. I am a fan of Lou Malnati's in Chicago so I ate here the next day it opened. The staff and service were marvelous. Our server was great and always made sure we were taken care of. Recommend!

I wish I could give this theater negative stars.  The remodel has not helped the chaos that has always reined at this theater, only made it worse.  Only 6 or 7 theaters have "premium" seats which is not clear at all anywhere on their website. The concessions are a joke and the line is a mile long so you have to get there at least 30 minutes earlier than you planned to if you want a drink.  Carmike and now AMC in Tennessee need to go back to the drawing board and study how real movie theaters operate.  I recommend that management of these TN locations take a trip out to some AMC theaters that do it right (AMC Town Center 20 in Leawood KS for example).  Take my advice, save your money, skip the headache and drive on down the road to any other theater.  I will never step foot in there again.

Dear sweet baby jeebus, where do I start? I've wanted to check this place out for a while, and my boyfriend decided to take me there for my birthday dinner yesterday. It was a Wednesday night so the pace was relaxed. We did the whole shebang. We bought a bottle of wine that our server (Cristianna?) recommended. It was nice and light, just enough citrus, and a nice light hint of almond. Nice start. We ordered the mussels and the charred octopus appetizers. I very much enjoyed them both, but the mussels were something extraordinary. There was some sort of fried pork mixed in with the mussels, and each perfect trifecta bite of sauce/pork/mussel had me reeling. I'd be more embarrassed admitting that we ate the leftover sauce like soup if it hadn't been so damned good. We decided to stay with the seafood theme, and ordered the seared scallops and the capellini Nero for our entrees. They were nice enough to split the capellini for us so we didn't have to go at it Lady and the Tramp style considering we were sharing everything. I didn't know what to expect from a pasta with squid ink in it, but it exceeded my expectations. It came out beautifully dark, and had a nice little zing from the lemon and jalepeno. The seafood in it was nicely cooked too. The scallops were another nice surprise. They were large, tender, and interestingly paired with two executions of peas, beech mushrooms, kale, and a carrot reduction. I love peas, but I've never thought to pair them with scallops. I was apparently missing a satisfying food experience this whole time. We couldn't leave this place without checking out the dessert menu. We ordered the pistachio semifreddo, and the Meyer lemon panna cotta. Both were delicious, but the semifreddo was mind blowing. It was accompanied by a peach compote and candied pistachios. I'm still thinking about this dessert. 
It was a great experience. Our server was friendly, she helped us navigate the menu, and she wasn't pushy when we were trying to make our choices. You will drop some money here if you do it right, but I assure you it's worth it. You do seem to have to wait a little for each course, but I wouldn't expect that anything that hit our table last night would be done instantly. I can't wait to go back!

I went there for the first time today. I drove from another county to try what everybody raves about. The portions are great. But the food was bland My husband got the 1/2 lb Stuffed burger and fries and a tea. I got the french dip, onion rings and a tea.. Like I said the portions were great but the burger really had no flavor and the french dip with cheese had more than the menu said  It had mushrooms, onions and orange sweet peppers.
