Well 1st off my 1st experience with them was the delivery driver showing up an hour and a half after i ordered the pizza and it was crumbled in the bottom of her bag and all she had to say was i have other pizzas to deliver call the store i guess THEN 2nd time delivery once again an hour to get to me and it made it in the box but was crumbled inside of it! And when i called and askes for it to be fixed they called me a liar even after i brought it down to them and showed them they made a comment i must have done it to the pizza myself........rude.......then the 3rd time i ordered they gave me the completely wrong pizza and then to top it off tonight they told me they couldnt make me a pizza because they closed in 25 minutes even though it takes 10 minutes to make a pizza and i was picking it up at the atore i didnt even want it delivered and i was under the assumptuon if a buisness is open until 11 they are supposed to serve until 11. Also im sick and tired of every time i walk in there hearing people curse and seeing them playing on there phones and laughing and joking that may just be the problem.....staff mostly rude managers ive talked to....rude and terrible service im really thinking about not going back again its just ridiculous and getting ahold of higher managment is even worse....they dont answer the phone so i guess the buisness will continue to fall ubtil it ahuts down....that is so sad i wouldnt recommend this location to anyone.

After four years of living in Philly, I finally made it to Sampan for happy hour! I wish I had come sooner. Drinks were reasonably priced and happy hour snacks were good. The best thing was the broccoli, which was pan fried to perfection and seasoned with garlic. The edamame dumplings were also excellent. The tofu "tacos" were the only disappointment. They were encased in fried wonton wrappers, and the flavor was dominated (ruined) by sweet and sour sauce. (The menu description didn't even mention sweet and sour sauce.)

I would gladly come back here for happy hour, though I wouldn't bother coming for dinner, since the vegetarian dinner options were pretty sparse.

I will heap my praise upon the growing pile of steamy, spicy WMD love. Giac K and I went here with our Philly host Christopher R. Most hot sauce stores are fun because of hilarious painful flatulence related names (ex. Bayou Butt Burner, Ass on Fire, etc, etc), but WMD is one of the few that simply brings it without worrying how clever their name or label is. 

The owner is clearly someone who cares passionately about the sauce he makes as well as someone who loves his job. He was very enthusiastic in sharing his creations with us when we asked to sample his "ghost pepper" sauces. I want to have a business or job that makes me as happy as making hot sauce seems to make this guy. 

Anyway, the ghost peppers. These carrot based hot sauces made my trip down to Philly worthwhile all by their lonesome. There is so much flavor packed in each level in addition to the heat. And good lord is the heat there. You may not pick up as much when sampling, but once you get a bottle home and pour it on your meal, you will most definitely feel it.

Ask for Rafael if you want to find out more information regarding the various programs offered. Rafael is knowledgeable and very professional. I had a TON of questions prior to committing to the RT program and he always had a quick response!

I went in here with one of my friends for an early breakfast.  The cashier lady could not have seemed less happy to be there, but it was Monday Morning at 8AM so I guess I can't blame her too much.  I ordered an omelet with toast and grits along with a cup of coffee.  The coffee was delicious and my meal tasted like it was homemade.  From walking in to food on table took probably took 10 minutes, so the service is lightning fast.  Would recommend to someone looking to get a quick bite but I had to knock off a star for the cashier.

The Spanish food served here is good for what it is , fast food served on the spot, the cuajito is a bit over priced for what it is , sautéed pig ears dredged in a vinegar and oil base. The morcilla was good but somewhat dry i needed to dip it in some vinegar to really make it pop, the potatoe balls were good but lacked a bit more gravy over all I can say that the food was good but for the prices I expected just a little more food I was still hungry after ordering three items.

Reserved for a planned three night stay for the Big Ten Basketball Tournament.   Drove in and they have either valet or self park.   Check was easy and our room was quite modern and comfortable.   Location was fine with about a ten to fifteen minute walk to the downtown spots but also restaurants in the immediate area as well.   Unfortunately the games were canceled and so we left for home after just once night.  Our bill was adjusted accordingly.   Would highly recommend for convivence if driving as well as friendly desk help and clean and modern rooms.

I wish I could give this place ZERO stars. Too bad that's not an option. I've been a loyal customer here for years and consistently go here for Pho when I'm in Chinatown or taking a lunch break from work. This happened to me about three months ago, but since I decided to start yelping again, I feel strongly to write this and put this out there.

I usually get the pho. When I got it, it had a visible piece of hair. I usually don't like to make a fuss about wrong orders or my orders at all, but come on... a visible piece of hair!?! So I call one of the waiters over and he sees it and takes my bowl away. Less than a minute later, I get my food back and guess what... THE SAME PIECE OF HAIR IS STILL THERE and it just looked like they stirred the other stuff around. 

I really wanted to walk out at that point... anyway, don't ask me what ended up happening, but needless to say, I WILL NEVER BE RETURNING TO CHOO CHOO'S AGAIN AND WILL BE ANTI CHOO CHOOS FOREVER. Go to Pho Ha in South Philly if you want some decent service or Pho. Choo choos is garbage.

The only reason I won't give Zaytoon 1 star is the ambience. The location is beautiful but not the food. I spend much of my time traveling between Los Angeles and Santa Barbara and after eating middle eastern food from many other amazing places I would have to say that this is some pretty horrible food. The only reason this restaurant has any success is because it's the only Middle Eastern in town.

The hummus is bland and tastes store bought the meat isn't seasoned well or cooked in a way that I would expect from a good middle eastern restaurant. The pita was stale. I wish there was more authentic middle Eastern food in town.

Came here on Saturday night while wandering around the city. We were hungry so it was amazing that they were attentive and the food came quickly. The Golden Triangle tofu was soft yet also crispy. Came out hot which was perfect. The peanut sauce was so good I took heaps on my first triangle, which caused a problem for the later triangles haha. I ordered the Pad Prik Pow because of the baby corn, peppers, onion mushrooms and hot chili sauce. Really enjoyed the dish. Pretty nice sized portion with a mound of rice and the sautéed mixture on the side. The location of the restaurant was nice and the service was very good. Would recommend going!

my first time trying Hamentashen - triangular poppyseed-filled pastry. VERY DELICIOUS-  especially with a glass of milk.

All the cakes in the display were gianormous and i am planning to come back and try some ..very soon!

This is the 4th time in as many months that I've dined at the Bonefish on Vets and had a horrible experience.  I've NEVER seen such unfriendly and rude bartenders. This restaurant's drinks are generally weak already so nastiness certainly doesn't help.
Very cute place.  Loved the cat decor.  The wings were great, we would definitely go back here.
Channeling my inner Valley girl: So, like seriously, these are the best tacos--ever. Chips and guac are like totally awesome. The neg reviewers--oh my god-- clueless! Whatever...

Super awesome staff!s! 11/10 

negatives are that this site rarely has flower, seems to be especially afraid of sativa flower as seemingly always hybrids....and, well,, lacking variety in general.

This is hands down the best burger and grilled cheese in town!!  I almost hate to give it a great review cause I don't want people to find out about my favorite new place!  But, the owners are too amazing to not share how great this place is!!!

I generally have written posts about places to eat and drink so this review is totally out of the norm for me!  
I recently had my check engine light go on so I took my poor Civic to my trusty neighborhood AutoTire.  I regularly go here for my oil changes, tires problems and basic car care for two main reasons.  First and foremost, it is super close to my apartment, actually across the street so it is easy to drop off the car and walk home, rather than get picked up or sit in the waiting room watching FOX TV.  Secondly, I go there for their professionalism.  I used to go to a variety of different places all of which had good prices but would take advantage of me for being a female.  More than once I was told to let men deal with cars and not try to self diagnose the car myself from other local establishments.  That does not fly with me!  At AutoTire they assume I know MY car and they listen to my ideas before still checking for anything that could be the problem.  
Aside from those two undeniable facts they have handfuls of other great qualities.  They are very fast!  I hate to not support local businesses and I am not a fan of nationwide chains, but my car is a part of me and I like that they can fix any problem without ever keeping the poor girl overnight!  Aside from fast they also seem to have the nicest guys working at the counter...they are always so friendly and very upfront about pricing and what needs to be done.  They also once recommended me to another shop for a problem they could not fix...rather than leaving me stuck with the problem!  They always get me the best price!  On more than one occasion I told them I remember seeing coupons in the mail or online and they would look them up, see what I could use and applied them to my cost!  
I recommend this place to everyone and never take my baby elsewhere!!

We have dined at Guadalajara grill on East Prince many , many times. Paul, Margarita and the staff have been phenomenal. We moved NW recently and decided to try Guadalajara in N Oracle Rd. 
What a mistake. In entering the restaurant we obviously interrupted the hostesses day. When she looked up and finally acknowledged my wife and I, it was with a look of "your bothering me." We asked for a booth at the bar( there were two or three empty)and she studied the map for 10 seconds , sighed and said follow me. She seated us at the outside door where servers were going in and out ( it was cold). I asked for another booth and here comes that look again. What a pleasant lady. The server thankfully chimes in and said "open seating at the bar sit where you would like." We found one of the three empty booths.  Food was not quite up to Prince road but the Margaritas were perfect. Not enough to bring us back.
After a really frustrating day, I met Smiley at the Dale Mabry showroom.  She was so kind and helpful!  The tile I bought was great and my salesperson was the BEST!!  Thanks

Have gone here on and off for years and years. Never been disappointed. Nothing astonishingly good but to be consistently good for so long in Philadelphia is astonishing. Great salads, and the savory crepe are just as good as the sweet, not always the case at other crappy crepe places. sorry no accents on crepe. Decor is elegant and wonderfully french. Fairly quiet considering only one block from South St.

I was very excited to try this. And I was NOT disappointed. When I walked In I was greeted with a smile and got in a line with about 10 orders in front of me. Now, I you have seen my other reviews, you know I am not a big fan of waiting in line, but I smelled the pulled pork and decided to wait it out.

Ok, four orders later, and I am STARVING. How much longer is this line? However, I told myself I had already committed to this, so I had to see it through. 

Finally at the line, I order my meal: pulled pork sandwich with a side of creamy cole slaw. I watched in fascination as the staff created the meal, very fast (why the line was slow, I have no idea) and my mouth started to water. I finally got to the cashier and paid for my meal. Not too bad in terms of price.

THE TASTING:
Wow. I was blown away at the flavor that this meal packed into one sandwich. After putting the cole slaw on my sandwich I screamed (don't worry I was at home) at how good it was. I will definitely be back, I will just have to find a time where they are less busy. (I came around 5:30).

Also, I highly suggest thinking of them for catering. I hope to use them for my next family event.

We were originally thrilled a few weeks ago when we went to the new Weekends Only store on Manchester.  We found a bedroom set for a great price, however, they only had the floor model.  They told us they'd give us 10% off the price since it was the floor sample and we said we'd take it.  We waited an hour while they were ringing it up, but eventually our sales rep came over and told us there was a mix-up and someone else was taking the bed out of the set.  He said that they'd give us 10% off the price of anything else in the store or they could call us when they got more in of the one we wanted and they'd give us 10% off a new set.  We decided we liked that set and would wait.

They called last week and told us the new furniture had arrived.  We went in today to get it.  The price on the set had gone up $100 since we were last there.  Our sales rep said that they coudn't honor the price they had told us, but they'd still give us 10% off.  We told him we weren't going to buy it for $100 more.  Feeling like we had a bait and switch situation.

We called the store and spoke to the manager when we got home.  Waiting to see if they do anything about it.

Update: Manager called back and said there had been some miscommunication on their end and they would honor the price.  Looks like we're headed back up there.

I am not sure how this delightful little bakery and restaurant has not made it on the list of Happy Cow/veg must haves in Nashville, but it definitely deserves it's spot in the limelight. I only discovered it with my family while visiting because we took a wandering walk while waiting for a table of six during busy Sunday brunch hours at Wild Cow. Oh my that apple fritter was good! I bought enough for the whole family. Can't wait to come back and try the raw cheesecake too!

Stopped by 2nd story on a Tuesday afternoon while we were in the area, and needless to say they weren't very busy during this time. They looked like they had some good brews, plus they were participating in the limited release collaboration beer, the Veterans-made Memorial Day DIPA.

The bartender today was super friendly and helpful. We decided to try a flight of My Better Hef bavarian hefeweizen, 3 Sheets belgian tripel, Ol McDonald farmhouse saison, and C's the Day imperial IPA. Each brew was incredibly delicious and unique from the next. I was happy with each of them, and thinking back, I probably should have left with a six pack of something. The limited release Memorial Day beer, Hurry Up and Wait, was delicious, satisfying, and complex in flavor.

If in the area, I'd definitely return again- and I'd recommend anyone else in the area to check them out as well!

My husband and I had lunch at Frida's.  We have wanted to try this restaurant for awhile and we are so happy that we did. First, the salsa and chips were delicious - this is a very good start.  I had the red sauce enchiladas with beans and rice.  Four enchiladas loaded with white meat chicken - delicious.  Even the rice and beans were good.  My husband had the beef tacos.  It was two delicious flour tortillas with cheese in between and then loaded with beef and some cooked onion (not overloaded).  They were delicious.  We weren't hungry but we had to try the churros. The churros were cooked perfectly and even better - had a filling.  So delicious.  The service was very friendly.  The fun, colorful artwork creates a nice environment. We found out that it's BYOB also. A great addition to the area and we will add this restaurant to our local favorites list.

I came to Juno with a few friends and really appreciate everything that was done to adhere to social distancing and keeping everyone safe. There is outdoor seating available that is really beautiful and well-designed. The tables were separated far apart and it was comfortable eating there.

We got nachos for the table and we all enjoyed them. The chips stayed crispy and did not get soggy. My favorite part was definitely the pickled onions.

I got the carne asada, there are three tacos that come with a sauce. The flavor was really good combined with the sauce. I have definitely had better asadas elsewhere but overall these were pretty good and definitely filling. 

Try to check out Juno if you're looking for somewhere with outdoor dining, reservations have to be made beforehand through their website. I really enjoyed my experience here and it made dining out feel like normal again. Good food, good atmosphere, and good service!

I've been to a lot of Indian restaurants in Edmonton and Origin India takes the cake! My one word of advice - skip the buffet order off the menu. Sure, the buffet is good, just like most indian buffets, but the food on the menu is fantastic! The service is excellent, so again, take advantage of their attentive servers and order off the menu. I also love the beer selection - they have a very large variety of international beers and are happy to make recommendations to go with what you've ordered. It's our first choice for dinner on Whyte!

Perino's is a casual, very lively, middle-class boiled (and, some fried) seafood restaurant along U.S. Hwy. 90 (business route) in Harvey, Louisiana. The outside is plain, and parking is also available at the hotel spot (which seems to be owned by Perino's), behind the restaurant building. The interior is decorated with numerous big-game animals that the owner bagged on an African hunting tour. We ordered the fried shrimp plate and the fried soft-shell crab plate. Both plates come with curly fries, but not salad. The shrimp were big, juicy, and plump. My friend's soft-shell crab plate came with three decent-sized crabs. We both remarked on how nicely spiced the items were and how none of it was greasy. This is definitely a landmark neighborhood joint, and we were very impressed. Highly recommended and would return. RJT

So far this the best I can give them for the service department just do to the simple fact that if you take car in for service they don't offer courtesy car or even courtesy ride, they said they will call you a cab. This is on my daughter's car that she bought brand new. Will update after service happens. I guess I just got used to Audi Boise service which is absolutely top notch and really want their customers happy and after reading a lot of reviews they haven't done much to improve sounds to me like they either need a new GM or a new owner not sure who doesn't care about their customers. I will update after first service in the next week or so.
Drinks aren't made well. Staff is rude. Music is the only good thing. Give it a miss!

When I sustained a bad knee injury, Urgent Care told me it was broken but that I should see an orthopedist to determine whether it would need surgery. I got a recommendation from my PT to see Dr. Yau, and when I called for an initial appointment, they were able to squeeze me in immediately to check me out!

After examining me and my x-rays, Dr. Yau determined that my knee wasn't broken after all, and recommended that I follow a PT regimen in order to speed recovery and minimize atrophy and loss of mobility/flexibility. Thanks to his diagnosis and advice, I got back to 100% and am now back to distance running and my regular workouts with no trace of pain or weakness. Dr. Yau was kind, knowledgeable, and you could tell he wants the best outcome for his patients.

I always saw athletes in the waiting room, which is just another indicator that this is the place to go if you are active and want to have the best results.

Absolutely fantastic dining experience at this upscale Mexican restaurant. We found out that the chef has been working for 32 years! The service, food, drinks and ambience were seriously outstanding! You MUST check this place out of you're in the Tucson area...you will not regret it!

This is my favorite Chinese restaurant and possibly my favorite restaurant across genres in Philly. Every dish I have ordered has always been delicious and expertly seasoned and tastes homemade with love. My favorite dish of them all is the spicy diced chicken with chili peppers, peanuts, Sichuan peppercorns, and more delicious spices. I crave this dish no matter where I am in the country and haven't found a restaurant that prepares it quite like this. I also love their sautéed lotus root and spicy shredded potato, and mapo tofu. You really can't go wrong here!

No wonder they are empty! Sign says new temp hours 11a-10p, walked in at 1145a, no one there at all, and I dont mean customers, waited 10mins and no one ever came over to seat us, didnt even see a person at all.

Good for a week night dinner. You get to pick all your own ingredients which I like (I'm very particular on my shrimp to broccoli ratio) and you can watch the cooks make it. Seems a bit pricey for what you get and I'm kinda iffy about the raw meats sitting out on ice because it looks like food poisoning just waiting to happen, and most of the time the meat leans towards overcooked while the veggies lean toward undercooked, but it's a cool place to go if youre going to the movies next door or something.
The service was extremely great, honestly, the best waitress I have ever had at a steak n shake. Kaitlyn was such a kind and helpful presence in our dining experience. highly recommend.

I was treated to an early Birthday dinner by my cousin at Raaga. I had heard it opened in the last year, and while it had good reviews by some other well-trusted reviewers, I had not managed to get to eat there despite it being basically a hop, skip, and a jump away.

Raaga is in the same plaza as Bank of America, Crunch Fitness, Peabody's, and Hungry Howie's. Upon entering, you are basically entering a yellow and brown cafeteria with a single Hindu statue at the front. There are a few Indian paintings, but the main seating area is bland as heck.  There is no Indian music playing. Heck, there is no music playing at all which is weird. There are some TV's with Bollywood stuff muted. Ok then.

Raaga is apparently owned by Andra Pradesh people, which is part of South India (but not my peeps).  However, they serve many of the North and Central Indian staples as Chicken Tikka Massala, Tandoori etc.

Instead of tap water in a carafe with ice, we were given bottled water at room temp. One should note that ordering sodas is "a la carte", meaning you get the can and are charged per can. (No free refills like most US sit down restaurants)

I ordered Lamb Rogan Josh and 1 garlic naan. The curry came with some plain rice.  The servers checked on us every so often.

While the food tasted great it was lukewarm on arrival and in 10 minutes it was stone cold. I suspected they just reheated pre-made food out of a container. Thankfully, the naan was served hot  and fresh. 
I probably should have complained , but I'm usually not the type to make a scene especially since I Was not paying.

There were only 4-6 other people in the restaurant

1) on a Saturday night
2) during Xmas season, 
3) and in an upper middle class area (Tampa Palms).

Brainiac: This is highly improbable, Kal-El
Superman: Life's been full of surprises these past 21 months.

Overall: Potentially good food , but diminished by temperature and ambience. 
I would suggest Taj for better ambience for similar prices.

I haven't really eaten Indian much outside of grilled meats as Apna Bazar/Grill. since Jai Ho went out of business last year, it would be nice to have a nearby Indian restaurant that could be great, but I doubt it will be Raaga.
The service was great. I was shocked at the fact that it was a ghost town on $5 Tuesday.

Went there for lunch and ordered seafood gumbo which was good but a little too salty. Then I got the shrimp remoulade salad which was supposed to be on a fried green tomato. The restaurant must think I am color blind because they tried to fry a slice of red tomato and served it. Needless to say it was very soggy and greasy with the water content of the red tomato. The waiter was nice and checked on me so I told him politely what the issue was. He went and talked to the manager who also came and checked and said that their sous chef made a mistake. I said, that is ok and did not return the food as I had already consumed my shrimp. 
The waiter talked me into flourless chocolate cake which was very good and a cup of coffee. I was shocked when my bill arrived that they did not even comp me a cup of coffee or my glass of iced tea for their mistake. I don't think that is a sign of a good hotel. I am sure if I had raised a stink, i would have my whole salad for free. So niceness does not pay here.

Great home style restaurant.  Reasonable prices, good food and a clean restaurant.  I took my boys there for breakfast, I had not been in years.  The food was and still is very good, the menu has the regular classics.  My boys were happy, food was good and the waitresses were quick and caring.

We love fried chicken so while having drinks our bartender suggested that we come here for good wings. Went on a Tuesday afternoon. I must say I was impressed. I tried the garlic pepper, 0017, exotic Cajun (new flavor not on menu), original fried, and one more I can't remember. All were full of flavor and the customer service was great. Tried all three punches; Oprah, watermelon (tastes just like watermelon), and the concoction. The young lady let us sample flavors because it's so much to choose from. Definitely going here each time I visit Nola!

This district in St. Louis has a really hip feel to it, and The Mud House fits right in.  It has all that artsy, jazz, book-reading-y kind of stuff.  I passed by it and headed in for a little breakfast snack, and everything is pretty affordable.  I do not eat breakfast foods on a normal basis, but with only a single morning to do St. Louis food exploring, breakfast was my only option.

I found this joint while yelping around for "local" restaurants, and I figured this would be an upscale eatery geared around locally sourced ingredients.  It was actually more of a cafe.

I have not eaten French toast in quite some time, mostly because I do not eat sweets.  Alas, I still tried it out.  The French Toast was $6.50, and it was pretty dang filling.  It offered 2 huge slices of toast, slightly crisped, but more on the soggy side.  It was drowned in syrup, but I do prefer my fattened-up refined-flour baked good to be very crisp with just a light drizzle of sweet stuff.  They do give you tons of bananas and pecans to balance out the sticky sweetness.

My French Toast took about 20 minutes to make, and it was pretty nice to see that time and care were taken into my dish.  The Mud House is a great place to grab a cup of joe or a bite to eat.  Nothing is extremely unique on the menu, but it is all done by hand.

I have been coming here for years and not sure why I never took the time to write a review (probably because I don't want it to become TOO popular and then never be able to get an appointment!)

Bill is an excellent hair stylist who does my highlights, cut and blow dry. Every time I leave feeling beautiful and ready to take on the world. He also is fun, easy to talk to and reasonably priced.

His dog Reese is super chill and a nice addition to the relaxed vibe of the place. I highly recommend getting your hair did at Aqua!

What a nifty find on my bike ride this afternoon! Friendly, helpful staff that encouraged sampling. An ever-changing array of interesting flavors. Super-fresh, organic ice cream. A beautiful, spacious building with cool wood ceilings and exposed brick walls. Basically, perfection on a hot, sunny summer afternoon and one of my best ice cream experiences.

Diner food was okay but priced high with fancy decorum. Our server Denise was very nice. Chicken parm was over coated with breading and smothered in cheese. It's probably just a bit overpriced for diner fare. The interior is very well appointed. It doesn't feel like a Diner experience when you're in the dining room, but when your plate comes you'll remember you're in a diner.

I've been here twice now and hands down it's the most consistent and best Italian restaurant in Tucson. Every single thing I've had here is amazing, both times. This time we had the shrimp and garlic starter and the calamari, both perfect. For my entree I had a chicken dish that was with artichoke hearts, shrimp and cheese. It was so good and plentiful the leftovers lasted for 2 meals after we went- and they may have even tasted better!
This was a great experience. All the food was tasty and delicious and especially guilt free. Ready to go back.

Melissa in the front greeted me.The woman was unbelievably RUDE!! I own 4 homes have spent a ton of money here on marble and tile. I went in to try to match an old broken tile. She rolled her eyes, was very sarcastic wanted to know who the imbecile was who referred me to her. I asked if she could help me. She refused. I asked for Jeff who works in the back. She got up to go get him (as opposed to paging) . To give him the downlow no doubt. I asked her name she replied 'It does'nt matter'. Jeff found me a match tile. I will NOT go here EVER again!

The best nova lox i have ever seen or tasted. Hand sliced by an artisan.  You can see your fingers through the slices. I have been buying nova for 50 years and this is the best 
hand sliced nova i have ever seen or eaten. Ask for Joe to slice yours.  He will take a whole side of fish and slice one long / huge slice.  Will also trim it perfectly and layer it on wax paper perfectly.  I am sold. Who would have thought that an Italian Store had the best nova.  A job well done.

Were seated in the bar area. Immediately felt the slippery tile floor...oil from tossing salads. 
Holy SALT! Both if us thought the paella was ridiculously salty... Not just to taste, but the gut response was noticeable.  When our paella was served between us, my husband got all the shrimp and I got all the scallops...had to sort that out. Will probably not rush back. Too many other choices.
They have changed appointments on me twice already, and at the last minute too.  This branch is not very reliable.  Best to try other nearby branches.

Florida Chain of Tex-Mex food, multiple Tequila options bar and bustling crowd no matter where they are located.   In International mall on the food strip we hit Rocco's after the Giants Victory over Tampa for a celebration cocktail and some drinks.  We sat at the bar and service was fine all evening.   Prices for everything are High, drinks, food etc. just an FYI. 

Chips and Salsa for $4.50 probably best thing on the menu and not for the price but generous portion of hot chips with plenty of Pico and a red or green sauce to dip as well. 

Two wet Burritos are massive, and they are rolled and stuffed with your choice of filling $15.00 each.  Both the chicken and the pulled port were very tasty while they were so big, we couldn't eat them. 

3 Carne Molida $4.50 each tacos ground beef was simply Ok and that's a reach.  Not quite sure what the mystery meat was but it wasn't very appealing.  

3 Carne Asado tacos wood grilled flank steak $6.50 looked a little better but def not worth $6.50 per. 

Stick with the burrito and salsa and chips and have a beer instead of the $11.00 overpriced margarita and you will enjoy yourself.  Good vibe, very nice staff and very accommodating.  Just a little pricey and a little disappointment on the Tacos. 
peppers

Couldn't decide where to eat our last night in New Orleans. Chose here and were very happy with the choice. I got the voodoo pasta, wife got shrimp and grits, kids got jambalaya pasta and seafood basket, and we got the crawfish and alligator nachos. We also got the bread pudding and pecan pie fore dessert. Everything was really good, I would definitely recommend the nachos, the voodoo pasta and the bread pudding.  Brittany and Stacy were great servers.
Great and great value... Took my fiancé here because she had never been to a Crispers before , she thoroughly enjoyed our meal... We will definitely be back

My sister and I can find most of what we need to make Korean food. We made a quick stop the other day to get some Korean sesame oil and some other things. I can't remember.

The produce isn't always fresh from my two visits so far, but we've always gone in the evening, so maybe that's a factor? I also haven't gotten any fish because it doesn't look too fresh.

But I like the variety of Asian products on the shelf.

The food was delicious, but wow are the portions small. I had to ding a star for that. I would technically give 3.5 stars, but since they don't allow that, I am rounding up to 4 stars for the good food. We got there around 7pm, when it was a busy time. The only table they had available was at the oyster bar. It ended up being a pretty cool spot because we got to see the oysters getting shucked. You also get a closer glimpse into the kitchen and how they cook the food. 

My fiance and I shared our dishes: we started off with gumbo, then had the cauliflower steak and BBQ shrimp. The gumbo was perfection - it tasted so good, we were hungrier than before we started eating. The BBQ shrimp had a lot of flavor and seasoning. I thought the cauliflower steak was unique and tasty, but my fiance didn't end up liking it. To be fair though, he really likes to eat meat, so if there's a non-meat dish, he's not going to like it.

Overall, had a good experience dining here. Our waiter was a little inattentive at times and the portions are ridiculously small. My fiance and I can eat, so we ended up finishing our dinner at the Halal Guys. We were both still very hungry so we got a lamb & chicken platter to take back to our hotel.

NEVER order from here. It doesn't matter how terrible or great the food might be (I still don't know) because you'll be waiting until the remake of Game of Thrones before your food arrives. We ordered, got a delivery time of 9:45 pm, and the food never arrived that night. And we never heard from anyone about its status. Having to call the next day to get our money back, that's such a great business
I tried their rotis and it was horrible!!! Well I kinda figured out how other dishes would be from my experience after all rotis are basic

We had dinner here the other night with our friends.  It was amazing.  We ordered 12 wings, combination appetizer, pub burgers, holiday pasta and the gilroy pizza.  Everything tasted great.  Service was great.  The decor was great.  Everything was GREAT! We need to come back for happy hour. 

Plenty of parking.

Meh, coming from the southwest I wouldn't say that this place was anything spectacular. 

I ordered a plate special that set me back 7.99 and came with two enchiladas a crispy taco and some beans. The menu states that rice comes with the dish and I asked if it came with beans - I was only served rice. The sauce on the enchilada was pretty weak and tasted like marinara. I asked for an authentic sauce and the waiter kept warning that it was spicy. I said , "bring it dude" (in Spanish of course). The "red sauce", as he called it was nice and spicy although it was cold. I'm pretty sure it was meant to be a salsa. I wouldn't complain that the food was bad but by no means did it knock me over. 

The salsa was pretty mild and very tomato-y. "What's wrong with that", I hear you ask. It just didn't taste rather authentic. But again, I wouldn't say it was bad. 

My two kids each got a taco salad and a burrito off the kids menu. My oldest son thought the burrito tasted "weird" but I think he was turned off by the sweet tomato marinara flavor. 

All in all the meal was a little cheap for a sit-down Mexican restaurant and while it wasn't a terrible meal I don't think I'll be going back. 

Keep in mind that I grew up on Mexican food so take that for what it's worth.
My new favorite pizza buffet in town.  Excellent fresh salad bar, tasty baked ziti and cheesy pizza goodness in a comfortable, serve yourself atmosphere.  Tell Lewis I sent ya!

I used them twice and both the times I had to wait more than 15 mins for someone to pick me up. They use vans to shuttle passengers to/from the airport instead of jitney's which I felt was inconvenient (getting in and out of the van).  

Their price is cheap compared to other parking places around PHL.

If only the food and service was as wonderful as the interior decor. Have eaten here twice and will not be coming back for a third time. Main reasons for the one-star review is based on the quality of food (or lack thereof) and the service (missing in action).

First dining experience was surprising and not in a good way. Ordered the liguria pizza biancha. In one word - disgusting. Bottom was burned and the top actually had a total of  five sliced shrimp. Not much to cover the diameter of a 12" pie. Because the crust had burned, the pizza itself was as dry as the Sahara. 

Next up, the butternut squash ravioli. The ravs themselves were average. Nothing that  wowed our taste buds. The standout element was the watery pool that came with them. Guessing that these were either frozen and that was some of the thaw, or they weren't properly drained from the pot. Either way, they were more yuck and less yowza!

Despite having a off dining experience we decided to give Babe's another chance. Unfortunately, things weren't any better the second time around. Ordered the margherita pizza, and like the liguira pizza we had before, this one arrived with a burned bottom and about half of a small roma tomato that was sliced to cover about a third of the pie, or balsa wood frisbee (it's a disgrace to call this pizza or a pie).

Moving on to the service. Arrived with children and other than our party of four there were only two other tables that were occupied bringing the total patron count (including us) to eight. From the time we sat until food was brought out - 45 minutes. Unbelievable! For parents with little ones it made for a very challenging dine-out experience.

Needless to say, Babe's needs to upgrade the quality of both food and service. Will not be eating here again.

Food is okay, a bit too salty though. What drove me nuts is that they charged you 18% for the tip without your constent, even if you are all by yourself. This is the second restaurant I have been to that has such kind of aggressive policy. Would not come back again.

I am from CT, and to say I am an ice cream addict is an understatement.

Hands down, best ice cream I have ever had. I love the hazelnut, but last time I went they didn't have it so I had the berry berry and was equally as good. Aside from the ice cream, the staff are so sweet.

If you are in the NJ/Pennsylvania area, definitely take a trip to Nina's-- you WON'T regret it!!!

I was really impressed with Tired Hands Brewing. First off, the space is great and well-designed. Exposed brick, neat wood tabletops, Built to Spill over the speakers, and an intimate layout with a few tables near the bar make for a really great place to grab a casual beer.

The beers and presentation were also great. They do both IPAs and saisons, which are lighter, lower alcohol content Belgians. I enjoyed the FarmHands, but I think those who like lighter or wheat beers would be happy with any of their saisons. They offer three different sizes: 4 oz samples, an 8 oz. small glass and a 12 or 16 oz. (can't quite remember which) larger glass, which is a nice way to try a few different beers. They offer growlers too, and I saw a lot of people coming in to get them filled.

The duck prosciutto and bread and butter were both delicious, I am pretty confident that any of their light bites would pair well with the beers. They also said that all their ingredients come from within a 1 hour radius of their location which is totally awesome. 

Overall, for just opening last month I think they're killing it so far. They've got a great local, earthy, neighborhood brewery thing going on and I'm interested to see how they develop.

Went here for a brunch, and it was killer. The location is great, right in the square with huge windows so you can people-watch while you eat. The cocktails were strong and tasty which is all you can ask for with brunch and they had my favorite brunch meal ever (crabcake benedict) and it was perfection. I also loved the beignet fries, saved us waiting in line to try them across the street at cafe du monde and I think they are better anyway. Would absolutely go back next time I'm in Nola.

Adelaide's Made My Wedding Cake Into a Piece of Art And It Was The Best Tasting Wedding Cake...

Let me first start by telling the readers that I had wanted the cake I picked out since I saw it 8 years ago in a wedding book (well before my engagement).  The design was credited to a baker, (because of its tilted style)  from Manhattan that I will not reference in this review.  

Anyway, when I was planning my wedding, I went back to the book and contacted the baker.  Her assistant knew I was having a small wedding (25 people), but knew I had a decent budget to work with.  The only thing that I really HAD TO HAVE was this particular cake.  In fact, it was a running joke in the family because my (now) sister-in-law, who lives in Manhattan  said, "Don't worry about the price, you get your cake."  My husband agreed, You get your cake.  

So after several e-mails to the baker's assistant and an appointment scheduled 3 days before I was set to go to Manhattan to meet with her, her assistant cancelled.  At this time,  I was informed that the baker did not make the cake for under a 100 person wedding.  On top of that, the price quote was $600.00 more than stated if I wanted 3 tier instead of 4 tier.  ADELAIDE'S to the rescue...

After a week of research, I stumbled upon Adelaide's and e-mailed them with a picture of the cake I wanted and asked them if they could do it, Stefanie (one of the owners' and baker told me yes) and she could do it for 50 people (I had no problem with upping the amount of cake, since I knew we would eat it).  My husband and I went to a cake tasting, reviewed the colors, price, flavor, etc.  (It was actually one of my fondest memories of our wedding planning because we tasted and picked the flavor together and had fun)!  The price was so REASONABLE for what I wanted and Stefanie did not charge a ridiculous amount for delivery. At that point, I found out that Stefanie looked up to the baker in Manhattan that said she could not make the cake, she is a "legend" according to Stefanie.   Well Stefanie had that all wrong; after my wedding,  She is the LEGEND.

We touched base a few days prior to the wedding to go over where I wanted the cake placed, delivery time and confirm colors, flavors.  Lavender, coco, cream with chocolate cake and cream cheese icing, fondant overlay, flowers and pearls to match.  

The day of the wedding,  Stefanie arrived promptly, she delivered the cake herself and since it was 4 tier she had to assemble it and add the decorations made out of edible sugar to the cake once it arrived.  

When I saw it, I could NOT BELIEVE MY EYES!  It was STUNNING, exactly the way I envisioned.  It was the talk of the entire wedding, everyone from the pianist to the photographer to the guests could not get over its beauty.  I nearly wanted to die when we had to cut it, my husband talked me through it(: Where it gets even better is the quality of the cake to the taste buds.  Again, it was the talk of the wedding, no one could believe how delicious the cake tasted.  
Literally a piece of art to look at and to eat. 

To summarize, hit the mark in every category.  Stefanie was so sweet to work with and is truly gifted.  I hope to post pictures of the cake as soon as I get the professional ones back.  It won't do it justice but, I will post one my friend took.

We actually went back for New Year's Eve and had a special mutli-course dinner that included lobster and Peking duck. The hostess remembered us from the week before. I thought that was pretty cool given the amount of diners in and out of this place! Anway, the meal was good and we had a nice time. I am a fan of this restaurant!

I think the very best thing on the menu is the dinner for four Peking duck, which is served with many other dishes -- truly a feast! I cannot wait to go back with another couple just so we can order this!

There was little about this menu that was fresh or inspired. It is an overpriced diner. At best.  I'm not a fan for what it offers itself to be in pricing. Is be okay with it if they didn't seem to present themselves as more than a diner.

This place is absolutely adorable! I went with my sister around 5pm. We were able to get a seat by the window overlooking the street, but there is not much seating otherwise. 
I ordered the tempura crunch but added carrots and fried shallots. My sister customized her own pork belly sushi. This place isn't "proper" sushi by any means but I give this place 4 stars for friendliness, creativity, and deliciousness! It's a creative twist and though it doesn't taste like traditional sushi, it doesn't make it bad by any means. The sushi seemed small but ended up being more than either of us could finish. My only negative comment is that the green tea was watery and too sugary

This review is for management. Presentation is everything. I came to see Endgame, and I decided not to order food. I don't trust a place with sticky floors to serve quality food. It's disgusting. Ive saw the comments, it seems like everyone's experience depends on the day they go, or whose in the kitchen at the time. This establishment is far from consistent, and you should see that as a problem. I also didn't realize gratuity was included on the bill, so I tipped a total of $18 for a $45 bill. I'm only okay with it because the wait staff was nice enough, and opening weekend for Endgame was probably crazy for them. I just think it's shady for customers that probably aren't aware because it's likely they're first time. Among other things, it doesn't leave a good impression. These reviews should motivate management to improve. The community this theatre serves as well as the customers traveling to this establishment deserve the same attention to detail as if it was located in King of Prussia or the Main Line. I can't say for sure I'll visit again.
This is the BEST Italian food in the area.  Pizza is really good. Service is wonderful!  We go at least once a week!

We were looking to eat some oysters on Super Bowl Sunday. Every other place was closing early since it was a Sunday. We came in a little after 8pm and were seated right away. I ordered the seafood nachos and my husband the Turtle soup and we shared a dozen oysters. Everything was going great until my husband went in for his last spoon full of his soup, which is when he found a long hair. That killed my appetite and I couldn't finish my food. They took it off our bill and offered to get my husband a dessert but at that point he didn't want anything else. We'd probably come back for some oysters, nothing else.

For dinner we ordered seaweed salad, vegetable and shrimp tempura, and the sushi & sashimi platter with some sake and Japanese craft beer. The seaweed salad was rather dry, but the tempura was pleasantly crispy. In terms of the platter, I think the regular maki was the best part of it. Overall, the food was decent but didn't stand out from other trendier sushi spots we've tried. We did go on a Wednesday, so that might explain why the fish didn't seem amazingly fresh. 

On the plus side, it is really convenient that you can get your parking ticket validated for the garage right up the street. Parking in Old City can sometimes be a pain. Also service is prompt and courteous.
Bomb ass New York pizza!  A bit over priced tho.  You gotta pull teeth for extra ranch dressing
Discovered that this restaurant has great choices on weekly fresh fish. A nice find from this standpoint and the other menu items I've tried have been good.

I've used them for 10 years and never again. I prebooked a return trip and have them
My flight details, etc. 45 minute wait bc first come first serve whenever the hell they feel like it. Their customer service could care less, we're rude and uneducated. Their vans are in deplorable condition as well. Cracked windows, loud noises, super bumpy. How are they still in business? Stay away. They don't care. Take an Uber or Lyft!
Great place to watch games.  I find myself there a lot during the NFL season.  Lots of TV's.  Staff is always available.  Never had an issue here.
A 1330 afternoon flight is the best. The airport is empty. Security lines are empty. no wait at any of the shops or restaurants. This is a small simple Airport.

These cupcakes are soooooo good.  I have trouble walking by without running in to grab one.  The cupcakes are also pretty big, so 1 is plenty (each cupcake is 3 bucks).  I am in love with the sweet potato cupcake with the cream cheese frosting.  The cake is wonderfully moist and the frosting is just creamy deliciousness without being overpoweringly sweet.  The people working there are always really kind and helpful and offer great suggestions and let you take your time when deciding.

Best breakfast or brunch spot in Tucson number 1. So many options for food so many different cocktails so many beers and wines and so many coffee or latte drinks to choose from. Been my favorite and in my opinion the best spot for 10 years now. Location is good right downtown lots of parking and if theres a wait theres also a bar so you'll be ok

Outstanding!  My Chile en Nogada reminded me a lot of the Chile rellenos I used to enjoy in Orizaba, Ver. -- beef and sweet filling (including raisins and pomegranate seeds).  The Chinito Gordo version was different in that it isn't egg battered, and it's topped with a sweet cream sauce instead of tomato. Wonderful!  And the cucumber water was very refreshing. A very unique take on Mexican cuisine. Can't wait to explore the rest of the menu.

Yum yum yum!! Our server was terrific and helpful - explains that they print the menus daily as it is a "lab" and they play with drinks and food items. 
The potato crusted oysters are worth the hype - the honey, dill pickle 'sauce' they are served on is absolutely Devine! I scooped it up to put on the oysters. You get 5 good sized oysters for $18. 
I tried the pork belly appetizer for my main entree. It was delicious as well! The spices to the amount of pork belly, adding a couple Brussels sprouts in the mix too. The pineapple was my favorite, because it added a delicious flavor twist I just didn't expect. 
The tequila cocktail ($12 I believe) was yummy, but the charred orange on top made every sip of the drink smell so awesome. It was a unique combo that just worked. 
My friend ordered the filet - and I'm not a fan of onions, but EVERYTHING on that plate just complimented each other so nicely. 
The only thing I will say I wasn't completely sold on was the sugar crusted butter cake. The sugar was a bit too much - think more of a creme brûlée topping - but the ice cream served was on point!!! I enjoyed the caramel drizzled more on the side, as it wasn't an overly sweet caramel. I'd say get it rather than not, since I believe I am in the minority of my opinion for this particular dessert.

Starting off; I would like to point out my friends and I were genuinely excited to try this eatery. We heard good things from Tik Tok but ultimately this place really fell short on our expectations. 
Our waiter, Angelo D. did his best to make us feel uncomfortable and essentially unwelcome; his over confidence in his service was off putting and at points really disrespectful. Statements made by this waiter from our Wine choices to how we ventured to this restaurant were met with heavy sarcasm and criticism. Other tables were mentioning they found this by Tik Tok as well; this waiter seemed to be very keen on informing us that their normal clientele is exclusive and that certain people were not welcome even famous celebrities. 

 As for the food. It wasn't bad but after the environment the server established for us we were not able to dine comfortably. 

On a personal note: a lot of eateries have suffered under the pressure of Covid. Most of those eateries are genuinely excited to have more seats filled. That obviously not the case here; I would much rather dine in a space that not only welcomes their guests but serves them without criticism.

I came here for a restaurant week dinner which was an awesome deal. I loved all the courses and shared with my friend so was able to sample quite a bit. The sheep's milk ricotta was awesome. For the first course we got something that resembled fancy cheese balls but was called wild mushroom arancini and giant two meatballs (fontina stuffed meatball) . We got a flat bread called butcher's pizza but I wasn't a fan. I loved the pan seared lancaster chicken saltimbocca which was a classic chicken. Of course we got the salted caramel budino. It was pretty delicious but I thought it was overwhelmingly salty. Overall everything was delicious!
Jill did such an amazing job on my glaze, trim, and blow out!!! Love the results and I'm so glad I found my go-to salon!

Hot chicken and onion rings were decent appetizers and they had a good beer selection. No wine on the menu, although you can bring your own and there's a corkage fee. Great patio seating to enjoy views of the lake across the street, and after your meal, a walk around the water is lovely. Clean bathrooms.

The word I would use to sum this place up is "okay". It's nothing special, you're better off going to Culver's for a cheaper price or handles for way better ice cream. The prices are high, and I got the Reese's sundae. They are skimpy with the Reese cups and only gave a light dusting. My husband got a tornado and said it could have used more toppings.

Came here with my family on a Saturday afternoon. We were too late for dim sum but we were able to try their noodle and rice dishes. We got the wonton noodle soup, beef chow fun, seafood fried noodles and roast pork and duck on rice. Our favorite was definitely the roast pork and duck on rice. It might be a little too salty on it's own but with the rice, it was amazing. The roast pork had a good balance of fat so that it wasn't too dry and the duck was succulent. Our second favorite was the beef chow fun. It was drier than ones I've had before but also had great flavor and the meat was tender. The seafood fried noodles weren't bad but they got soggy very quickly, I felt there was a bit too much sauce. And the wonton noodles were just ok, the noodles lacked the bite typical wonton noodles should have. Their portion sizes are also appropriate for the price and for family style. Service was good, they were attentive and patient when we were deciding what to order. Would definitely recommend this place and come again, especially to try the dim sum.

This place was as good as it gets. Worth the trip for breakfast regardless of where you are staying in NOLA. Staff was great, prices were great, and all four of us loved every bit of everything we ordered. The Country Fried Chicken with eggs and maple praline bacon was heaven. My wife ordered peanut butter & banana stuffed pancakes that were also to die for. Would go back in a minute. Awesome, awesome breakfast.

Visiting the sanctuary really opened my eyes to see how animals are treated by the hands of humans. These poor primates have been given a life of captivity just so some humans can live more comfortably. I'm just thankful there's a place that is helping these animals as best they can. Go and donate! Volunteer! Or at least get educated. The animals seem to like the attention anyways.

Easily the best Italian on Girard. Yes, I know Modo Mio is a few blocks down but...

The ambiance leaves a lot to be desired. I loved Murph's for being a great hole in the wall. Now I love it so much more. 

My husband and I walked past the patrons bellied up to the bar doing shots and screaming obscenities to sit in the back room for dinner. It was incredible!  We've traveled to Italy many times and Francesco is a man who knows what he is doing. 

Go with an open mind and leave with a desire to come right back. Go now!

Wifey was looking for shoes on our visit. The staff is awesome. The shoe section is nice. Prices are not bad either. She's been looking for a new pair. And she found them here. The staff isn't pushy but very helpful. If you or your girl is looking for a good pair of shoe you have to check out this place.

Been here a few times over the past few years.  The burgers are always amazing!  Recently had the Cheese Burger - added Jalapenos and grilled onions - YUM!  I loved that they used fresh sliced Jalapenos - so rare.  Regular fries are far better than the sweet potato fries.  Tater tots - not special.  Will continue to keep this spot in my rotation.

45 minutes of my life wasted that I will never get back trying to purchase 4 simple items. Worst experience at running store.  Long wait. Staff not trained well on the different types of running sneakers. Kids working in the store doing the best they can with no help from manager. Deceptive advertising.  Manager had the personality of a stone. We are a household of avid runners and this visit today was really unfortunate. First time ever at the store and it was a terrible experience all around.

Less than 7 days after a pedi and my polish was chipping. This place is pretty & I've only been here once so I wasn't going to review thinking MAYBE me and the bestie caught them on a bad day...but a bad pedicure combined with polish that doesn't last means I won't be going back. 

I should've thought twice when I walked into a place that had ONE customer being served. Issue number 1: there's only one other customer in the entire place yet you sit me & my best friend directly next to them without any "personal space"...why?? Were you expecting a crowd that never showed up? 

Issue number 2: my tech never said hello, my name is, which pedicure would you like, is the water temperature ok, NOTHING. I had to specifically ask for the pedicure menu which only had 3 pretty boring options anyway. Not sure which she would have defaulted to if I hadn't asked for the list? And the tech working with my friend asked me if I wanted a water, thankfully. Maybe my tech didn't speak English. Issue 3: I had to guess what her hand taps meant because she sure wasn't assisting me. I think I was tap one time, bend your leg, two taps means put your foot back in the water? Every other pedicure I've ever had, the tech would take my foot and do what she needs with it. This was annoying. I know how petty it sounds but it would've been less frustration if she just told me what she needed. 

Issue number 4: the massage, or lack thereof, was awful. Don't advertise your pedicure coming with a massage if it's merely rubbing lotion on my skin. I can do that myself.

Went because of awesome Yelp ratings but there's too many other options to repeat any place that is less than amazing.

Hour long wait thru drive, no movement at ALL. You figure it's cash only once ur stuck in the drive thru with no way to exit. They don't even answer you thru the drive thru speaker, or tell you if it's broken. If it's broken why isn't there another piece of paper taped to it letting us know instead of having cars out here waiting for minutes with no response. Not even kidding when I say during this time 5+ employees be exiting the store at once during it being busy as hell just to look at you dumb.  This happened TWICE. How 5 of y'all got a time to leave when there's a 4+ line inside AND outside? How this place is even open is beyond me. Workers don't even work, and I wish I was exaggerating.


HOW hard is it to fry up some pre made chicken n food. Brain dead.

This place was absolutely awful. I can't begin to understand how a chain restaurant can be so different (or worse) from one location to another. 

We ordered a stuffed crust pizza, overpaid for it of course. It was not even cooked, we had to put it into the oven for 15 minutes to make it somewhat edible. The toppings tasted like poop, the crust not fluffy at all, dripping in oil, just horrible. I will give them this, it came fast! Probably because it was not cooked! Pizza but, you disappointed me and my boo. This just does not carry the quality that your products did like 10 years ago, when it was the best fast food pizza around. Bring back the buffet wih deep dish and fluffy stuffed crust pizza, good toppings, and even decent service. I feel bad for the people who are forced to deliver such a sup par product to someone's house. Thanks for ruining my nite

I ventured to St Elmo's one Sunday evening with several coworkers while visiting Indy.  

Having read their website and the reviews, we all wanted to try their "Sunday Dinner" menu.  I'm not sure if all of their servers do this, but we had to ask ours for this special menu.  And when we did ask, he told us the portions are smaller, and we should order a couple of extra sides.  I felt he really tried to upsell us, which was really unfortunate and the only negative part of our experience.  

Their Sunday Dinner is a three-course meal with a few options.  I chose their famous shrimp cocktail (with three, instead of four shrimp), salmon (served with mashed potatoes and green beans), and creme brûlée.  The shrimp were every bit as hot as others say (due to the horseradish) - so much so that I could feel it in my nose.  The salmon was fully cooked, and yet still tender and juicy.  How did they make this so good?  Even the mashed potatoes and crispy green beans were delicious.  The creme brûlée was a slightly smaller portion than what I usually get, but it was perfect for me and my coworkers.

Two of my coworkers did get sides - the creamed spinach and au gratin potatoes.  Both were delicious, but they really weren't necessary, as the portion sizes were good for all of us.  

Other than discouraging us from ordering the Sunday Dinner, service was otherwise good.  And it was such a good deal, in comparison to their regular menu, I would definitely return on a Sunday, if I'm in town again on a weekend.

My my my 
It has been a while

Mother's Day brunch was perfect 

We made reservations using the Resy app, there was a Glitch, never the less Janie ( with an N ) was extremely helpful is salvaging the situation 
SPECICIAL thanks to Janie (with an N)

Beth was our server, courteous and attentive 

We started with a Bloody Mary and Cesar salad, not sure what they put on it... the vinegarette has a slight sweet taste- perfect

They are know for their oysters ( it is in the name). So of course we started with sample plate, some east coast, some west coast and some from the Gulf- the west coast were the best today

Chicken and waffles, my son was convinced the prepared the waffles with angel tears, tasted like honey and vanilla. Simply delicious 

The burgers were great, perfect temperature, thickness and taste. Tasted organic, these were very happy cows that went into the making of these burgers, one with sweet potato fries and one with Idaho fries crisp and delicious. Oh BTW they put jalapeños bacon on the burgers- perfection

The Southern's answer to eggs Benedict- poached egg over steak ( its in the name) served on a biscuit, who thinks of these things... absolutely delicious- perfection

4/4 family members rated the Southern a 5  

The Southern has been around a while, long before these pop up hotel/Restuarant 
Now if you are not from Nashville you have to give them a try, if you are from Nashville and you haven't been by in a while come on back

Came upon this restaurant when looking for delicious breakfast with a dog friendly patio and this did not disappoint! The waitress had incredible recommendations and both the food and drinks were the best I've had in a while. Highly recommend!!!

We went to dinner last night (Xmas eve). We were disappointed. The drink order was incorrect while we waited at the bar for our table, yet they charged for an extra drink that wasn't ordered. ( They did take it off the bill, when asked at the end of our meal.) Our appetizers did not get delivered together. After 5-6 minutes we asked for the salad and he brought it. Our entrees, as well, also did not come out together, with a lag of 3-4 minutes. 

For a restaurant of this caliper and price, we were disappointed. No apologies were offered, only the excuse that they were busy.

The jazz musicians were excellent, but I doubt we will return here. There are so many great restaurants in town that do it right every time.
Went there for a birthday party. Everyone loved the food, service and drinks. Great place to have a get together for 20 + people. Staff was great. Band was good as well.

What happened to the old Crab Shack ??

This place used to be great!  Then something happened and it went completely downhill.  So when it reopened under new management we were excited!! 
This has been the third time we have been there since it reopened and it will definitely be our last ! 

Im not sure if they are understaffed but each time the service has been virtually nonexistent.  Somebody takes your order then disappears!  We couldn't even get drink refills after asking several times!  And the food takes forever to arrive! 

My wife loves oysters and always gets the appetizer.   The last two times they have been inedible!  They smelled funky and looked awful. The blackened Frog legs were horrible!  Half of them were cooked and half were raw! 

The steam pot I ordered was cold.  From the corn to the crab legs... just cold.   Like it was sitting out for awhile. 

My daughter did enjoy the grilled cheese though. 

I sincerely hope they fix the problems there because we really enjoyed the place and used to highly recommend it.  Now it's just crappy food and crappy service! 

Oh, The band they had there was good and thank God because it passed the time while we waited and waited for our food.  I just wish I could have gotten another ice tea to quench my thirst but the server was nowhere to be found. !!

Finally checked out Blaze Pizza (07-18-18) was surprised how busy it was after 9pm on a Tuesday night. The wait time to order, was a bit long. When the lady did get to us, she started taking my order, then walked off. Which was odd.

I ordered the Plain Jane and finished it with ranch + hot sauce. It was delicious. I love a good cheese pizza. My pizza was black/burnt around the edges (the cook apologized but nice to know it's not a big deal to them).

Pizza was 3/5 (the burntness really affected the taste but totally has the potential to be 5/5)
Service 2/5 (the apology bumped them up from the original 1/5)

Maybe I'll try it again when it's not busy and they are trying to rush through making a dozen pizzas...just expected a place like this, to know how to handle a mini rush.

Great up scale pizza restaurant and more. Not really into pizzas, but they have great salads and  well stocked bar. Good location to get in and out with little parking problems. Relaxed enjoyable atmosphere. Oh, and deserts to die for.

This location is HUGE. They literally have a line to get into line for overflow drive thru. There are two lines for drive through like most banks, I do not believe I have ever seen this before for a quick service restaurant.

I've always been a fan of Chick-fil-A but what blew me away today was when I came right when they opened at 10:30AM and did not want waffle fries this early in the morning and they offered me at least four other items to sub in. You can get macoroni and cheese, fruitcup, parfait, chicken noodle soup and I think they offered one more. I went with the chicken noodle soup side which I am still wondering if was the best choice as who can turn down mac and cheese!

I probably will not be back to this location as my go to location is the one in Neshaminy but this location was five stars today, great service and great food.

Thank you staff of Chick-fil-a Bensalem! Especially during these tough times with the COVID-19. Keep up the great service we appreciate it!

Buca di Beppo was very, very well received for a luncheon that they catered for us. Their catering menu carries nearly everything on their restaurant menu, so the variety of options was appreciated.  Their Chopped Antipasto Salad was very well received and their Chicken Limone was to die for and the first tray to be emptied.  The Ravioli al Pomodoro was a close second.  

Proscuitto Stuffed Chicken, Chicken Saltimbocca, and Eggplant Parmigiana will definitely be on our next order!  Can't wait to try those next!

I got some really awesome smelling soap and I only paid $15. For one bar. Of soap. It's soap people. They have some cool things to look at, but I have buyers remorse. It's worth a visit, but definitely a hipster destination, which is fine, but, some of us do not need $15 soap and $22 bath salts (8oz). Definitely rolled my eyes many times to the prices in this place (as the previous reviewer stated).

I could have cried I was so happy to eat here. Being veg in New Orleans makes for limited dining options but Seed is a GODSEND. The enchiladas and veggie pasta were so fresh and beyond delicious. Topped the meal off with chocolate mousse which was divine. New favorite restaurant!

The place is lovely. Very 19020's Paris. The vibe was casual, a typical French bistro setting. We ordered the French onion soup and steak tartare for appetizers. Both delicious. The bread was excellent but not plentiful. As a table of two we were delivered three tiny pieces and would have loved a tad more but when we had finished those our waiter whisked the butter and bread dish away. Our mains were good, although in my opinion the mac and cheese side dish was bland. My husband had the trout which was really amazing. My steak was unfortunately raw (I had ordered it medium). It was sent back and after a long wait, my husband had finished his meal (which to be fair he did share with me), I received a new steak, which was good. We came for our anniversary and not only was it not celebrated or mentioned with a happy anniversary there was no apology for my steak or comp of anything, a glass of wine, dessert, etc. Despite the negatives the positives outweigh them so I definitely recommend.

It's kinda dark and dirty in this Starbucks. The girls working here were friendly but opted to gossip about the customers instead of cleaning the very dirty dining room. Also, a lot of homeless people hang out here.

I needed to get a coat altered and came here based on a friends recommendation. The woman at the front desk was one of the nicest people I've interacted with at any business. The alterations were high quality, completed quickly and super well priced!

Horrible,Terrible, Garbage!! these are some of the words that come to mind when I think of 21st Century..This is by Far the Worst Company I have dealt with and one you cannot Ever Trust or Rely on! There Customer Service is Dreadful..Nonexsistent!! It should be called Customer Disservice!! They should have there staff train with the people from Geico to learn Customer Service because there is none here!! Good location. Bourbon St is walking distance, and Harrah's is right across the street.

But their rooms were weathered, and do NOT trust them when you upgrade from double beds to queens. When confronted about it, they tried to tell us they were queens. Ha.... no. No they weren't. But we were still charged for the upgrade, of course.

I hate to write a negative review for a business like Goodwill, but when their own employees don't care enough to take care of those that are trying to take care of others, I take great offense. Here's what happened...

We spent today clearing out our house, and set aside all of the useful items to donate to a good cause. We've dropped items off to this Goodwill location once in the past and found the process quite simple, so after the last box was packed and loaded, we checked for a closing time and saw it was 6pm. We had 6-8 minutes to go no more than 2 miles, so we hopped in the car and raced down. 

As we arrived we saw a vehicle just finishing their drop off with the customer still inside getting their receipt, and noted the time was 5:59pm. The doors to the building were still open, three employees were standing around, and we had the trunk open with 4 things to quickly unload. They insisted they were closed, all clocked out, and refused to  allow us to donate our items. One long haired male employee stated management doesn't allow them to have overtime and the place needs to be locked and armed by 6pm.

Overtime? 1 minute extra? Are you really saying this to me? We all do a little extra for our jobs from time to time, but the least you could do is operate the business for your employer during the operating hours. 

Here's a solution to this "overtime" dilemma Goodwill. Fewer employees on at any one given time. Maybe one of these three  could've clocked out earlier and left the other two to close the store. Surely if they can clock out and lock the doors at 5:59PM then they weren't all needed until that time.

Donating our items would've been done before the third employee, who was still at the door, collected her belongings and was ready to leave. Still they refused. 

As a business that helps those in need and relies on the kindness of the community, I'm appalled that they would not instruct their staff to service customers. The donation could have been accepted and easily be processed in the morning, and all would've been fine.

Goodwill you need to revise your customer service standards. This is unacceptable.

The Pennsylvania General Store could easily be dismissed as something useless, junky, or touristy. It is full of things you don't need and everything you never knew you wanted or needed. 

I got a kick out of the variety of goods in the store. It's perfect for gifts to take back home, trinkets, and for trying out all the local things that make Pennsylvania special. Cookies, chocolates, keychains, etc. The reason I go to the Pennsylvania General Store is the candy.

Prepackaged licorice is the way to go. This is the same licorice I find in NY at Dylan's Candy Bar or Dewey's for 8.99/lb. At the Pennsylvania General Store it is $3.75 for a whole bag. It's amazing. Sure I'd love to have a chocolate Liberty Bell, but when it comes down to it if I can save 50% off on candy I can down on a daily basis, I'm there.

The bags of licorice come one type of flavor or a variety pack. I picked the variety pack and now I'm stuck with four strands of nasty coconut flavored licorice. Next time I'm going to just stick with one flavor bags. And since it's 1/2 the price of NY candy, I can buy two!

It's easy to feel like a kid in a candy store at the Reading Terminal Market. Do not miss the Pennsylvania General Store!

One of the coolest little joints I've ever been to.   We went for the ice cream not knowing the Cuban was all the rage. Missed that opportunity but will definitely go back!  As for the the ice cream... 32 flavors, awesome staff, and the line moved quickly. 

Worth the 10 min wait...if it was even that long.
Nice atmosphere in this trendy cool restaurant. Really keen friendly service and delicious food. Also good for a drink at the bar.

I came here for a small party Friday night with some coworkers to make ornaments. I had never been here before but most of them had and they all raved about it.

The place is located far back in a neighborhood in Algiers. It used to be an old movie theater. The front is the gallery where you can see all of their wares and purchase pieces already made if you like. The middle area above is where you choose your colors and sign your waiver form, etc. It is also a large waiting area with a table where you can put food and drinks for your party/gathering. There is a couch and chairs. The back area where the film used to be shown is the actual studio with the furnace and ovens. It is very hot down there!

The staff is friendly and helpful as they guide you through the process of creating your piece. You have to leave your creation there and pick it up another day so it can cure.

All in all, it was a very fun experience and I look forward to going back again.

Great little place staff was friendly food was good but it didn't wow me. We found most of the rolls we ordered to be prepared and presented well but something was off about the flavor I feel like there wasn't enough umami I think. You know how you start to chew a great bite of food and every chew new flavors mix and the food changes with every bite, I didn't get that here. Not to say it was bad it wasn't by far the quality is there and you will be satisfied if you have that craving for a good meal but I  did not have that WOW experience . It wasn't awful but it wasn't great it was just good. A great place to get some ramen and sushi with out having to take that ride into Tampa.

I am going to rate the services I have had here:

1. Regular blo out- 5 starts-----Amazing... my hair looked great and I got tons of compliments. I felt that the "teasing" of my roots went a little overboard, but tons of compliments.

2. Blo out with curls- 5 starts-----Amazing... first he gave me a blow out and then did tight curls as the wedding I was going to was 5 hours after the appointment. Loved it & again received many compliments.

3. Make up with Carmilla- 4 stars.... make up looked great for the most part... I did a bit more blending when I got home but she did a bang up job on my eyes and eyebrows. I was told by multiple people that I never looked better!

4. Lashes (strip)....Zero stars--NO NO NO NO.... just NOOOOOO. Ok, it's $15. They use the same lashes you buy at CVS for $5. They came off within 40 minutes. I should have just thrown $15 in the toilet.

5. Blo/Up Updo.... Negative stars---This was by far the worst experience I have had here. First the receptionist hesitated having the girl I got do my hair... the girl said "no, I can do anything" and so the receptionist shrugged and said "oh well this is my last week here".... then the stylist told me I should have washed my hair the day before... and I told her they should tell people that online or in the confirmation email... I had no idea..I didn't have a look in mind just something clean, casual, and yet classy. The stylist showed me 1 picture on her phone (back of a head) and I said it looked good.  What I got was the front looking like a helmet (she said she had to improvise since "I" didn't show her a picture of the front) and the back being a frizzy, knotted, uneven mess.
