I am in full agreement with the previous poster's assessment on Coquette.  The food was absolutely on target but the service, specifically the timing was a bit off.  

I went with the fiance and we had planned on having a low-key, slow, drunken dinner to give the place a try.  I have to say that I love the decor of the building, especially the set-up.  We were ushered over to a table and immediately presented with a pretty thoughtful drink menu and wine list.  I, of course, went with a Sazerac just get the mood going and try to catch the vibe of the place.  It was delicious, maybe even one of the better ones I've had in a long time (certainly good enough for two of them!).  She got the special drink of the night, a champagne ponchatoula strawberry cocktail.  Let me tell you, that thing sang in your mouth, delicious!  The first course came out quickly; she got the soft-shelled crab and I got the pork belly rillettes.  Hers was juicy, crispy, fresh; mine was savory, fatty, delicious, especially when paired with the sour cherry compote or the dijon that was provided on the plate.  Got another Saz at that point, then about 5 minutes after they took our plates from the apps, the entrees came out.  I got the cobia with bacon, onions, and peas.  It was perfectly grilled, hot and well-seasoned.  I especially loved the way the sweet onions, salty bacon, and fresh peas played off of each other.  She got the redfish with some sort of pea puree on a bed of crawfish risotto.  It was just as good as mine, as buttery and delicious and redfish should be, and the risotto was freakin' divine.  I would like to point out at this time that the kitchen obviously really enjoys the fact that peas are a very fresh and very delicious ingredient right now, because they used fresh peas in 3 out of the 4 dishes that we ordered.  This was definitely a good thing at this place.  Also, I ordered a white burgundy to go with the fish and it came out stingingly cold and perfectly complimented everything.  This place made me happy but they definitely could use some work on the time.  I mean, I definitely would've had at least a few more drinks had they slowed things down and let us take our time.  That being said, I definitely will be adding this to my list of place to eat at again!

I read the google reviews and saw all the positive comments so I decided to bring my car in for maintenance. But my experience wasn't as great as those reviews and there were a couple things that made me feel not right about their service. 

First, I called for an estimate on a 90K maintenance and the lady persistently said she couldn't provide me the estimate till they look at my car. So I brought my car in and the staff (another person) gave me an estimate just based on the make and year without even looking at it.  The estimate was over $600, which was fairly expensive for a maintenance but since I already made all the ride arrangement, I went with it. 

Second, they told me the Drive Belt has to be replaced and quoted me $450 to replace it. I thought it was very expensive so I called a service at a dealership and they quoted me for $210, which made much more sense but skeptical on Paul Campanella's side cause they almost charged me more than a double for the same service. 

Third, they also told me one of the windshield sprayers did not work and needed to be replace. Since they didn't have the specific part for my car, they ordered it for me and would let me know when it comes in. I tried the sprayers after I got my car back and both of them worked perfectly fine. So I asked for a refund on that since it never needs to be replace. 

All the things added up and Paul Campanella's definitely did not sound ethical and honest to me.  It seems like to me that they will try to rip you off if you don't know anything about cars and service charges. I wish I did more researches before bringing my car in based on the positive reviews they got online.  I strongly suggest people who consider to bring their cars in to get an estimate from them and compare with other auto shops before bringing your car in. I will never go back again.

My husband and I stopped her per a recommendation from a friend.  We loved the tomato pie, it was warm, the crust was great, it was nice and crispy.  We will definitely be back.  The service was also great.

Great trip! Allen was very friendly and accommodating, he was also very knowledgeable about the area. He offers many choices of aquatic activities, something for everyone to enjoy. The boat ride itself was fun. Snorkeling was amazing, we saw many different fishes. We also went shelling, the kids enjoyed finding unique shells and sand dollars. Paradise Park Trailer Resort is a honky-tonk bar and restaurant that opened on Lower Broadway in downtown Nashville in 2007. I visited this past Friday night and learned, later on in the weekend, that this place is closing soon. It's supposed to close this month (July 2018) so I wanted to get my review out before they closed.

We showed up just before midnight on Friday and this place was packed. The line to get in wasn't very long, but it was very crowded inside, especially on the first floor. There were two bands, one on the first floor (ground level) as soon as you walk in and one inside on the rooftop (fourth level). I believe both bands were cover bands (definitely the band on the top floor; I remember one song they sang was the Alien Ant Farm version of Smooth Criminal). Both bands were pretty good and most people seemed to be having a good time.

There are a lot of lights and neon signs on Broadway. You can't miss Paradise Park's sign because it's one of the biggest. It's green and red and spans over two stories. It's one of the most prominent signs on the street. The space has colorful and kitschy decor (neon signs, string lights, Christmas lights, a disco ball, and more). Just inside the entrance is a photo booth and Skee-Ball. During our visit, the second and third floors were closed. The second floor was home to a dueling piano bar called The Big Bang.

We spent most of our time on the rooftop patio which was a lot more laid back and relaxed than downstairs. The rooftop has both an interior and exterior bar. The outdoor portion of the rooftop is covered in artificial turf with picnic tables, lawn/porch chairs, and high tops for seating. There was always a game of cornhole going on while we were up there. The highlight, to me, is the view from the rooftop. You get to see the beautiful downtown Nashville cityscape as well as all of the activity below on Broadway. Paradise Park seems to be in the center of it all. If it's not closed by the time you read this, the rooftop is definitely worth checking out.

The thought occurs that I spend a worrying amount of time eating at places that bill themselves as "shacks." Prince's Hot Chicken Shack, da Poke Shack, the Reggae Shack, the Maximo Fish Shack, Texas Jim's Discount Beefatorium and BBQ Shack--the list goes on. What does it say about me, my culinary and social preferences, and my place in the world at large that I actively seek the company of... shack-dwellers? Surely this anxiety presages some dire revelation concerning the very purpose of my life itself.

Yet existential crises are wearying--on some (most, all) occasions, it's easier to just head for the shack and have some fish without all this soul-searching.

Like the fabled Labyrinth of Crete, the Maximo Shack demands that you pass a battery of tests to prove your worth:
*The Test of Wit: can you actually find the place? It's not next to the marina, it's IN the marina, floating precariously at the end of one of the piers. Signposts are obscure and may lead you to a watery grave. Only the cunning will survive.
*The Test of Valor: can you reach the Shack without being crushed and maimed by an enormous forklift carrying a pleasure yacht? The parking lot is a hazardous place to be, what with all of the industrial-strength maritime equipment being shuffled around.
*The Test of Not Wearing High-Heeled Shoes: the pier leading to the Shack is weathered and, at times, flimsy. One wrong step and pelicans will feast upon your bloated, waterlogged corpse.

Your reward for passing these tests is a lovely venue on the water and the freshest fish you'll find in Tampa Bay. Amuse yourself while you wait while watching one of the shack-jockeys slice up the day's catch on the fish-cleaning table overlooking the marina, wait for the appearance of a legendary (and, rumored, uncatchable) tarpon, observe the ospreys doing osprey stuff (a category of activities that must remain, perhaps mercifully, utterly obscure to humans), note the variety of fun-loving boaters loving the fun they're having on their boats. Toss in homemade (shackmade?) hot sauce and the opportunity to grab some fresh fish or shrimp for later (this is one of only a few places where you see periodically see wahoo, known as Ono (literally, "delicious") in Hawaii, for sale), and, baby, you got a stew goin'.

So why only four stars? Not to put too fine a point on it... the Shack's buns are terrible. Anyone who accuses me of parsimony clearly hasn't seen the gold-plated Q-Tips in my medicine cabinet, but still--this is a $13 sandwich, incorporating a half-pound chunk of some of the best seafood you'll find in these parts, and it's served on an off-the-rack 99-cent-a-bag hamburger bun. Actually, I suspect it might be potato bread owing to its somewhat jaundiced yellow hue and its uncanny softness--the latter quality making it utterly, *woefully* inadequate to the task of supporting the aforementioned fish-slab. As a result, the sandwich falls apart, with grim predictability, almost immediately after you hoist it toward your slavering gob. So, c'mon, Shack, shape up those buns.

Decent hotel at a motel price.

This is such a cute place!  We got Thai Tea, shrimp tempura, crab rangoons, mango sticky rice, and pad Thai. All of it was great and the ppl who work here are so sweet.
I eat at this spot at least once a week. The fish is always very fresh and served up nicely. You cant beat the "All You Can Eat"!!

Pros: You can walk in. Convenient location. Low price. Clean place.
Cons: NOT good for kid's cuts. Bad customer service.

I brought my son here because he needed a cut and we didn't have time to get over to his usual place. I asked if they frequently cut kid's hair and the two employees up front assured me that they did kids cuts all the time. We were told to take a seat and wait until our stylist was ready. Ok. Couldn't one of the people I just talked to cut his hair? You know the ones who said they cut kid's hair all the time? The place was completely empty.  They said our stylist was eating lunch and would be right with us. So they chatted idly while we waited about 10 minutes. At least Sponge Bob was playing on the TV. 

When things got going, it became clear the stylist really didn't have the skills needed to keep him comfortable and his hands occupied during the hair cut. As a result she was unable to cut his hair evenly. Rather than making an effort to put him at ease, she actually asked me if she could restrain my child's head. Of course, my son was freaking out. You can't just take clippers to a little boy's head, use force to restrain him and hope for the best.  I am the first to admit that cutting the hair of a three year old is not easy, but that is precisely why I came to a professional. So I walked out with a slightly traumatized child who was sporting a ridiculously uneven and  incomplete hair cut. No apology or explanation was offered.

I've never stayed at a Ritz, but somehow this hotel made it on the list of company preferred hotels and our corporate rate was comparable to other non-luxury hotel chains.

The room was big with a very large bathroom and had a small balcony overlooking the courtyard in the front of the hotel.  It definitely had the perks that I would imagine a Ritz to have.  Bathroom robe, plush hangers, soft, pillow top bed.  There was evening turndown service with chocolates, bottled water & glass placed on the bedside table.  I left my toothbrush and toothpaste on the bathroom counter, and they even put it in a glass for me and cleaned up the counter.

The staff was supremely nice and high-class from the front desk, bell hop, waitress to even the parking garage attendant.  They make you feel welcomed and treat you well.

The breakfast buffet at the restaurant is pricey though. $23 but they have a nicer selection of items to go with the price.  Eggs benedict, yogurt parfaits, biscuits & gravy, great selection of pastries, lox/smoked salmon, etc.  Still expensive though and getting an entree is better off if you have the time.
Finally, the Mexican restaurant I've been searching for. Fantastic menu, fantastic drinks. Absolutely love the huge beers and the pina colada margaritas as well.

Only once a year this place opens for three days. Great outdoor music food and fun games for all ages. A wide variety ofAuthentic Vietnamese foods for all. From Pho to Banh Mi. You have to check this event out at least once in your lifetime. You will not regret it.

Was visiting the Tampa area, this past June, & I knew I wanted to get a pedicure at some point during my trip. Searched yelp ahead of time & found this salon. Was attracted to the idea of getting a professional pedicure while avoiding inhaling toxic fumes during the process! This salon did not disappoint! The staff was very professional, the environment was clean & comfortable, & there weren't any strong chemical orders. My pedicure look flawless (Dajah was my technician) & it lasted forever!! I highly recommend this salon! Wish there was one where I live!!!

I've been to probably half a dozen or so dispensaries in the Reno area. I'm giving The  Dispensary five stars because to the best of my knowledge they give the best discounts. Veterans  get 20% off,seniors get 10%. Another thing that I like about it is a soon as you pull up to their building there's always a Big armed security guard visible. Checking is easy,they're very nice. The Budtenders are very knowledgable about there product. One of the reasons I smoke cannabis is to increase my appetite loss from a medical condition(really!). When I mentioned this to the Budtender he explained  all compounds in cannabis  and KNEW which would  actually increase my apperite. I purchased the bud he recommended. 
T- shirts are only $15 too. 



 which

One of my favorite places to go for Korean food and sushi. First time I had Korean food was here and ever since then I can't get enough of it, definitely recommend ordering something from that menu. I haven't had one bad sushi roll here. The only negative thing I could say is I wish the staff was a bit more informative when it comes to the food. Half of the time I don't know what I'm eating, I just know that it's good lol. Instead of just putting down the small plates of side dishes they could at least give us a quick description of what it is. But, I could always just ask if I'm really curious. This place is a must try regardless

At least 4 stars!  The front desk staff was great at check in!  The newly renovated rooms are fantastic! I was upgraded to the bi-level suite, how nice is it! Two levels to relax in!  It almost feels like a small apartment, making the traveling for work experience that much easier.  I will be coming back as this is convenient to everything I need to do while in St. Louis.

FRADULENT BILLING PRACTICES.

But let's first address the quality of care received here. The entire operation is pretentious, with leather couches, artwork, etc. Yes, it's a fine environment to be in, but you're clearly paying out of pocket for those adornments. The base fee is $130 just to get in the door, which is at the upper end for an urgent care. After that, instead of having a qualified medical professional take a look at you and know what's wrong, you start off with somebody in a Carrington College scrub who basically just orders one test for another after you, costing you or your insurance to pay for each one.

With common cold symptoms, you'll get the following: steroid injection, blood test, strep test, chest x-ray. Yes, it's good to rule things out, but it's a system clearly designed to order as many tests as possible when an experienced medical professional could determine your ailment in many less steps.

I saw the RN once throughout my hour or so in the exam rooms. At the end, somebody from the front office came in and said "OK, it's time to pick up your prescriptions," yet I still didn't know what was wrong with me. I had to actually request to see the RN again to find out why I needed the medicine prescribed to me.

Unfortunately over $200 later, I never improved, but I wasn't going to levy any complaints.

Then within a week, I receive a letter in the mail saying that I owe them $70 for unpaid services. Obviously this is a mistake, as I had paid them for this charge and all other charges for this visit, so I call them to nicely let them know they've made a mistake.

Instead of being greeted with an apology, I'm rudely greeted by their a representative from their billing department named Richard, who accuses me of not paying the money and takes no responsibility at all on their end. I then send in a billing statement from my bank, clearly showing the charge in question going through.

Did that end it? Of course not, I receive a rude phone call an hour later pressing me for more information, still with the attitude that I had not paid them and that they would be launching an "investigation" into the matter. 

So here I a few weeks later, still sick and dealing with the constant stress of trying to prove I paid $70 of my bill when I immediately had proof. Who knows how many people they have done this too who simply double pay because they're too sick to deal with it?

This place clearly puts the almighty dollar first and treats their patients like walking ATMs.

Such a cute brunch spot! This place is very cozy and has such a great atmosphere. There is a great variety of tasty treats on the menu from sweet to savory. Pictured is a waffle sandwich, an omelet, and a ham and Brie crepe. Everything was so good and left me feeling so stuffed! Would definitely recommend to people!
Great on site management.  It's not easy to find this kind of value so close to the water.

Chez Leon was a very nice restaurant.  The staff  members were  professional and made the dining experience quite relaxing.  I felt, that for the price, there are other restaurants in the city that I would choose first.  However, if you love french food, it's worth a try.  I loved the lamb dish that I ordered, and all the desserts were to die for (we tried the chocolate torte, creme brulee, and the souffle.

I'm visiting the area and was looking for a place with craft beer. The craft selection is decent, however mostly everything's "best by" or born/bottled on date was 1-2+ years old. Other than that, there was a huge selection of liquor and the place seemed clean and organized. I would not recommend going here for anything other than liquor.

A wonderful small, cozy pizza bar. They made me feel right at home after a really bad experience at one of the high-dollar restaurants in the neighborhood. 

Wonderful pizza and Kylie is pleasantly delightful.  
(so are the guys in the kitchen)

This will remain on my list of places to come back to visit!

Loved this place!!!  Went there yesterday for some tasty hop soda.  ;)  The beer menu is extensive!  Unfortunately some of the ones listed weren't available.  :(  Love their tasting tray with a mini chalkboard with the name of the beer listed on it.  I had a great IPA & a wonderful Coffee Porter called Buzz Buzz.

I had a half BLT with avocado & sundried tomato mayonnaise.  Served with Delicious fries.  I could eat it everyday of my life!  One friend had the salmon cakes with brussel sprout slaw.  That stuff is good!  Don't be afraid of it try it!  The other friend had the sinfully delicious mac & cheese.  

Great service.  This place has some seriously good looking clients.  If I was single & lived in Boise I'd be coming here everyday!  ;)

My sister had Federal Donuts delivered for my birthday and I was super excited because I hadn't tried them yet. They travel really well because of the way that they are glazed.

This box was made up of fancy varieties: Cannoli, Chocolate Toffee, Blueberry Lemon, Peach Marshmallow, Banana Nutella, and some chocolate thing I couldn't figure out. they were all delicious but I am looking forward to trying some of their more basic flavors.

Federal Donuts is an institution here in Philly. They have built a great brand with recognition locally. This is definitely something to try when you are in town

Suggestion for owners: If you have reviews that tell of rude employees and you still keep them as employees, it may be you prefer for customers to go to another beauty supply store, which is what I shall do from now on. Losing customers in addition to the Covid situation isn't too lucrative. If someone forgets to put their mask on, you can realize they must be very busy, and a gentle reminder will do the trick instead of a self righteous attitude that holds a grudge. (Having had an appointment in another store for nearly 2 hrs. prior to this one with a mask on is something you would have not known, tiring as it was. I simply forgot and didn't hear what the cashier said initially. She was on the phone, so I figured she had a free moment while conversing and wanted to know what I needed.) In addition, if someone wants to return something because appears defective, s/he is unsure whether the whole lot is defective and so it should be respected first (I know you need the sale, and perhaps a replacement would work, so I let it pass). The customer is always right if you want continued business. Attitudes don't play well with customers. There's enough trouble in a day than to sense inconsideration. You don't have the corner on the market; other similar shops may be more careful (like the one in Voorhees I experienced, before I moved to C.H., if it's still there) to treat customers more gently. If customers aren't dressed as they would be from a church or work situation, think of them dressed to the 9's if that visual spurs a sort of humility - that someone would shop at your place at all - if that is what you are basing your respect on. Better to look at the inward, which runs far deeper and takes more exacting measures to root it out.

I have been to PYT several times, but I had stopped coming as frequently due to the poor service, the time to receive your drinks, and the limited menu.  During my most recent visit, I was surprised to find that they expanded their food and drink menu. 

My favorite thing about PYT is the cake shakes!  They are delicious.  I often can't get enough of them.  However, they are super sweet and you can't drink that many.  They also had a limited selection with not special "shake" of the day or week.  During this visit I was excited to learn that they added an entire new menu of special shakes.  We tried the Banana Foster shake -- which was very sweet and quite tasty. However, the real treat was the Birthday Cake Shake.  The shake came in different colors, with sprinkles.  On top, was a large piece of actual birthday cake.  The shake also had delicious pieces of cake among the alcohol and ice cream.  The best surprise of all, though, was the time to receive the shake.  In the past we often waited longer for our shake then for the food.  This visit, the shakes came AHEAD of the food, which was nice (although shouldn't it always be that way!?).  

In addition to new shakes, they also cooked up some new food items, including the delicious Krispy Kreme sliders and the Pickleback Burger.  The Tasty Cake sliders were perfectly cooked mini-beef burgers with chocolate covered bacon on top.  They were placed inside to cut-open donuts.  The sweet and saltiness was a perfect blend.  The Pickleback Burger was a full-sized burger with fried pickles on it, peppered bacon, jack cheese, Jamison reduction and sprouts; served with dill fries and a spicy pickle spear.  While this could be the most fattening burger ever created, it was also delicious.  A small item to note was the delicious spicy pickle!  I could have eaten a bowl of them! 

The service also improved.  It was faster and more responsive.  It still is not up to the exact par of other establishments in Philadelphia, but its much improved.  Overall, the visit was a good one -- and it is recommended that any stop to Northern Liberties include a shake or burger at PYT.
Overly priced for the age and condition.Wasatch.property management,and leasing agent all lack professionislm.Will not renew lease here.

Everything was good! Happy I decided to try Brotherly Grub cafe for brunch. I ordered the salmon and grits platter and it was tasty. The salmon tasted just right, being made with fresh salmon and peppers. The grits were cooked well and buttery. Yum! I also got a side of home fries and they were soft and flavorful, with onions and peppers. It was a tasty meal and I'm excited to try more deliciousness from here! The customer service was wonderful and very much appreciated. Please continue to deliver quality food and service!!

Michaels has everything I ever need for crafting. The sales are always great and I get coupons when I buy.  Recently I received a 40% off a single item. I came back and they took it off my highest price item $38, which is a great deal. I love the framing. Although they provide coupons, it is still pretty pricey for a custom frame.  There is a great jewelry making selection for some filler beads if you tend to buy stones elsewhere.  These plastic beads are nice and there is usually a deal on them, but over all they are cheap.  The scrapbooking section is always a favorite.  There are usually good deals on sheets of paper you can find for 10 cents marked down from 50 cents.

Be sure to stop by the week of and after holidays because everything is usually 50% off. Also never get a custom frame without getting a coupon.  Usually they have bogo deals.

Please - for the love of your pet, do not use these groomers.  Awful experience!  Took much longer and charged 40% more than what was originally quoted and only partial services were completed.  Owners/staff are more concerned about squeezing their customers for maximum cash than caring about good customer service and the welfare of the animals.  Will never, ever go back!

Always great service and food! have yet to be disappointed in either. Tried several dishes with chicken, fried plaintains, a rice. The 3 sauces that are offered are a must try. Highlights the dishes even more.

Disgusting experience. A power salesman knocked on my door telling me that my windows are in bad condition and need to be replaced. I let him know that POWER installed the windows only a few years prior. He gave me the customer service number for warranty. That was on 8/11/17. 

The first appointment was made for 8/31/17. They didn't come because, supposedly the window "broke". (Incompetence)

Next appointment 9/11/17. The call me 2 hours before the scheduled time, telling me "the window sash was not put on the truck". (Incompetence)

Now today 9/20/17. NO CALL NO SHOW! THIS IS THE CUSTOMER SERVICE I HAVE GOTTEN. OVER PRICED WINDOWS, AND FAR FROM EVEN SUB PAR CUSTOMER SERVICE. More incompetence. They have no reason for why no one showed up, not reason for why no one called. 

So now over a month an a half after my initial call. I still have no replacement, and nothing but EXCUSES. this is the worst experience I've ever had. Be very careful when giving this company your money. They claim they offer lifetime warranties, and large smaller places will be out of business and you'll never be able to find them after 5 years.... Well.... Seems like power is the same way. I could only imagine if this was winter . All I would have to keep me warm is their empty promises.
Mary( Murphy )the the server was sooooo nice . With soo much going on she still had a smile !!! Will definitely come back next time I come to this great city !!!

I adopted two kittens from ARNO and with the adoption fee, included spay and neuter by Laspca. I chose to bring them here myself because I didn't want them to have to stay the night back at the ARNO shelter, if I could just drop them off in the morning myself. I left Baton Rouge at 7am but didn't arrive until 850am, 20 minutes late. I called ahead to let them know that I had been stuck in traffic and took the wrong exit (Siri is the worst), but the woman on the phone was understanding and told me to still come anyways. 

The girl at the front desk seemed to already be having a frustrating morning and was aggravated when greeting me, but was helpful in finding someone else that could track down my animals' paperwork (since it was from a different shelter). 

The facility is really clean. I was impressed with the cat rooms and how much space they have to play and roam around. I only saw 2 cats, maybe because most of the others had been adopted, but y'all... I'm not joking, one even had a big screen tv of a fish tank. LOL! 

When I picked up my cats at discharge, the workers or volunteers were very friendly, informative, and caring. I had brought them in one cage (litter mates, I didn't think it would be a problem because it hasn't been) but the girl was worried that they would fight since they were hissing at each other post surgery. So she went and found an old cage in the back to separate them. (btw they cried and just stared at each other the whole ride. Lil sis was worried about big sis because she wasn't shivering til we got home) 
 
I had a good experience here and will be back!

This is a "just fine" airport. It always seems better arriving than departing for some reason! I'm sure it has nothing to do with hating to leave so much. Anyway, they have pretty limited food choices, but what they do have is pretty OK. There is a "Lucky Dogs" cart, one of my favorites. One thing that I do appreciate is that even when it's busy, it doesn't compare to ORD. Every plane I've flown either to or from MSY has stayed in the air the entire flight, which I appreciate. Aside from that, nothing spectacular to review.

The lady who makes the appointments is more than rude. After waiting on hold for over 10 minutes you are finally connected with someone who has no patience. I had trouble hearing her so when I asked her to repeat herself she hung up the phone in my face! I have never... I do not have to go here. I would have been a new patient but with service like this why would I want to be.

I hung out with mom here for about 2 hours and ate the most delicious toast ever!!!  I waited a long time to come here because baked goods really arent my thing, but now that I know about the toast.  . .well I'll be back!  I thought process were affordable, quality EXCELLENT, service wonderful, and atmosphere was chill.  I prefer tables that are more private, but that's a very minor detail.  Coffee was good, not my fave, but definitely good.  I'll be back for that toast and to take my out of town friends.

everything that i've had at this restaurant is fantastic, and i'm especially impressed with their vegetarian options.  the best part of woksabi is that the menu is not all sushi; it's not even all japanese.  you can get a wide range of popular dishes, including thai.  this place is definitely a gem among all of the other collingswood restaurants.

Mama said "if you don't have anything nice to say, shut your mouth"!
I couldn't stop complimenting these beers! Great job!
I will
Visit again!
Very authentic and very delicious Mediterranean food at Aroma. Great menu and good pricing.

Great Place for breakfast/lunch - love their healthy options! 

Their coffee - from DC is amazing too!

Terrible experience! First of all there is zero communication. Once you haul all your luggage out to the rental car parking, they advise you that you have to go all the way back into the airport to sign some paperwork ( 8 min walk). This may seem logical to them however many airports and companies have you go to the lot. So, they can save the attitude. Second, the car was filthy. There is no one in the lot to complain to. Third, AFTER renting online I couldn't take it to Indiana which was the whole point!! I was in a hurry and it was late so I had to stay the night and rent a car the next day and use a different company. Such a cluster F! And added an extra day and several hundred dollars to my trip. trust me, not happy.
Quality pizza and dessert worth visiting Edmonton for! The toppings on the Donair pizza melted in my mouth. I may visit one more time before we leave.

A great place to meet unique and interesting people.  The live DJ's add a great touch and the mellow feel to the bar is a nice change.  Booths for those who want a little privacy, a Bar top for a more social crowd.  A personal favorite is their Jameson's specials!

Absolutely delicious!! I'm from Miami and spent a good amount of time traveling in Israel so I'm fairly pick about Middle Eastern food. I agree with other reviewers-- dining area is nothing fancy but come on... its really a grocery store! Extensive grocery selection, great prices on mixes (most were around $1.50 sooo yummm some homemade kofta kebab comin right up!), halal meat butchered in shop, etc.

Lunch was fabulous-- they have wraps and full plates. I just wish there were more options on hot sides to go with my wrap. Plates come with rice, hummus & pita. 
The man at the register must have been the owner (had that vibe) and he was very warm to us, you could tell he takes pride in his business. 

Will certainly return.

Carolyn is in a class of her own as far as photography goes...she, not only is a photographer, but she is truly an artist. Her work speaks for itself. She did my kids photos when they turned exactly a year old and she is actually shooting them tomorrow,..they are now 9 and 12! Carolyn is always looking to better her craft and is always finding new ways to create a moment,.. she never settles for doing the same kind of shot. I look forward to Carolyn shooting my children's high school senior portraits in the future and perhaps even their weddings

Tuesday is my favorite day of the week when I'm working at my office. That's because they serve wicked Thai, my favorite soup at Fife N' Dekel. My office is steps away from the restaurant which is so convenient. I am ALWAYS tempted to stop in and see what is freshly baked as the delicious smells of pies, pastries and bread waft into the alley and surrounding parts near the restaurant. Lots of people from my office love the breakfast and lunch options here. There are 4 locations of around Edmonton.

I like that the menu is always changing and they make seasonal treats. For example the pie flavor of the month is pumpkin. My favorite pie they make is the key lime pie but they only make it certain times of the year. Most of the non standard menu pies are available with 24 hours notice. 

My favorite sandwich is the Auto Bahn. The sandwich has turkey, roast beef, and ham on your choice of bread and toppings. I get the sunflower bread as that is my favorite they bake. I get extra pickles on the side. They offer a good assortment of sandwich toppings. At lunchtime Fife N' Dekel can get pretty busy but the staff keeps the line moving pretty well.

Fife N' Dekel also does catering and we get it every once in a while that we have functions at work and they do a really good job and the trays present well and are tasty. The do sandwiches, wraps, squares, salads, drinks and a few other items. Check their website for the catering menu.

Speaking of their website. It is a pretty good spot to check out the menu for the week as well as daily specials.

My favorite part about art shows is that it can appeal to such a broad audience. The young. The elderly. The hip. The shy. The musically talented. The travelers. The ones that don't know much about art, but are at least curious about it. Art has its way of reaching each and every soul, whether you like it or not. 

What was neat about this event was that it was basically an open house party. And by party, you better believe there was music, drinks and grub. I spent most of the evening by the band, and boy oh boy was that an energetic space! A real sense of community swept through the halls of the Stutz Building as people shared their recent art finds and danced the night away.

My personal fave was a piece I found on the fourth floor. It was a cat dressed in what appeared to be Renaissance styled clothing. Yes, that piece really spoke to me and if I had the funds, I would seriously consider making space for it at home.

Food and staff were amazing! Highly recommended and make sure to make reservations in advance. Enjoyed the building, but try not to get the spots right next to the tracts as trains do go by pretty fast.
We loved this place!! The biscuits and gravy are amazing!! The service was great and so were the bloody Mary's. It's a small venue so you may have to wait a bit. Well worth the wait though.

Amanda just massaged me with her HEALING HANDS. I use a computer all day and I store a lot of tension in my upper back, neck and shoulders. Amanda spent the entire hour massaging alll of the knots out of those areas.

I communicated what i needed and she delivered. She didn't talk too much, was very attentive. My back hasn't felt this good in ages!

THE FACILITY IS IN AN OLD BUILDING. YOU WILL HAVE TO WALK UP THREE LONNGGG FLIGHTS OF STEPS - "Stairwell to Heaven"

It was a slightly muggy night for October.  Williams Blvd was blocked off in Rivertown.  A German band from Texas was playing polkas as we entered the festival grounds.  We found our friends and got in line for the German meal.  Dinner plate was great, plenty of choices, and good quantities.  Of course, the dark German beer to wash down the cabbage roll and sausage.  It was a fair size crowd for a Friday night, but you still could move around easily.  Amazing how loud it was under the tent even when band wasn't playing.

Upon entering you immediately notice how much work was put into the place. It has a very nice atmosphere very calming yet upbeat. The hostess was very accommodating and quick to get us a table. The waitress the same, we could tell she really cared about the people she was helping. We started out with the Mac and Paneer this was ridiculous tasty. If you do not order this you are doing it wrong.  Its like heaven in a bowl, I'm really not kidding.

Moving on to the main dishes. They tell you that the food is "family style" portions. I find this to be incorrect when you think of family style portions you think of Buca di Beppo so much food its hard to eat it all. We didn't have that problem. My wife and I aren't super eaters by any means and we didn't have a problem eating the Fried Tandoori chicken or the Dan Dan noodles. The Chicken was amazing but the chutney was lacking. Not a game breaker by any means. Now what is a game breaker for me is the Dan Dan noodles. It was way way over spiced, to much so for me to eat. I informed the waitress and she apologized and offered to get me milk?  I appreciate the offer but milk with Dan Dan noodles isn't going to be something I'm interested in. So most of my main course went to waste, leaving the restaurant I was still hungry. Would I go back again no, would I go back again if someone requested. Yes.

Best local bar atmosphere even experienced. A true home away from home type of place. Jamie is awesome with the friendliest personality. Crystal is always quick to get u a drink & if ur looking for someone to harass u in a fully entertaining way well Brandy is the one to fill those shoes. Cheers has nothing on the Jug.

This pasta was exactly the comfort food I was hoping for, a very hearty bowl of pasta with a generous amount of sauce. I'm really pleased with the number of vegetarian options and the mushroom bacon did not disappoint!

What a little gem we found on vacation!  Sat upstairs on the deck, seating is not that comfortable but you forget all of that when food comes to your table! Dishes are so thought out, special and dynamic. My fiancé is a chef so I didn't have to use my phone to google what half of the items were so with that being said, this place is for people who appreciate the art behind food and are culinarily cultured. I won't say foodie because the term has been watered down but something along those lines. Service is great, everyone is friendly and knowledgable! Not a place for kids, this is an adult hang out spot. Can't wait to go back again :-)

Dr. Katy hoeft, has always spent the time and care in helping me maintain a healthy lifestyle. This lab is very professional, clean and welcoming. The nurses make sure you feel comfortable and very accepted through out your visits. Dr. Katy as well, has gone above and beyond to have a personal relationship with myself, no woman likes going to their gynecologist, it's a nerve wrecking, scary thing. The doctors here at Desert Bloom OBGYN, go above and beyond to cater to you and genuinely want to get you to the best you can be! I know my vagina is in good hands :)

Very nice inside, but it felt a bit pretentious from the music to the decor, but it was a Sunday evening right before a concert at Ruth Eckerd Hall, so maybe we weren't quite in the mood!  Even so, it was trendy and still fun!

The food was quite good and the service was a match as well.  The Saucy Shrimp appetizer had a great color, texture, and taste.  We each had a glass of wine, and while the list of wines-by-the-glass was not extensive, they were excellent.  I had the sea bass and my wife tried the shrimp tacos; we enjoyed both of them very much.  To end our meal, my wife wanted to try the churros which came with caramel and chocolate.  I normally pass on the churros, but these were something different entirely!  They were fantastic, but thick with cinnamon, sugar, and other yumminesses.  If too much for you, it's easy to tap, tap, tap the excess off.

Our new criteria is whether we would take out-of-town friends here, and Besa Grill gets a definite yes!  We will be back, out-of-town friends or not!

Update: We visited Besa Grill again a month later with my mother-in-law.  She enjoyed the decor and couldn't decide what kind of drink to get, and the servers were quite gracious and accommodating.  The meals were a mixed bag.  My wife ordered the 6 oz filet (which was to-die-for tender!) and my mother-in-law and I ordered the grouper.  Quite disappointing!  It was too dry/firm (overcooked!) and a bit fishy tasting.  We had raved about Besa before, but we'll temper that for now; maybe they had an "off night" in the kitchen.

I wish I could not have given a star. I called 2 hours later and they lied and said the driver quit on them. Then I call back and now they haven't been taking orders for delivery for hours. I'm actually standing here now due to I had to come and get my order. They really suck. Never again will I order from them.

Nice hotel with big rooms. I was surprised on how big the hotel was, the rooms kept going on and on! Comfy beds and I like how they had Paul Mitchell products. Good Complimentary breakfast with a good variety and fresh fruit

The energy and people of the 37th annual great Italian festival was truly amazing.  From commercial row to six street, there was nothing but positive vibes, nice smiley people, delicious fresh food and great entertainment. 

The action started right as I stepped out of my car one block from the event.  I could hear live music playing and it was good music.  "Let's twist again" and "dancing queen" rang out into the streets, performed by three passionate performers who sang their hearts out.  My two little ones couldn't help but dance and I couldn't help but sing along. Plenty of seating was available.

After working up an appetite, we walked down Virginia street and smelled a delicious aroma in the air. Our noses led us straight to the mushroom raviolis. Man were they super fresh and delicious. There's nothing better than handmade fresh pasta.  My son loved the raviolis so much that he didn't want to share hahaha. 

Right next to the raviolis was the tri pasta plate including meat ravioli, tortellini eldorado and gnocchetti with pesto. Same great news, super fresh and very delicious. All at great prices and big portions. My daughter tried helping with carrying the plate to our table and because it was so heavy she accidentally dropped it. The gentleman at checkout didn't hesitate to replace our plate. I appreciated that so much. 

Check out my picture of the festival map to check out the other foods available. 

After loading up, we walked down the street and ran into characters dressed in veggie costumes (artichoke, garlic). They were very welcoming and gave balloons to my kids.  Alongside were people dressed up in Italian attire and on stilts.  They were very entertaining as they danced Italian style dances in a comedic way. Everyone took pictures with them of course. 

I loved that there were lots of different sections at the festival including a kid play area, winewalk, mini farmer's market, souvenir vendor area (art, goods, yard statues), grape stomp and sauce contest area and multiple stages for entertainment. 

Our trip was very memorable esp. since we ended it with chocolate gelato and a free event picture at their photo booth.  The gelato was out of this world!!!

The great Italian festival is a two day event that takes place during Columbus day weekend.  It's just one of the many events that take place each year and has added to my reasons of why Reno is so special. What a way to experience Italian culture. Many thanks to all and El Dorado (where the event is held) and can't wait to go back.

Holy Moly, this place kicks ass!! I have lived in Tucson for 8 years and haven't really ever thought twice about this museum as I drove by on my way to the desert museum or saguaro west. Well on a lazy Sunday, I thought, why not, and hopped in the car to explore. I am so happy I did, my friends and I were immediately impressed by the grand entrance, the front door is massive! Once inside, the bug room was sooo cool, so many bugs and they have really unique and not usually seen bugs... They also have a very rare butterfly that is half male and half female, beautiful! From the bug room the rest of the museum opened up with a combination of animals you could touch, horns you could pick up as well as lots and lots of animal busts and full size animals in little scenes both behind glass as well as out in the open. There were three rooms that really really stood out. The Man Cave was crazy, huge and filled with animals, they even have 2 full size giraffes and an elephant head. The polar bear and tiger were also super impressive! My next favorite room was the goat and sheep room. This is literally the center of the museum and the center of this room is a full size mountain with goats and sheep scattered. I loved the descriptions of goats and sheep, I never really understood the difference and this room did a fantastic job of helping me out! I love to learn! And finally, the last room that stood out was Arizona at Night. I loved wandering through the desert at night to see the cute bats, the bobcats and javelina! Such a great room for visitors to our area as well as for us locals to get reacquainted with our area! I started to allude to the education in the goat room, but I want to just let you know how much I learned when I was exploring these rooms. There were many many educational a kiosks and because of the way this museum is structured, it's all very easy to digest, understand and remember! And finally, there was an overarching theme of conservation throughout the museum. This also made the experience even better for me. I was at first against this museum because I didn't support all the hunting, well after leaving here, I know understand the right approaches to hunting, how animal conservation is supported and how I can get involved in saving the animals I love. This is a Tucson gem!!

Considering that Nashville is a mid-size city, we have a pretty impressive farmer's market.  The pavilions where vendors can display their wares are well-designed, and well-used.  There must have been at least ten different produce stands, all with enticing fruits and vegetables at prices lower than you find at grocery stores.  The only problem is deciding which vendor to buy from (every one I've patronized has had great-tasting produce.)  Beware that the produce isn't necessarily local or organic just because it's being sold at the farmer's market, although you can find both local and organic products there.  In addition to fresh produce, you can also find honey, handmade soap, and jam at the farmer's market.

The flea market next door offers an almost overwhelming array of unique products: pottery, carved wooden bowls, clothes (including some pretty stylish Obama T-shirts), sunglasses, shoes, rugs, jewelry, perfume, hats, etc.

After many years of using them, I finally call it quits, main because of degrading laundering quality over the years and escalated prices.

The name $225 cleaners don't match with their price increase to $2.99.  They also charge $2.99 for Shirts, which is ridiculous considering the fact that their shirt launder quality is by far the worst in the area. They have destroyed my shirts previously and refused to acknowledge the damage or do anything about it.

I came here recently with my boyfriend on a food crawl experiment through Old City. We decided to try some entrees here and were not thrilled at the experience. I'll only come back with recommendations on what I "need/should" get here or with someone who can give recommendations... because this was a pretty blah meal...

Ambiance: Small. Simple/Chic decor. Quite busy and expected. A bit tight so on a busy night I wouldn't go here for an intimate date. Good place for a small group.

Service: Nice but a bit disorganized. 

Food: This was where I minused points. Though I also leave room for redemption in my future update. I was massively craving udon noodle soup and some simple sushi creations so...
Udon noodle soup was a fusion fail. It came with pho like noodles ... thus defeating the purpose of UDON noodle soup ... The broth was relatively bland and if anything was a bit sweet (not usually what I want from udon soup...) The biggest sad face was that they didn't have any shichimi (a pretty standard Japanese 7 spice seasoning) ... which is a pretty common seasoning found in lots of the usual Japanese restaurants. They did give me lots of vegetables, which was nice.
Spicy tuna roll was not spicy. It was mashed tuna with almost no flavoring and was packed with tons of crunchy tempura or panko flakes which made it seem like I was eating sawdust ... 
My boyfriend and I enjoyed the presentation or rather were bemused by it. Almost every dish had one or two orchid flowers on it. Either they are recycling some of these delicate beauties or it just rains orchids in their kitchen ... 
I won't go into the details of the bf's meal because he's vegetarian and realistically we never have any expectations for his meal at most sushi restaurants ...
Overall, the amount we spent was just not justified to what we ate. 
Hopefully I was just ordering the wrong items for this place.

Drinks: BYOB which I appreciate. We brought a bottle of Morimoto's Hazelnut Ale by Rogue. The beer was great but I'd match it carefully. The Hazelnut can bring out a bit too much fishiness in the sushi... 

The price just didn't match to my experience but I probably need to try my hand again with better menu choices. I look forward to upgrading in my update..
