I stumbled upon this place while on business travel. The food was enjoyable. My favorite item was the minestrone. It was so flavorful and tasted nothing like the typical minestrone you might find elsewhere. It was quite a treat. It had cranberry beans, pasta, tomato and then a piece of bread laid overtop of the soup with pesto and some shredded cheese and it all melted into the soup.  I also had the romaine salad which was not quite as good as the soup but the soup really made me like this place.

I just went back here and was severely disappointed. This time I got ENTIRELY JIpped on a massage. The guy who cut my hair was clearly junior and the people on BOTH sides of me got a massage--- I did not. They even charged me more this time. AND THE WORST part about it was the guy who cut my hair, without asking, used a straightner to "style" my hair. For me this is sinful because anyone can style their hair with a straightner. It does not take skill. In addition to the fact that I was getting my hair cut because I wanted it to be healthy and when you immediately put a hot starightner onto my freshly cut locks, IT CAUSES heat damage and in my view, takes away from the initial point of the hair cut to begin with. NEVER again will i come here. SAD =(

Met friends here for lunch and was so impressed.  Outstanding pizza and arancini and my friends were very pleased with the beer selection.  Oh, and the gelato was excellent!  I recommend the hazelnut.  And it was all topped off by the friendly owner and and waiter Rocco.  I'll definitely be going back for dinner very soon.

Food is good, but they downsized the serving a couple of months ago and vehemently deny doing so.  The size of the to go salad is approximately 1/2 the size it originally was.  What was once good food at a great value is now the same good food at basically twice the price.  I can appreciate the need to adjust portion sizes, but arguing with the customer while denying the change offends one's intelligence.

Thought I would give this place a try for dinner. Ordered the "Caplingers Special" with Chipotle Coleslaw and Red Beans and Rice sides. The order came to my table in acceptable time. The Basa ( whitefish) was expertly grilled and I appreciate the grilling choice of " no salt" that I was given.  The slaw was enjoyable..... nice " kick" ....but the red beans and rice was just so- so......go to Yats for that......and the hush puppies were not noteworthy. Overall I will come back for the fish and slaw......they were very good.

We came here for our one year wedding anniversary meal last Sunday the 3rd and it was spectacular from the service to the food! I wish i could remember the waiter's name because he was excellent! We were treated like royalty or like we were famous. He brought us a sample to start with and a special pina colada ice cream dessert. We would barely drink from our water and they would be right there filling it up! Best steak my husband has EVER had and he's traveled worldwide so that's saying a lot. Highly recommend it!

I had never been or ate at an only raw food place so this was definitely an experience. I enjoy eating healthy but I'm not vegan or anything near. The women at the front was amazing she really explained everything let us try samples of their sauces and took her time until we decided on something. I had the burger plate, I enjoyed it considering it's all raw. Personally I would not eat here that often just because it's not my way of eating but it's a place I would enjoy from time to time!

Seriously life changing ha! You couldn't pay me to eats ribs until I found this place. Now I can't get enough! I loved them so much I thought maybe all ribs are delicious and I have just been missing out all these years. I made the mistake of getting ribs at another place and was very disappointed. Will never order ribs anywhere else ever again! Plus I love their family meals. Makes it so easy to pick up dinner after a long day at work.

I had a great deal of options for laser surgery, and chose St Luke's because it was nearby and highly recommended. This was a mistake, and my fault entirely. It is a factory, interested in selling eye operations only. All my insurance was used and $6,000 out of pocket - that should have been a clue, I have great insurance and if they won't cover a procedure then I should have done more investigation.

There is no bedside manner here, an assembly line for eye procedures and emptying wallets. Your surgeon will spend very little time with you and answer questions only with vague - "that probably won't happen" - remarks. As important as your vision is the normal person just doesn't know what to ask.

My operation left me needing glasses to read, something I've never needed for 75 years.

Please, find a smaller facility that will treat you as a person.

Move over, Nekter, this place wins. While visiting Santa Barbara, I got the PB+J quinoa breakfast bowl and it was so filling and tasty and warm. It was a huge portion for the price.

The setting was nice, you get to sit outside, and the staff are extremely friendly. 

Highly recommended!

Our favorite Mexican place in the city! It can seem a bit pricey but it's definitely worth it. Their margaritas are fresh and the tacos all have great flavor. Their chips and guacamole are some of the best I've ever had, not easy to do in Indy!

Totally rad giant warehouse with tons and tons of books, music, movies and more! I was a little sad that it moved from Charlotte to the new location - but it's really okay because the new spot is bigger, with more stuff and more parking! I love checking out the free bins outside too & I think it's super cool that they have a taco and/or coffee truck parked outside. Great place to find a gift for someone else or yourself.
Most expensive bagel place I've been to ( including NYC).  Bagels are good and fresh, but just not worth the expensive price.  One employee overcharges every time.

Super friendly employees and the best ice cream I've ever had. Everything was extremely fresh and prepared carefully to our standards. Restaurant was extremely clean and well kept. Free wifi! Great price for fresh made to order ice cream with unlimited toppings
I heard this place used to be good but not anymore. To many other places around to bother going to Freddie's. food was bad, service was worse.
The service is quick, the food comes out fast and they know how to do breakfast. If you ask for eggs over medium they come out over medium. My favorite breakfast place.
Awesome gelato with super friendly owner. We tried many different flavors and loved them all! Freshly made. We had the strawberry, pistachio, chocolate oreo, mascarpone, and lemon.

A work of ingenuity. Came in for my husbands birthday and loved that the entire menu was already taken care of. Whenever I go to a restaurant I always ask- what would you recommend? What does the chef create that is good? The Zatar flatbread bread  smothered with zatar was a miracle and the myriad of 6 dips like  a tart eggplant  ( I need to reread the menu)) perfect tender crunchy carrots, beet salad, best   hummus I have had with this spicy aoli, and my favorite was the crunchy tangy cabbage...reminded me of Indian thali with chutneys.  

I can go on and on with the wine pairings flavors and write an entire novel about the layers flavors ambiance superior hospitality of this restaurant and meal. The chef came to the table- I was thinking how do you do it? Wish I took a picture with him.

Just another thing- my daughter said she was dreaming of the chicken- she is very picky and has eaten in many restaurants around the world ( we all have)-

I took my family out for a pre-xmas meal and decided to give this location a try and what I saw disturbed me greatly. We had just been seated and were given the menus when the staff was finishing clearing the table, someone had only eaten 1/2 of a club sandwich and it was taken back by the kitchen where they wash the dishes but what the chef did I couldn't believe , some else had ordered a club sandwich and he took the half from the previous customer's plate and served it on the new order and the waitress brought it out to the unsuspecting guest. The guest was seated too far away from me and not wanting to cause a scene I simply got my family out of there, I have contacted the board of health about this because lord knows what else they are doing there and honestly I don't want to find out but that is a brand new way to keep your trash fees down !

You might be better off homeless than renting from Wolfe. Unprofessional. Irresponsible. Take your money somewhere else! Things don't get fixed, sometimes for years. New agey property supervisors that let tenants park wherever they want and leave their junk lying around outside their units blocking walkways making life a hell for disabled people. "Let's just all get along and live like animals!" Cheap. That's about all! I'm lucky, I'm gonna die soon so I don't have to put up with them much longer. Really a terrible, ruined company. You'd think they'd have gotten it together after nearly fifty years in businesses but, sadly, not. They just don't care but get paid anyways. In the SB property management business capitalism is broken and so they get away with it.

It's really bad when Starbucks runs out of ingredients for half of their menu! However I stood there waiting for nearly 10 minutes while the two employees working here we're busy talking and gossiping and catching up on what they did from the night before. I had no idea that to women could sit there and just gab so much when you have a customer standing in front of you. I'm not sure if these are actual Starbucks employees or just target people working the Starbucks counter.
Perfectly chaotic!   Shopping was great, food was delish and bathrooms were clean.  Definitely kid friendly!

This was a very clean hotel with great ambiance. The staff is super friendly and are there to help with any questions you may have. 

The walls are a little thin and you can hear doors and closets opening as well as....

The pool is heated but it could be warmer. The gym are great and has free weights and plenty of treadmills. You are on the 8th floor so you can see some of the city.
Great variety of dishes. Everything that we tried was delicious. Good selection of beers on tap. Highly recommended. Our favorite place in St. Pete's, Treasure island area

I have been reading the reviews left on this site and I could not disagree more.  My mom was at Handmaker Memory Care the last 9 months of her life.  I was present every week multiple times a week and at different times of the day. Some weeks I was there daily.  My experience in these types of facilities comes from taking care of not only my mom, but also my dad and both my  in-laws in other facilities for their final season, since 1999.  My mom was our last in our family legacy and heritage. My hope was always to keep our loved ones home till they finished their journey here.  It didn't happen with any of them.  I have to say that it is easy to cast stones, without living the lives of a caregiver at these facilities.  I have met my share, many good and those who are not invested in the path they have chosen.  Is any place perfect?  Is anyone perfect? No, not even a spouse or a sibling or the child of a loved one suffering with any physical disease or Dementia/Alzheimer.  

My review will come from what I experienced while my mom lived at Handmaker.  Physically she was always clean, her room put together and the meals, well they were much better than what I had seen in other facilities where seniors were given corn dogs, or grilled cheese sandwiches for dinner on a regular basis.  Because of the overall culture in this place of Honoring God and Honoring Parents,  I saw from the top down a level of respect for the person/the humanity as to my moms care.  Were there exceptions and those who possibly worked there just for a paycheck?  Yes,  but that was the exception in my case, not the rule.  I saw and heard the care and respect in other dining rooms as I walked by, and when we joined in the activities from other areas.  

Can anyone work for the pay these people make and do the things, many family members don't want to or can't do for their loved ones and all be judged with a wide brush?  I do not think so.  Would we want to be judged that way?  Do these people have families? problems? Yes....Yet, each day they came in and sometimes did double shifts so that the residents would have what they needed.   It would be so much easier to sit in front of a conveyor belt assembling a product than the interpersonal care needed towards another human being, especially one with Dementia or Alzheimer.  Even being a CNA or nurse at a hospital is easier because some heal and go home happy and that is rewarding.  In the K Unit, the challenge is to accept however the day comes with new ever changing circumstances that present themselves daily.  This is due to the changing levels in a residents mindset.  For example, my mom would be peaceful and fine for days then one day more demanding and anxious, so they would have to find new ways to re-direct her.  Multiply that by several people doing that at the same time with only a handful of help.  Yet, they found a way to work as a unit and I saw that every time I was there.   Exhausting work both physically and emotionally. I saw what they went through when someone died, yes they cared.  I saw with my eyes the genuine pain in several of them on my moms final day.  They met her needs, not only physical but emotional, by being there when I could not.  My mom had her favorites, who stole her heart, you know who you are because you made the effort to make sure she ate till the end.  Sometimes she would eat for you and not for me and you helped her even more when I was not there.  I will forever be grateful for you, for your love and service to my mom till the very end, when you prepared her body lovingly in your pain to be transferred. I didn't see you come out of her room but my family did and they saw you tears.   I know you shared our pain.   
Thank you Handmaker for being there for my family.  For the staff at Unit K, I love you and thank you for being my family all those months.  You see,  we are living in Tucson temporarily due to my husbands work, and we didn't have other support.  You were our support.  Thank you for providing a service, no, for being present in a time when someones journey is the most difficult, and often the hardest for their families. You choose daily to be present, you choose to expose your life to the most emotionally draining aspect of humanity, the decline and end of someones soul's journey on earth.  

I will be Forever Grateful!!

This was amazing!!

We came about 5 or 6 years ago at old location and left without a desire to come back.  However, A birthday party brought us back tonight and wow what a treat!  The food was so good, fresh, delicious.  Our chef JC is someone we will ask for time again.

The entire staff was friendly and efficient.

The shrimp, vegetables and apple sake

This is my first day at this hotel. It is clean and I don't find it to be dated at all. The room is comfortable and amenities are good. Evening reception and free breakfast order in the morning is always welcome treat for a business traveler. There is a restaurant on premises. It is in close proximity to the airport. I would stay here again.  Only negative is the lighting in the room. There just aren't enough watts in the bulbs in the two bedside lamps.

Fries are way too salty, like biting into a salt lick. Chicken strips very greasy. Oil needs to be changed. I haven't eaten Chick-fil-a in a while and each time I go it's always bad. It reminds me why I don't go.

Waited at the counter for about 10 minutes to be acknowledged by one of the 3 women standing behind the counter, counting their tip money and swapping smaller bills for larger bills out of the register. They were having personal conversations as we as if I was not standing there. Finally got acknowledged and told there would be an hour and a half wait. The place was empty at 5:30 on a Sunday night. Not one person at the bar and maybe 3 lanes being used. I think they may have wanted to go home early ?

Here is my take on Jimmy Johns -- decent quality ingredients, limited menu, blazing fast speed!

This is the only sub shop I will go to when there is a line.  The JJ employees manage to plow through the orders quick!  Sometimes my sub is ready before I can pay and get to the other end of the counter!

If you need a quick sandwich in downtown Tampa during the lunch hour--this is your place!

We were at their main restaurant next door and we were underwhelmed. We hadn't been here for a few years and other than the great bread and asparagus soup, the rest of the meal was over cooked and tasteless. The scallops special was a huge disappointment and when we complained, they did nothing. Not a repeat, sorry to say.

Family owned business very caring very honest. I've known the family for over 40 years and their integrity extends into their business and into their personal life. I trust that any work they do is done because they truly believe that taking care of your car is the same as taking care of your family. You may be able to find cheaper but you will not find better.
Well here we go. After waiting 87 minutes for our entrees, 4/6 of them arrived soggy and Luke warm.

I found McCormick and Schmick's very enjoyable, especially given that cooked fish is rarely on the top of my food list. The location is a great one at 1 South Broad St, directly across from City Hall and The Wanamaker Building. Parking is easily found and there are a number of bars and cafes for after dinner cocktails. 

The menu is primarily fish and seafood, augmented daily with fresh catch selections. The fresh catch are not only what type of fish, but also where it was caught. According to the server, any of these fresh catch options can be added to an existing entree, including create-your-own surf and turf platters. Yes, for those not fond of the piscean choices, there are a few land-based options as well...of which I took advantage. 

We had a group of 10, so were able to taste several of the appetizers. The oyster sampler was excellent, really highlighting the difference in taste and size of what is available. The crab/shrimp/artichoke dip was served with pita chips and had a great sweet and salty taste. Fried calamari with garlic butter and banana peppers are seers with a spicy tomato compote, and of the three appetizers mentioned, should not be missed. 

I skipped the fish for an entree, an tried the Carolina roasted chicken with smoked Gouda mac and cheese...INCREDIBLE! The mac and cheese is also available as a side to be ordered with any entree, so definitely check that out. Really great comfort food option. Garlic French fries are also a side option, and worth the over-stuffed feeling you will inevitably feel after eating. No desserts this time, I was way to full and had already loosened my belt a notch.

Very rude yelled at us for looking in the freezer he raised his voice and told us if your not buying anything leave the store but we bought something and he slammed the cash register thats how you lose business and we asked him a few question how much were the food and he's like umm 1.25 and he's thinking stop asking all this questions.

Great cozy restaurant with an amazing wait staff!

Food was reasonably priced for the area and definitely did not lack anything in taste. 

Everything we ordered came out quickly and tasted delicious. Oysters were great, steak was great, shrimp and grits were great, even the creme brulee was good!

Only thing we wished for was if we were around for happy hour!

I can't say enough good things about David and his business. I use this service every time I need to travel to Indianapolis or my father needs to travel. David goes out of his way to make my travel and my father's travel stress-free and he really goes the extra mile. I don't even look at other options for transportation, the outstanding customer service has made me a customer for life!
Very good quality for a very reasonable price. Try their "all you can eat" for $20. It is so worth it! Their quality surpasses a lot of "all you can eat" sushi joints. I will be coming back!

I hope people indeed read my update.  I mentioned before that I had mixed views of this place.  Well upon receiving a personal message from the owner apologizing I feel like I can over look some flaws.  No place is perfect and knowing that one place does care enough about it's regular patrons to personally talk with them about flaws is huge in my book. Relaxed bar with cheap drinks...check them out!
Food and service were amazing. The edamame hummus is really good, and the miso soup was awesome. The manager, Ace, even came by to thank us which is always nice to see. Will definitely be back.
The drive through was painfully slow, they would not accept our coupon that was valid for bogo, and when we finally received our drinks they were wrong.

Richie is such a gift! I got my second Covid vaccine today and was feeling sluggish. I've also just been majorly stressed out lately. My best friend who lives up north purchased the hydration iv for me to help with everything. A major thank you to my BF because Richie was just what I needed today. He was super fast to respond and let me know when he was on his way. He was professional but also felt like a long time friend! He is funny, smart and knows his stuff! He explained everything to me helped me understand the benefits of what vitamins would be useful. And honestly, he brightened my mood because he is just such a joy to be around  :)

I already booked 4 more sessions with him. I couldn't be happier. I feel much better as I mentioned earlier that I was feeling sluggish. He checked in with me later to see how I was feeling. He truly cares and it shows. 

Thank you, Richie!!

This is definitely one of the best pizza places in the area--and their chicken saltimbocca is delicious!!  Their white pizzas, spinach pizzas, and regular pizzas are all good, salads are fresh (they make one with roasted red peppers and fresh mozzarella that's delicious!),  etc.  For those of us that like peppers and onions on our pizzas, be forewarned: the peppers and onions will be more fresh and crisp than they are on Papa John's or Dominos.  Delicious!
Also, it's BYOB if you like wine with your pizza.  :-)

I ordered the chicken sandwich with fries. The chicken was so dry and flavorless. The bred was super oily, and fries taste so bad someone forgot to tell them to change the oil. It felt like they didn't change the fryer oil for a month. It would have been better to purchase gift shop prep cold sandwich. I'm surprised health department  didn't closed them down. Price very expensive and quality very poor. I hope you will read the reviews before wasting your $$$$ unlike me

Stopped in for a quick breakfast while in the area. first time here. You walk up to the counter and order and they bring your food out to you. Small inside, but they have outdoor seating which I liked. The front of house employee wasn't too welcoming, but all the other service we had was nice. I ordered the grits bowl, subbed bacon for more spinach ( I asked if I could sub the bacon for anything else, and the only response I got was "more spinach" ok..) but the grits were to die for. Buttery and creamy goodness. My breakfast came out quickly but my friends avocado toast took a while and was pretty small for $8. My grits bowl was well worth the $9.
Not much to look at but good solid food. We split the Coop's taste plate twice. Gives a good taste oaf everything for a reasonable price.

Tonight was not to good for me to order the lady who answered the phone was rushing my brother and she hung up before he could ask for the peppers on the side and napkins and menu...... all in all I like this place

I have been an Apple fan for over 4 years now and as they say, "Once you try Mac, you never go back.

Whenever I have had a problem or a question, I was always able to go to the Apple Store to get the help I need. Not once was I pressured into buying something I did not want or need. The service Apple provides is second to none, and unlike other so-called computer companies, they honor their warranties instead of trying to get you to buy a new machine instead.

I can't say enough good things about the Green Hills Apple Store, and will always be shopping there for my computer needs.
The best hotel in downtown Santa Barbara. Walking distance to lots of great restaurants, a nice rooftop pool, beautiful rooms and really friendly staff.

Best wings I've had since moving from NY state 21 years ago. Pizza was very good, ingredients were fresh & tasty. I would have given 5 stars but had to wait 25 minutes past my carry out time, it was a playoff weekend though! Good food, definitely recommend

This review is not for the food.... we showed up at 7:15 and were told the wait would 1.5 hours. So we walked around and had a few drinks and came back around 8:45. We were no closer to the getting a table then when we started. So we waited down stairs in the bar and had $10 of the smallest drinks ever. Finally about 9:45 our name is called. Now please note the entrees here are huge!! Per what I've see on Yelp. So we wanted to split the steak with ocean sauce. No one needs that much food esp when you want to keep the party going on Frenchman's St. so we finally sit down and order and the wittier says "oh it's one entree per person" like wtf?!? Why!!??? Why waste that much food!?
I mean you can charge us a split fee or something that's fine, but we don't want that much food! AND if that is truly your policy have a sign up or something so ppl don't waste 2 hours of their night! So I'm sure the food is good, but alas we will never know cause we left.

FOR THE RESTAURANT...The ONLY reason this place gets 2 stars is because of the drinks, otherwise the food is disgusting! The "pizza" tastes like a tin can thanks to the tomatoes and sauce and the crust is uncooked dough. My husband ordered the chili cheese dog and he would have been better off getting one at a 7-11 convenience store it was so gross. The chili was so nasty it could have possibly peeled paint off a car and the cheap cheese wouldn't even melt. Unless you are intentionally looking for gastrointestinal upset, do not eat here!
Its a good size toy store with friendly staff. Its a little messy but it is a TOY store and some people have bad kids.
Awesome ice cream, I had the cherry vanilla and mint chocolate chip!
We had a great server and experience - thanks, Tre!!  Food was excellent. Drinks excellent. Price is high but worth a splurge.

I have been going to this Italian eatery for many years and last evening had a terrible experience that seems based on new staff, both servers and chefs (though in this case "kitchen staff" is more appropriate than "chef").

First off, the outdoor heater near us didn't work so we had to change tables.

Second, the server took fifteen minutes to greet us.

Third, I was served the piddliest glass of wine I've ever seen in Santa Barbara.

Most important, the food:  Almost inedible.

The pizza was a disaster area, even after two tries from the kitchen.

As John Junor of Fleet Street used to write, "Pass the sick bag, Alice."
Whitney T. is the best! Servers are friendly and it's a cool casual atmosphere.

The place is ok.. I wish there's a better place around the music row to just wind down as long as I wish, but there isn't..

Place is very casual, almost kind of run down because of it's dark decor and ambiance, but if you're into sitting in a position like L in the anime Death Note, this place is great because the furniture looks like it takes quite a beating already, so what's the fuss with another shoe mark on the seats..
LOVE this place. Pre-covid I had several bible studies there because there's tons of space. Great place to get work done and food and drinks are all good quality! Always something to try

I have been staying here a week so far and I have to say that every employee here has been extremely attentive and engaging! They genuinely seem happy all of the time and will ensure your stay is the best it can be. Also, when I found my refrigerator wasn't working at 10:00pm, I told the front desk. Maintenance was at my room in the morning with a new unit. Excellent service! I can't say enough about the current team!

Great place in a cool part of downtown Boise. While the wait was long, it was a nice touch to have a coffee table outside to help pass the time. 

Once inside the wait staff were both attentive and informative. We went with the Malt Waffle and Breakfast Burrito. These are two excellent choices, especially if your better half likes to "share". Sharing is caring. 

I would definitely go back since this place has a funky feel which should be comfortable to anyone from Seattle or Portland areas.

The happy hour is a great deal and snagging a spot at the bar is the best seat in the house.  This place is very popular so even on a Sunday at 3:00pm (their daily happy hour goes from  2:00pm-5:00pm) expect a substantial crowd. You order at the counter and then get a server that sporadically checks up on you but the service isn't adequate generally at the tables (so you can go awhile without a drink refill so sit at the bar, if possible, where you can get full service).  I also wish you got a bit more choice in building your own pie instead of the set menu as there are very few options.  The pie here does have a nice crunchy crust with good flavors that can stand on their own even without toppings.  They did a really great job with the build out here and its a very nice space to enjoy some pizza and drinks.

Overall I would only go here for the happy hour and it might be worth it to wait for a spot to open at the bar for the vastly improved service available there as the table service is a disorganized mess.  If it is too crowded here or you miss happy hour just go to New York Pizza for the $5 pint and a slice deal.

Great little spot for a Mexican meal that's quick, cheap, and tasty! They have about anything you want, but tacos are the special of the house. I had a big burrito with ranchero sauce and it was delicious. And quick! I had barely ordered and it was already out! Small selection of beers on draft, but they're repping the Mexican beers correct! The decor is luchador to the hilt and there are plenty of TVs to catch the game, etc. I would definitely recommend you stop by if you're in the area!

This restaurant is awful and the prices to match it are dreadful. Don't be fooled, because the restaurant looks beautiful from the outside. Unfortunately the sushi is not up to par with other places such as Mikado and Kobe.

Huge organizational and marketing issues here. I enjoyed the food (all you can eat crab legs), but the place needs help. Unprofessional service. Very empty which is a waste of beautiful landscape on the water. They have the perfect location and set up to have a great place. Rooftop patio, sizable dining with a water view. The bartender was our waiter, which prolonged the  situation. The table next to us was going off on the manager because that waitress touched his daughter's food with her hands. 5 minutes later, the table behind us left without paying and the bartender and manager chased them down the street. It was a lot of drama and it seems like they need a management and discipline makeover. When my sister'a crab legs were refilled, they brought out a plate of separated legs that were not on a cluster. It was ghetto and unprofessional to bring scraps to a customer who is paying 150 bucks for dinner. This place has potential but doesn't know how to capitalize on it

I'm trying to think of something I don't like about this place.... I'll work on that while I write this review. The Block is styled as a neighborhood restaurant/butcher shop. Granted, it's a pretty nice neighborhood. But The Block is always welcoming, never stuffy. As far as the butcher shop - they do have a nice, but not huge butcher case. Most of their butcher skills are shown off in the menu, where they do delicious things to mostly very local meats. Lots of pork - smoked, pulled, grilled, made into jam (yes, bacon jam). Beef is offered as a burger and a butcher's cut of the day. Chicken is a lovely roasted breast. But these folks know what they're doing with veggies, too. The flash-fried brussel sprouts will bring tears to your eyes. Their seasonal salads show off produce like gem-colored beets and tender asparagus.
And their bartenders know what they're doing - from the fancy-schmancy cocktails to the craft beers and a nice wine list. They are skilled and knowledgable. I love this place.

The first time deciding to try this place. We did go here on a very busy night, I tried to order a frozen margarita then our server told me the machine was broken so I was very disappointed with that. I ordered 3 enchiladas and said 1 cheese but I got 1 filled with chicken instead, I asked our server if I could get the cheese enchilada like I ordered, she said fine. But it never came out. I asked a couple more times and it never came out and I waited a very long time. I guess its good to point out, that our original orders came out very quick, the food quality is pretty average, nothing to rave about. But the service here is not great at all. I don't know if I would come back again. I could not even get my water refilled when I asked. There are better cheap Mexican type joints around town. If I can't get good service or my order right, why even bother to come here?

I recently wrote a review about an experience I had with Intelligent Design, and they were quick to follow up, own where they had missed the mark, and helped me spot a leak in my coil that the AC company provided by my home warranty had missed, saving me a ton! Although my initial experience with Intelligent Design was not the best, they listened to my concerns, and turned my experience around by being honest, genuine and thorough.

Sure, this place is fun to walk through.  But the tourists who think this is a key food place to visit in Philly are seriously missing out.  Philly is a foodie paradise with INCREDIBLE restaurants!  Venture to 13th Street to try Lolita, Barbuzzo, or Jamonera, and to see all the gorgeous little shops on the street, including the artisanal chocolates made fresh at Verde; or go to Bareburger, Bluestone Lane, PS & Co, Buena Onda Tacos, V Street, Dizengoff, etc., for casual but DELICIOUS fresh food. Go to Cafe Karma (four locations) and sit in the beautiful gardens at their locations on 22nd/Pine or 10th/Pine.  Go to Whole Foods Center City and check out the delicious food hall!  For high-end restaurants, go to Talula's Garden, Zahav, Vedge, Res Ipsa, Suraya, and more!  To explore food heaven in West Philly, go to Kilimandjaro or Manakeesh restaurants, or try Chez Yasmine food truck.  For Vietnamese, go to Nam Phong or Vietnam Restaurant on Washington.  For pizza, go to Mama Palma's, Stella's, or Giorgio's on Pine.  Go to the fabulous Saturday Farmer's Market at Rittenhouse Square or the equally fabulous Sunday Farmer's Market at Headhouse Square. In South Philly, go to any of the treasures on Passyunk Avenue or to Stargazy for British pies. You get the idea...

Ever have one of those moments where you're like, "Only in Philthy?"

Yeah.

So I was on a date (!!!) with someone who had scored us free tickets to Gayfest: Crumple Zone.  We met up at Plays and Players.  For the record, she was carrying a huge bag of food, and I was in black jeans and an Oscar the Grouch t-shirt.  The person (queer!  how delightful) who met us on the first floor didn't even blink and let us know we had to go upstairs.

The building is currently under renovation, which just adds to the "what the FUCK am I in Oz??!" feel.  There is a giant brass gate just chilling on the landing to the second floor and a busted window next to an immaculate one on the third floor.  We were directed to the pub (yes, the pub) which is to the right of the third floor stage to wait.

It is ... tiny, air conditioned, blaring very gay music and -- yes -- you can carry your drink into the show.  Which is precisely what my companion did.

The theater itself is very intimate.  I'd say it seats no more than thirty something.  The a/c was on full fucking blast, so we were both shivering within minutes.  However, good acoustics, and I have nothing to complain about for the scenery.

Uh, Gayfest, on the other hand.

Look, everyone should go spend 25$ on this because queer people in queer plays is really fucking important.  It is REALLY IMPORTANT to support queer artists and writers and play companies.

That being said, you're going to laugh at the wrong parts of Crumple Zone because the writing is absolutely god-awful.  There is a monologue from one character to his lover (who is cheating on his bf of four years ooooooo dramz).  It goes approximately like this:

"I have a dream of you and me ... on a deserted beach."

That's as far as I got before I was desperately holding back sobs of laughter, and my poor benefactor was grabbing my arm and doubling over too.  There are a lot of those moments, interspersed with actually quite good performances from a few of the actors, as well as two sexual assaults which add nothing to the plot.

so idk
Higher end cost but you get what you pay for! If you're looking for a more formal dinning experience this is the place. Cuisine is the creole you're looking for and the quality is equally matched.

Great little bookstore!! I bought a Michael Crichton for one dollar! How sweet is that. Plus the inside is not too cluttered. It has just the right about on clutter to make the perfect cozy and cool bookstore. Plus the guy who worked there looked like such a sweet old white haired man. For all you who love to root through books to find a special gem, stop by Whodunit?

We don't have any food allergies or restrictions but live nearby so decided to try it out one day. We have tried their breakfast sandwiches on numerous occasions, and have been consistently impressed. There are lots of options and ingredients are fresh and flavorful. The lunch menu also seems good, although we have not yet tried it. The place is pretty empty so it is nice to linger over  a cup of (great!) coffee.

The burger was good!! Much better than Five Guys!! The French fries not so good. I won't complain as they were free. About the same as McDonalds. My fries were cold but  it was taken care of. The sauce bar was not really a big deal. A little overpriced! Best to go during the week when there are specials!

They cleaned my new house before we moved in and did a great job. They were very good about following up and making sure the job was done to my satisfaction. They also cleaned out the refrigerator and it was sparking!

It inexplicably took more than 2 hours to get an exam and order a new pair of glasses. I'm still not happy with the glasses (remade 3x but they still hurt my head). Two calls to optometrist went unreturned and the office manager was less than helpful. (By the way, you don't have the best return policy in the industry. ) Some staff are pleasant, but for others, it's just a business (), instead of it being about eye care, health, and wellbeing.

Volume Hair Studio is AMAZING!  Everyone here is so friendly and personable.  It isn't easy for me to find a salon I like...I spent years looking for the perfect salon where I used to live and then I moved and was at a loss.  A friend suggested Volume and I decided to try it out!  So happy I did, because I think I found one of the best salons in Philly.

I never have to wait long, even when I am pretty early for my appointments.  When I walk in, I am always met with a friendly face and the offer of a refreshment.

  I go to Rachael B. and Lauren as my color and cut "team" and I just adore them!

Rachael B. does my color (usually I get highlights, sometimes I change it up with other types of coloring techniques) and she is so amazing!   She makes everything look on the natural side and really listens to what I want and advises me from there.  I trust her judgement and opinions so completely that I can easily give her complete control over my color. Rachael is a genius when it comes to color and I cannot speak more highly of her abilities.   She also always makes sure I am happy with my color before I head over to my stylist for my cut.  I appreciate that because she really takes her time with each of her clients.  We never run short on conversation topics, Rachael has a great sense of style and I always get so many compliments on my hair after she does my color! 

Lauren is my stylist.  She is a true artist when it comes to a cut and style.  Not only will she listen to what I want, but she explains what she is doing before she starts and also explains how she does things after the cut when she is styling so I can try it on my own.  Very  often, I will tell her to do what she wants with my cut. Lauren is great at reading the client and knows my taste and style.  She knows what I wouldn't be happy with and also can visualize what will look good on me.  I have utter and complete trust and confidence in her ability that I often let her take complete control...she is that good.  She is also so personable!  We also never run short on conversation.  I also get tons of compliments on how fantastic my cut is after I leave the salon!

The prices here might be a bit up there, but it is well worth every penny spent. Plus, they often have deals, such as 20% your first appointment, check in deals, loyalty cards for products, etc.  I will gladly shell out a little extra for the great experiences I have had here.

Rachael and Lauren also give great advice on hair-products.  I often have questions about things my friends talk about using and they will always tell me what they honestly think, will offer alternative ideas, and never tell me to get something they don't think I need.  Lets face it, I am an impulsive shopper, so I can easily be talked into products.  I have never felt like I was pressured to buy anything or talked into anything. I really appreciate that, as I could easily walk out of any salon or makeup store with bags filled with product.  When I do need or want a new product, everyone is super helpful!

One day, I came in to get a new shampoo, I had only been to the salon maybe 3 or so times before at this point in time,  so I was amazed and excited  that as soon as Lauren saw me (maybe less than a minute after walking in) she came over, knew who I was (name, hair type, things we spoke about at our last appointment, etc) and was able to advise me on shampoo and a few other products I was looking at!  I felt very special and it was like I had a personal consultant!  This is not something that happens at a lot of places, so I really liked how I didn't feel like a burden but a valued customer when I had a million questions and needed help with the products I was looking at.  It actually meant a lot to me that this happened, I cannot express how much I appreciate that kind of hospitality and customer service.

I have never seen anyone leave this salon unhappy, so I highly suggest coming here.  I have been coming here for about a year and a half now, and I personally always leave looking and feeling so fabulous!  I can't say enough good things about this place and those that work here! Thank you Volume Hair Studio, you rock!

I moved buildings so don't get here as much as I wish I could, but after a fine lunch today I decided to update my original review and give them that 5th star they so richly deserve.  Great food, great people, great price.

We had a relaxing, delightful dinner!  Our server grasped quickly that we were interested in a leisurely path through the courses and was great at going with that pace. The charcuterie board was outstanding!   I paired it with a Sazerac and could have stopped there happily.  Everything made in house, so everyday is different. Every bite was a delight and we had some fun, new things to try - alligator sausage, alligator "ham", pickled beet, pickled okra. The board was huge for the 2 of use, but we ate every bite!

We continued on with BBQ shrimp appetizer...lick the plate clean!  Then for me, alligator Bolognese paired with a delightful meritage and hubby had the pork chop.  He was really happy with how moist it was and the dirty rice with it was so flavorful.    We were so full just could not even contemplate dessert.    

Service was great.  House managers obviously watching how things were going.  We never felt we were being rushed, even on a Saturday night.  Wish we lived in NOLA....I'd be back for another charcuterie board tomorrow....maybe an afternoon snack in the bar. I will be dreaming of it for sure.

Everything is so flavorful, tasty, and you definitely will have more than enough food to fill you up! All their combo meals come with 2 sides; HUGE portions for even the side items too.

Gyro dinner is always good, I love their chicken combo, and their chicken shawarma. There's always freshly made baklava by the front counter (if you're not already going into food coma).

I loved everything about Casa Vicente!! We ordered the Paella Valenciana Mixta which has chicken, seafood and vegetables. Side note- you need at least four people for paella and it needs to be ordered ahead. 
As it was a Friday night (and we wanted the paella) we had reservations- I would highly recommend reservations as there did not seem to be any available tables.
The atmosphere was great from the moment we walked in. It was like I was back in España again! The flamenco dancing was great and really added to the experience!
We ordered a carafe of red sangría and tortilla española while we waited for the paella. The sangría was amazing- not super sweet like it typically is in the US. The tortilla española was exactly how I remembered it from Spain! Simple but delicious!
Shortly after we finished our tapa, the paella arrived. It had lots of seafood- mussels, shrimp and calamari. It looked amazing and tasted amazing.
For dessert we ordered Creme Catalana- sort of a Creme brûlée type dessert. It was very good, definitely very sweet but I would order it again.
I have been looking for an authentic Spanish restaurant with authentic paella and I finally found it right here in Tucson! I can't wait to go back for more paella, sangría, and to try more of the tapas!

We had a work retirement party there yesterday.  As usual, the pizzas were excellent and the salads and appetizers were delicious!  We have NEVER had a bad meal at this place.  Did I mention that they make a great martini at the bar!  A definite 5 stars every time!
I love this place! Close to my house and in a convenient location. It is always clean and tidy. I have gotten the majority of the people who work there, and all of them are great!
My first time at this clinic, I was VERY IMPRESSED with the quality of care my cat received, I also LOVED THE TECH!! She  is a wealth of knowledge, AND NICE, kindred spirit, she is care lover .
The place is seriously beautiful, even in the winter.  Seeing the site covered in snow is gorgeous.  Unfortunately, the joggers don't see to care much for everyone else trying to use the space.  :(

Very good food, well worth making the stop. They have very friendly employees, great service. The food was spot on, we tried the signature chicken and waffles (well worth the try) and had something from the sweet side. Definitely worth a try if you're in the area

We came here upon the recommendations of a few friends. When it comes to Japanese AYCE buffets, this one beats Minado by a slight margin.

We stopped by on a chilly Tuesday evening around 5:30pm and the place was pretty empty. We were seated quickly and asked for instructions on how to order the AYCE food. 

The AYCE comes with two sheets of paper fill with a variety of rolls, hand rolls, sashimi, and Japanese dishes as such wakami salad, kani salad, teriyaki tofu, beef and chicken teriyaki, and beef negimaki. You're given a pencil and simply jots down the number of pieces you want. 

As long as you finish the food in front of you, you can keep checking off the order list but keep in mind that any wasted food will be charged. 

Overall, the food was well prepared and the quality of the sashimi are decent for the price. Is this authentically Japanese? Absolutely not. However, it'd be difficult to find any real Japanese restaurant charge this kind of price for authentic Japanese food.

Went for the first time.  I always order bacon & eggs at a new place to see the "quality" of the food.  Over medium eggs came out over easy & the homefries where sooo salty I couldn't even eat them.  Waitress tried to take my cousin's plate without asking if she was finished & when was told still eating off of it she sort of threw it back  down on the table & gave us a dirty look. Only 1 piece of toast included in the price seems a little chincy.  Will we be back? Probably not.

I stopped by their Truck for Food Truck Friday.  I tried the Jambalaya Balls and a Pork Poor Boy. The balls were tremendously good.  Sausage, rice, pork, spices, all in a fritter... or over sized hush puppy.  Maybe the best thing I had at FTF.  The sammie came sitting it a pile of grease.  I ended up eating the pork out of it with a fork.  The innards were good, but the grease ruined that dish for me.

Yeah... So I had the zucchini cakes and mashed potatoes which were good but the ravioli was practically inedible. I couldn't finish it and had to spit it out it was so bad. Also, not sure it's worth the price. I ordered from caviar and it was $31.45.... what.

Bartaco makes delicious food. Wish we could have enjoyed their amazing indoor decor, but we braved the 28 degree weather and dined with the snow! They couldn't have been more attentive! They walked out every 5 minutes to make sure our heaters were working properly (one of our two heaters was a little faulty). Their food was absolutely delicious, I couldn't pick a favorite if I tried but I got the chicken, sesame ribeye, and chorizo tacos and a side of street corn. It was so good I'm already looking forward to going back. Was it cold? Yeah, a little. Was it worth it? ABSOLUTELY! Wear two pairs of socks, throw on your Ugg's, and bring a blanket with you like we did! You'll be comfortable & cozy and it's actually a fun experience dining outside in winter. Made for a fun spontaneous date night. Great job, Bartaco!

Okay, so this is one of those new places in town that I was REALLY excited about trying, and REALLY wanted to love, like whoa.

Instead, I had a horrible first experience that makes me not want to ever come back.

We show up on a Sunday evening around 6:30 PM (yes, yes, we knew it would most likely have a wait at that time of the evening) ... and to our surprise, we only really wait for 10 minutes to talk to the hostess. Even more surprising, we are immediately seated after reaching the hostess - amazing for The Pharmacy, right? I was pretty pumped.

Our waitress shows up pretty soon thereafter - all signs point to a great experience, right? Well, this is when it starts to all go downhill, so brace yourselves. I had heard from numerous people that their "phosphates" and cream sodas were the way to go, especially ones with vanilla. So, I ordered a simple vanilla phosphate ... only to have the waitress tell me they were entirely out of vanilla syrup. STRIKE ONE. Okay, so I ask to go last out of the 4 of us to order a drink, scrambling to find something on the list without vanilla. I ended up settling with what the BF chose - the "Rickey" (lemon and maraschino cherry syrup soda). 

Then, she decides to go ahead and take our orders since we're ready. Now, keep in mind ... I'm not a beef-eater. And I know some people are under the mindset that "real" burgers can only be made out of beef, but I severely disagree. Just the night before, the BF and I made a stellar goat cheese-stuffed turkey burger that could easily beat out many of the beef burgers that the BF has had in life before. So, at the Pharmacy, I was all ready and EXCITED to try their falafel burger, that came topped with yogurt raita and goat cheese (I'm a little obsessed). Guess what? Only after I try to order it do I find out from our waitress that they're entirely out of the falafel burger, AS WELL AS the black bean burger (a.k.a. all vegetarian options). The waitress then asked me if I was vegetarian, and I said no, that I could do turkey. She said they had that, 3 of us ordered turkey burgers (the Pharmacy and Farm Burgers with turkey instead of beef), while the BF ordered a beef burger. 

Guess what? About 5 minutes after we had ordered, the waitress comes back and tells us "how embarrassing this is," that they're actually also out of turkey burgers. REALLY?! It was so ridiculous, in fact, that our entire table's reaction was to laugh out loud, really hard, at the waitress. She goes on to say something along the lines of: "Yeah, Sundays and Mondays are always really bad - we tend to run out of stuff by then, so try coming back another day!" ARE YOU SERIOUS?! One of the friends in my group told me then that he had read a review online of someone else having  this problem on a Sunday, back when they first opened. If this has happened before, you would THINK that The Pharmacy would've planned for this to not happen again. And if that's such an issue, that you can't possibly manage to plan for enough food to cover the options you've listed on your menu, then CLOSE DOWN ON SUNDAYS. Or, the least you could do is to let your table know what you're out of BEFORE they order. What if we had waited in line for an hour for a table, only to sit down and order a vanilla phosphate AND/OR falafel/black bean/turkey burger, only to then find out that we can't have any of these options?! Oh, I shudder to even think what my own response to that situation would have been.

Seriously, if you were actually a vegetarian, you really had NO options tonight, and would probably have to leave. And that is exactly what we did. Oh and guess what? The waitress didn't even apologize and offer to take care of our sodas for all of the inconvenience. It still irks me to have even paid them $8 for two drinks that weren't even that great. 

All in all, the atmosphere seemed fun and lively, and the hostess was nice. But seriously, GET WITH IT! ORDER MORE MEAT/PRODUCE TO MAKE SURE YOU CAN MAKE ALL OF THE BURGERS YOUR MENU SAYS YOU DO! Especially when most people I've heard from have said that The Pharmacy's burgers aren't the best in town (with Burger Up being noted as having better ones) ... if you aren't the best, you better damn well know how to have good service and not further turn away potentially frequent customers.

Then again, it is run by hipsters ... and usually, that can mean awesomeness in the restaurant business. But this time, absolutely not. Pitiful. Outrageous. Disappointing. Ugh.

The expertise was impressive, and way above what I was paying.
Highly recommended.
I was impressed.

I have friends who work in the same field who were also impressed with the product and service received. 
Again, I would return as a customer, and would recommend to others

An OK place but as to the overall food grade benchmark, I found it not all different or of special noteworthiness from similar sit-in restaurants and/or garden variety Asian take-out places I've been to in SNJ. Rather expensive also, but remember you pay for "the show" as well as the food. The atmosphere was pleasant and the staff attentive and courteous. Kids will love watching the Chef preparing your food. Again however, The only dissapointment I noted was, while the food was good and prepared well, it really did not taste all than much different from our local Asian take-out place and cost much more. No coffee served. (a minus, sorry!) Soft drinks, liquor, beer and tea only.  Parking in their adjacent lot alongside. Note: Hey guys! If you go during weekday lunch, stop by Harbor Freight Tools a short walk in the Bldg located right behind them, great "toy store" for us grown up men)

This hidden gem is a block off Williams and absolutely worth it!  This bakery, grocery, sandwich shop is like a little slice of Cuba in Kenner.  Have you been looking for a Cuban sandwich?  Well look no further.  For about 8 dollars you can have a delicious fresh Cuban sandwich.  Still hungry?  Pick out one of the many fresh baked delicacies behind the glass, yes that includes churros.

Eating here as i write this. Super friendly workers. Great patio with music at perfect volume and lighting. The food is fantastic. One of the best burgers ive had and even the tater tots were seasoned perfect. Not your standard tots. We came on friday night at 8:00 and got seated immediately. Great place!!

I'm new to the area and saw this vegan spot. The location is great, the ambience is good and the place is clean. 

The food choices are great. I tried the veggie pizza and it instantly became one of my favorites. I will definitely be back for more.
Nice gelato place for dessert. I like the their pistachio and mascarpone flavors the best! It's just melting so quick! Although slightly too sweet to me, but creamy enough! Tiramisu cake is good too

We love LaSpadas. Their food is very reasonable and consistent. They also have the best chicken cutlet sandwiches! We love ordering from there or picking up. The service is great and everything is made fresh. I highly recommend it!

Modest, friendly, with great food.  This is an unpretentious restaurant located in a strip mall.  But the chef and staff clearly care about what they do.  We went on a Wednesday night and the place was packed.  Ordered tandoori chicken hit, it was the most flavorful and delicious that I've ever had.  Would go back again in a heart beat.
I used Uber last night for the first time. The service was great, fast, and reasonably priced. It's worth trying out. Use this code to receive a $10 credit with your first ride: TR64V

If you plan on having an all-you-can-eat crab leg feast, like they show in their website gallery pics, it is not what you will get. It's not all you can eat crab legs. The crab legs are charged extra by the pound, $5.99, on top of the buffet price.  I went to the manager with the online picture they advertise and she said, "oh no, we don't do that here". So why advertise with another restaurant's pics?  The rest of the buffet is what it is, an oriental buffet, which I'm not interested in.
Update: after coming here three more times after my first review, accepting that they charge for crab legs, I'll add more stars considering the rest of the food. The sushi is really good. There's a lot!! The hibachi is awesome too. The rest I haven't tried.
Great burgers shakes and fries.  Ice cream treats root beer floats.  A must stop on the way to/from the shore.  This place has been a local favorite for as long as I can remember.

Saturday afternoon lunch with 10 friends .... 

* called ahead and no issues with seating a big group by the window ... was a bit slow when we arrived but by the time we left the restaurant was hopping!

* Service ... our server, Raven, was great!  Friendly and positive she was our only server taking orders but we never seemed unforgotten or rushed.  When the food was served pretty much everything came out at the same time, which was impressive for a large table.  At the end of the meal we ended up with 5 or 6 checks, and again - service with a smile from Raven ... nice job!

* Food - everyone was happy ... I ordered and loved the huevos rancheros.  Good balance of ingredients and good taste multiple flavors coming through.   Wife had the chopped salad and was good value and spices for the price.

* Drinks - The drink selection was good as always ... I ordered a cider and at $7 for a smaller drink was surprised at the price, but in prime retail space of Germantown I guess that is normal.  They have a great tap beer selection.

All and all, Sedona is a nice place to bring family and friends - very large menu and drink selection which = happy diners!!

I traveled to the KOP area recently and found myself with time on my hands before I checked in to a nearby hotel. I conducted a Google search for nearby restaurants (did not have Yelp app installed on my iPhone, sadly), saw this gourmet pizza restaurant and thought I'd give it a try. 

I walked in at 11:15am thinking that was a good time to ensure "fresh out of tbe oven" experience.  I was the only patron there.

Both pizza slices ordered (one pepperoni, the other eggplant and mozzarella) were literally disgusting. The dough was so dense I was sure I was eating formerly frozen breadsticks. The red sauce(?) was completely flavorless and the mozzarella was incredibly rubbery and almost inedible. 

The one bright spot was the charming and handsome counter staff.

The best thing about this place is the "groovy" music streaming from Sirius satallite service.

After a few minutes I gave up and left; but only after I downloaded the iPhone Yelp app to write this review. 

Unless you want to be disappointed I'd stay away.

We came to St Louis on business and were fortunate enough to be within walking distance of the Arch. We had a blast! I hadn't been here since I was a child. The museum is very educational and interesting. Everything was clean and the employees were helpful and hospitable. Our tour guide prior to taking the tram up to the top was hilarious. It wasn't terribly busy so my daughter and I got to ride the tram up by ourselves which was nice since it is a small space. It can seat up to 5 people. We shared it with two adults on the way back down but it wasn't uncomfortable. We got some amazing photos and she had a blast. I highly recommend taking the time to go up to anyone in the area. It was educational and pretty darn amazing how the structure came to be. There is also a gift shop that has everything you can think of Arch related and a restaurant. Time very well spent at this iconic National Historic Landmark.

Ordered salmon salad, poke bowl and side miso soup. Simple. 

Salmon was deeeeelisssh, BUT the salad was overwhelmingly drenched in dressing and to my surprise was spicy. 

Poke bowl, decent with fresh ingredients including the fish BUT again spicy for no reason, no explanation, no advance notice.  

Mind you, I LOVE spicy food but when I want it. I still finished my meal because it was decent and I can handle spice but if you are sensitive to spice I would be careful here. 

Miso soup? Now they may call it miso soup but what it REALLY was was the soup from ramen. I'm Japanese and grew up eating real ramen. When the "miso soup" was brought out, I immediately recognized the ramen, not miso, scent.  Tasted it,  and sure enough or was ramen soup with tofu in it. My Japanese mother and I couldn't help but laugh at the surprise.

Too bad. The salmon and poki was truly fresh and or cooked well.  Other than that, I don't recommend their "miso soup" and mind the out of nowhere spice.

Overpriced Americanized Mexican food BUT great margaritas! The second half of their menu is just a list of different tequilas you can put in your drink. It's $8-$9 for a cup of margarita BUT it will definitely make you feel some type of way after one drink lol

The food was okay. Nothing special. The service was so-so. The guy had too many tables but he was nice to us.

Don't come here expecting special food but if you're looking for a strong margarita, you came to the right place.
My girlfriend is allergic to pineapple and they added it anyway after we put it in the notes and called useless dumbass restaurant

This place has one of the best pizzas in the area. Their buffalo chicken pizza is phenomenal. You can choose from four different flavors of sauces. Delivery is usually about 45 minutes, but it comes hot everytime. I would highly recommend this place. It's starting to become the only place I go to for pizza anymore.
The food is actually pretty good and the store could use a little recognition.

Yes! Yes! Yes! You can't go wrong! Great service! Great drinks! And there's food and a great view of the reservoir near by. Tina was excellent and the bar tender was attentive. Great customer service!!! I will be back!!! I made the track from San Diego, CA. It's that awesome!!!

NOLA's airport was a tiny bit disappointing. I mean, when you fly into Las Vegas you sort of fell like the plane is going to pull up to a large slot machine. (Maybe the prize is that your luggage will arrive on time?)

But Louis Armstrong felt a touch dated and a touch staid. A strange vibe in a city that is otherwise over-the-top. But it worked fine and we got through security and such without a hitch.

Have eaten here about three times. The food is great but the service is terrible. Visited again a few weeks ago because we love Italian food. The staff was different this time. We had better service ourselves but the table behind us had an elderly couple that was very angry because they had been waiting 45 minutes for their food. The restaurant was not that busy for that kind of wait. I don't understand why they cannot handle the service there. If you want to pleasant atmosphere and good food this is the place however be prepared with lots of patience.

WOW!! From the Fabulous greeting to the AHHHH....mazing Fiesta Fries-YASS GIRL- to the Monster Burrito!! We were muy impressed 
Perfect last minute find for us
I've been here for both brunch and dinner and while both meals were decent, it definitely was not worth the price. I would not go out of my way to go back.

We usually shop at Costco, so I have rarely been to a Sam's Club, but we came here with our friends as Costco is much further away.  

We came on a Saturday and was surprised how much quieter this place is compared to Costco.  Also, there were no sampling going on! I admit I am pampered by Costco, but definitely serious stars docked for not having samples.  The store just doesn't look as bright and clean as Costco. 

My friend likes to get the meat here, it's a good price and the quality is not bad.  However, the fruit platter we got here was awful.  The melon had such an off flavor we threw the whole tray away, the day after we bought it.  While they do sell some of the stuff Costco has, Costco definitely has more premium products.

Just waited 10 minutes for someone to serve me.  Both women were busy with soccer. One did say hello to me... Twice. One woman then went over to the other to give her instructions on what to do next.... something about Chuck apparently they're stocking and marketing is more important then actually sales. I left without my food, because I was actually on the road to San Francisco and needed to get going. And food sounded wonderful, but I guess I will never know, because the  service was atrocious

Some of the best hot sauce you can buy. I grew up eating their salsa ranchera on almost everything. Contrary to what yelp shows, the place is open. The phone numbers I have found online don't work, but the store was open today. Thanks Oscar.

High hope quickly fled.  It's housed in a beautiful southern mansion that founded in 1934.  This places is outdated and seems targeted for the 60+ crowd.  The service was inattentive and lacking quality.  All of the food wasn't seasoned properly.  The website says generous portions of whiskey and that is a lie.  Upon asking the waiter to recommend a wine to pair with the steak, coincidence the most expensive glass was brought out.  Not a fan and won't return, much better steakhouse options in town.
Great pub and grill atmosphere!  Fun and friendly service.  Love the tap take overs and the rotating craft beer selection.  A must try...  If you love craft beer this is the place to go!
Fabulous food and service!  Visited while on vacay and had a really enjoyable experience.

Not worth the wait.

My food wasn't seasoned, absolutely no salt in the grits, which anyone who eats grits knows is a sin. Once I doctored them, the grits were fine, seemed like the standard grits you can buy at the grocery store. Fried catfish, also not salted, looked flaky and moist but was just smoosh once I ate it. The fried shrimp were good, though not freshly cooked.

Cup of ettoufee was barely room temperature, though the flavor was OK. 

Husband had the baked ham dinner with green beans and red beans and rice, he was happy with everything. The green beans are very tomato-y, so if you're a no-tomato person, like me, you'll want to skip them.

The food preping area was very messy and the floor where the servers were standing was covered in dropped and walked on food. The management had that air of "showing the employees who is boss" and were calling out to them across the room to ask for basic things and pacing about the rooms. They also didn't allow tipping, which seems odd.

We also overheard a waiter arguing with another customer when he said his sandwich was cold. Not, was hot and now room temperature, but cold. The guy had to ask 2 or 3 more times and I think eventually got a replacement.

Decided to order carryout.  Spicy Thai Basil Chicken.  Was pretty flavorless.  Not what I expected for spicy Thai basil.  Barely any basil.  Sauce was thin. Spice was mild.  85% of the dish was onion and peppers.  Disappointing.  Other dishes have been better.

I order wings from this place through Uber eats at least 2/3 a week all flats , blue cheese and most time lemon pepper just order some right now with different sauces but I LOVE YOIR LEMON PEPPER ... I appreciate these wings and you're service

Visited for the first time this year for the Garden Glow event which was excellent.  Enjoyed the property and beautifully decorated scenes with great colors.  It was a warmer evening for December so expected it to be crowded and hard to get around on the path, however, they time it correctly every 15 minutes to let crowds enter making it very enjoyable and easy to get around.  Grab a hot chocolate once in and enjoy the beautiful scenery of lights.  Looking forward to returning for spring and summer now.

Can't beat great takeout!  We ordered our staples, veg lo mein, chix and broccoli, eggrolls and bbq spare ribs.  All excellent and tasty!  My new go to for take out!

The restaurrant has a smattering of 10 tables, it is bright and the service is quick and friendly.

We're visiting from Ohio and were driving back to Orlando from the beach. This mom and pop shop caught our eye and we stopped. Everything we ordered was really good. 

We had a chocolate vanilla swirl sundae with pb and hot fudge sauce and Oreo topping. The vanilla peanut butter milkshake was also good.
Wonderful place to visit with family or friends of all ages, specially during fall season

Great food selection and good, efficient process of entry through security. Points of improvement: Have more specific instructions on the website of what can and cannot be brought in. Empty water bottles are not allowed apparently, although the no open containers rule on the site seemed only to apply to alcohol.

During our cross country trip my wife and I found ourselves wandering around St. Charles looking for dog friendly place for dinner and ended up here. The wine list has a good selection and is reasonably priced and the food was quite lovely. We had a sampler place with homemade salami and some tasty cheeses. The caesar salad was a knockout and we had a lovely conversation with the owner. After subsisting on subpar midwestern fare for over a week The Vine was a much needed culinary respite.

Fantastic Tucson bakery, and a must-stop place when in town.  In the past I have purchased numerous bakery items and have never been disappointed.  Just wish this place was located closer to where I live.

Please don't even waist your time here. I have eaten here a handful of times with friends when I visit Santa Barbara and it has ALWAYS been very disappointing.  My friends go for the beer and the location but that is it. Every time I have been there the service is HORRIBLE and extremely slow. I was in back in May and our server ( never said her name)  seemed like she was on drugs. Literally our table was informing her to attend to people as she was just blankly staring at the wall or her phone. It was packed but she apparently didn't care. We asked her for water, ketchup ect and she would just go behind the counter and drink water and polish silverware.  I was in there and for the last time a few days ago. Our waitress once again was so slow and continued to get our order wrong. She was young with curly hair dark hair, Annie  I think it was. She was very rude and very unhelpful. The friend I was with had her before and couldn't believe she was still working there as she isn't a good fit for serving/ restaurant industry. 

Please spend you money else where. There are far better places to go in Santa Barbara than this place.

This review comes from very strict food critics. Me an my husband deciede to celebrate our anniversary this past valentines day at this restaurant. Let me start off the greeting from the hostess was very good, got seated right away. Let me just say that our server Jessica her smile was priceless. She kept checking on us about every 5-8 minutes. Sometimes she would come up to the table and others she would just peek around the corner to make sure we were ok. If you ever go there definitely ask for her. Were talking 6 star service, can't beat that. As far as the food, from the appetizer to the meal I could not find one thing wrong. We are ones that really look and make sure our food is prepared and cooked to perfection. Nothing more and nothing less. The other 5 star reviews on here are quite accurate. If for some reason you have a bad experience here, not only would it be a surprise but I am sure they will make it up to you if you let them know. Enjoy and a really big thumbs up to Jessica.

When I eat dinner at a restaurant, 90% is for the experience and 10% for the food.
After my experience on Friday night with Outback Steakhouse in Glen Mills, PA, I have no desire to ever visit an Outback, in any state.

I put in my request to their "Get Seated Faster" list, for a 6:30 seating. We arrived at 6:20 and waited in the lobby. Watched others arrive after us get seated. After 15 minutes in the lobby we saw high-top tables in the bar area. Asked if they were available and was told it was a seat yourself area. The four of us took a seat, and waited.

Three employees and a manager walked by us with no acknowledgement. After 5 minutes I set my cell phone on the table and started the stopwatch to see if we would get attention. Another 5 minutes goes by and my wife said something to the manager as he was passing by. He offered to buy us desert and to send someone right over.

Another 5 minutes goes by and a waitress is heading our way. Only, she goes to the table next to us that had just seated a couple minutes earlier.

Everything was wrong about the experience.
We left when it was apparent that we were not going to get served, and no objection from any employee or manager.
Went down the street to the better steak place, and had a great time.

By the way, our group of four are aged 52 to 60.
An age group that has some disposable income and is respectful to others.

Found paper in my coffee and when I told waiter instead of apologizing he said "take it out and put on the side"!
Very rude!!!!!

Hawx had a sales rep. in our neighborhood going around.  I told them I was already using another pest company but told them I was still having issues with lawn gnats.  They said they could get rid of them with no problem.  I told them if they did I would keep using them and if not I would go back to my original pest company.

Sales guy was nice.  Service tech was nice.  Unfortunately they were unable to do anything about the lawn gnats but refused to let me out of the one year agreement that I had to sign, even though the sales rep. said it wouldn't be a problem.

Customer service is garbage.  I spoke to two account managers, one of which said they would cancel upcoming appointments so I wouldn't be billed until they could contact the sales rep. about letting me out of my agreement.  My house was serviced 3 days later and I was billed.  Second account manager said there was nothing they could do and there was no one above her that I could talk to.

Also, my other pest company is better in every way.  They do more.  They cost less.  There customer service is amazing whether it be by phone or e-mail.  (Hawx doesn't even respond to e-mails.)

Stay away, there are better options that don't require contracts.

Two stars because I mean...they do come out.  That's something.  Never seen a dishonest pest company before.  Thanks for being my first Hawx.
Visited for breakfast, awesome meal!  Staff friendly and quick food portions large.  Lots of tv's for sports fans.

Smallcakes is the appropriate name for these huge cupcakes of deliciousness. Got a couple to try out, went back and got some for my friends. Should have gotten the half dozen and saved a buck fifty. Everything was moist, red velvet and yummy banana were the winners of the bunch. Open floor plan, clean, nice layout, easy to understand menu/options. I'm not a big sweets eater but I have my binges. At $3.50/a piece not what I would call cheap, but from what I read standard for the "gourmet" side of the industry. If your into these kind of sweets I think Smallcakes will scratch your itch.

The salad bar is good with many options and the menu has a good variety of steak and shrimp and chicken. The down side is the price. 3 adults, 2 getting salad bar with an entree and 1 salad bar, with only ice tea or soda, $72.00 plus a tip. Considering I can got to a seafood buffet at a casino as a local and pay $14 each, not a great value.
Wow cool little cigar bar with full bar, OK humidor selection, lounge in back, cool ambiance.

So, to say we got a little bit of everything g (pizza wise) is not an exaggeration! Traditional crust with pepperoni, thick crust with veggie and a paper thin crust with veggies and pesto. Absolutely delicious. 

We are in and salad was complimentary. The owner let me know this before ordering additional antipasta for the kids. Super sweet!

We had cannoli after - excessive but oh-so-delish! 

Only complaint... Not sure what wine I ordered as I failed to note that there were multiples of different quality. Whatever I had was not good. I kept drinking it because hey - wine! Would have been even better if the wine was on point.

"Having fun isn't hard... when you've got a library card!" Really, this review is best experienced with that Arthur library song playing faintly in the background. (here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lbXz3MXx2DU ) Make of that what you will.

The libraries I'm used to are either colossal historical landmarks (Rush Rhees, Rochester) or hulking monstrosities of modernity (Burton Barr Central, Phoenix). The Downtown Reno branch is neither of those things, actually verging on being too small -- even for the BLC. Yet somehow, in true 'Little Engine That Could' fashion, this little library manages to be surprisingly substantial.

The space is a beautiful 60's relic that's stood the test of time enough to really impress with its modern retro chic.
