The geometry of the walkways, stairs, and flanking multi-level stacks gives way to an open space basement atrium that looks and feels like an indoor park. The greenery winds all throughout the space, helping to offset the otherwise dusty, musty feel of the older books. +10 points for ambiance.

My first visit was last summer to satisfy a Stephen King binge, but I ended up walking out with a chunk of my to-read list in tow, Easton Ellis and Palahniuk included! Their growing collection of new releases and the killer ambiance have kept me coming back. On occasion, they also host event series in their tiny auditorium downstairs. Just a few weeks ago, I unwittingly walked into a concert featuring a famous New Orleans jazz band and some UNR musicians. Wonderful afternoon surprise!

As with any public library, the lack of prime funding sets up problems for upkeep. The uppermost level, originally the young adult fiction collection, is currently being renovated into a low-tech fablab. An interesting, if not puzzling, concept with slow progress that's left that space looking a little worse for wear. Also, the space around the bathrooms (unfortunately, a large chunk of the bottom floor... right next to the children's books) is always prone to smells that I can only tactfully describe as suspect. Still a fantastic place to bury yourself in a book. If reading's not quite your thing, the free wifi is fast enough to reliably stream Netflix. But you didn't hear that from me.

I just got delivery tonight from Baan. I ordered the Veggie Tofu Green curry and Mun Too (fried sweet potatoes served with sweet and sour peanut sauce).  The service was fantastic. I received my order very quickly. The food was good. I was expecting the green curry to be a little thicker, but it was still tasty.

I'm a personal chef so My husband and I appreciate great food and great service. Brick and mortar exceeded all expectations as every dish we had from appetizers through dessert was creative and amazing.The atmosphere was bustling and all associates were friendly and knowledgeable. Though it was our first time there Jason (one of the chef/owners) made us feel like we were old friends. This was truly one of the best restaurants we've ever eaten at. We are returning next week.  Chef Eileen Morris.

Definitely the best meal we had in Philly.  

RESERVATIONS: Make them 2 months in advance.  Unfortunately, we didn't hear about this until 1 month before our trip so we missed out on the window of opportunity and had to rely on walk ins.

WAIT: Came on a Saturday night at 5:15 pm and they said the bar and chef's table was already full AND the waitlist for both were already full so we would have to wait 2 hours before coming back JUST to put our name down! Ridiculous, we left.  We came back on a Sunday night at 4:30 pm to get in LINE to put our name down and there were already 3 groups ahead of us!  They let us in at 4:45 pm and we got to choose where to sit.  The bar is literally the bar stools, with a bartender as your "waiter" but it serves the whole menu.  The Chef's Table (which we chose) only seats 6 and it faces the kitchen so you can watch them cook, it also has an actual waiter but it serves the entire menu.  I would suggest the Chef's table if you have a choice.  By 5:00 pm there was literally 1 seat left at the bar so it was probably just wait list.

ATMOSPHERE: It's located in a weird business park area in what seems to be an office building so easily missed.  Look for the sign on the side of the building.  The inside is fairly small with a little alcove area, then the main dining area with tables, the bar and the chef's table.  It's dimly lit and a nice dinner location for a date night or a birthday.  It's not SUPER fancy but not a fast casual either.

FOOD: They have the tasting menu and if it wasn't 5pm and we were more hungry I would have opted for that ($45/person) but instead we just got 3 dishes.

HUMMUS - everyone gets the salad and hummus combo with the tasting menu but if you order a la carte there is no combo.  We got the Tahini hummus which comes with the laffa bread.  It was AMAZING.  We've had Dizengoff in Chelsea Market (NYC) which is the same hummus and it was equally as amazing.  Olive oil and a few spices on top and a huge piece of warm, soft, lavash bread made this one of the highlights.  One tip is they do give you refills on the bread, you just have to ask.

HALOUMI - this is a smaller plate and is basically square of cheese lightly fried on both sides and then strawberries on top.  Everyone on Yelp said it was amazing...it was definitely flavorful but not sure if I would order it again.  It wasn't a super standout dish.  If you don't like cheese or more sharp flavored cheeses you probably won't like this.

BRISKET - On their entree section they have different meats and since my husband doesn't eat lamb, we got this.  It came with 2 brisket meatballs and a little cast iron skillet of rice.  Definitely for 1 person but if you're not starving and if you're sharing a lot of little dishes, it's not bad for 2.  The meatballs were VERY flavorful and tasty.  It tasted like a typical middle eastern seasoned meat or kabob.  Very tender and fresh.  The rice was also very good.

BONUS - we got to try the Branzino as compliments of the chef and it was very good.  Soft and moist inside with a crispy skin on top of a dill sauce.  The dill sauce was a LITTLE salty but not overwhelming.  Overall, also very good if you prefer fish.

We also got a bonus dessert, which was like a fudge with sesame I think.  Also very very good.

Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant if you are coming to Philly!

Soulard Coffee Garden has the best variety and quality of food in the area. It has daily specials and seems to reach out to a variety of tastes. Not only is the coffee great, a great Breakfast Club Scrambler and good selection of offerings. The staff is playful and funny. Seems to work to create a hospitable atmosphere for customers and visitors. They offer rotating art shows by local aritsts. Good great little place.

When you advertise happy hour all day Sunday and it takes 45 minutes to get just the appetizer served while Everyone who sat AFTER YOU is already eating their ENTREE....you missed the mark!

And when your server asks you your wanton is ready, would you like it now or with your classic combo??? Sir, do you see that I am losing weight ....and how sunken my cheeks are getting waiting for a morsel of food???? Yes, you failed.

Sure the manger tried to appease my hangry attitude by offering to 'adjust' the bill was just not genuine enough.  The thing to say to a hungry woman is "let me get you some pretzel bread, a tomato, CRumbs off the table" ....something. Offsetting my bill is not pacifying my hunger! I come here to eat , not save money!!! I can afford your 50% half off appetizers 

If it wasn't for their crispy lip smacking good wanton taco , I wish I could say I would NEVER come back,,,,right now I'm just so hurt 

Applebee's, today you failed miserably, but because I am fair, I will eat your food again....in 6 months.
UGH

Recommend beefing up the staffs on Sundaya, specially if you are running a special!!!!

Really solid choice if you are looking for sushi! They have tons of seating so it's very unlikely that you will have to wait. Service was fast and friendly and the food was on point. 

Prices were pretty standard and would recommended it if you are in the mood for Japanese!

Great service by Tracy for our mid afternoon club sammy, that we split. It was good and they get a beautiful breeze running through the place!  The prices were good as well. I'll come back next time I visit fo sho. Thanks Tracy for making us feel so welcome!
I would give it 5 stars but they took away to bourbon street steak tenderloin medallions. It hurt my feelings
Very polite and a decent enough cleaning crew.  But nothing spectacular for the massive amount they charged me.  Easily double what my usual service charges for a slightly less impressive cleaning.

Cotton candy bacon. Say no more. OK maybe the bread. Oh yes the steak yes the steak. In fact just try all of it. Honestly have not had one thing there that I would not highly recommend. Will be going back and back again.

Filet mignon was good and at a decent price. Comes on a simmering iron platter. However, I was disappointed that a non-chain restaurant in Idaho--that  prides itself on an 'authentic' brand--seems to be using fries from a distributor, rather than potatoes cut in house.

I never even noticed this place when have driven by 100's of times. I will never skip it again! The waffle was delicious! The caramelized banana French toast.... to die for! Staff was super friendly and food was quickly delivered to our table.... on a Sunday busy morning! You will not be disappointed! Looks are deceiving from the outside.

I lived in New Orleans for a couple of years and believe it's the finest food city in the U.S., so when I find a restaurant has been around for over 25 years serving New Orleans style food to rave reviews, I have to check it out. Such was the case here, in Santa Barbara of all places. 

The Gumbo was authentic. The first taste almost brought tears to my eyes. The house special oyster appetizer was so good I could have had it for a main course. Instead, I had Crawfish Étouffée, and it was the real deal. But the star of the show was the Blackened Redfish...flown in fresh and perfectly cooked. 

The service was outstanding, and as we left, I met a fellow Tulane graduate waiting for a table. He was not going to be disappointed !

We love this place! It is so fun and our daughter is seven and she loves it too! It is always an awesome experience! The food is sooooo good and you always have plenty with some to take home! Love this place!

My fiancé and I stopped here for breakfast today and were not disappointed. We both got breakfast sandwiches and coffee. The sandwiches came with some sort of sauce on them. We were initially skeptical of the sauce so we ordered it on the side but ended up dipping our sandwiches in it because it was so good. The coffee was hot and they give you one free refill. The staff was super nice too. We're not from the area but if we are ever in town again we would definitely come back!

This restaurant did not disappoint. Yes there was a wait but used the dinetime app wasn't that long. As newly open restaurant and having  eaten there its understandable and worth it to wait. Man i was  impressed by the overall experience server was attentive food came quickly sat at the bar so i got to see first hand the amazing attention to detail on each bowl got the marinated fried chicken as starter and got the champon it was so good could have drank the bowl and the noodles are amazing much different than ramen i had elsewhere. Love the music and the vibe of the place will be back again ppl they just open so there be a wait use the dine in app. So glad to have them in the heights.

Went here while on vacation, and found a welcome contrast to the dry, prefabricated donuts that dominate San Francisco.

Got a glazed, a cream-filled chocolate thing, and a coffee for $3.  The donuts were fresh and kinda warm with just the right amount of chewiness and buttery-fried flavor.  Excellent.

hand down WORST PLACE I HAVE EVER BEEN TOO. I decided to drive 30 minutes from my house because I saw all these great reviews to sit there for two hours and then wait three weeks for contacts that I don't know when they came in because they didn't  tell me highly do not recommend. The service there is terrible they treat you with disrespect  and they don't know how to talk to their customers they're rude, they're ignorant, and they simply just do not  care. when i called asking for information they had NO IDEA WHAT TO DO i was put on hold for ten minuets just to find out if the contacts i ordered were ever even ordered. I wouldn't even send a rat to get there eyes checked out here... they cant even run a business. id give it -6 stars if i could.

I normally am very happy with the staff at BnB but my daughter and I have had 2 horrible experiences with Joey. He was extremely rude and condescending to my daughter when she had a question about her total. Unfortunately I wasn't there with her that day, but today I experienced his rudeness. He had trouble validating a coupon I had and basically acted like it was my fault. He was dismissive and did not want to help me until I asked to speak to a manager. It was a simple fix that it took the manager 5 seconds to fix but his tone and demeanor were as if I was an imposition. He has definitely soured my wanting to shop there.

Waited 30 minutes on a Saturday to order prom flowers for exactly a week later.  Three employees, but only one operating the store.  He was redoing an order in front of us, answering multiple phone calls.  I left thinking that I would just call, as that obviously gets more attention.  When I called on Tuesday, I was told that it was too late to order prom flowers, even after I explained that this was my second attempt to place an order.  I will use Gilbert's Flower Shop for my floral needs in the future.

I've been here many times, and this is the only place in the area I've found that consistently carries ginger beer, and they have a good craft beer selection, also. I got a great deal on glenfiddich 18 a little while back and the staff has always been super knowledgeable and friendly, which is not always the case in a liquor store. It's basically the only one I shop at now. It's pretty big, so they can have more of a selection than a lot of others.
Friendly atmosphere, fresh bagels, and great coffee make this neighborhood spot worth a visit.  It is the quickest way to get a good cup of coffee on the way to work.

If you find yourself in New Orleans, run (do not walk) to Salvo's. It was the best po'boy I have ever had, hands down. We went for lunch. Busy. So plan ahead. And you'll need a car. But again, SO worth it. The cole slaw was great, too. And the staff was all so friendly. I cannot say enough good things about this place.

Was in town visiting friends and they decided to take me axe throwing. This was a great experience, a lot of fun, and I highly recommend if you're feeling adventurous. Kierstyn was an awesome instructor and was patient with teaching the group and has an awesome sense of humor. Had a blast at this place!  I definitely recommend that you stop by and give this place a try!

Is there a way to leave 0 stars?

They straight up lied about mold in our HVAC. Called for a second opinion from a licensed gentleman. Came the next day, opened everything up to find nothing, even told me he wouldnt even recommend a cleaning as it was not warranted. This is a scam company that gives you a 50 dollar cleaning coupon (actually costs 135, not 50), and then tells you that mold has infested your home to later try to charge 700. 

Avoid at all costs.

Update: We called to complain and they picked up as a different name. Apparently they are in the process of getting "new management."

I am a huge fan of family owned diners, so we couldn't pass up breakfast at Peg's Glorified Ham N Eggs.

We were seated right away (table for two at around 9am) and really liked the authentic diner-feel of the place. Take some time to read the history of the place on the menu!

Had the Island Chicken Breast - and I still dream about it to this day. I'm Filipino, so I already love the eggs and rice combination- but the added teriyaki chicken breast and sliced cantaloupe made this breakfast feel like HOME. Filling, tasty, and very satisfying - I can't wait to recreate this meal for myself (maybe with a smaller chicken breast - the portion was VERY generous). 

Coffee was good, service prompt, atmosphere homey and welcoming. If we could we'd go back!

Stopped by here while visiting New Orleans. Was nervous at first seeing the ambience, but the pizza...was phenomenal! We ordered "The Godfather" and it was so good we stopped by the next day! 

Things to note:
Customer service is not that great. 
Only late night menu (pizzas only) is available after a certain point and they might tell you all you can order is a large. This happened to us the second night!
This place doesn't even deserve 1 star. They will rip you off and sell you a lemon. Don't ever go here. Extremely unprofessional and everyone there is nothing but a crook ESPECIALLY the owner

Over priced - don't go here ! People are nice but was just charged $100 for a synthetic oil change .  And had no choice cause they dumped my oil before they told me how much it was. Would have been cheaper for me to go to the dealer.
Loved our experience here, from the cheese plate to the delicious bread pudding! Service and atmosphere was amazing. Anxious to go back and sample more menu items!
The food is AMAZING, my family and I love coming here to eat. Can't go wrong with anything off the menu, it's all delicious.

My experience is that they have always been friendly.  
Usually crowded which makes it rough to get drinks in a timely fashion. 
I do find it crowded in the store, but again, that comes with the territory of being in a "coffee shop" setting.  It definitely is nice and comfy if that is the type of setting you want.  There is outdoor seating, but with FL you can only use that every so often - when it is not super hot, not raining, and not filled with some type of bug flying around!

Overall, this place is really good.  They make good coffee and other beverages and the staff is nice :)

I have never been so happy about spending $20 on lunch for myself.

Disclaimer: I am not a vegetarian nor am I vegan, I just like to watch what I eat and eat as clean as possible.

A crispy hipcity chicken ranch, buffalo'd, and an order of sweet potato fries with sriracha aioli. About four times the price as the less healthy, golden arched alternative but LET ME TELL YOU... I have never eaten such a deliciously sloppy sandwich in my life without feeling like complete garbage afterwards until now. The sandwich was huge. Fluffy bun, packed with toppings, and encompassing a giant chunk of chicken alternative that could fool even the most carnivorous meat eater.

My Wednesday was instantly made better by the vegan ranch and buffalo sauce that ran down my wrists as I sat in the corner of my office and stuffed my face with that deliciousness. I originally gave this place 4 stars but by the time I finished writing, I bumped it up to 5. My only complaint is the price but 1.) they're located in Rittenhouse and need to pay rent too and 2.) it's delicious. I'll drop 20s here every month. Make it rain.

Tap only review.

We walked in here only to use a functional bathroom before we drove to our hotel. After a show this is not the worst place to wait out the cluster f that is leaving the parkimg lots at Susquehanna Bank Center. I have literally waited almost two hours to leave the parking lots at Susquehanna....had this place been here then it would have been amazing. 

Nice addition to the area. My g/f had a Blue Moon I had a Double IPA from a Cleveland microbrewery and both were  $4.50 which felt like a amazing deal considering where we were. Bar had a familiar feel too like a place we stopped after a Steeler's game which added to it's appeal.
Love it. A must for visitors from out of town . Right across from Jefferson Station go out the Western end.

Found this place accidentally on a walk in Bywater during the summer...lucky, lucky me! They offer a variety of classes (hip-hop, belly dance, contemporary, etc.) taught by a variety of (super-nice and encouraging) instructors, and you will get both a workout AND a chance to learn some seriously dope-a$$ choreography. Don't expect a fancy, pure-barre-esque studio or anything; DO expect a quality hour of instruction for a fair price ($10/class).

Gloppy, yellow Italian dressing on a narrow plate that meant lettuce chunks fell off the side with each forkful. Pub pretzels that were dry and several rungs below those at the mall or a high school sporting event. Slow, slow service despite not being crowded. Probably won't return.

I've purchased two scooters from Ooty's, first from the original Ooty, Chris, and now from his son Ryan. Both are wonderful to work with because this has to be the best job ever! 

I also always take my bikes here (mostly on schedule) for quick and reliable service. They're fair and honest. My scooter is my main source of transportation so I need to keep it running and problem free. Ryan and his mechanic Ryan always get me what I need. 

I've also purchased scooter covers, riding helmets and other gear and accessories from the shop. 

Ooty's has lots of bike options for everyone's style and needs! Santa Barbara is the perfect town for scooter riding and I would recommend Ooty's to anyone.

Unbelievable, I took time off from work to specifically come to that dealership to have my Dodge serviced. All I need done was a simple oil change. And oil change, not an engine rebuild, not an inspection, not something that is super labor-intensive, just a simple oil change. The process of changing of vehicles oil takes approximately 30 minutes, I know because I was a mechanic.  Upon my arrival at this magnificent dealership, I was told to leave my vehicle overnight. That is flat out unacceptable. I was fully prepared to wait an hour or two, not being told to leave my vehicle overnight. This dealership in good conscience can tell customers that they're going to have to be without a vehicle for a entire 24 + hours, for procedure that takes approximately 30 minutes. Save your time folks if you're going to buy a vehicle here and have to use their service department.  I would suggest going down to Essington Ave., Northeast Philly for a Dodge dealership. Brought my vehicle there as a walk in without an appointment for an oil change and was done within an hour and a half tops.

I'm not surprised that Goodburger closed down. Especially with such competitors as 5 Guys or one of the many gastropubs that offer some very tasty burgers.

Goodburger was just A-OK by my standards. But I won't go crying over it anytime soon...

This used to be a hangout of mine when family would come into town.  The couches in the middle were something fun and different and were a conversation piece when we ran out of things to talk about.  However sadly my last visit was disappointed and I have taken a break from venturing back. The food is horribly inconsistent, I did see on indeed that they were looking for a new chef so maybe that had something to do with it.
Sunday a few weeks back we went for brunch and three quarters of the restaurant is reserved. I thought people just made reservations, we were seated with no notice and not a clue what was going on.  Did I mention the tables were reserved for a hockey banquet? Did I also mention they were using a microphone and video equipment, oops guess I forgot and so did the hostess to tell us that.  We would have happily left and gone somewhere else to be able to enjoy the company of family.
The service was horrible mostly due to being understaffed, the waitress was flushed from the time we sat down, she was apologizing while the high school kids just kept ordering food and sodas.  My parents who are a bit on the older side, were not a fan of the noise, the coffee served was cold and on the second attempt could have used another minuet in the microwave. The server insisted it was brewed fresh and was hot.  A mistake to argue with a customer and something off putting to me, the tip reflected though I'm sure it went over the server's head as to why.
The chicken pot pie was always my comfort food go to but as of late it seems a bit to runny in the middle.  Might need to add a bit of roux or reduce the cream more. The flat bread is another good option but based on the day will come out with an inconsistent amount of a bitter green known as arugula.  

Now for the good; They have an amazing Bison burger, the best in the area thus far. Great beer list and are not shy about running a happy hour special or a drink special for brunch which is refreshing and sometimes hard to find. It might be time for me to give this place another look, im getting hungry just thinking about Bison.
Very different king of pizza. Delicious light rectangular crust with not so much cheese in the  toppings. Not the kind to of pizza place for a whole pie. Slices about $4 - $5 each.

Went to a party last night ,around 11pm, with friends and the bouncer and security were incredibly rude and inappropriate towards my friend,she rsvp for the event and her name still wasn't on the list so she had to pay and while she was putting her things back in her bag to go in (mind you the bar is dark) they were barking at her to go in the club like she was inconveniencing their job. If they were on top of thing in the first place she wouldn't have had to go in her bag period.And they were rude to many other attendees.

This place is essential. They are super nice, parking is great, and the cuts are second to none. I grew up in Indy, but I live in Hawaii. I could be sitting on a surf board here, but thinking of Claus'.

I'm a fan of this little place, even though there are a couple of oddities.  The other day I walked in and about 6 people were standing around waiting for there food.  The guy at the counter was trying to talk to a picky cusomter and the only other employee was back in the kitchen looking at his phone and NOT COOKING.  After a few minutes I had a hard time believing I'd be able to convey my order and left.  

I've been here 6 or 7 previous times with no issue.  Also, the portions here are large, the quality fine.   I like the egg fu yung lunch special. It's all you can eat and with a sods under $10, so a good deal.   As I said in my first review, the Singapore noodles were really good the times I had them.  It was also a meal I couldn't finish.  I think they were $8.99.  

If you walk in and the lady's not working the counter, you might want to come back another time.

Great pizza and great service!  They pile our bacon and pepperoni on our pizza and even top it with oregeno (I'm pretty sure.  Whatever it is, it's delcious.) You can't beat their attention to detail on every pizza they create.

Five stars in the context of the many, many Fred Meyer stores I've shopped at since back in childhood days with my grandparents at "Freddy's" in Portland when this was an Oregon family owned chain to the current time when it is part of the Kroger empire.  This store is only two years old, well stocked, well organized and best of all super friendly and helpful staff.  The biggest surprise was how good is their organic produce section.  Use it or lose it though, that great produce section.  I'm hoping this review might encourage more shoppers to check it out.

PRODUCE
Better than most Fred Meyers for breadth of choice.  They even had organic escarole and curly endive...no kidding.  Even the non organic options were plentiful with local and regional options for fruit and vegetables.  As example, the cherries were from Idaho (and delicious) and the basil was from Gresham, Oregon and the blueberries from a Willamette Valley Oregon grower.  

TRIVIA disgression:  Particularly appropriate for the local Idaho cherries sold here to be so good since the original Fred Meyer (who like my hubby was a native of Brooklyn, NY) started out back in the day selling cherries on the street corners in Brooklyn before moving to Portland, OR to start his retail biz.  How about that fun fact? 

CHEESE
Speciality cheese section is smaller than in other Fred Meyer's.  There were good options from which to choose but if I could wave a magic wand, I'd expand this section. Still we found the burratta we wanted to go with the organic tomatoes and basil.  

OTHER GROCERIES
My hubby and I are not so much commercial brand grocery buyers so on that score we look more to places like Co-Ops or Whole Foods for the organic, smaller brand labels we prefer.  If I were Queen of Decision Making for the FM chain, I'd expand their organic and specialty brand labels in processed foods, like canned tomaotes and frozen veggies and jarred jams and nut butters and even clearning supplies.  Yet, they do carry some organic labels and some regional speciality brands.  For example, they had Moonstruck  (a Portland company) chocolate bars on a great sale. 

HOUSEHOLD ITEMS
For household items like drawer organizers or buckets or hooks or potting soil or...the list goes on...it is hard to beat the all under one roof convenience of Fred Meyer. 

FLORAL
A good selection of fresh flowers and of living plant arranged baskets at super reasonable prices.  Also, they had "candy bar" arrangements in glass vases.  Cute.

SERVICE
The people here make this a good experience.  From coming in the door where we were greeted by a very nice guy named Mike who was handing out food samples to the woman at the cheese counter to the employees who asked "Are you finding what you're looking for?" as we wanted the hardware aisles to check out.  Including the manager who was inspecting produce and to whom I offered  a "helpful hint" for leafy greens and who took my suggestion graciously.  Good service culture is nurtured top down and grows bottom up and both are working here.

THIS N THAT
1) PARKING:  Ample amount in the lot.

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  Level in and throughout with ample aisle space.

3) TWINKIE LIGHTS:  Love the big bramble tree in the entry with LED strings.  Twinkie lights in my mom's vernacular.  They appear elsewhere in the store too.  Nice touch!

Chez Leon moved from the hip Central West End scene to the more pretentious Clayton scene.  The restaurant is small and quaint, with a lovely area at the front of the restaurant to wine and dine yourself with comfy counches (that look illegal to sit on) and a great bar area.

I had lunch here with my Grandma and boy- does she LOVE to dine and sit and dine and sit and eat her food slowly...Lovely she says!

I ordered a house salad as my appetizer and the mussels as my main lunch dish.  My Grandma ordered the onion soup (and hoped that it was like what "real" french people made) and as her main entree she had the Nicoise salad.

The bread came out first, a little slow to start, but then once we got our appetizers seemed to pick up a little bit.  My house salad was great, lightly dressed and straight to the point.  The onion soup indeed was absolutely delicious.  The soup was in a small goblet filled to the brim (and more) with cheese.  The cheese on the outside was burnt to a small crisp, which is how the French do- My Grandma said. 

My mussels were to die for. They were lightly sauced with garlic, lemon butter and were amazing texturally. I was in heaven with my mussels.  My Grandma's salad was also great. The tuna was mized in with a light house vinagrette, potatoes, and some celery and chives I believe.

Everything was great! I had only wished I wasn't rushed for time, and I can't wait to see the dinner menu. YUM

Average airport. It's small and didn't have many dining options. The options weren't terribly attractive either. Gates were not that roomy. For my flight, folks spilled over to the adjacent ones just to get a place to sit. I couldn't find a place to plug in to recharge my devices. 

I transited through BNA easily, so I guess that's the most important part!

I was pretty hungry but after waiting at the window after five minutes of the three kitchen guys standing there talking to their bud and counting money, looking at me, I decided to give up. I may go back up there unless we can leave soon, but definitely won't tip their lack of service.

This place has been a let down every time I've been there.  I've given this place a few chances, after bad service, which I understand was due to lack of staffing.  I've worked in the restaurant business for a long time, I know the blame falls on management.  The last time, about a week ago, We waited over 2 hours for food, before going to a play at the Murat. Had to leave before getting food. They didn't charge us, but damn, get it together with staffing for events.  You're on Massachusetts ave.

heHad a wonderful experience at Campbell/Prince location this morning.  Made an appointment on-line and was taken right away.  Samantha, the provider, understood my somewhat obscure problem immediately, talked about alternative treatments but recommended one, and spent some time going over home care.  She was obviously very bright, very pleasant and helpful.  Front desk staff and nurse were fine too!  I was hesitant about going, but now am so glad I did!

I love coming here and strolling through the different vendors admiring the oddities, strange quirky little shops, and just people watching. It's better then bird watching! I always seem to find myself purchasing the Carnival soy candles. They last such a long time and smell heavenly. Also, I love the unique glass rainbow earrings that proudly state "Made in the Ghetto." They have a huge market for Asian art here and I love the selection of Buddhas. There is a lot of folk art, paintings, hand-blown glass figurines and many other unique and beautiful items. I would definitely recommend if you're in the area stopping by to check out The French Market.

Very beautiful bowling alley. We visited during a weekend night and it was surprisingly not crowded. We originally parked far away in a dark area where I did not feel safe walking around. We then realized they have a few spots right in front. They should have a sign saying this parking area is for their customers only to eliminate confusion. Some nice features at this bowling alley are they have a charging station for your phone which I took advantage of, parking on-site especially for the area, and two bars one downstairs and one upstairs. The beer selection was not anything special so I quickly switched over to cocktails which were decent tasting and not weak. 

Overall an ok bowling alley but not worth going over the bridge to visit. It was mostly convenient since we were already in philly.

Visiting family for the holidays in St. Pete.  I'm pretty rough on watches, and the bar that holds the wrist strap to the main watch face snapped.  I called up, was told they had the piece in stock and was quoted $8-10 for the repair.  I stopped by 30 min later, took all of 5 minutes, and paid $8.  (bring cash)

When I searched watch repair in yelp, I first got a bunch of big name jewelry stores which I try to avoid when it comes to actually repairing a watch (as opposed to buying a diamond ring).  

This is a real small shop, very friendly and knowledgeable owner with very fair pricing.  I don't know where much is in this city, but if anyone asks me where they can fix a watch, you can bet I'm sending them here.

I went for Wednesday Center City Sips happy hour.  $2 Blue Moon pints.  After about 5 of them, I had a great time.  A little bit too yuppy-ish crowd but it was fun.  I was memorized by the waterfall water faucet in the unisex bathroom.   Clean decor and decent music.  I would definitely go here for Center City Sips again.

I also ended up there for Saturday night.  This time it was way too crowded.  Music was so loud I couldn't even hear myself talk.  Also, it was way too dark.  I was shocked when the Blue Moon was $6.  I probably won't be going back for a weekend night.  I would give Saturday night 2 stars.

Ok. This 24 hr CVS is right behind my building so it is very convenient to buy stuff in an emergency. I do run out of milk, bread or some basic things every now and then. I use my CVS card and try to use coupons when I remember, otherwise things are pretty expensive here compared to other convenience stores.

This place is a great bang for your buck! Parking is usually full because Everytime I come there's a line out the door! I've only ever came for breakfast/brunch but they pack normal breakfast food full of flavor. One of my favs I've had from here is the shrimp and grits! Must try! Huge portions as well. 

Be careful of the breakfast cocktails they offer at super reasonable prices! I ordered a screwdriver once, (yes it was breakfast but it was my day off so whatever lol) and I assumed it would not be that strong because of how inexpensive it was. I think my waiter was extra happy and heavy handed that day because.... let's just say I was buzzin at 11am lol! 

Will continue to make the drive to come here with my hubby.

Is it a good sign when you look at your recent activity, see a place you checked in at, and go, "what the hell is THAT? Was I there?" I had to go look at the pictures to remind myself of my forgettable experience here. While running errands late one night, the misses and I found ourselves looking for something to nosh on. She, being on a healthy kick, wanted no parts of Wendys, and me, for the absolute life of me not understanding how Chic-Fil-A has become the freakin' Studio 54 of fast food spots, having a line, WRAPPING AROUND THE BUILDING, AT EVERY HOUR OF EVERY DAY, we wound up taking a drive over to.....Bobby Chez. After missing THEM closing by about 8 minutes, we FINALLY decided; wait; resigned ourselves to the fact that our only option was, B. Good. Full disclosure, I can't stand these artisanal, free range, gluten free, kumbaya, BURGER joints. Its a BURGER. Its SUPPOSED to be fattening and messy, and delicious. I don't need lettuce that was grown in a temperature controlled field and read poetry every Tuesday by an Amish grandmother. And sweet potato fries can go straight to hell. Having my tomatoes being given honorary degrees from Johns Hopkins is just a way to charge me $12 for a burger. Ugh. ANYWAY, we go in to order and I swear to god there was even talk of just HER getting something here and then going somewhere ELSE for ME to get something edible, but I decided to take one for the team. We order and then go sit down to wait for everything. They call "Matt," but apparently the ONLY other person in the store was also named Matt, so they pump faked me on even giving me food. When they called MY Matt, they had me come get half of my food, as they forgot my wifes sweet potato fries (ugh.) They promised to bring them out and we decide to eat in the mean time. I forgot what she got, and had to just now go check their menu online to remember what I got, which was the El Guapo, but the only thing I DO remember about the food was the the "natural ketchup" was naturally nasty. I'm even willing to concede that I am just accustomed to regular, sugar laden ketchup, but it was a jarring change that I didn't particularly care for. Whatever.

Long story short, I personally won't be back. If you like to pay a premium to have the flavor taken out of your comfort food, heres your place. It wasn't HORRIBLE, or even BAD, but it wasn't anything to write home about.

However, since I wrote that I had two negative social experiences there; one doctor, now gone, who scared the bejesus out of me telling me essentially that I would die of cancer if I didn't do what he said, and the other just another receptionist who announced loudly that they didn't take welfare insurance. Plus the one that's always hustling the jewelry she makes. 
I stopped going, but the chiropractors still there are still good. If you're near New Hope, you might try Dr Janet Wolf. Pleasant and good.

Interesting decor.
Nice delivery from staff.
Food rich in flavor, but no overwhelming.
A really good meal.

When I say it was the BEST shrimp I've had in Indiana, I am not exaggerating. It's a shame that the food was so amazing....... I ate too fast to get a picture to go with this review. Delicious grilled fish taco, quite flavorful. I personally did not care for the curried sweet potato version. My partner quite enjoyed the bbq pork and beef short rib options. I took a break from my diet to try this place out and  let me tell you; the slogan is right:

The staff is super kind as well which is a nice plus

Hmmmm so one more failure in an unfortunate location. Wish they would deliver something that stood out and was appetizing. Last time I went they didn't have 3 sushis or noodles for the kids.

Okay so i feel like i have been secretly stalking Jeni's ice cream for a few months. I ran across a powerful post that she had posted on instagram, and wandered into the wonderful world of Jeni's ice cream. So i was super excited when i found myself in Nashville and realized i could go! First off the location is in such a cute little area! Immediately we pull up and see a line, it was around 10:30 pm. Before you consider going to the Clearwater Aquarium, you should consider the following: 

1st - it is NOT an aquarium with a variety of sea life.  This is a hospital that only houses the injured sea life and mammals they are rehabilitating. 

2nd - they do not put on 'shows', but do have a routine schedule of presentations that coincide with their daily routines of handling and treating the animals.  Check the schedule on the back of the map before proceeding in order to get the most out of your visit.

3rd - as you arrive, bypass the parking lot and park LEGALLY on the street to avoid the parking fee.   

4th - In the busy season, even if you purchase your tickets online to pick up at will-call, you have to stand in line, and as it becomes later, the lines are much longer. I recommend arriving as early as possible - ideally just as they open the doors.

5th - book cruises a day, or days, in advance. There were no cruises available when we tried to book at the door.

6th - pick up a map at the Information Booth just past the entrance/food area.  The Information Booth is easy to miss, but a map is required to make sure you don't miss something. 

7th - consider going to the 3rd level first.  The 3rd level houses the large dolphin tank and you have a better chance of getting a good seat and seeing the early morning routine with Winter, Hope or Nicholas. (Remember, there are not any 'shows'). 

8th - ask questions! There weren't any formal presentations like in the movie, however, ask LOTS of questions. The volunteers and medical team were more than happy to provide lots of information, but we had to ask. 

9th - If you travel to the movie set - drive your own car.  The trolly from the aquarium was quick, but the line for the returning trolly was well over an hour long.   Another option would be to download the 'United Taxi' app and order a taxi for the return trip.  The cost was about 10 dollars plus tip, but a bargain compared to standing in line with tired, screaming toddlers.  However, DON'T place a phone call for a taxi, or you may end up in a tussle with others that ordered taxis over the phone.  The app provides confirmation and a taxi # to prove the taxi is yours.  We avoided an argument with a lady who had placed a call for a taxi by showing our confirmation.

I was VERY upset with my experience here.  My regular hair stylist was on an extended vacation, and I badly needed a cut, so I did my research, and Luna came out on top. As we talked though, I got more and more worried.  She talked about how she went to art school then dropped out and went to fashion school and dropped out, and finally settled on hair.  I thought, you know, that it takes some people a little longer to find their calling, but ok, whatever.  THEN she said that in college, she would cut her friend's hair all the time, and that they "would look great, but would be a technical disaster". I got the cut last year, September, and I'm STILL trying to grow out those 2-inchers.  I was obviously very upset, and will not be going back there again.  In my opinion, a stylist that can't even do a decent, simple, layered cut should not be a stylist!

It became VERY clear that they weren't doing anything but taking my $125 fee and pretending to remove my tattoo.  Do not go here!  This business is a scam.

My husband and I recently had an OK bike purchasing experience at Danzeisen & Quigley.

We actually ended up at D&Q after test riding a particular bike at another shop and running into availability issues when we went to order it. When we spoke with the manufacture, they suggested called D&Q since they knew our bike had been in stock there at one point.

Luckily they had the bike we were searching for and were able to put it on hold for us. Although we knew exactly what size and model we wanted, I did find it a lot odd that one of their employees was trying to talk me into a different size over the phone.

Within a few days of having the bike put on hold, we went into the store to purchase it and pick it up. My husband called earlier in the afternoon and let them know we'd be coming later that evening. The bike wasn't ready when we came in and still had to be checked that it was good to go. I didn't realize that they only did fittings by appointment and never on event pick up days, so we weren't able to get it fitted. That didn't matter because we were heading back to the first shop to handle fittings and accessories, but I would have been kind of ticked otherwise. 

All of the employees were encountered the day of the pickup super friendly and answered all of our questions not related to our new bike, such as info about a duathlon and how to sell a brand new bike. 

D&Q was out of our way and our overall experience wasn't standout, but bottom line was that we were able to find a bike that was on a hard-to-find list.

Thought I would give it another try, but again disappointed.   The advertised "hickory smoked slab bacon hand cut daily" was 3 cheap thin slices of breakfast buffet quality bacon.  The sweet potato tots were good.  Service was friendly enough but slow because they are understaffed.   

Overall it's a lively place but food is hit or miss.

Visited on Monday Feb. 11 at about 4:30pm.  The atmosphere was casual, comfortable, and right on the water which was great.  I really liked the food here as well.  I could only give this place 3 stars because our waiter was needlessly very rude.  I do not write anything negative, ever unless extremely deserving.  This waiter.....wow.   About their house wine selection (of 3 wines), I asked which one was the least acidic tasting so that I could choose one.  He did not know.  I requested he might ask the bartender.   His response was "I will ask but we are not wine specialists here."   Really?   Later on with dinner which was quesadillas, I requested sour cream, he said "we are really busy here but I will get it."  Amazing.   Tall boy, brown short hair, wearing sun glasses.  He needs to get out of the customer service business because his attitude is simply unnecessary and very bad for business.

I used to go to Headlines in High School and College but really wouldnt go back. They do not take credit cards which is so annoying I always had to bring a check to pay. They often gossip about clients and employees which is typical of a salon but this was a little too far. The prices varied so it always seemed to be a surprise thus the reason for a check. I wouldnt recommend them to a friend.

If you are in the neighborhood this is a great place to grab whatever you need to keep you fortified for a few days. Of special note (mostly to me), whoever makes the call on wine selection is a golden god because everything I have tried there is solid!

We went here with a group of about 6 people and the service was extremely slow. I ordered an omelet and after waiting about 25 minutes I inquired about the status and they told me they are working on it. I asked about how much longer because at this point our entire group had their entree with the exception of me. The waitress stated she was unsure how much longer to take and ask if I wanted to make it for a to go meal. Being as though almost everyone was done their meal and I didn't want to continue to wait so I informed them they can cancel the order. I don't plan on returning to this establishment.

I have visited Philadelphia four times and the last was the first time I entered the walls of Eastern State Penitentiary. I had previously heard from friends who had visited about Steve Buscemi's guest narration on the self-guided tour, but would never imagine it would be as awesome as it is. 

ESP is America's oldest prison. It was fascinating to walk the original halls and peer into history. I had no idea that the facility was used as late as 1971! Al Capone even had a cell there. 

This would definitely be a must for history buffs and those in search of quirky landmarks to visit in the city of brotherly love. The self guided tour leads you through several areas of the penitentiary but then has another 20+ points of interest that you can key in while you wander the grounds. There are periodic tours of the green house and other areas that you might make note while visiting.

There are also art exhibits incorporated into the tour. There were small vignettes from one artist to an installation called "Ghost Cats" representing the feral cats that inhabited the grounds while they were abandoned for several years. It's astounding that there were proposals to  have the area leveled and for it to be the site for condos or a shopping mall. It's also really awesome that they left parts of the prison "in ruins" as well as restored several areas so the touring get the best of both histories. 

I have heard raving things about the Haunted House events they do in the fall. If I find myself in Philly in Autumn, I would so be there. 

Note: Student rates are available, but even without, it's more than affordable, and well worth it.

Great place, we were just walking by and decided to try it out, ordered vegi burger and linguini and both were great 

Desert is amazing!! Really worth to try it

Great place, friendly workers .. would highly recommend it
This is a great late night place to get a greasy cheeseburger and chicken nuggets. The service was great and the prices are great. They are open 24 hours too.

My only disappointment is that I didn't find this place sooner.  I regularly pull my hair out trying to find cards appropriate for my neurotic friends and family.  This has become my one stop shop.  While the selection is vast, it is also unique.  I also bought a note pad that says "bull shit" on the front, something that some how makes me feel better while jotting notes at work.  The staff is friendly and store is welcoming, but to be honest I'd still go there even if they were mean.
Cattltown steak house was everything and more than I had ever expected. I recommend Cattltown for anyone who wants to have a fun and memorable night out with the kids or that someone special.

Just came here with the family. The food was delicious.  I loved my biscuits and gravy and the fam loved the burgers and fries. For the adventurous of us, had the shrimp boat, crab biscuits and kitchen sink which were great. Great service too!

This is an easy 5 stars. If you have ever visited or even driven through Santa Barbara and not stopped at Brophy's...you need to go back.

Living in SB many years, this place was always a favorite. Whether filled with tourists or locals, sunshine or fog- Brophy's is always such a wonderful experience. It's not a place to eat and move on, it's a place to gather, enjoy and soak in Santa Barbara. 

Mussels, clam chowder, linguine with clams...I could go on and on. Brophy's is a staple of the area for good reason. Wish I was there now.

We stopped in Philly on the way to DC last may.  We only came there for steaks, the lights, pictures and police patches tipped the scales in the favor of Geno's over Pat's. 
I got "1 wit" that comes smothered in cheese whiz, then I had grilled onions and no mushrooms.  Fries and a drink.

One of the tastiest sandwiches I've ever tasted.  A couple guys went over to Pat's but I couldn't make the trip after the sandwich and fries.

I'd go again but I wouldn't go out of my way to get there from Chicago.

This was a great philly cheese steak spot. I prefer it over Pat's and  Geno's. I got the ribeye steak with mild provolone (taste like sharp) onions and mushrooms. I was in heaven. the onion rings were amazing as well and a nice size. my boyfriend got the original style with  the cheese whiz and just onions and he loved it as well. We both plan to go back. I might even try it with the broccoli rade next time.

The hotel is good for the value. I thought the rooms were a good size, everything was clean. It is a little outdated but nothing too bad. I wouldn't call this a "resort" though, it only had 2 on site dining options and one was basically always closed. The casual eatery near the pool was never opened the entire time I was there and the bar closed early everyday. The walk to the beach is a little far but they have golf carts that take you to and from.

PLEASE SHUT THIS PLACE DOWN!!!  It doesn't deserve a star or anything... I understand that u get what u pay for at $89 a night but I shouldn't and I won't pay to stay at this place.  It was bug infested, unkept, smells like mold, and the check in staff is EXTREMELY RUDE... We literally waited hours and hours to check in to this hotel that clearly has code violations.  The police were called and they said they come to this place for problems on a regular basis... We had enough of this place after seeing all of mess in lobby, we left...  I would have filed a lawsuit if I slept there and a bug crawled on me.  I can't believe Indianapolis or the mayor is not doing anything about it... This looks really bad for your city.... The city should be ashamed... We won't be back ever!!!

Not sure I would call this place a antique store. More of a yard sale outside and I was looking for Fred G. Sanford on the inside. And the G stands for Got to be kidding me. Half and half flea market stuff and antique stuff, as in wore out household stuff. Not sorry I went but wouldn't go back. Not a fan.
Great happy hour, good food. Service is inconsistent but a very good value.

I had visited St. Petes while at a work conference and stayed at the Vinoy. Frescos is in walking distance so had went with some work mates and enjoyed a wonderful dinner and $5 margaritas as the drink of the day. I had ordered the bacon wrapped scallops and the asparagus. It was wonderful!! The scallops were PERFECTLY cooked. No complaints!!

Disappointed. New is not always better. The restaurant has been redesigned to add a large bar downstairs and also incorporate a large amount of neon. This changed the vibe from French Quarter jewel to Vegas cheap diner. The menu has also been changed and now has an Asian influence to most dishes. Some of the old favorites are still available but only on one day a week (BBQ shrimp, fried chicken, etc). What we are left with is a menu where the food is just ok in a city full to the brim with world class cuisine. Do yourself a favor and try one of the other great restaurants (Emeril's maybe?) until they figure out this mistake and fix it.
This place is worth the wait!! From the Mimosa to the Bloody Mary, Irish drink, delicious! The food, the service were also great!!

I have to give a quick review update for this recent order.  The pizza I got was delicious.  I ordered the Chicken Parmesan pizza and it was very good.  The amount of chicken could have been a little bit more, but the overall taste was a nice blend of chicken parm and pizza.  Also, shout out to the delivery dude who proudly proclaimed, "I got the yum yums!" when I answered the door.  And, no, I am not 8 years old.
Why close at 12am on a Friday night ? I can drive to Miami from Tampa and still make it on time for a carry out/pick up or delivery .

Very impressed with their parts department. Many items are in stock and readily available. Parts dept staff is very friendly and knowledgeble. Haven't tried them yet for service, but will post a review when its time.

First time here today. Wonderful staff, courteous and knowledgeable. Reasonable prices and great selection. Would definitely recommend it and will be back to by soccer equipment in the future (bought for children).

I have tried to many years to stay far far away from Restoration Hardware furniture. I hate the lack of color, I hate the huge mailers, I hate that everything is made in Vietnam or some far east country. And here I find myself, having placed an order with them for a sink/vanity that I just could not find replicated anywhere else. In hindsight, I should have gone custom with a machinist.

$8,000- that's how much I spent on a vanity and piece of furniture on one order. The vanity gets a 6 month lead time. Ok, I'll buy the matching P-trap and supply lines later, no big deal. Surprise surpise, the vanity ships 5 months early (your estimations are off that much?!) and now I need those lines and P-trap. No worries, it will only cost you $100 to ship those two items after you just spent thousands including a ton on shipping. Can you ship to the local store? NOPE. They "do not have room to receive items for customers to pick up". Right.

Not to mention their taxing practices. I live in Soulard where there is a 3 block box with a special sales tax (for "tourists" in bars). Fine, whatever. Well, since my address is in that box, RH charges me that ridiculous sales tax rate, which, at $8k is a TON. It's like 12%. Not a single other store or online outlet charges me that because of my address.

How can Amazon and 500 other hardware companies ship this small stuff for free yet RH needs to charge $100 to ship it, especially when it's because their time estimations were off by four fold? It REALLY costs you $100 to ship those pieces of hardware? Get over yourselves. I'm back to my "never RH ever" policy and plan to stick to it. I dipped my feet and I'm done.

The food was decent. My boyfriend got a burger and we split fries. They don't have fountain drinks so we got a cold bottle. The two females who were waiting on customers on Sunday, May 24, 2021 were not wearing masks. One had a long, blonde ponytail and the other had dark hair in a bun. The only male employee that I saw was wearing a mask the whole time we were there. He was very nice too. They don't require customers to wear masks when they come in, although most who walked in had them on. Also, based on the recent 70 health rating (you can read it on this site), they were cited for rodent droppings in the kitchen. For that reason and the lack of mask wearing by employees, it's one and done for me.

My first time there but probably not my last the one because there was snow on the parking lot my friends only reason I gave it 4 stars was my friend had his car serviced at the car dealer next store we walked over we had to walk in the road to get in the side walk was not clear the food was great though.

Biggies is a South City neighborhood bar that offers the same charm as other local classics.  The interior is plastered with pictures of local sports heros, regular patrons, and kids teams in which the sponsor.  It's easy to see why so many frequent this place regularly.  

We started with the mustard shrimp, which were really shrimp in buffalo sauce.  They were good though.  For entree I had the Chicken Oscar special.  This was a fried chicken patty topped with a crabmeat and asparagus.  It was just ok.  The chicken was overdone, and the topping wasn't all that great.  The salad that it came with was good.  And my friend got homemade provel sticks which in my opinion were much better than mozzarela sticks.
New favorite. Best fried chicken in Indy.  My wife and split the 1/2 chicken and ordered the cornbread. Great outside seating area.

I love everything about this establishment, great service, great food and great atmosphere and even better drinksss!!!  It's a unique concept with the pizza shop in the back of the restaurant. Brunch is very entertaining and Affordable, Bello is a must go in Tampa.

Mexican chef in the back cooking. Went there for pho and let me tell you, their broth is so nasty, it's the Mexican chef who puts some kind of mexican ingredients in the broth. I took three bite and left. This place is not Vietnamese authentic food, but a twist with Mexican ingredients. If you want real authentic asian food, make sure their ain't no Mexican making your food. I WILL NEVER GO BACK TO THIS PLACE!!

This pub is located right behind Northeast Shopping Center in another smaller strip mall. Their address is on Roosevelt Blvd, but the strip mall where they are located is behind Burlington Coat Factory. It is a hole in the wall gem. The bartender, who is also our server was very friendly and knowledgeable. She recommended dishes for us to try which were all very good. The wing special of the day is coated in a strawberry infused sauce of which arrived to our table piping hot and delicious. It was finger licking good. The Harp Battered Fish and Chips were satisfying, delicious and not greasy at all. They made the tartar sauce in house that came with the meal of which was really tasty and complemented the fish very well. the chips that came with the meal was crispy, flavored with a little bit of "secret" spice and they just melt in your mouth (no greasy fingers here). The Grilled Chicken Breast Sandwich was juicy and cooked just right. To complete our meal, the Killkenny Chocolate Cake with Ice Cream is the icing on our meal. I regretted having to share this dessert, because that is how delicious it is. Our server refilled our drinks several times, and stopped by to check on us many times too. There is ample parking spaces available since they are located in a strip mall, the bathroom is handicap accessible. And one more thing...they offer FREE WIFI  connection. I most definitely will return here again to try the rest of the menu.
terrible cut and color.....paid a fortune and they overbooked clients, would never recommend !

I went to Lotus Gardens in Indianapolis back in the 60's before I moved away.  I'm back, and this week someone told me they were located in greenwood and had a buffet.  Looked it up on internet and showed dinner was 4PM to 8PM.  Three of us decided to try the buffet.  We arrived about 5PM.  The buffet was not ready.  Finally at 5:30 they announced it was ready.  The   crab rangoon and egg rolls were very good.  The crab legs were the best part of the meal.  As for the rest: fried rice was white rice with soy sauce for coloring, the spicy BBQ pork was not spicy or BBQ flavored just cooked pork, the generals chicken flavor was good but fried too long and hard, the deserts were snack packs of vanilla pudding and fruit cocktail. The salad bar was lettuce and two bottles of dressing.  Had the food been good the price would be very reasonable.  There are too many better chinese buffets around,  we will not be back.
Chicken fried rice was tasteless , spicy salmon roll and spicy tuna roll both were grinded up. The shrimp sumai had imitation shrimp. I'll pass on this

The service department took their time to check a problem I have been having with the transmission shifter on my 2013 Sonic. While it was not under powertrain warranty, the service advisor went out of his way to see what he could do to reduce the bill.  In the end, I drove out of the dealer with a new transmission shifter.

The amenities offered by Maher Chevrolet's Service Department including loaner cars plus the extra helpful service staff is why I keep coming back when my 2013 Sonic needs any service.  If and when the day comes to buy a new car, it will more than likely be another Chevy Sonic and I will definitely buy my next Sonic from Maher Chevrolet.

It just couldn't get any better!

I stopped by here looking for a specific cable type.  I wanted to convert an HDMI signal to a component video signal.  I've seen cables that perform this function on the internet.

When I walked in the store 2 salespeople were helping two other people and one guy was just sitting there.  I wasn't greeted and I decided to look around on my own for what I wanted.  I happened to notice a third salesperson after a bit and asked for some assistance.  He wasn't particularly eager to provide it, but didn't resist.

The guy helped me look in the section that I'd already perused and said he didn't think they had the item for which I was looking.  He then asked the no longer busy guy behind the counter and he said they don't have the cable I sought, partly because you don't normally convert between the signal types I sought.

I asked if a converter box was necessary to do what I wanted and they said yes.  They also said they didn't have one.  They didn't offer to order one nor did they try to be helpful and suggest where I might find one.

I just opted to leave as it was pretty clear they had no strong desire to be the least bit helpful.

I suggest researching the internet and buying from there rather than this place.  One of the lamest (and there have been plenty of lame) customer service experiences here in Reno.
Fantastic pulled pork and chicken...good sized portions and sugar beverage selection. Potato salad!

Stopped by today since it's the first time I have seen any life at the place in 6 weeks to ask how delivery or pickup worked only to have an armed guard start running at me telling me to get back in my vehicle over and over. I wasn't close to the store, it was a parking lot outdoors. I have been a long time customer and thats over. I simply stopped to ask a question, again no where near the damn door. Nice way to treat people.

As one friend aptly described this place, it's like Chuckie Cheese for grownups. Well, for 20-somethings at least.

Ping pong, shuffleboard, TWO different kinds of air hockey, pool tables for days, darts, karaoke, beer pong, those punching bag games, etc. etc. It's a veritable explosion of activity, and all game rentals are just $2/hr on Monday nights. 

It's a great place for friends looking for something to do other than sitting around a bar, always a fun birthday destination, and almost always a late night. 

Bar prices are reasonable, they have a decent beer selection, and even some food options. Done deal.

I don't come here as often as I'd like simply because of the location. This place is located on a very busy intersection, and the parking lot sucks! Very limited spots and not to mention a tight squeeze. 

If you don't know the area then I recommend parking on the street but that's only if you're lucky to find a spot. Weekends are usually the best to get parking. 

Aside from that this place is a must try if you're craving authentic Mexican food! They offer burritos, tacos, sopes, alambres, etc...

My fave has to be the chicken Tinga sopes which is shredded marinated chicken and the gorditas! The sope and gorditas are both handmade with masa. What I love about them is the thickness is made just right and not too much. I can actually finish them without being overly stuffed. 

I've also had the chicken taquitos plate which was a good deal under $10! Very yummy and satisfying. 

The carne asada burrito was good but the amount of meat was lacking yet again! Another restaurant that skimps on the main feature. 

Overall this place is legit and I look forward to trying more items on the menu.

The Reef is in a blink and you'll miss it strip mall off of Naamans Road and I only point this out because upon entering this unassuming establishment I found a packed house.

The place is huge. There are two sides divided by a huge bar. I did not realize until later why one side was more heavily packed than the other. They have a stage area for live music. My companion secured a table on the less crowded side from which we could not see a thing but we could hear just fine. Getting to the ladies room was a challenge during the set however because of course it's on the crowded side.

The wings did not disappoint. You can order by the 1/2 dozen better to try all the sauces. We had regular Buffalo, Habenero and BBQ. By the third Habenero I had to give up on them, my mouth was a flame. 

My friend had to actually get up from the table to get the bartender to make me a drink. No one checked on us until I got one servers attention and she took care of us the rest of the night. Still had a good time and would definitely go again.
Amazing breakfast spot. Not too l'IUT still able to hear conversations with others.food is very good and comes pretty fast. Love love Keke's.

If you're looking to adopt a dog or cat, please visit this wonderful shelter first. Tucson is lucky to have a no-kill shelter and the volunteers who work with the animals and take care of them are the most generous, hard-working, and kind-hearted folks you'll ever meet anywhere.
They are always looking for ways to raise money to care for the animals, so please consider this non-profit when you are ready to make a donation to a most worthy cause.
My two favorite critters there are Max the cat and Leo the Aussie...both senior citizens who would love to meet you and show you around!

Nasty bunch of people working here, save the headache and order elsewhere.

They could care less if you order from them, I did them a favor and did business elsewhere.

So I've decided to learn to snowboard and I've found myself at Bobo's twice in the last week.  Both times they were my last stop after checking out some other local options.
The first time I went in to get snowboard boots and I was lucky enough to have Tosha help me.  She was AMAZING! Answered all of my questions with the utmost of patience and let me try on a ton of boots until I had my Cinderella moment.  
The next trip was after a day of checking out Snowboard prices.  I started at Arbor up in Truckee (those people are legit!) and once again found myself at Bobo's.  I checked out the new boards but I have a problem paying $300-500 for something I am going to learn on. So we hit up the rack with last year's boards and do you know what the awesome sales chick found? An Arbor board from last season! So I got the board I wanted at the price I wanted to pay.  Then, of course, I had to get bindings and I went with Ride based on her recommendation.   She was cool enough to put the bindings on for me (with my boots in them) and wax the board so I am ready to go.  
The customer service in Bobo's is seriously top notch.  They listened to all of my questions, gave thoughtful answers and basically made the buying process a ton of fun.  THANK YOU!

Sizeable. Each airline seems to have their own wing. During the time of COVID, August 2020 lines were all short. Masks are required and 6 feet social distancing is recommended. Nothing special to write home about.
We love Bru Burger. The food is amazing every single time and the service is great. They need to put one in Carmel!

Ordered a chicken parm pizza and were charged $27 yes you read it correctly $27!! Super disappointed that another small business could rip people off this bad!

We have been here numerous times and had a white pizza for $17. They added chicken to a cheese pie and that equals $27! I can't justify the cost and how we were treated when we called in to ask a few questions.

There's pizza and salads --- and then there's Falora. This place is awesome. I'm not going to go into what we had, because we've eaten there 3 times in the last 2 months. Each time the food is just amazingly good. It's really not pizza. It's a step above. And the salads are not really like a salad you'd get at, say, some other restaurant. They are a step above as well. For those of you who can appreciate this comparison, Falora is to pizza what Jeff Beck is to guitarists. An original that leaves one in awe. I feel strongly about writing reviews about restaurants as eating is one of my great pleasures in life. When I eat at a restaurant that has had good reviews and come out disappointed, I'm not a happy camper. Falora makes me happy. I not only feel lucky to have found this place, I feel lucky that I live so close by. Definitely worth a visit .... or three ... or four... Oh ... and did I mention that the service is great as are the vinyl records they play.

I will no longer take my dog to this location. Last Friday I was rescheduled a grooming appointment to an earlier time. I was under the assumption if u tell me come in , there is an opening. Petsmart has never had a problem before telling me there is no opening in the book. Anyway I took my dog in time for his appointment and was told he would be ready in four hours. I returned after four hours and my dog didn't even get a bath. They had him locked in a cage for four hours. I was beyond pissed. The manager said they tried to do me a favor by seeing him earlier well no one said that; Also the groomer that initially took him when I arrived was working on another dog?? He then gave me the dumbest look and said my dog is a quick groom it will take him about 45 mins well why didn't u do that 3 hours and 15 mins ago when I brought him in at the time u told me too.  I will  now be using a private groomer. Very dissapointed with the service I did not receive at the Roosevelt Blvd location and the stupid response from Jim or Tim the groomer.

Very good pizza. Was recommended to me by neighbors as being very delicious. Did not recognize the name until I showed up for a pick-up order. I've gone to the location in Ybor City and its just as good. I wouldn't dine-in since it's not the best looking place to sit down and chow down. But, nonetheless the pizza is good.
Very good. Lobster meat mixed with some mayo on a toasted hotdog bun. The Mainer owner was friendly. Authentic and very tasty.

This is probably my favorite ramen restaurant in Saint Louis area, I have tried other ramen places here but Ramen Tei is the number one for me. The Shoyu Ramen with Pork belly is the go to ramen here. They also have the best chicken wings here and the Gyoza is amazing too the sauce that they use is perfect. 5 starts for Ramen Tei this is one of my Favorite restaurants. IG: Pigzout
Lots of energy, very friendly coaches and most importantly RESULTS for a happier and healthier you. Stop postponing and COME IN!

One of the best cheese steaks around. I usually go with the 'Jacked Up' steak, which includes loads of extra fillings, but the standard cheese steaks are just as good.  I sometimes get the hot chicken wings & broccoli bites too, both of which are great appetizers.  Not tried any of their hoagies or other sandwiches yet, maybe next time.

Even though I live about 0.5 miles away, I've not actually visited Cosmi's yet.  I always get delivery...kind of lazy I know. They even delivered after the terrible snow storms we had last winter, when most South Philly roads (especially mine) were a semi-melted lumpy mess.  I don't think the delivery guy managed to get down my street, but parked nearby and walked to our house.

This is a cool spot for coffee and breakfast breads. Better get here early if you want first dibs. Seems like there's a lot of people who like to come by. 
They have nitro cold brew. And their expresso is the real deal. Don't miss the chance to try the pastry.

I've been to this place quite a few times and always have a good experience. Good atmosphere, great food! I enjoy every menu item I've tried -- although I especially recommend the fish & chips or the tortellini.
Definitely give this place a try if you're in the Cool Springs area!!
I truly think this is the best chicken in Stl . The spicy is amazing and the chicken is top notch! Get to Gus's u will not be disappointed!

Wow, I am impressed. Was looking for a waxing salon here in Edmonton, and decided on Kaya Kama after reading the good reviews. Well, they were justified. I didn't know what to expect when I pulled up to the tiny storefront in a strip mall, but once I entered, it was like another world...and a lovely one, at that! It smelled so good!!! Hemali was my technician, and she did a great job...very thorough and professional. For a sometimes painful procedure, she made it less so. Can't wait to try some of their other services, especially the massages and hammam!

This was my first time at a Turnip Truck location. The only reason I'm giving this review 3 stars is because the food and juice weren't bad. But this place definitely needs some TLC.  I bought a fresh squeezed juice and a cold chicken salad. It took unreasonably long to get the juice. There was one guy working and I saw people who ordered after me get their drinks before me. Maybe there should be two people working in that station? He looked tired and overwhelmed with the business coming through. Also, the counters to the fresh salad bars had dried food stuck to them which were attracting tons of flies. Looked like it hadn't been wiped down in awhile. The market just looked a little dirty. Super bummed out considering I was really excited to come here. Just a bad first impression.

Dr. Fabbiano is the best, I've never been to a more well run and beautiful chiropractic office. I have pretty bad neck problems which result in me not even being able to turn my neck at times. Dr. Fabbiano has completely changed my life and would recommend him over and over again. Thank you Valrico Spine and Rehab Center!
Dr Fry has been my family's dentist for years I'm really happy with him and his staff I've never had any complaints.

Great spot. There was lots of outdoor seating and they had heaters at each table. We didn't need them on this day but it's nice to know I can go back in October and enjoy a night without getting too cold. FIVE STAR PIZZA!!! So so good. Beer is also really good, I recommend their 2nd St Fest brew. Four stars because the service was slow. It was a Saturday night and I wasn't in a rush or anything but I like to order my next beer before the one I'm drinking is empty and I never got that chance. I always sat there for 10/15 min with an empty beer. Bothersome but absolutely wont stop me from going back or recommending.

It has been a while since I have gotten good service in the Brandon area. Our server was Tara and she did an amazing job with drink recommendations and the overall presentation. 

My outback 9oz steak was not very tender but cooked correctly. The other steak we got was with the $11 3-course meal. It was 6oz and perfectly made and much more tender.
Bloomin onion was amazing as always and I love their Caesar Salads. It has the perfect combination of salad dressing to make it taste amazing.

We have been to the outback a few times and have always received excellent service. I appreciate great service and always tip more for it!

1. the guy that came out to clean the carpet gave me a different estimate than what was discussed over the phone. 
2. the guy who came out showed up 2 hrs late.
3. I called to complain. the guy on the phone said the same excuse as the one in the previous review.

Stopped by today. Walked in with my family. Dark haired girl behind the counter said, "how are you?" I said, "great, how are y--"... she cut me off and said rudely "just so you know we are trying to close."

Lol, okay. We had seen the "closing early" sign on the door but didn't realize it was after five. There were plenty of people still in there and your door was still unlocked. MY BAD. I understand businesses need to close sometimes early or just close in general. But when you have employees that cannot communicate in a nice way to potential customers-- that's unfortunate. Especially in this climate, you probably don't want to be rude to people when so many small businesses are hurting. Just a thought. My family and I are locals. We aren't tourists. We would have been potential reoccurring customers. Not anymore. 
Again, this review is on the "service"-- not the product. Your ice cream could be great, who knows?
