Do yourself a favor and don't go trust what I say, trust the pictures that I took 2 min as soon as he got done" doing" my nails.

This place is A+. I eat here at least once a week. Relaxed ambiance, friendly service, great cocktails to welcome you. The half-chicken is delightful - crisp with the right blend of salt and spice on the outside, juicy and flavorful inside. The burger is one of their most popular and justly so - the (not too) spicy Korean sauce and the cheese are really an expert blend. Duck fat friend chicken wings are worth a visit all by themselves, and the pastas are hearty - very solid. Wouldn't recommend the salmon, but it's the only real miss on the menu for me.

Overall, this is just a great neighborhood restaurant that does all the important things really right.
Awesome food,drinks, and service is great. If we r ever in Nola again. We stop by here for dinner.

my wife and I have dined at Scape several times over the last 3 years. our first two visits led us to return. professional service, great stmodohete and of course excellent and creative dishes. this past Saturday nite was very different from our earlier experiences.
 food was served cold, server was very nice but had no clue what fine dinning was about. when we asked her describe certain dishes, she couldn't, her response was that she was new and really did not know much about what she was serving. the good we were served and overcharged for will has motivated me to never return. sorry Scape, you use to be a fine dinning destination.i think I will go to Bar Louie, for their service and food are by far better quality and price fairly. I do believe will will return. sorry. frequent fine diner.

My friend and I checked out this place on a whim, as we have both lived in Bristol for a bit now. We really enjoyed the atmosphere, everyone was friendly and the bartenders were very attentive and nice. The beer selection is great and the food was awesome too. This will become our new spot instead of the Irish Rover in Langhorne (which is still a nice place).
Seeing the DDD episode that featured this restaurant brought me in here.  The meal was as expected.

I got a chocolate cake from virago twice now for birthday parties and I loved it both times. if you are trying to top your party, you want to get a cake from this place, its that good. It is kinda expensive but it is worth it, everyone will be talking about it. I was very shocked to find a bakery like that in Lansdale. It will be much better than your giant or local grocery store cakes.

Most unfriendly and unhelpful one I have ever been to. Just tried to get a strawberry lemonade-aid. It's not on the menu but they have strawberries and frozen lemonade. But all I was told is they are not allowed to make it. Even the manager must not have enough common sense to be able to make something. I also didn't know they allowed piercings through the lip and gums. Good luck for a Christian bass company.

This is a nice movie theater as it is part of the Perry Crossing outdoor mall.  You can eat and shop before the movie.  The sound and picture quality are great! They have many screens and have any movies that are in 3D.  Check it out!

I don't even like pretzels, but I LOVE these pretzels.

Whenever I visit Philly, I make it a point to stop by Miller's Twist...and I can't stop after one pretzel.  I have to have at least two.  I literally find myself dreaming of these pretzels when I'm back in Indiana.  

I usually get the plain ones (I think they're  $1.75 each).  They're already packed with flavor.  

Definitely worth the visit!

This place was DELICIOUS! 
We got here a little in the later side of things but they served us and did no rush us at all! The server, forgot her name, was very helpful and her recommendations were what made our sushi date SPECTACULAR. 
I implore you to try the basil fluke, halibut dish the server said was the most popular. We also had the sashimi seared ahi tuna. I ate every single piece of that off. I refuse to share! Cannot wait to come back. Santa Barbara staple for sure!

I might give the Grille at Innisbrook 3.5 stars.   We've stopped in for lunch a couple of time after a round of golf.   The greek salad, tuna club and grilled veggie sandwich were very good - - -  and so were the waffle fries.   The lesser stars are due to service.   The wait staff is not very polished and at times slow and/or lacking of the common courtesy's (i.e. keeping the water glass full, responding positively to requests).  They are not rude - - - just not polished or what you would expect from a resort.   They could also use some help in servicing folks who stop in for a drink as they are rounding the turn to the back nine.   Their drink service is quite slow.

The ambiance with the outdoor patio is great . . . if they would just step up the quality of their wait-staff to match the service you receive at the rest of the resort, I would consider 4 stars.

On a recent Saturday, my husand and I ventured to Casona's for a romantic lunch.  Collingswood is a lovely strolling town.  Casona's porch is inviting and we were lured in by the music.
Little did we know that the service would be so completely lacking.  We ordered the ceviche which was truly delicious.  After waiting for another 45 minutes, a handsome and polite waiter appeared to tell us that there were no more black beans and inquired if we still wanted the Cuban sandwich that we ordered.  Where was our waitress?  What happened to the promise that our food would be "right out"?  Why did people who sat down only fifteen minutes earlier have their food served so swiftly?
The Cuban sandwich was really disappointing.  It consisted of very dry  and gristly pork with plain deli ham, flavorless sauce and pickle remnants on half the sandwich served up on a wonderful roll.  Pretty sad overall!  We will never go back and never recommend this restaurant. 
Our waitress did not check back to see if we enjoyed our meal or if there was anything to make our experience 5-star.  She vanished until it was time to give us our check.  
I believe that the F-troop was on duty this Saturday.  Very disappointing overall.
P.U.

I'm all about a cheap pizza buffet, the pizza that was fresh wasn't bad. There was a lot of really in fresh pizza, lettuce was turning brown and I refused to allow my kids to eat dessert, the ice cream machine was so dirty and only had one pizza dessert the whole time and it was not fresh! 

This restaurant should be a fun place to take kids to eat, but really needs to clean up the atmosphere!

Yep. Believe the hype. Hip City is BOMB. 

I'm on and off vegan, aka during the week I try to eat plant based as much as possible. But burgers, fries and a milkshake are staples in my diet (not necessarily vegan friendly or the healthiest of cravings). So when I stumbled across hip city veg I thought why not?! 

Ziggy burger, sweet potato fries with Sriracha aioli and a chocolate shake. Good god.  You would have absolutely no idea this food was 100% plant based, I genuinely did not miss my usual beef burger or dairy shake...and believe me, I am a burger fanatic. And even if it wasn't the "healthiest" of options, I felt next to no guilt about indulging and my craving was definitely taken care of! All of the flavors and textures were spot on..juicy burger, crunchy fries and creamy shake. 

Whether you're a vegan, die hard carnivore or somewhere in between, everyone can find something they will enjoy at Hip City Veg. So if you haven't gone....GO!! (Also, delivery was insanely quick, especially for being lunchtime in the city. 30 minutes max, which to me is pretty freaking speedy)!!

A friend and I went there for dinner and had a great time. The food portions are big and well done. There are a lot of fried options on the menu so health conscious people might want to try the baked chicken. Go in with an open mind. The servers are serving food and performing for you! So have fun with them and they will have fun with you!

Yum!!
I love chocolate.... when it is done right.

I was really just passing through town, and stumbled upon this place randomly.  The chocolates had so much character and detail, and so many different types, flavors, colors etc - I had to try one!

I ended up buying some for gifts.
Of course, one gift was for me.  A little chocolate buddha with fleur de sel I believe.  Yum, yum, yum.

Not the cheapest chocolates, but that's probably because they are hand made by a French chocolatier, not in a factory.  Another small business worth supporting!  Next time you are near/in La Arcada, stop in - and if nothing else, try the buddha (did I mention yum?).

We got the Total Eclipse pizza off the not so much secret "secret" menu. 
It's supposedly all their toppings minus anchovies. 
We also asked for no onions.
Super good! Love that the veggies were still somewhat fresh, like they didn't put them on the whole bake. 
The crust is good too!
Adorable spot if you want to enjoy your pizza there, outside.

We were VERY disappointed with our afternoon tea from the moment we walked in. We went to the desk, there was no one there. About five minutes later a young woman with a plate of food walked past us and behind the desk (saying not a word to us) Eventually she came out and without a smile asked if she could help. We said we had a 2pm reservation, She said she would see if our table was ready.  She went in the back many times (hungry?) Never saying a word.
We stood for at least another 5-7 minutes waiting for the table to be set? Finally we were seated. The waitress (who was a pleasure) took our tea orders and I told her I was vegetarian (actually vegan) but had known that could not be accommodated. We were told they were pre-made (which was quite obvious when they came.
The bread was cold and somewhat stale. They were obviously in the refrigerator for quite a while. The cookies were fair (not homemade). We were both looking for the clotted cream (cream tea??) The waitress brought us a tiny little jar and then brought another on request.  The tiny scone was excellent. When we (thought) we were done we asked for a check and she told us there were were truffles and petit fours. We were expecting homemade truffles but no they were not (Lindt is good) just not what we expected.We have both had high tea both in and out of this country and this did not compare.
The tea, scones and the waitress were great. She took a percentage off the bill which we greatly appreciated

Very bad experience with "complimentary" shuttle service. Even if the shuttle is empty, it's totally up-to the driver's wish if you can get a ride or not. When you board the shuttle the driver asks you why couldn't you wait for your vehicle. Disgusting customer experience at 7:30 in the morning.
called store to see if they did a price match with petco they said yes.had to talk to 3 people.manager came out and refused to do price match.very rude and ignorant.never will shop there again.

Let me first start by saying that I moved to Indy over a year ago and had yet to find sushi that I could rave about.  Well, I found it here.  FINALLY!!

It actually took a Groupon and my Sister saying, "I am in the mood for sushi" to get me here on a random Friday night.  Lame, but so glad we went.  We arrived around 7pm and were seated immediately.

Sensu has a nightclub feel to it, but is also an upscale restaurant...in my opinion.  Dining and sushi bar upstairs....dance floor and nightclub downstairs.  

Elliott (sp?) was our server and he was FABULOUS!!!  I haven't had that great of service in a long time and I do eat at some great places.  Being new to Sensu and serious sushi lovers, he covered the menu for us from A to Z and his recommendations were fabulous!

Everything is served in sharing portions, so when you see Miso Soup at $11, don't be alarmed.  You get enough for 3-4 people.

For three, we ordered:  Edamame, Shiitake Miso Soup (hands down, BEST Miso Soup I have EVER had), Krusty Krab (OMG....delish!), Spicy California Roll (super YUM!) and the....some other roll....can't remember, but it was darn good.

I was impressed with everything we ordered.  The service was outstanding....OUTSTANDING!!  Request Elliott....seriously.  Left full and super happy.  

Sensu, I will be back.  Gotta try that Toast and Jam.  I hear it is great.  Thank you for flying all around the big cities of the USA to research other great sushi restaurants and bringing something similar to Indy.  I love you for that!!

The Dapper Doughnut is awesome!! Located near the middle of Plymouth Meeting Mall's lower level, I wasn't even aware this doughnut stand was here and I love doughnuts!! I first discovered the Dapper Doughnuts through a friend, and when I stopped by I was blown away! The cakey doughnut with all the different toppings is to die for, my favorites being the chocolate and vanilla drizzled ones. It is also quite interesting seeing them made in front of you and the prices are decent as well! I also need to give a shoutout to Toni, the manager of this location. She's pretty cool to talk to, remembers the customers and is great at her job too!! All in all, if you are in the Plymouth Meeting Area and at the Plymouth Meeting Mall, stop by The Dapper Doughnut. They weren't named best donuts of Philly 2019 for nothing!!

The present address is 6017 keystone st Philadelphia PA,he has been in several locations in the last 6 years- he did work on my Lincoln MKX about 4 years ago and the work was substandard- the passenger side door he supposedly fixed is wavy and when you open the door on the body side of the door it is still dented from the accident due to they never bothered to fix.his locations were originally in bridesburg,then he had a place @ old Lincoln highway and street Rd ,then he moved back to bridesburg,then to hellerman st,and now to keystone st near the tacony bridge- use only as a last resort,paid $1500 for the repair and eventually I have to replace the door and fix the unfixed damage

every single
thing ive tried is delicious! staff is wonderful, so happy this place is in my new neighborhood!

We found our fave po boy spot.  I had the off menu "Tony Bourdain" (shrimp, roast beef, gravy, provolone) and my wife had the fried shrimp.  She has not been a fan of the po boy, but she finally found one that meets her exacting standards.  The fries are damned good too and the staff are friendly.  YES!

Sushi is good. But the customer service is HORRIBLE. We arrived at 830 pm and asked for a table for 4. The hostess said she has a table available she just has to set it and will be like 5 min. Perfect! Well 5...10..15 min and nothing. As more people are walking in, the hostess is taking names and what not but never asked for our name bc we were suppose to be seated soon. So finally at 9pm I asked about the table. The hostess actually told me she was setting up our table and a waiter stopped her and told her to not seat us there because she's saving it for her friends. Yes, you read the right. We didn't get the table we were told because someone wanted to save it for when their friends arrive  
So, the hostess tells us it will be about 20 min before another table is ready. Cool. Well 930 and nothing. Again. But another group of 4 who came in way after us, got seated. After asked the hostess again, she seemed baffled and said she's waiting for another table to get up for us  long story short, We ended up not getting seated until 10pm. 

I understand we have to wait, but being offered a table then told we can't sit their bc some dingle berry wants to have some friends who weren't there to sit in her section when they arrive is absolutely ridiculous. Then having another group that came way after us being sat down before us too is a load of crap.

My husband and I happened upon this restaurant and while looking over the menu posted outside, we received a very friendly greeting.  The service was excellent, the restaurant is quaint, and the food is finely seasoned.  Highly recommended.
This place is closed. No sign of it. Wasted time driving and looking for this place. Wish it was posted someplace from yelp or any other site that it was fine.
Just picked up 2 cobb salads at the Montgomery Ave location and when I got back to my office noticed they were missing the eggs.

We ate here on a Friday night, got a table easily at 630pm and saw the rush come around 7pm. If you want to be the dinner crowd, go around 630pm.

The food was good. I recommend getting the Mozzarella sticks- they were big in size (comes with 4) and cooked perfectly (oozing cheese).

The seafood platter was rather large after eating 2/4 mozzarella sticks. Comes with shrimp, scallops, and white fish.

I'm giving it 4/5 stars because the server did bring us fried scallops with the seafood platter when I asked for blackened and shrimp tacos without the guacamole... which, we ate and didn't send back and was still good.

Lastly, it was a nice spot to watch the sunset from while dining outside.

I saw this place on the food network and made it my mission to try this place! My friends and I were on a two weeks east coast trip and I made sure we stop by philly so I can eat here! Yes, that is how much food mean to me! 

Tommy is located inside the reading terminal market. If you are from sf then it is similar to our ferry building. 

We tried the pork & beef sandwich and both with broccoli rabe & sharp provolone. Both were very good but I think I like the roasted pork a bit better. The peppers also made the sandwiches. Yums! 

A little hint, there's always a long line but the counter seats are first come first serve. If you see an open seat, sit down and order. Everyone in line might hate you but who cares when you get to eat this awesome sandwich before they can! :P

What a great place for date night! 

The dim lighting & settings make this place an ideal spot for a fun time with that special someone. When we were there, we ordered a meat & cheese sampler along with a wine flight which had us feeling a nice buzz after we finished our glasses. We will def be coming back for more date nights in the near future!

They also have a nice wine shop in the front of the store with many selections in store to choose from. Makes for another cool part of the store to walk around and hang out in !

Parking can be a little tough as any place in south tampa so just remember to prepare for a parking fiasco during peak hours. i would recommend to go during weekdays just so you dont drive yourself crazy looking for parking.

**** 4 1/2 stars ****

--------------------------------

What a charming little spot to have breakfast or lunch!  Treehouse Cafe is located in the Trinity neighborhood, right on the corner of Monroe and 11th.  A glance down Monroe shows well-kept rowhouses on a tree-lined street.  Treehouse reminds me of times long past where many neighborhood streets had either a small corner store or cafe.  In the past, the owners would get to know the people in the neighborhood who regularly frequented the business.  Enter into Treehouse and you will find a comfortable, cozy environment.  Most of  the seating is at the counter but there are a couple of tables.

We were here in the late morning on a Tuesday.  When we entered, we weren't sure what to do and one of the employees told us to sit wherever we wanted, so we sat at the counter.  There were 3 women working there, one of whom was the owner.  Everybody was very friendly.

We gave our drink orders first.  My husband ordered a cappuccino and was asked what kind of milk he wanted in it.  He chose regular milk.  I ordered an iced tea.  At first, I was told to go to the refrigerated case and grab a bottle.  However, before I got out of my chair, one of the ladies brought it to me as well as a cup of ice.  The same thing happened when I was asked if I wanted sugar.  As I made a move to get some packets, they were brought to me.  My husband said that the cappuccino, while flavorful, could have been stronger.

We both got breakfast sandwiches.  My husband ordered the "Treehouse Breakfast Sandwich" which consists of: "Western omelette, avocado, green peppers, onion, tomato and cheese".  I wasn't sure which sandwich I wanted until one of the women suggested the Apple Tree Breakfast Sandwich" which consists of:  "Western omelette, cheese, caramelized apple, bacon on croissant".  That sounded interesting, so that's what I got.

As for my sandwich---all I can say is --- wow!  This was the most unique breakfast sandwich that I ever had!  The croissant wasn't at all greasy.  Instead, it was flaky and tender.  The apples added an amazing flavor that melded very well with the other ingredients and gave the sandwich a touch of sweetness.  I'm going to dream about this sandwich LOL!

My husband, whose sandwich also came on a croissant, really liked it.  He thought all the ingredients worked very well together without one item overtaking the sandwich.  We both agree that next time we're in town, we are beating a path to Treehouse.

As we were eating our sandwiches, the owner was making the soup of the day from scratch.  We watched as she cut up all the ingredients for the chicken soup.  The phone rang and it was a customer asking when the soup would be ready!  It's so very impressive to see soup being made from scratch plus the fact that someone would call and ask about it, tells me that the homemade soups have to be incredibly good!

Later, when we returned to our hotel (which is 4 short blocks from Treehouse), we were chatting with the front desk clerk and told her we ate there.  She had never heard of Treehouse and asked us how we found it.  I said I found it when I was searching Yelp for places to eat near the hotel.  We told her all about our meal and she said that she will definitely go there!

Breakfast for the two of us cost us $21 before the tip---and it was worth every penny!  Just note that they are only open for lunch and breakfast and are closed on Sundays and Mondays.

BAD SERVICE RUDE AND AGRESSIVE CUSTOMER SERVICE. I have needed my air repaired waited and was repaired and in less than an hour stopped working. When I tried to call after 10 tries the customer service guy was so rude. He was defensive and inappropriate I am writing this waiting on AHS to speak with them about this and get some resolution. This is so bad!!!
Wow! Fresh daily made bread great prices wonderful humas! This place rules- hands down the best chicken schwarma sandwich in the South. Love this place- take out or eat in just as good

Great location; very nice rooms and sweet staff. The only change I would suggest is the way breakfast is set up- move the toaster and waffle iron out of the main buffet line, it creates a huge traffic jam. If it was on a separate table, the line would flow much better.

Tolerable in taste and in flavor dishes. Passable plate presentation. Undersized,  bland cocktails. Chocolate cake and a frosting appeared as the one I make from the box. Inferior service. A star goes to hostess who sat us at the table. She was super courteous and complaisant.

We enjoyed every bit of what we ordered from Thai Town; Crab Rangoon Pad Thai?, Amazing Sauce Vegetables, Veggie Soup and Spring Rolls. Yum! will definitely visit again. The driver got lost to my apt..other then that loved it!

First time I came to Sugarbowl I had mediocre food and horrible customer service. Decided to give it another shot and well.... Mediocre food and horrible customer service. Our waitress Willow did not come by once after taking our order. When I stopped her to ask for cream and sugar she threw them on the table and walked away. I ordered the eggs benny and one egg was soft and the other was medium. The one star is for the homemade ketchup. Thanks for another disappointing experience.

We went to G.W. Fins for our one year anniversary dinner. The food was amazing!! We had the deviled crab stuffed Maine lobster as our entree with tuna tar tar and sashimi and blue crab stuffed pot stickers as appetizers. One of the best meals we've had in recent memory. Don't know why it's not rated higher on yelp.

I love this place. It's meant a lot to me over the years. In fact, it was where I proposed to my wife (and was also the site of our engagement pictures). Becca, the propieter, is helpful, informative, and not snobby. I appreciate her humility and patience with my incessant questioning. I told her exactly what I liked in my tea and she prepared a perfect cup of Chinese green tea. Excellent. I love coming here, just to sit; it's warm, quirky, and interesting. Not necessarily the best place for a private conversation, but that's OK.

I stumbled into Vino Divino over the weekend when I need a great white wine for my friend.  I had already stopped by Gelson and Trader Joe's but I just couldn't find anything that I like.

When I was about to give up, I drove pass Vino Divino on the way to my friend's place.  The wine store is small but it got all the good finds.  I am not a wine snob nor a wine expert.  I just told the "super chill" (described by MScott) staff what I like.  He gave me couple of recommendations and I finally got one of his picks - a bottle of Breggo Pinot Gris.  It was so refreshing and delicious.  Everybody loved it.

If I am in town again, I will definitely go back to explore a little bit more.
Best Salmon on a plank ever. Traveled over 50 miles to have their salmon again. Great fish and chips and the buffalo cauliflower appetizer is outstanding. Always impressed by the food and service.

Beware - I got an oil change here for my 3 year old car and it cost me $150 MORE than the oil change. The guy disconnected a hose to take my air filter out - without my permission - and failed to clamp the hose back on securely. So it jostled around, working it's way loose over time and caused the check engine light to go on intermittently. I took my car in for service only to find out that I had to pay $150 diagnostics fee to find this out. SO ANNOYING!! Wasted my time and money! It is unfortunate because I previously went here and gave a 5 star review. I will not go here again.
Sushi rolls with more roll than sushi.  It's pretty good if you like cold rice. Yikes, that's mean.  Oh well- add more sushi!

What a DUMP! Do you not bring your car here. Incompetent technicians. Brought my car here twice to be told that they don't have enough technicians to Do a oil change at my schedule time because they have callouts. Not a customers problem if their technicians are useless and call out consistently. There are plenty of other places take your car. The one time I did have a oil service done, wiper fluid wasn't replaced and tires were not rotated. Plain Loser.

You would think they can't mess up breakfast right?! Well, they can! Simply not good. Dried out scrambled eggs and nasty homefries/bacon.Springfield Diner is much better for breakfast! This place used to be good a very very long time ago, like 30+ years ago, back when I was a little kid! Just isn't the same place anymore.
To make a breakfast taste as good as my homemade corned beef hash skillet was is truly amazing.  That it was served as quickly as it was was a great feat. This will be my go to place in Brownsburg
I just stopped by for a which lunch. The lobster roll is very fresh and tasty. I'll come back for sure.

Customer service, there  is none  in the "service" department. Can't look up to say hi or
Be with you in one minute. Overall seemed bothered to have to wait on customers. I do not care to help support their salaries.

If you need me, I'll be at Indie Coffee Roasters, my new home coffee shop. 

I've been twice in the opening week, and it's already a place "where everybody knows your name" like Cheers. Co-owners Diane and Alec truly care about their customers and the rest of the staff is great, checking in to see if you need anything.

Admittedly, I'm not a coffee drinker but I love coffee shops for the atmosphere to meet with friends or get work done. Indie Coffee Roasters  has done it right with bright, clean decor and a variety of seating arrangements. The large windows provide lots of natural light in the morning hours.

Pastries and treats are from Porter Books & Bread and there are plans to bring in a donut trucks on select weekends.

Don't forget to sign up for the rewards program at check-out! For each purchase, you get a star. 10 stars = $5. Great deal.

Despite the last unacceptable experience I had with a to-go order, and the promise never to order again,  I went back for another chance. Frankly, it's the EXCELLENT BAR STAFF that keeps me coming back. Perhaps I need to order food IN the restaurant, but clearly, to-go is a sad experience given my multiple disappointments. This time, I paid "extra" for steak "Oscar Style" along with my wife's fish order. Got home and all on my better half' order seemed ok, but, looking at my order, I forgot I had paid extra. There was ZERO Bernaise sauce, a couple of asparagus stalks that I thought were mistakenly added to my side of French beans, and so few crab pieces that I thought they were grilled slivers of garlic added to the steak. Then, I remembered what I paid extra for. Should be ashamed, especially since the very first Bonefish opened its doors minutes away. This establishment needs to give the bar staff a big raise because as far as I can tell, they are what keeps customers coming back - certainly not their service/ to-go orders.

Elitist is a better descriptor for this company than 'elite'.  I've lived in a dozen states over a period of 50 years and have never in my travels seen a company so persnickety about the garbage that they pick up.  They publish lists of rules about how to bundle and put out your garbage.  A minor misstep on your part will result in them leaving your garbage where is sits and them taking a photograph of it to document how you broke one of their rules.  I realize that there have to be boundaries for residential garbage collection, but I'm not talking about gross violations here.  I've placed used Christmas wrapping paper in a closed 2 x 2 x 2 foot cardboard box that they wouldn't take it because it wasn't in their prescribed plastic bag.  People, relax a bit. You're picking up garbage, not organ transplants. This company takes their rules to ludicrous extremes.  Something that would take 5 seconds to throw in the back of their truck will instead get an impromptu 30 second photo shoot from their trash collector. I advise you to take your business elsewhere.

People and room were nice. Only complaint I have is that they were doing construction on floor 20 and placed us on floor 19 so we had a nice wake up call. Even though we had checkout in 2 hours I felt like it was unnecessary to make us or other guests listen to that noise and if they were doing construction they could have placed us elsewhere. They had 26 floors but I felt like they did that since we booked on a 3rd party site. Also the hotel was not busy at all so we could have been placed in another room to avoid the noise. It sounded like a drill. It was obnoxious.

Easily the best bar on Main Street. It typically lacks the popped collars and sweatbands on the forearm crews that seem to inhabit almost every other bar on Main Street. The beer selection is top-notch and the bar tenders are pretty knowledgeable about their trade. There is almost always a place to sit, which is great, to talk to your friends over one of the many bottled beers that I can guarantee you have never tasted before. The entertainment is pretty standard fare, your typical guy rocking an acoustic cover set that never seems to end, which is awesome. After a few hours of downing a couple of rounds, it is inevitable that you will be singing every single word to some mid-nineties classic that you haven't heard in a decade. Never had a bad time here and I am always willing to go back.

Amazing food! Our favorites were the Palm Sugar Ribs and the chili garlic noodles. We were truly blown away by how much flavor was in each bite. I can't wait go back and try the rest of the dishes on the menu.

Parking lot was a cramped.

BIG store that was clean. I got my bagels and tried to pick up some orange juice. Unfortunately, my credit application for $10,000 was denied (the amount I needed to buy a small cup of orange juice). So, I took my showboat over the circle K to get their litre of Orange Juice for less. 

I think they are pushing the "lox" cream cheese. Not big on the lox. I did like how my bagels were sliced when I opened the bag, I guess I missed that part of the operation - made me happy.
Efficient and courteous employees left my car perfectly clean.  And bonus -- their bathrooms are clean, too! :)

The problem with the Sparks Popeye's is an obvious  lack of supervision or employee training.  Table tops  are usually uncleaned, the table salt and pepper and napkin containers are generally empty and the trash container area is often untended.      Popeye's has got to be a great franchise, it's hard to believe that a franchise owner would allow this sort of neglect.

Lovely folks, nice to have choices and they allowed me to have my pooch (Black Kettle doesn't, Rabbit Hole does)...all
pluses but my cafe latte was really really weak.  It caught me off guard because they're using a quality Italian brand. Most places get at least a 2nd look if there were positives but not when they mess with my drug of choice!   I'll stick with the hoods best beans- Rabbit Hole, & if I need bread Black Kettle gets the nod! Happy eating.

UPDATE AFTER YOUR REPLY (BELOW)

1- I posted 'Cafe Latte' from memory...I think most who read get the point. When I ordered a 'Latte' in Florence this past May I got a cup of warm milk.  Thanks for clarifying my review of your weak Latte= a Cafe Latte on the menu. 
2- My review wasn't meant to be 'negative', just honest..sorry if you took offense. I know you have a premium Italian bean featured, I saw it, but the LATTE was weak period. No intent to be or sound unfriendly or negative, just brutally honest feedback so you can adjust & other customers can compare and contrast & either report you made a change or they've had the same results.  I'd think you would appreciate unabridged honesty.  I highlighted some really nice things in the review as well & others have had good things to say. 
3-If you're implying I have some dog in the fight so to speak for Rabbit Hole, I have no affiliation except I have spent a lot of $ there on espresso drinks.  My career involves international travel virtually every week, and it's not as an employee of R.H.  I thought the point of a forum like this was to 'promote' quality so other foodies could benefit & make the best informed decision on spending their hard earned greenbacks & ultimately competition would improve; that was why I mentioned Rabbit Hole.  Fair or not, I live in the neighborhood & they were my first, & thus far, best cuppa so they're my yard stick. When I see consistent glowing reviews about the espresso, I'll be back.  In the meantime, no ill-will & a 3 Star review is NOT negative, just 4 & 5 Star aspects pulled down to a 3 Star by 1 Star weak espresso. Cheers & best of luck.

The pizza here was good. Your average after drinking pizza. I got the Chicken Spinach Feta pizza. It was so big I had a hard time finishing it but it had good flavor. It was fresh too. I just wish there was more variety then just two different types of pizza. 

My sister is a vegetarian so she opted for cheese pizza but the guy kept trying to get her to eat the chicken pizza. After she told him 3 times, no meat, he finally understood. He said the cheese pizza would be out in about 10 minutes. It came out hot and was tasty. The cheese seemed a little smaller than the other pieces.

The place is pretty small and there are no tables at night. Most of the staff is nice and does their job. I'm not sure if there is a bathroom or not. Plenty of standing room. The line was out the door when we went. With the construction on bourbon right now it's hard to get to but just look for the neon lettering signs. I would suggest ubering if you can. There isn't a whole lot of parking close by the pizza place.

My first experience here was ordering take out with a friend. The person taking the order on the phone was apparently kind of rude, but honestly the food was really good. I have since eaten in the restaurant two more times and have actually had very good service. The pho is done well and is fairly priced averaging $6.50 to $8 per bowl. And surprisingly the Vietnamese taco (I know the name is weird) is very good. It has super tasty marinated barbecue meat with veggies in a soft rice bun served with plum and siracha sauce on the side. I highly recommend the taco.

The bad service continued. Someone from the Chart House commented on my post and asked me to send the details. I sent and no follow up at all! I heard nothing from the person or the restaurant. Thanks for confirming my position!

Very poor job. I asked the guy if I could pay extra due to dog hair in my car. He told me to purchase the full service wash, and it would get done. It doesn't even look like they vacuumed because the dog hair is still present. I was willing to pay EXTRA. I will only be returning if I need a quick exterior wash.

Really good food!
Filet was cooked to perfection. 
Cowboy chicken sandwich was juicy and delicious. 
The BLT (bacon and brisket) was huge! And good. 
The Blackjack burger was also very good. 
The fries were good but the potato salad was Tex-Mex and a bit spicy. 
Overall a wonderful dinner!

Crème Brulee Donut
Whiskey Caramel Donut
Birthday Cake Donut
French Toast Donut

Already planning a Saturday brunch at Datz it seemed only appropriate to pre-order some Thanksgiving Day treats from its sister bakery and picking up several items on Wednesday, as well as a few more after Saturday's breakfast, one could make a strong case for either space being worthy of 'destination dining' status to those toting a substantial sweet tooth anywhere near Tampa Bay.

Truly a spot focused on tongue-in-cheek whimsy with an extra helping of 'fun' it was nearly two weeks before leaving Las Vegas that I contacted Dough and arranging for a pie as well as a few tartlettes to take to a family gathering I was assured that several additional items  would be available a la carte in store, the eventual selections ranging from cupcakes and donuts to fanciful candies including a pair of peanut butter pudding balls dipped in chocolate that bested any I'd experienced during my 30+ years as a resident of the Buckeye State.

Sourcing many local purveyors, both for production and items offered on the store's shelves, it was to the tune of a half-dozen donuts and a single cupcake that our in-store order was conducted and with a dense base beneath thick frosting suffice it to say the Salty Caramel Cupcake is a dish best shared, the richness of the chocolate not even close to reined in despite a creamy core and saline topnotes, while each of the donuts featured far less heft, the cake options unfortunately a bit drier than would be my preference while the filled squares were all reference standard; each leavened brioche base piped to bursting with housemade jams and custards from which the crème brûlée and pumpkin pie should both be considered 'musts.'

A bit underwhelmed by the portion of each $5 tartlet despite up-front fruit flavors and textbook textures in each it was finally in the Pecan Pumpkin Pie that we indulged and although perhaps not as interesting as it sounded on paper it would be tough to argue that fresh pumpkin puree topped in crumbled housemade pralines could ever be less than delicious, the $14 pricetag a veritable steal for a nearly two-pound serving with an all butter crust that remained crisp for nearly three days.

I never made it in to see the doctor, so no review for them.  However, I absolutely concur with the other reviews' statements that staff here are unprofessional and discourteous.

It started when I called to schedule: they absolutely did not listen to my request for a "weekday evening after 4 pm next week" and repeatedly offered me weekend appointments and next day.  This may be a plus to some, but seriously, LISTEN TO WHAT I AM TELLING YOU.

They never called to confirm, but then called me with some attitude 10 minutes before my appointment because I wasn't there yet.

When I got there a few minutes later, none of the staff bothered to acknowledge me.  I waited in the eyeglass area for a while before signing my name on the clipboard and going to sit in the DEPLORABLE waiting area which offers no comfort beyond folding chairs.  There was garbage left on the table and the whole place absolutely REEKED of marijuana.  A staffer did come through spraying some perfume to cover the weed stank, but that somehow only made things worse.

I waited within eye line of the doctor for more than 20 minutes past my appointment time with no acknowledgement from staff.  Finally, someone came by and asked why I was waiting there, and seemed surprised that no one had given me paper work.  Another staff member insisted they had already called my name for my appointment.

When they finally did bother to take my info, I was informed that my insurance (which the aforementioned rude scheduler told me was "fine") is actually out of network.

So, thanks for nothing, Pearle.

Now I'm angry that I've wasted my time, AND I smell like cotton candy.

The food is decent, but I highly doubt I'll ever come back when they're getting ready to close. Everyone ( except our server luckily ) had an attitude and looked like they hated their job. We felt very unwelcomed... But hey as I said at least the food was decent. I recommend coming during lunch/beginning of dinner.

I tried this in Dec. Since I didn't make reservation I sat at the bar, lamb shank with tomato is quite nice, I particularly recommend the dessert，forget the name , spell like "BruXtlee"， in a shalllow bowl, soft and sweet, crispy caramel on top.
If you order UberEats from this place plan on going to bed hungry because they don't make your order for the driver to pickup.

Holy mackerel!  Victor, the owner's nephew, is one enthusiastic dude, sweetly welcoming you and then talking up the business when you're comfortably seated. 

I had planned to get a quick fish sandwich next door until I saw this place. I jumped on my YELP app and saw the high ratings so I went in. So glad I did.

The large portion of pescado mojo de ajo, $10.99, was very tasty and the plate well-presented.

This place gets high marks from me for friendliness and hospitality.

Food tried:
- Bayou Black Bean soup ($4/large)

I had the pleasure of trying Circle City Soups as part of the Shakespeare at the Yelp! event last night. I'm not sure which Chef was running the booth, but I had the even greater pleasure of trying the Bayou Black Bean soup. Now, I've had me some black bean soups. I used to eat them in the dining hall back at college, and they generally made a pretty respectable soup, and their black bean wasn't half bad (wasn't my fave, but it wouldn't kill you). 

That black bean ain't got nothin' on this black bean. I mean, damn.

Spicy, smooth, and piping hot, it was absolutely, as Trevor G. and Benjamin H. before me note "the best soup I have ever had".  It was even good COLD, and I think cold soup is about as illogical as clothes for pets (they have fur for a reason, don't they?). I would not hesitate to recommend Circle City Soups to anyone, even my enemies, so they can be jealous that I tried the soup for free. 

I eagerly look forward to heading back to the city market to sneak past Circle City Sweets to the corner where the chef wears a Sun King Brewing shirt under his whites (I wonder what beer they use in the beer can chicken?), to make my tastebuds do the cha cha again.
The food, the banter, the service....the best.  On my way to pick up my order right now and can't wait!!!

Friends took us here tonight and OMG, I'm so sad there isn't one in my city! We had the Singapore noodle, cauliflower bites, "ginger beef", and spicy eggplant. Everything was well seasoned and delicious, but the standout was the ginger beef. The restaurant was clean and cheerful and our waitress was very sweet and helpful. We'll definitely be returning next time!!

What can I say.. Keyana is a curl god! I called very last minute searching frantically for a salon to go to in the area. I came across this salon and they kindly accommodated my request. The salon is absolutely gorgeous! The staff is very friendly. Keyana was so amazing very friendly and made me feel at ease. She walked me the process of what the Deva Curl cut would consist of. I am so pleased at the end results. She brought my hair back to life and give me some helpful tips! If you are a curly girl looking for a salon who specializes in curls, please visit. Trust me you will not be disappointed.

The place is always clean and quiet. We went there more than 10 times over a couple of years. I like the lunch special with 2-rolls ($7.95), 3-rolls ($10.95) and bento box (around $10.95). The food is tasty. Sometimes the bento box is bit on the salty side, but you can always request less salt when order.

I gave this Arby's three times and I am done. I love Arby's but it's hard to find a location that is on point with their service and with their food. I ordered the 5 piece chicken tenders and received four chicken nuggets. Shame on me for being in a hurry and purchasing fast food, but I hate that feeling of disappointment when you realize they messed up your order and you're already blocks away. Stuff happens but it shouldn't happen more then three times at the same location. The Arby's on East Hillsborough Ave. is always on Point!

Amazing place to stay - for a few nights or a month!  Prices are great, all units are beautiful.  Be sure to look for Coco the dolphin in the channel.  Bikes, laundry facilities, docks, pool, grills, and more!

Terrible company. I ordered from Amazon and they used this company. It said expected by sat 8pm and I pulled it up today (on Friday) it was expected to arrive a day early awesome. I pull it up again around 5pm and it now says they attempted delivery but couldn't get to my front door so call Amazon to give instructions. I live in an apartment with the buzzers listed as the apartment numbers there's no reason there should've been a problem and I was home at the time. Now it's a long weekend and have to wait till Tuesday because they don't do weekend deliveries (then why was it expected on a weekend??) And there's nowhere I can go to just pick it up myself. The Amazon customer service filled out a complaint for using them as a courier and I sincerely hope they are no longer used. The only explanation is the didn't want to do anything before a long weekend and didn't attempt at all.

Villa Wine Tour was such a great experience all around. Walter was so nice and knew so much about the area. Highly recommend him. He made sure we had a perfect lunch set up. Very nice car with plenty water. He took us to 3 different family vineyards. He introduced us to Bia at Grassini who was such a fantastic host. If you're in the Santa Barbara area I recommend Villa Wine Tour. I would do it again.

We were in town for a wedding and staying at a hotel close by... was in the hankering for a late night meal so we ordered from Sage Diner.  We called at 10p and was glad to hear they were open til 2am.  We ordered the food for pick up and didn't dine in, but I did see the inside and it looked pretty old school classy.  There was a dessert counter at the cash register with about 25 different varieties of dessert!  The food we took home hit the spot, so I would definitely recommend this place for dinner...and also if you're in the mood for some dessert!
it says open at 11 for both yelp and google maps. We had just walked 15 minutes to get food and they say it's closed. Waste of time

I visited this store on 9/4/18 and was helped by a lovely young lady named Courtney. She was able to answer all my questions regarding products and she took her time applying and explaining them for me. I have visited this location a few times since it opened and the associates are always nice, but this has been my best experience thus far. Thanks to Courtney!

After reading a few reviews mentioning the "best wings in the city" I started thinking about all the places I need to try(now along with cheesesteaks...Steve's is across the street) because apparently there are a ton of the best out there.  Growing up in the NE I lived on these wings almost weekly and got a chance to indulge recently one late night after returning home from a night out.  My dad got 100 wings for a family party the next day and in my drunken stupor I managed to put a rather large dent in that 100 and I could not stop eating!  This wings are amazing but I will be the first one to mention the STUFFING.  This is the craziest, largest, most amazing, better than yo mama's stuffing you have ever had with enough gravy to clog all three branches of your aortic arch.  
It's funny, I have never eaten in and remember as a kid looking through the dark dining area wondering if anyone actually ate there instead of bringing it home.  Oh well, go try the stuffing!

I have had the experience of buying and selling cars for quite some time.  I do my homework prior to my visits, and I have been met with varied responses.  Some places are happy to see me (with my research).  Some are not so happy and border on being rude and condescending.  Being a female should make absolutely no difference but unfortunately that is not reality.

Sooooo....when I say that Clearwater CarMax will now be my go-to location for buying and selling any vehicle I have, I don't make that statement lightly.  We took my mom and her car to this location and were greeted warmly.  In fact, each person at CarMax seemed genuinely appreciative that we chose their location in which to see her car.

Damian handled our request with professionalism and compassion.  He informed us of what was going to happen and made sure we were comfortable during the wait.  He checked back with us several times  giving us the latest update.

Brian handled our paperwork and presentation of the check.  He was expedient and apologetic for our wait (which was not unreasonable at all).  In a day and age where customer service sometimes is nonexistent, it was a true pleasure to have these two young men handle our mom's affairs.  I would recommend them to anyone in our same position.

Our experience was sooo very important to us since having a parent voluntarily give you their vehicle is a huge step.  Our mom was treated with the respect she deserved from virtually total strangers.  We will always remember this experience.

Laura Hohman for Lorene
Came here at 8:30 with my wife and daughter. the doors are locked... I come here about once a month and the service keeps getting worse and worse. I don't suggest coming here for breakfast.

The one star is for service and time everything took.  I would give a 4-5 stars to the food if it wasn't for everything else.  We came in about 9 pm last night.  They were not busy at all, but said it would be a 20 minute wait.  When they finally seated Us, it was at a table that had been empty the whole time (mind you there were only about 6 tables with people in them throughout the whole restaurant).  The waitress did not even come over to our table for over 10 minutes to greet us.  Took us quite a bit longer to get our drinks, and a long while before she even took our order.  While waiting for our order to come (which took about 30 minutes after ordering-by this time we'd been here about an hour), they sat a party next to us of 15+ people.  They had their drinks right away and order placed quickly.   
The person who brought out our food was nice, but our waitress was a fail.  She was slow, seemed to forget we were even there, was inattentive, didn't give us silverware, etc.

My mom and I stopped here for lunch after attending the Flower Show at the convention center. We were seated immediately and our waitress, Damaris, was quick and attentive. The rest of the staff was great as well.
We both ordered burgers and they were decent. My mom had a side of onion rings and they were a pretty decent size.
I liked how there was an entrance from the convention center right into the bar.
There are a few arcade types of games on the lower level. I have only been upstairs once or twice years ago so I don't remember much.

Tri County Produce is amazing. The freshest stuff for the cheapest price. The grains are amazing as well. The customer service is very friendly, and this is the only place so far i've been able to find the boathouse farms smoothies (excellent products).
First off for the record this is uniquely Pakistani restaurant, and it's Superb. You can't go wrong with anything you have here. Simply fresh and clean and simplicity of ordering.
Great cozy place for breakfast! Everyone was friendly and attentive. I had the Eggs  Benedict and my friend had the granola. It was delicious. Will definitely go back!

The freshness of the food was awesome.  The portions were generous.  The quality of the food was superior.  It was good to see the owner again.  She is polite, welcoming and earns your business.  I will be ordering carry-out more often: the food was still hot when I got home!!

My first visit at Franklin Burger was good.  I should say really good because their burgers are really good hand-crafted , locally sourced , cooked right sandwiches.  Sides of kale/corn salad and delightful fried.  Check 'em out

We have loved their pizza for years but tonight we decided to try their pasta and we were very disappointed. We ordered the chicken Alfredo and Chicken Marsala. The chicken Marsala didn't even look like chicken Marsala. There was no Marsala wine in it. The alfredo sauce was very watery and bland. The chicken was bland, no season and didn't even look grilled. The salad smelled funny and we come to find a spoiled tomato and browning lettuce. The only thing that was half way decent was the mozz sticks. This was definitely not a good delivery or dinner experience with them. I think from now on well just stick with pizza, the only reason I gave a 2 out of 5 was for that.

The bloomin'. Onions are delicious. Been back a few times for them.  The burgers are great for a PLNT burger.  The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable.  The only drawback is at lunchtime when I was there 1 very pleasant young lady was cook, cashier, answer question, etc. lady.  It was a bit overwhelming for me to even watch.  I would definitely go back and hope things improved.  Great for children too.

I went here last night for a friends birthday and the restaurant was fabulous. We had a group of 14 people and the staff was so accommodating, friendly and helpful. They had relatively quick service with the food and made sure we weren't without water or drinks at any point during the dinner.  

I ordered the Pan d'olive flatbread  without olives- sorry I'm not a fan of olives. It was delicious but really rich so I was not able to have more than 3 slices. I also tried the Napoletana which was simple yet fresh. I think I liked that one better, but then again I do love my lycopene
.
The nice thing about going in big groups of friends is that you get to try different dishes. I tried a bite of the lamb kofte appetizers and they were amazing!! 
Also equally appetizing (to my eyes at least ) were the salads and rib-eye. (I was too stuffed from the flatbread to try any more)

I've heard good things about the happy hour so I will be back! T'was a great experience!
We had a surprise birthday party for my grandmother and they did a wonderful job! The food was delicious and the staff were so great! I haven't had a chance to go back but I can't wait until I do!

I recently moved to SB for grad school and was in desperate need of some hair therapy.  Months have passed between my current state of hair despair and my last cut and color. After checking out yelp for some direction, I decided to take a leap with Hair Underground.  I called, described my needs (color, cut, for curly hair) and they made an appointment for me the following day with Justine. My takeaway: if you're looking for a hair artist, go with Justine. She took my shabby, dull, dry curls and transformed them into the most radiant ringlets I have ever seen surrounding my face.  Seriously, this lady has talent.  Not only did she give me a super awesome cut with perfectly placed layers (she cut it wet, to boot, which is really hard to do), she also added these brilliant highlights and lowlights that made my locks pop. Then came the true testament for anyone with curly hair, the blowdry. And the result? Justine styled styled the sh*t out of my hair.  She had the perfect products, and knew exactly how to time that whole finger ringlet thing while diffusing it dry.  My fiance was in awe when he saw the results.  For the rest of the day, I felt like I was someone who did something worthy of being in a photoshoot.  Thank you, Underground Hair Artists and Justine, for making my hair the absolute best it's ever been!

No stars or even negative stars if allowed. Stay away! All they care about is taking payment from you. They don't fully understand secondary insurance. They care about collecting copayments than caring for you. All the users' comments stated here are all true. Rude, condescending, unprofessional, takes advantages of you and especially the Chinese speaking community. If you know English go somewhere else like a few blocks down to Jefferson Family medicine associates. Again stay away.

My colleagues and I needed a place to take a hip guest speaker from NYC for dinner, and Kauboi Izakaya appropriately matched the speaker's coolness. Let me begin my review with some education: the first word in the restaurant's name is pronounced "cowboy." I say this because in my mind I was initially pronouncing it with three syllables, "cow buoy," and that is just not correct. 

Construction on S Virginia means that the best way to approach the restaurant is from Holcomb, where one has access to their dedicated parking lot and lots of street parking. The restaurant does not take reservations, alas. We were able to snag a table upon entry, but not a quieter one towards the front windows. The restaurant accepts credit and debit cards, but does not generate a printed itemized receipt, which makes it less than ideal for folks who are submitting expense reports. 

Our server was attentive and did an excellent job explaining the menu to us and keeping our drink orders coming. The four hungry adults in our party demolished six shared items and four "final dishes," although the final dishes arrived after only three of the shared items appeared. The food was inventive and delicious and filling. The almost open-kitchen aspect to the restaurant makes for a very lively atmosphere.

Let me say again: it was noisy. The music was loud, and while it contributed to the fun atmosphere, it also will deter me from taking slightly less hip university guests here. I arrived first, and I asked the bartender super nicely if he could lower the music, and he was like, oh man, no can do. Really? Whatever, man, I say. As a millennial, I was digging the garage rock soundtrack, but I also would have preferred to have worked a little less hard to make sure I could hear my colleagues.

One of my colleagues was sad that they do not offer any desserts. I know, I know taverns don't usually, but come, on: people like dessert.

But this is definitely the hippest place to go for dinner in Reno at the moment, and I hope to have reason to return.

A nice juicy patty with fresh lettuce and tomato inside a potato bun with just a dap of sauce is heavenly and what i look in a burger. 

Since this shake shack in on the Drexel campus , i wasn't expecting much. Maybe its my low expectation, this location is surprisingly good. 

I usually get a single shack burger and try to only eat half to save the calories , lol . But its really hard to resist. 

Other than the 90% ice and 10 % soda, no complains.

Not a good experience.  The girl who gave pedicure was very rough & cut a small chunk out of the corner of my big toe.  Bled a little & has been painful all afternoon & evening.  Put peroxide on it a couple of times so hopefully won't get infected.

I don't think it's as bad as people make it out to be but it's still not perfect. I've only dealt with the Hallmark store there. Not bad, it was great to have the ornament area pretty much to myself even if they didn't have two ornaments I was looking for at all the morning they were coming out. The FYE is acceptable and the food court is nice. It's not THE mall I'd go to but it serves it's purpose.

I have no clue how this place has 4 stars. We went here because of the high reviews on Yelp and had a really awful experience. First I had a chicken quesadilla with rice and beans. The chicken was a greasy disaster and I'm pretty sure the rice and beans were cooked weeks ago. Very overcooked to the point of burnt. We also had a medium Margarita (12$ mind you) and it tasted like sour mix. I am pretty sure there is no tequila in their margaritas because it's neon green in color. I ADVISE YOU TO GO ELSEWHERE...$53.00 WASTED MEAL....
Have been getting the buffalo chicken stuffed pizza slices and buffalo chicken cheesesteaks from here for years . Love the service and food!!

I called in and they fit me in their busy schedule! I got a deluxe pedicure which also included hot stones,which was a first for me! 
I love that they have the plastic liners for the water while you're soaking your feet. It's nice to know they are so sanitary! 
Hoping I can come back soon. 
I heard Pam is out of town on vacation but they are managing great and hanging the busy swing of things!

Called to see if they had a front wheel spacer for my bike, they said not sure just come in...
Was a bit worried to waste my time but lo and behold, I was greeted by an enthusiastic younger employee who stopped what he was doing to ask how he could help me. He bled my brakes while he sent another guy searching for a spacer. Turned out they didn't have it but in stepped who I assumed was the owner, he proceeded to modify a spacer on his lathe to get me riding that day! He said he could order me the correct one, at which point I told him I was only in town for the day. He then said come around here and took the time to show me local trails on their website and point out good rides!
Great shop, great people working there with the passion and know how to make it happen!!
Thanks Great Basin, I went out and had an awesome ride above Lake Tahoe.

Great family owned business with wonderful English speaking hospitality!  The brothers are amazing chefs and hard workers.  Tried chicken shwarma, grape leaf dolma, lentil soup and my new favorite Fatteh!  All was delicious.  Easy parking right on the street out front.  Affordable pricing compared to other Mediterranean restaurants on Grand.

The only reason I am giving them 2 stars was the service was good. Our server Jessica tried to take care of us. 

The food was substandard at best. The fish was under seasoned and over cooked. The broccoli was over cooked and the coconut rice was white rice very dry with coconut sprinkled on top 
There was little to no seasoning on the food, I wore out the salt grinder just trying to coax some flavor out of the food.

Los Compadres is my go to Mexican food place in South Reno! Whether I've been with a large group or just two of us, I have NEVER had bad service! The food is always consistently good and there's chips and salsa being placed on your table before you're even fully seated! The prices are very reasonable and this is such a clean place! Even when I've ordered items for take out, the orders have always been correct and the time between ordering and the food being ready had been really fast! I will continue coming here!

Rice was rock solid. They didn't cook it fully. I wouldn't even be writing this if it was the first time it has happened. Has been multiple times now. Over a span of 2 years. If I wanted to eat rocks I'd save myself the money and trouble and go munch right outside my front door. I ordered chips/salsa. I feel like a human-dragon hybrid. It is so hot it is not edible. And I love spicy stuff! I ordered regular and received the flaming hot red sauce of death... which was also what I ordered in my meal... just completely unsatisfied and I'm trashing the whole thing. 

If I could give this a -10000 stars I would

I usually think food trucks are hit or miss. This hit me with a brick in the mouth with flavor. Holy s***b**** it was probably the best bbq I have had in awhile. You can tell it was made with love, not too much love I hope. I have not visited the restaurant yet, but the food truck is enough to get me to show up from here forward.

I am brand new to Spring Hill. Dropped off my daughters hand made, pearl detailed, Dupioni Silk christening gown, my dress, and my husbands suit to be cleaned and pressed. I had them all back before the time requested and they were all flawless. I will never go anywhere else. Great customer service, also.

Good Sales, Decent regular prices also. Friendly people. Only gave them 2 stars because the employees are as slow as Christmas! We stood waiting for help for 30 minutes in the ammo section and it never came. Waited another 10 minutes up front for a price check. No one was in any kind of hurry to help customers. It was a Thursday and they weren't busy at all. They also had PLENTY of staff in the building. Many were just chit chatting in the aisles. I don't shop here often but it would have been nice to have some better service while I was there. Disappointed.... :/

Nice funky coffee spot. Nice people working and friendly atmosphere. Guitar plucking in the background-someone pulled it off the wall for an impromptu. Coffee is superb. Muffins fresh. What more is there?

As others have stated, come here with low expectations.  It's definitely a motel.  The location is great and free parking.  That's where the positives end.

There's no heating in the room other than an electric Amish fireplace.  I've only seen those in SkyMall, which gives it the one star.

The rooms are small and everything about the place is old.  For just under $100, it's not bad.  I definitely wouldn't go here for a weekend getaway with the lady.

I compare it to a sketchy room in Vegas, which you don't mind because you're only crashing there for a few hours.  That's what I suggest you do here.

Hidden Gem!! All I can say is Wow!! Breakfast is Amazing!! Tryed this place a couple weeks ago and Loved it!! Had the Biscuits and Gravy ..eggs..and Home fries...Super Good,!! Potatoes were perfectly seasoned and I had them smothered with gravy. Awesome..ordered Two weeks in a row!! Check em Out guys!! This place is on Point!!

This place is tiny and extremely old, it seems like they built it and then never touched it again in its probably 50+Year history. However, the food is delicious. This place was recommended by a local and it is a little bit of a walk all the way to the end of Decatur street but I say well worth it! There's only like 2 people working here so you have to have some patience but they do work hard to get people in and out and I imagine there is sometimes a line out the door. 

I ordered a shrimp po boy and fries with a mint julep and it was the best meal of that day. So simple but executed really well. It seems like a lot of tourists stumble in here unexpectedly but locals know this is the place to go when in the area and I liked that there was a mix of the two while we were there. 

Special trip? No, but if you're in the area it's a must!

Really good pizza by the slice, plus they're open late. Tony's is a perfect snack after bar hopping in Dunedin. 
I've never tried their other options, but all flavors of pizza have been good. The pepperoni is usually my go-to. The veggie is also amazing; it has fried eggplant on it.

Plain slices are delicious, nice little pizzeria. Overall quality and taste of pizza is great, however, I was expecting more choices to choose from. I got a buffalo chicken slice which was a little thick than usual and got my little brother a plain. The plain looked better. They need more pizzas. But overall atmosphere is nice and simple, service is kind and fast. Little pricey, but it's ok.

My family ordered me flowers from here for Mother's Day. Not only were the flowers beautiful, but on Mother's Day they called to let me know they were at my house (I was not), and they didn't just leave them on the doorstep! They took them back to the shop with them, when I told them I would pick them up the following day. The following day came when I called and asked if they would deliver them to my work in Medford which they did. Never heard of a flower shop going out for delivery, bringing them back, then going back out for delivery a second time. everyone I spoke to is super friendly, great customer service. I'll be making sure to get my flowers from them in the future.

Honestly, I haven't left a comment on Yelp for years but this was such an amazing experience with our server Sarah and Derek the manager but it was super pleasant and inviting! We will definitely be back! Amazing beers and environment!

If I had my way, I would travel the entire globe, eating my way from continent to continent.  If I had my way, I'd have no use for a place such as Saraga International Market.  However, since I don't get to trot around the world at my leisure, at least there is a massive grocery store that brings it to me.

If I were to write a review detailing all that Saraga has to offer, Yelp would probably have to purchase additional servers.  In a trip to Saraga, you can purchase any grocery item under the sun.  If you want Asian fruits, they have them.  If you want the rarest variety of ramen noodles, they have a quarter-isle of them.  Should you desire to make pho, Saraga has all the ingredients.  Would you care for some Russian tea or some French coffee?  They have those too.  If you're looking to make an authentic Middle Eastern, Indian, Jamaican, or Mexican meal, you'll also find everything you need at this one-stop shop.  Of course, you'll find your typical American groceries here as well.

Saraga also has an impressive assortment of meats from across the world, as well as an outstanding seafood department.  You can purchase live fish, lobsters, and even Dungeness crab.  The fish didn't look nearly as happy to be at the market as I did.

My only criticism of Saraga is that it seems to lack a true variety of European items.  Sure, they have an isle that is exclusive to the lands of my forefathers, but the selection was light in comparison to other places.

Happy travels.

We took a rental car to Burning Man and needed to get it washed down before returning it in SF. 

We pulled up to Jimmy's and for $20 they were giving a thorough washing to all BM cars. I asked the attendant if they would also spray down under the hood since it was   a rental car. His response, "They all are."

They did a great job of getting most of the grime off the car, including under the hood. They also have a vacuum station with rags and spray bottles for detailing. Such a lifesaver!

We were visiting the STL area on a Sunday evening and decided to visit some local breweries. This place had great reviews so we were excited to try it! When we arrived the bar area was full. I noticed a guy sitting at an empty, clean, table waiting on his to-go food order. The hostess gave him his order, he left, when we approached the hostess at her stand, I informed her that we were just wanting to have some drinks and we could we sit at that empty table in the bar (thinking that at some places the bar area is open seating). She sarcastically said "Um no, I have a waiting list. You can get a beer at the bar and take it outside." I said "Ok great, do we get to the outside area through these doors?" (pointing to an area to the right were I see people sitting). She then acted even more angry and replied "No, NOT through those doors. You can go out front unless you wanted to be on the waiting list which is 20-30 minutes. But NOT through those doors!" I'm not sure why she was so rude but in my opinion it was uncalled for. After this I decided I wouldn't order a drink. I went outside while my boyfriend ordered his beer. Outside there were five metal chairs (all occupied) arranged in a small circle. There were no tables and no additional seating. We literally stood against the building in the sidewalk while my bf quickly finished his beer so we could get out of there. I completely understand that the place was busy and nothing can be done about table space. However, to be treated that poorly was unacceptable. We visit lots of craft breweries around the country and have never had to stand on a sidewalk outside to drink a beer. As much as we would like to try more of their brews and food, we definitely won't be returning.

Great cafe off Lafayette Square. I recommend the mac & cheese or fried green tomatoes as an appetizer...both were excellent. The service was great midday during the week and was just a short walk from the WWII Museum. I would come back again without any hesitation.

This place operates as a scam.  They gave me a price for a iPhone 16 gb unlocked in flawless condition $423.  Communication is terrible because the website docent give you enough information on the status of you transaction so you have to keep calling them. After a week I had called to see were my iPhone was at and I was told that my iPhone passed inspection and I was transferred to the purchasing department (whats wrong with this picture) Now keep in mind that I have been selling my iPhones to gazelle since 2009 and I always got the flawless price. Every phone from the day I received it got a zagg protective shield and an air jacket so the phone never has any damage on it. When I take those items off the phone looks like the day I purchased it. Melanie in the purchasing department is a real piece of work. She than tells me my phone was worth $59 but she said that cant be right so she begins to describe the condition and there are some stuff marks on the phone and the button at the bottom shows wear.  She now tells me that the phone is worth $280 and that is the best price she can give me.  She never stops talking so you have a hard time interjection your opinion, very rude. I told here about the price on gazelle was $365 at the time and I decided to try their company instead. She checks gazelles price and looks at good condition and said they are at the same price.  Gazelle locks your price in when you start the transition not check market value afterwards. Gazelle flawless condition was $315 now and now I have lost that opportunity.  I asked to send my iPhone back and she just kept talking and telling me that if I do that the iPhone is going to less than that price by the time I get back and in the condition it is. I don't trust them to send the phone back because it might come back in poor condition.  I called back again and argued with Melanie until I finally got $305 for my phone I didn't want to waist any more time going back and forth.
