The hotel is a basic but very clean hotel. Very good value for your money.
Great place to rest when passing through Boise, Idaho. An oasis for weary travelers.

What an incredible surprise!!  I have been wanting to try this place but didn't know if it was a market or food place. Well it's kind of both leaning more towards a deli that is very comfortable to eat in.  The options here are tremendous.  From salads to sandwiches to fries and tater tots.  I had the tower special sandwich.  Just the way I like it.  Enough ham, turkey and bacon to fill the warm baguette roll.  The sandwich was nicely sculpted so that it was not overly messy to eat.  Perfect!   Plenty of vegetarian options and breakfast sandwiches all day.  The sweet potato tots were delicious.  Sweet, crunchy and warm.   A great complement  to any sandwich. Then you can get chips, coffee options from the cafe or any bottles or fountain drink that your heart desires.  I am very much an instant fan of this place.  The service was good and friendly too.  The only improvement is making it obvious where to pay or how the process of ordering and checking out works.  I highly recommend this place and will be back myself.  This is the type of place that a guest makes a staple visit!!  The instant yesssss feeling of this place has made it a five stars rating, one I rarely give out.

I met some friends here for some hookah on a Saturday night, and when I arrived things were still pretty quiet. There was one other party in the main area, and I didn't really get a look at the extension to the room so hard to say there.

Following my entrance though, I and the people I was with just sat there waiting for service. After 15 minutes I waved a server over as she was passing to the room extension, which she had visited several times over the period, and finally ordered some hookah for our group. A friend ordered some pita and hummus, and a smoothie, and I seconded the latter. Another group member ordered some Shawarma.

At 15 minutes the Sharwarma arrived, which isn't bad, at 20 minutes the pita and hummus finally arrived, which, I hate to speak in absolutes, is unacceptable. Of course already using 'unacceptable' leaves me with a dearth of descriptors for the continuation of this review.

See, when the smoothies made it to us at minute 25, I had already affirmed with my companions "Hey, usually when we order hookah at a place we have it in like 5 minutes, right?" and indeed in that time we had seen parties that arrived after us receive their hookahs. I asked if our hookah order was still on and was told it was, just the coals were still heating up (our coals take longer to heat up?).

At minute 30 since our order, another group show up. They have three hookahs on their table by minute 35.

At 40 we get our first hookah, and the others finally follow inside of 5 minutes. On receipt of our hookah, my friend orders some more pita, which had gone quickly in the absence of our planned inhalations.

25 minutes after that, there is still no bread, so when the server makes a rare stop at our table to refresh our coals, my friend asks about it, and gets told something that none of us can really pin down about it still heating or something. At 45 minutes, still with no bread, she goes to the counter to inquire, and gets waved off in a similar fashion. At 60 minutes after ordering (I'm still not sure what to go with after expending 'unacceptable,' but this is definitely that) my friend returns to the counter asking to see a manager. The bread finally arrives, notably without manager, 5 minutes following, but my friend gets told they're sorry and will give her a free desert, which miraculously arrives in the following 10 minutes (though I suppose it was likely something frozen being heated).

Later, about a half hour after the point where my party would have asked for a check if anyone had stopped by, we went up to the counter to pay.

As we left, putting an evening of being treated with what felt like outright contempt given the comparison point of other parties in the establishment behind us (and having had the privilege of paying for it), I felt a sense of calm knowing I'd never have to have that experience again, since I would surely never return to Alamodak.

I came here on Saturday night. The service (Food Service) is slow. The waiter was doing his best to handle 2 in half tables. It took almost two and half hours just to be seated at a table. I get it's Saturday night and it's very busy. But this is pretty unacceptable. Also, there is food in between the seats and it smells like moldy Broccoli. Other than the food service. It's a very fun place to be and have fun! Rating: 1 of 5

We ordered and paid for our pizza for a family gathering. Thirty minutes later received an email, not a text or call, that our order was canceled and that our money would be refunded 3-5 days. I tried calling, no one answered, and the voicemail box was full.  This is very unprofessional!

I absolutely enjoyed visiting this park which I passed by so often and always ignored.  Well this time I didn't and for 2$ entrance fee I was able to relax and enjoy the view. With everything being so expensive this is actually 'cheap entertainment'.
I didn't get to see / use everything so I'll give an update on that at a later time.  However, the few spots I drove / walked to were really nice, it was clean and well kept and I enjoyed the peace and quiet.
You can go play frisbee golfing (something I'll do for sure next time), there seems to be a little beach near the entrance which is nice, as well as lots of designated areas where you can have a BBQ and a boat ramp is present as well.  I enjoyed the nature, took lots of pictures (I'll post them at a later time),lots of places to explore and this park is huge.  My favorite spot was the walk out landing stage complete with a table and bench you basically sit in the middle of the water and get to see people fish, can do so yourself or just enjoy the scenery and the sun.  Very tranquil and lovely.

My suggestion: Go there, enjoy the nature and the quiet, have a nice BBQ with family/friends and just have an amazing time there.  It's worth the little money you need to spend to get in.

All city carpet cleaning is by far my top choice! They excel in costumer service, they do top notch work, and they are very reasonably priced! My carpets were badly stained and hadn't been cleaned in years, by the time they finished, my carpets looked new again! I definitely will be calling again.

I made a purchase on Saturday, March 1, 2014. Upon driver arriving, I voiced my dissatisfaction with him at that time and advised him that I would call to speak with Joe who was the manager on duty. I called 2x's on Saturday to rectify my concerns and was left on hold 3-5 minutes both times. I called again on Sunday and spoke with Joe to explain that pizza and garlic breads were overcooked. Joe stated that pizza was overcooked due to half of pizza being cheese only and said they were busy that's why I kept being placed on hold. Not once did he apologize. He aggressively asked me what would he like for him to do and I stated that I had not complaints with the lasagna & I felt it was only fair that the 16" pizza and garlic breads be replaced. He refused to replace and said I was only entitled to a $10 credit because the items had been eaten. I advised him that I tried to rectify my concerns the same day, but continued to be placed on hold and had no choice but to consume the items because I was having a sleep-over with 3 children whom I was feeding. He refused to replace and/or refund my monies. I informed him that was unfair and wanted to discuss with owner, Jerry. He recommended that I call Jerry on Monday, March 3, 2014 in between the hours of 10 am-2 pm. I called Jerry from 10 am-11:30 am and was told that he was not in. Joe finally advised me that he was not in due to inclement weather. He asked if he could assist me and I proceeded to remind him the purpose of my call and would like a call back from Jerry to rectify so that I would not have to contact BBB and/or my attorney over $20 which may not seem like a lot to him, but it is a lot of money for me. He stated that "I might as well contact my attorney if this is about an order!" then hung up on me.

When a customer is NOT satisfied the right thing to do is to make them very satisfied by replacing their order 100% or giving them a full refund. I made 2 attempts on Saturday to rectify issues which were rudely met unanswered by Joe. If this is how Imo's on Gravois wants to do business by not rectifying customers dissatisfaction, as well as hanging up on them under the management of Joe, then they have successfully lost a customer for life and have given me permission to gladly spread the word over their unprofessional attitude.

I went to El Barrio tonight for my birthday and wanted a flight of tequila. The bartender had no idea what he was doing. After waiting 20 minutes for a drink, being asked by a waiter if we were still waiting for drinks, and having a manger/owner/someone of importance stand behind us and doing nothing, we finally left. The sad part is, I live a short 3 minute walk from this place and I never want to go back again. There is usually a bartender who is very knowledgeable and puts on a great show while working but he wasn't there. Highly disappointed, especially considering the last time we had to walk right out due to the extremely loud dj. I go here for good craft beers and tequilas. Not for a frat party.

Fabulous Credit Union. This is way banking should be. 

Great customer service. Face to face tellers with smiling faces. Open desk area where you can see the customer service staff. No one is hiding behind a cube wall or door here. I have rarely had to wait for assistance and i am  always greeted with a smile and helped well.
And even if I had to wait, it wouldn't be a big deal because it's just a pleasant environment here. 

This was the way the credit union I belonged to since 1983 was until about five years ago. I still belong at the old CU but because  of all of the aforementioned positives here, most of my banking business is now done at Citadel federal credit union

Food was good, well cooked, crispy fries. The dinning room was dirty, there was a film of grease/dirt/grime on the non functioning juke boxes. I wish they still worked. The tv was on a terrible daytime talk show. The food though was tasty. Burger was juicy and perfectly cooked. Chicken sandwich was good as well. Our waiter was kind and attentive. It's a shame there was a layer of grime in the dining room. All cleaned up that place would be a Jem.  Nice view of the trees!

Amazing beer and amazing service, even though I'm sad they got rid of the local 30  :(. Regardless Kat was one of the best bartenders I've ever had and I can't wait to come back. I usually sit at table but tonight they were a bit busy so I just sat at the bar and loved it. Thank you Kat for the amazing service, I'll be back. Oh and of course the cosmic fries!!!!!
Wonderful live jazz, delicious food and great service!  Jamaican dishes and good vegetarian/ vegan choices.  Did I mention the Jazz?! Great place to spend a quiet evening

Well, finally got a chance to visit the new McDonald's on Emerson.  While I really like the color schemes, etc inside, I do have to say that I am not impressed overall.  

From an overall layout perspective, this is probably the most poorly designed McDonald's I've seen anywhere in the country.

For starters, the men's restroom is literally directly behind the cashiers' station, separately only by a six inch thick wall.  Everytime someone uses the hand dryers in the men's room it is SO LOUD you can't hear the cashier asking what you want.  In fact, my wife and I were sitting half way across the restaurant and could barely hear each other over the noise from that hand dryer.

There is also some really annoying loud bell that rings over near the drink station on a somewhat regular interval...seemed like every few minutes.  And, again, very loud.

Then, every buzzer and alert from the kitchen seems to be much louder that I recall from any other McDonald's.   

The seating design is an open floor plan and open layout.  Seating looks nice and modern....BUT, the "open" layout is such that there are no natural sound breaks throughout the room, making this the loudest restaurant I've been in for a long time.  The new design is definitely not conducive to any sort of relaxing dining atmosphere.   

I will likely stop in from time to time to grab a quick meal to go, but not likely to make it a dine in destination any time soon.

And,one more thing...I eat a lot of salads lately.  Just found out today that this McDonald's no longer carries croutons for any of their salads?!

I come here often to shop, eat, and see movies. It is pretty clean, I always see security, and they have a pretty good variety of restaurants and shops. The design of the mall is unique and very cute. My only complaint would be that the fountains are in an incredibly awkward spot, but obviously that's not going to stop me from coming back!

White Castle, one of the best cheeseburger sliders anyone will ever have the pleasure of enjoying in there life. Normally I would give this restaurant a 5 star but when you order a crave case (30 sliders) they make you enter the "crave zone". They don't have the sliders ready and they serve the people behind you first. They are pretty quick about getting your order out but they do take a while.
Food is great and fresh margaritas are awesome. Service is prompt and friendly. We'll definitely be back!

We went for the boyfriends birthday yesterday (free bottle of vodka if you're a vodka club member!) 
We both ordered Moscow Mules to start ($10 each) which were not served in the tradition copper mugs.. Odd.
Then we both ordered Burgers, he ordered the Bacon Bourbon BBQ Burger ($14) and I ordered two Sub Zero sliders ($13 - I chose to get a Classic and a BBQ Bison) with sweet potato fries - these fries were really good! 
However, both of our orders came out wrong. He got the the Sub Zero Bacon Boursin (this was not that good, especially when you're expecting a burger with cheese and drenched in BBQ sauce!) One of my Sliders, which was supposed to be the BBQ Bison, came out plain with a mango salsa on it? Not really sure if this was our waiters fault from putting our orders in wrong, or if the kitchen staff and bar tender just weren't paying attention. 
We are reevaluating if the free Bottle of Pearl constitutes the mediocre (and overpriced) food here. Probably not.

This Target's food court is awful!! I waited ten minutes today to be helped when there was no one else in line! I finally said excuse me to the girl working there, to which she mumbled something under her breath and then waited another few minutes to come over and help me!! The staff in the food court is always rude, so I'm not sure why I thought this time would be different. Also, half of the fountain drinks were labled "out of order"... Whatever that means. Awful place!
The sandwich was very good.  Had the Cochon muffuletta and the special seasoned lamb. A better than average sandwich by far.

Tortilla Factory is pretty much Costa Vida, but so much better! Their tortillas are handmade in house, same as Costa Vida and but these were absolutely delicious! 

Everyday they have special is so can get a full
meat for only $7.99. I went on a Thursday so I ordered the shredded beef burrito. First off, it came out super quick. We waited no more than 5 minutes which is impressive consider how busy the restaurant was. Second, the burrito tasted super fresh! I really liked the tortillas, it was so fresh. It tasted like it just literally just made a couple minutes ago. The greens were super fresh as well. I've been places where the greens are browning and it grosses me out so I appreciate a place that can provide the freshest ingredients! Since this trip, i've stopped by here several times and I've always had a fabulous experience. There's a little older lady who works there, I can never catch her name, but she is so sweet. I love this place so much, please go here to support them!

I've been to the location in Collegeville a couple times but glad this one opened as it is much closer. First time visit to Royersford location was great - thought it some of the best Indian food I've had in a while. Samosas were fantastic - and the three curry dishes were excellent. I'll be back.

Ticca, Vanessa and Kate you are the best! I am so happy that I found you guys! When I moved to Santa Barbara I couldn't find a good nails place and I thought I never would, until one day I found One Carat mani & pedi and I've been a loyal customer ever since. Thanks for being so awesome

I've stayed here multiple times and have always had a good experience. It's in a great location in the city and is very convenient. Breakfast right now is pretty limited but they are trying hard to keep the amenities we've come to expect. The only downside to this property is that they charge $32/ night to park.

It is a relatively new restaurant that opened in Smyrna. It has a comfortable atmosphere, with relaxing music and a smaller setting. The decor is simple and not overwhelming in the aesthetic. The owners are quite friendly, as they greeted each person. They make sure to check up on you, to meet your satisfaction. They make you feel at home. The food was a surprise, but a welcome one. Their menu consists of Thai and Japanese cuisine. You'll have your staple dishes, entree, and specialties. I had their Thai fried rice and it was absolutely delicious. It had the right amount of spice and the portion was perfect. Afterwards, I ordered two of their rolls. When it arrived, I was surprised by the presentation. It was not something aimed expect out of a small restaurant, but a four star restaurant. The first piece of the roll was an excellent sensation on the taste buds. It had a pleasant dance of flavors. To my pleasant surprise, there were hints of masago. Overall, I enjoyed this restaurant. I cannot wait to return and try something new on the menu. The prices are fair, for the type of restaurant it is, and the food is exemplary. I recommend giving this restaurant a try.

We have never dealt with such a horrible business in our life.

My wife called blossom from Los Angeles to have flowers delivered to our friend's grandfather funeral. We specified the flower arrangement and the message on the flower arrangement and left our credit card information. They charge us immediately. We sent 3 confirmation emails and requested a receipt.  The owner kept saying to us "do not worry".

We found out day of the funeral that no flowers were delivered but we were charged for the flower and delivery charge.  We called the next business day to find out what happened. The worker (Julio??) was unapologetic and kept saying he had no responsibility in the issue. Told us we need to talk to the owner. It has been 2 weeks and 10 calls later, and we still haven't heard from the owner.

We had to call the credit card company to get the charges reversed. Did they have any intention of letting us know that no flowers were delivered? returning our money? Apologizing? 

We got our money back, but we don't get a second chance to send our respects to the deceased.
They are new in town. I would say they are the best sushi place in East Nashville. I usually order avocado bomb, shrimp tempura, bento box, and rolls. Every thing was so good and fresh.
This place is awesome! Fresh food! Healthier options compared to the cheesesteaks and pizza. Similar to chipotle, but fresh food

I've been driving past this unassuming little joint for well over 30 years without once having enough curiosity to stop in.  I figured today was the day.  I had considered the nearby Bocella's Deli, but decided that could wait. T-bird had been in the queue long enough (and the last-minute recommendations from trusted members of this group sealed the deal) - Thanks.

I picked up my almost-fearless dining companion Azi, the better to divide and conquer.  As has become our custom, we split a  cheesesteak and roast pork and shared fries / onion rings.

The fried course was not noteworthy.  Hot, but nothing too special. The Thunderbird spice was spicy, and rings were crispy, but they were not standouts. Good solid, frozen carbs.

The sammies, on the the hand, were a hit. This is old-school Delco. They were extremely accommodating about our customizations (American AND Whiz, onions extra crispy on the steak.) Pork with sharp Provolone and fried long hots. Service was nothing less than "sweet."

We started on the steak. Lots of roughly chopped meat SWIMMING in cheese.  This was not a half and half American Whiz combo.. this was the full dose of each. Onions were crispy as asked.  Despite the liquid content of the molten cheese, the Conshy Bakery roll withstood the contents (though Azi had some challenges controlling the escape instincts of the slippery cheese-coated beef.) The steak was actually long strands..not chopped, but not plain slices like Pat's or Steve's. This is an exclusive technique and it works, showing off both taste and texture.

The pork came on a SEEDED roll (these were Conshy Bakery by the way) and was nothing less than succulent. The Provolone was gloriously melted.  The seasoned pork was tender as could be.  This is a holy grail pork sammy. They struck a balance somehow between the too-dry and  "overboard.". This could probably travel OK.

Will definitely return.

So I have never eaten at a place where I felt it deserved less than one star. The woman at the register was rude. I got the combo plate with teriyaki chicken, chicken katsu, macaroni salad and French fries. The chicken katsu was terrible and tasted as if it was fried in two week old oil. The teriyaki chicken was obviously made of fake chicken and had no flavor. The fries had black hard plastic pieces on them. Even my friends fries had them. The macaroni salad was worse than the stuff in boxes. Apparently salt or seasoning is the stuff that imaginary lands are made of because there wasn't an ounce of flavor. I would have rather licked the bottom of my shoe. At least it would taste the way I expect it to and should take. No one wore a hair net. Only the women wore uniforms. The black cook was out in the dining room talking to a customer he knew. I saw him in the reflection of the window digging in his pants. Like inside of them. Not the pockets. Where the underwear are. I really want my money back. Please do not waste time. I heard the location on speedway is better but don't take my word for it. Just avoid this place at all costs. Just eat bugs if you need to survive.

Hands down, the worst service I've ever had in Santa Barbara!!

This whole experience was a giant disappointment. I had been so excited to finally go to Hungry Cat since it had been recommended to me by multiple people on different occasions.. what a letdown! 

It started on a good note when my mom and I were sat by the very nice and accommodating hostess. From there it was all downhill. We sat in the dead center of the restaurant where we were ignored for the first 15-20 minutes! After trying to make eye contact with ANYONE, our waitress finally decided to ask what kind of water we would like. I'm sorry, but it is never, ever acceptable to sit at a table without water or some small form of acknowledgment for almost 20 whole minutes!!! We would have stood up and walked straight out of the restaurant if it hadn't been a busy night downtown and almost 8pm at this point. (Though we did have plenty of time to sit there and discuss our other options)

After we were finally recognized, not much improved. We continuously were left feeling abandoned with complete and utter lack of interest from anyone in the restaurant. This despicable serviced continued on until the check was finally dropped. 

The only reason for 2 stars instead of 1 is for the good food. However, no amount of incredible food could make up for our horribly disappointing experience.. it was all tainted. 

I will never return.

We ordered a feast for take-out on Father's Day.  Two apps, 6 different dinners and 2 Margarita quarts (Strawberry&Mango).  The order was ready on time, and we got most of it home without requiring reheating.  Everyone enjoyed their meals and Margaritas.  It was a welcome and different experience during these pandemic-times!
I'd never had Basque food until I came here but their's was delicious!
Very tasty and fresh, food was well packed and hot. Nice people who really appreciated my business, and nice small family business feel to it, I look forward to going back!
Last time. Place is filthy. And food was overcooked.  Filthy carpet and nasty tables.

I'm glad Cajé's expanding, but this is my least favorite Caje location. With cute, minimalistic decor, it's more of a grab and go type of coffee shop--good for a pick me up during your downtown shopping outing. There are no tables inside but some small end tables and chairs outside, which is great for people watching downtown. I wouldn't recommend studying here because there's not much space.

The Salty Cowboy specialty was just okay and a bit on the sweet side, but it was pretty with a gold dust sprinkling and star anise topping. The option for oat milk cost $1.25, which I think is slightly outrageous; sometimes, I don't want to pay $8+ for a coffee. Overall, I wouldn't go out of my way to come here, and I much prefer the Cajé on Arlington or Haley.

Every time I go in there the lines are so long, cashiers are extra slow. And the Manager guy with the Bald head is rude to his employees and customers. How are you as a boss yelling at cashiers in front of customers about being faster but won't even bother to help. The store was so much better ran when the female manager was there, bring her back. You can tell that the manager has no respect for the employees and in turn they are frustrated. I really feel bad for the staff there, with a boss like him. There's no wonder every time I come in there I see new faces, they probably quit because of his attitude. I've seen him close the office door when it's a line of customers, how does that show the staff that they are a team if he won't even help when it's needed.

All I can say is that might literally be the best burger I've had in my life. They get five stars on the basis of that alone. The waitress was a little bitchy, but not enough to ruin my experience. Everything else was pretty much what you'd expect from a main street restaurant in Manayunk. Chic, but not so much that you feel bad wearing shorts and t-shirt. Average prices, good location, etc, etc.

But the burger..........wow.

They're very consistent when it comes to food quality, it's always fresh, hot & crispy upon arrival. I like that they include a breadstick in platters. The food has plenty of flavor as well. The service is pretty good, prices are fair, definitely give it a shot. Support a local business. However, this is just a knit pick but...their barbecue sauce tastes absolutely nothing like barbecue, the smell, texture and flavor is like nothing I've ever tasted before, not a fan of the bbq. So a tip that I have, if you're someone who likes BBQ sauce, and need it as your dipping sauce, have some at home to go with your meal. Also, they generally take around 35-45 minutes for delivery, just keep that in mind. Overall besides those little things, great place!
We drove from Brooklyn to get an authentic Philly cheesesteak & to be honest it was just "alright". Ehh least we finally made it to Geno's.

Literally just left there.  YUCK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Rotten fish bowl??  The fish on our long rolls was so paper thin that we could actually see through it.  They use IMITATION crab in their rolls, too.  The rainbow roll was so pathetic.  Hardly ANY fish on it!!!!!!!!  When something called for cream cheese or avocado...that's all they used.  It was like, "EASY ON THE CREAM CHEESE!!!"  I came for sushi, after all. Then, the two guys next to us were ordering from the "off menu" which we knew nothing about.  They ordered a Mickey Mouse and Donald Duck which had HUGE pieces of sake...huge!!  We asked about it and the sushi chef told me, "Next time you can get."  Not this time??  Really?  Then, she took my stamp card and said that we don't use those anymore. Brought a new one back WITH LESS STAMPS ON IT THAN MY FIRST.  I left very angry and will not be back ever again.  EVER.  If you want great sushi, go the Kokopelli's at Circus Circus, Sushi Minato, or Tha Joint in Sparks.  DO NOT EAT AT THIS FISH TANK.
This place has amazing, authentic Mexican food. Everything we had was great! (Also get the churros!). Restaurant is BYO
Food and service  excellent.  This place is a little gem in Gretna. Staff very friendly and helpful. Have to try the banana beignets there awesome.

I'm sorry to have to report but the food is disappointing at this restaurant. The service for the meal was fine until we were at the end of our meal and our waitress just disappeared. We waited 15 to 20 minutes for her to return and give us a check. I am sure we will not be returning.

I've been to Golden Eagle many times, some for piercings and others for jewelry changes/other issues. Most times have been awesome - this is a no frills service (as it should be, you're getting stabbed).

However the last few times I've been there I've been unfortunately met with not as great quality of service. While everyone there is super friendly and welcoming, I'm not paying for personalities. I'm paying for an expertise and the skills required to execute it. 

That being said, I came in here for a conch jewelry change a week or so ago. Despite being super super busy I got in relatively quickly with Cameron working to put my jewelry in. She struggled a bit, but was able to get the jewelry on. Cool. Flash forward less than a week later and the back piece ended up falling off while I slept and I almost lost the piercing due to it closing so fast. Not ideal, but no big deal, I understand these are the "risks" associated with piercings and gave her the benefit of the doubt. 

I went in to get replace the missing jewelry and was met by Cameron. Once again, she struggled and this time she wasn't able to get the jewelry in at all. Josh had to step in and he was able to secure it within 10 seconds. Okay I thought, this is 2 for 2 now regarding her struggling with my jewelry. 

Today I went in to get some jewelry put in, some captive bead rings. Those pesky balls are annoying as heck so I figured I pay the minimal service fee to get them put in - I've done this before and Josh was able to put in all 3 super quickly, no more than 5 minutes, if that. Looking for that quick service again I popped in and was met my Cameron. A little apprehensive I figured I'd give her a third chance. Once again she struggled to secure a captive bead into the ring. I totally get these things are annoying but as a professional piercer it's unacceptable to have her fumbling around, dropping the balls on the ground and in my hair/clothing. Over 30 minutes later and she was only able to get one ball in. Really embarrassing honestly, I left upset and without the service I went in for.

This place is used to be so awesome it makes me sad to write a review like this. If you come here please try to get Josh. You'll get a pretty awesome piercing, despite his cold demeanor. Unfortunately the same can't be said for Cameron (although she is very frie

I've used Philadelphia Flower Co. on several occasions and have always been very happy with my orders and the service I've received. 

Before my wedding, I called to order arrangements for my mom/stepdad, dad/stepmom and fiancé's parents. When I asked if they delivered to NJ (where both sets of my parents live), they initially said no, but they made an exception since they are still relatively close to the city. The delivery charge was slightly higher, but worth it since I have been so happy with Philadelphia Flower Co. in the past. 

All of the flowers arrived the next day as promised. I was worried at first when my mom revealed that she had not been home all day, but there was a note in the mailbox that the flowers were left with our neighbor. All of the arrangements looked great and everyone was happy to have flowers in the house for the big weekend. I will definitely continue to call Philadelphia Flower Co. whenever the need arises!
They have the best pizza and great service!! My husband and I love going to Grimaldi's!!
My friends were in town so we went here? I booked a couple days in advance so we would have ours set and ready when we came. Loved it! We loved it so much we went again! Will be back again for sure!
Best ice cream in Hernando County.  It's wonderful and the staff is great.  This is a must try!

May 6, 2021 930 am, waitress Lakeshia. She is good, better than excellent. Woman of good taste as she likes her bacon like I do. Quick, accurate, fun to talk with. Food was fresh, hot and well cooked. Really appreciated the service, food and ambience.
Always good. Consistent and authentic.  I'm here at least three times a week.  Pho tastes great with all the fixings.
Great service at the bar. The duck wings are awesome. Bartender was knowledgeable and she provided great service.

A different establishment cancelled on me last minute and Star was able to take me in! I never thought getting waxed could be enjoyable until after this appointment. Honestly was the best experience I've had. A combination of wax and sugaring, she knew what to use and where. Literally - no pain. My mind was blown. Star has an awesome personality, too. My go to!
North tower is remodeled and feels good.  Thin walls and we could hear running upstairs and yelling in the halls.  Over all clean. Check in was a bit bland.

I ordered a bowl o gumbo and a shrimp po' boy sandwich. The soup was barely warm and devoid of flavor.  The sandwich was soggy and the grilled shrimp too salty. I was epically disappointed.  The atmosphere was decent but the waitresses seemed quite disorganized of course the restaurant was near capacity.

Having been to many many games I encourage you if you are in Nashville and are looking for something fun to do....GO TO A PREDATORS GAME!!!  Tickets range from a cheap ten bucks (limited number of these at the box office on game day) to expensive so you have your pick of what you want but for hockey games there is not really a bad seat in the house. Great atmosphere for all and it is family friendly (for the most part, please excuse the one or two drunks who are there and give the rest of the fans a bad rap...but these are usually quickly escorted out by the security). While Nashville might not be the best team in the NHL they do put out a pretty good team year after year on a low budget and compete very well. The arena does a great job with the games and gets a lot of fan interaction going and it makes for a fun time! 
If there is a down side to the games it is the parking downtown which can be tricky and expensive...but...if you research it online there are numerous options, some much cheaper than others, you just have to plan ahead. Max I have ever had to walk is a short two blocks. Go to a game and have fun!!!

Went here for the first time on Sunday and was mostly very pleasantly surprised. Overall it is a very nice place with terrific food. I recommend it.

First of all, finding any restaurant right by Stern's Wharf with semi-free parking (you do need to tip the valet) is a huge plus. Second, the location is terrific, looking out at Cabrillo and the beach.

Then there is the food. The shrimp and steak combo was stunning. In fact the steak tasted like it came from a fancier and more expensive steak house. The chicken pasta was also very nice (had it with the veggies). The sauce had a nice robust flavor. Finally, the desserts we shared at the table where terrific.

There are some drawbacks though. The first is that the place is way too loud. It actually hurts your ears at points in time. The second is that the place looks like it was built inside an old Denny's or Norm's. There is some neat decorating inside, but overall you still have a bit of a feeling that the Grand Slam breakfast should be available.

We did takeout for Easter dinner.  We purchased Chicken Marsala which was very good.  The part I found disturbing was what they charged for a loaf of Italian break.  $7.50 is a little excessive. This was just a case of gouging.  That is why we rated it a 3.  If the restaurant didn't get greedy it probably would have been a 5.

March 9, 2018 Friday - 5 PM for dinner
1 Adult

Atmosphere - 5 stars
Food - 5 stars
Service - 5 stars

Background - My wife is out of town and I am having pizza.

Atmosphere - Industrial and small.  Those two words explains the place.

Food
  Drinks - I had nothing, but soon Under the Rose will be open and you can get your beer fix there.

  Dinner - I love pepperoni pizza and the #10 is a double pepperoni.  You could not see the cheese with layers of pepperoni.  The red sauce was so light I wonder if it was actually there.  The dough was little thicker than a New York style pizza.  Crushed red peppers and oregano shakers are with the paper plates.  Wish they had the shakers on the table.

Service - Welcome when I came in.  Super friendly and informative.

Future - Sure.

My massage with Larry was really, really good. I prefer deep tissue, and he delivered. He is very intuitive, and speaking with him, discovered he is positive, wise, and very insightful, enabling him to effectively tune in and give a great, effective massage. I highly recommend him.

Excellent service and master craftsmanship. I was here for a conference and needed to get same day alterations on a pair of pants and dress. They were able to do both in record time. Later in the week when I found a gorgeous velvet dress on sale that almost fit, I decided to take a chance and buy it to see if this shop could alter it. Again, their work and promptness were truly exceptional. The dress fit like a glove after they tailored it. 
Their tailor's skill and attention to detail are hard to find, and I should know, I love fashion hunting so I have a tendency of buying outfits when I travel and then looking to get them altered later. Their prices reflect the very high quality of their work. Considering how skilled they are, I thought they were a good deal.

This place is fantastic. I had a Mango Maniac and loved it. The staff was friendly but quiet. A few things I didn't like was the time it took to make a smoothie, it was about 20 min after ordering. It was nice to relax but if I were in a hurry to be somewhere I wouldn't stop there to get a drink. I felt there wasn't a lot of energy in the room. It was really quiet and everyone was kind of sitting/standing around and not talking, which was a little awkward. I think if the music was a little louder or the staff was more talkative the energy would have changed a little. Those are my only complaints. I would definitely go back as the smoothies were worth the visit.

Unpopular opinion but I might actually like Lolita a little bit more than it's neighbor El Vez. Yes I know, how dare I speak ill of El Vez, but give Lolita a try and you'll see what I'm talking about. 

The chips and salsa are great and come with plantain chips and taro chips in addition to the usual corn chips. The enchiladas verde with mushrooms were awesome and I'm usually not the biggest mushroom fan. The food wasn't greasy and the portions were a good size. Most of the menu is gluten free and their fryer is dedicated gluten free so almost everything is fair game. It's always great to go to a place that is so knowledgeable and careful with dietary restrictions. 

Lolita is pretty small so make sure to make a reservation if you're going at a peak time and don't worry, your wallet won't take a big hit here, the prices are pretty reasonable!

Josh was amazibg and so so funny! We celebrated our dauggter Maria's 18th birthday. He was so cute! He  brought out a dessert with a candle! Love!!  We usually visit once a week now we have a personsl server and We wil be back for josh for sure!!!
BBQ Chicken Pizza and Beer... Enough said.

We had to wait for a table at the bar and spent $17 for 2 small mason jars (10 oz. used for all the drinks) of local beer (only 5 of 20 to choose from, they were out) while 25% of the tables marked "reserved" (handwritten on paper) were empty for the entire 1.5 hours that we were in the restaurant.  After we sat down, they served 2 other tables seated after us before even greeting us 15 minutes later.  When we stopped a server, she made it clear it wasn't her table and spent more time tracking down our server than it would have taken her to just bring us water.  I have no problem paying higher prices for atmosphere in addition to good food, but the decor is amateur, the menu sparse, the prices ridiculous for the portions.  The brisket Rubin was so greasy, I was nauseous after eating 1/2 the sandwich (3 bites).  The  8 french fries were cold when they were served and ice cold after another 10 minutes of waiting for ketchup (desperate for flavor) which was an odd homemade version of salted tomato paste. The first clue should have been when the server recommended a chopped up ham, turkey, onion and cheese sandwich at a smokehouse. I've never given a bad review in my life, but J&J's is a big disappointment.  It's basically bad pub food.  Perhaps the music venue will be successful, the speakers were definitely large enough to rock the block!
The place is very nice. I ordered Thai Hot Pot. It is not traditional Asia noodle. But it is good for this price. Make sure to order side dishes as the Pot is not big portion food.

The place has a great environment and music. Food is underwhelming. My burger was not cooked as ordered (and you'd expect that for a $12 burger) and based on the ordering method there is no recourse to raise the issue. I'd come back, but just for drinks and music.
What a great place. Best yogurt in town. Clean, reasonable prices, owner present, attention to detail, what more can I say!

Loved this place for breakfast. Our waiter was awesome and the food was the perfect taste and portion size. It's also conveniently in our hotel. It's worth going even if it's not connected to your hotel. Have to try dinner here now.

Anyone who rated more than 2 stars has never been to Rib Shack in Eagle. 

My visit tonight at BBQ4Life was my first. The food was barely warm and was definitely very cold by the time I was half way through. They only have 1 style of BBQ sauce on the table but sell several more flavors that were on display. 

The seating is on wood picnic tables like you use at a park. When I'm surging on higher priced BBQ, that's not what I would expect. 

There were several checks at our table. (Came with friends) And they ran our card on our friend's meal that was 1.5 times more expensive.

I was hoping for a better experience.

took 4 guests here for dinner and I was very happy with the ambience of the entire restaurant.   service was impeccable by all server's and very familiar with the dishes.  I have to say I have experienced many world class restaurants but this one had the most creative menu.  we were served complimentary appetizers with a mouse in an egg shell.  this was not enjoyed by all but I was impressed with the presentation and the unique flavour. 

keep in mind all portions are quite small but full of flavour.   in my opinion this is the best and most creative chef out there.  I never had ice cream with chili in it, a must try.  the only downfall is if you do not have a creative pallet or open to trying something new then you may be limited with the menu.

I am vegetarian and was happy that the server suggested some alterations that could be made to suit me.  I enjoyed the experience and recommend this restaurant if you want a posh or impress sort of  experience.

What an amazing day thanks to an amazing catering company!! We got married at a private venue and Rincon Catering was fabulous! They did our food, our rentals, and our day of planning, not to mention much, much more. Their professionalism and efficiency was top notch! We loved all the decor, the signage, and the way they put such detail into everything at the wedding. So beautiful!

We were so impressed at how clean the grounds were after the event. The home owner said she had never worked with such a thorough company!

Our friends and family have not stopped raving about the food and the overall smoothness of the evening.

We cannot thank them enough for making our wedding so seamless and wonderful!

Thank you, thank you, thank you!

In the office now due to chest pains. Not from Philadelphia so I came in as a new patient. So far the service from the greeters is slow. I learned that they do not do immunizations which is a new experience for me and I feel as though that should have been communicated over the phone when I inquired about becoming a new patient.  Apparently they send patients to the minute clinic @ CVS for immunizations.  Appt was scheduled for today @ 3:15 and is now 3:23. Waiting in the waiting room and this does not look like a place I want to revisit or call my primary care office. Will update this post after I've seen the doctor.

Update:
I was taken back into the room about 1 minute after my initial post so wait time was not bad. With the exclusion of the greeters (who were just average) all staff was extremely friendly & knowledgeable. The office does need to be invested in (new carpeting,  paint job,  larger rooms w/ sinks). And they are also not on the electronic system. Everything is done old fashioned (using paper) here which doesn't bother me too much. In short, this will be my primary temporarily just because with the amount of money I pay for healthcare, my primary office shouldnt be lacking in any capacity.

I was so excited to finally try your Plant City location last night, 12/16.  Imagine my displeasure as I stood in line and observed PEOPLE IN THE KITCHEN NOT WEARING MASKS or masks not covering the nose.  Also, the person putting food on the orders in the front line not wearing a mask appropriately.  I told the person making my order that I couldn't eat their food when they had such lack of care for their customers.  As I was leaving I met the manager outside coming back from O'Briens and explained to him what I had experienced and he apologized and stated all employees were to wear masks and he would take care of it.  I said "if all employees were to wear masks, when you were in the kitchen, why were you not wearing one?" He was one of those I saw only wearing 1/2 a mask.  I do not understand in a time where loved ones cannot be with people in the hospital or nursing homes, we cannot gather with our families for Christmas, so many are making so many sacrifices, why a business, especially a new one, would disrespect it's patrons in such a way.  You want me to consume your food, but you are not willing to make it safe for me to do so.  So many eateries are taking care, I think I'll be one of their patrons.

Not terrible, but very overrated.   We only had chicken things, which might explain the mediocrity.  The mole tastes like soy sauce.  There are several TV's playing daytime mexican gameshows.  Solid Horchata and salsa.
This place is absolutely legendary. Kid Rock shows up there a lot!! Also just a crazy 4 story bar with a different vibe on each floor. I'd consider it the best bar I've ever been to.
just wonderful.  service,  food and ambience.  this place has it all. shortcomings ...mmmm...that it is only open 3 days a week.
We stayed at a hotel near by. Walking around we happened upon this place. Probably the best food we had while in New Orleans. Food was great and cocktails on point.

I've changed my rating to "A-OK" because AAA called me a second time because they were concerned about my first Yelp review. The second person who called was empowered to make the issue right instead of just offering apologies. While I wouldn't say I'm a fan of this repair shop, I will say that AAA goes out of their way to make sure their customers are satisfied. That is above and beyond any repair shop I've been to before. And that emphasis on customer satisfaction is certainly worth something.

I hired Brooms N Buckets when I had gotten surgery back in September.  I was pretty much restricted to the couch or bed and couldn't attend to my typical cleaning routine....

  I was so impressed from the start:  the first phone call to ask what their availability was, Leslie (the owner) was accommodating, professional, and willing to fit me in last minute.  She went over the details and services of her business, asked me specifically what I needed done, and was very patient when I was trying to figure out what I may need (I had never hired a cleaning service before!)  I liked that she did not try to push me to add extra services beyond what I needed!  I am a grad student and this was definitely a splurge (but a WELL SPENT ONE!) Her sister was hired and arrived exactly on time.

I've never hired a cleaning service (my mother put a vacuum in my hand probably around the age of 4 lol) because I am very particular about what I like to be done.... Leslie's sister did such a fantastic and thorough cleaning.  I also had SO much laundry that needed to be done.  I was very impressed by the quality of her work and it was such a relief to not have to worry about taking care of my weekly cleaning while I was recovering.  

Both Leslie and her sister are extremely 
-- professional
-- hardworking, 
-- kind,
-- and provide a high quality service.

I will be hiring Brooms N Buckets again and I recommend their services to anyone here in NOLA.

So A+ to Brooms N Buckets!!!  Thank you Leslie!

This place has a lot of variety and product. Staff is friendly. But they are definitely overpriced. Higher than Lees Liquor and Total Wine. I do love the variety but they have beer that has been there since its opened. $39.99 for a 4 pack of a certain beer that hasnt moved since they brought it in. I would keep an eye out for expired product. Craft beer does have a shelf life! I stop in to try something new here and there but wouldn't purchase any liquor because of the price. They do have vape and other things. It is unique-ish and cool to look around at.

Had lunch today with two others.  We all had various burgers.  I did not like the burger.  Tasted and appeared to be the same as a frozen burger I could get at somewhere like Costco.  Overcooked.  Flat and hard around the edges.  Not much flavor.  Covered in great ingredients.  Not sure if bun was grilled but was ok.  French fries were generous but fairly ordinary.  Husband had the black bean burger and it was ok.  Mom had the plain Angus burger and it was the same burger patty as mine.  

Ice tea was bland and almost tasteless.  Refilled as needed.

Nice atmosphere with families and small groups.  Quiet until we were about to leave when they cranked up the music and we could no longer talk easily.

Service was excellent.

I really wanted to like this place :/. As a dairy sensitive and vegetarian individual, I'm always looking for dairy alternative ice cream. A friend told me about Cashew Cow and I was like excited to try out the ice cream. 
First the good: the consistency is about right, not too icy and still creamy. I like that it doesn't start melting right away like dairy ice cream does. Prices are fair for what you get (homemade nut-based ice cream and decent portion sizes)
Now the not so good: I was very underwhelmed by the flavor of the ice creams. I tried the coffee which was bitter and had no sweetness at all. I also tried the cookies and cream, which had the complete opposite issue- it was cloyingly sweet and had an artificial flavor and far too many cookies to ice cream. 
I didn't finish the ice cream, and that may be a first for me. I would consider returning if someone else wanted to go but maybe try a different flavor. Sadly still searching for the perfect non-dairy ice cream scoop

St Louis (my hometown which I love) has the mediocre-est Thai restaurants. Why? We tried lunch here and ordered a bunch of different dishes. It was ok but not up to the hype. Portions were small, ingredients were grocery-store quality, everything was just ok and bland. The interior seemed decrepit. The diners including us I guess all looked like middle-aged neoliberal clones. One competent and professional server was handling all the tables, so service was slow but not frustrating. I tasted and experienced nothing that would bring me back here.

Had New Years Eve dinner at FIORINO.
It was our fourth visit and best yet
Four beautiful courses including the finest lamb chops I've ever eaten.
There is not a better place to have a lovely Italian meal with a special someone !!!

This was such an awful experience, I actually signed up for yelp to leave this review. I have been a server/bartender for the past seven years and have never received such disrespect from fellow service industry personnel (we are in this together). This was a Monday night, 7/22 ( so check the schedule). The tall dark and handsome man was condescending and abrasive. Left his costumers feeling stupid for asking simple questions about the menu, while the bar was empty, so he had no excuse. His apathetic vibe left me feeling like I wanted to leave before I could even enjoy my beer. The bartender aside him (a nicer vibe but has been clearly following the disgusting apathetic energy of the other) wasn't much better. I grew up in this neighborhood and used to brag that this was my watering hole. I've been to this bar on multiple occasions since it's opening and I will never return. This bartender might attract certain regulars but it will NEVER bring back the type of costumers an owner should be seeking to gain. RUDE RUDE RUDE!!! Not a "gimmick" that works for this area. I am saddened to lose one of my favorite spots.

I'm sure that if Anthony's Pizzeria was in downtown St. Pete, or some other trendy, high-visibility area like 4th St, it would already be known as one of THE best NY/NJ-style Italian places in Tampa Bay, and not just for pizza!

I first tried Anthony's for the eggplant parm. Growing up in a predominantly Italian home, where Grandma Biagia not only made all her own pasta from scratch and by hand but was an eggplant cutlet artist, I've always been on the lookout for great eggplant. If the eggplant is really good and authentic, then everything else is likely to be. That's been my rule of thumb, anyway. Chef Rocco's eggplant is to die for -- delicious and al dente as it should be (not bland mush!). No surprise to me, then, that everything else I've ordered has been excellent. By the way, Rocco named his place Anthony's because that's his son's name. A very Italian thing to do.

I notice almost all of the reviews here are about his pizza, which also isn't surprising since the restaurant is called a "pizzeria" and there are so many great pizza selections. It's true that the pizza is first class -- unbelievable crust, fresh and generous toppings, not to mention the amazing Sunday to Thursday deal on a 20-inch version of one of these pies for only $7! But don't just stick with pizza. Everything else I've tried has been really good, too, and underpriced.

By the way, though I'm a native Floridian, my family comes from the New York-New Jersey area, and that means I also had a lot of NY/NJ-style Italian food on vacations all through childhood. Then, after undergrad at FSU, I lived in NYC for six years. I know the difference between good, bad, and middling in this style of Italian cooking.

The food at this restaurant is so good, and so reasonably priced, because Rocco is so good and caring. He puts his heart and soul into it. The first time I met him, I could see what a great guy he is. We talked. I found out that for many years he had multiple very popular, very successful Italian grills on the Jersey Shore. Then Hurricane Sandy came along and wiped them all out. He started over again here in St. Petersburg.

Last, no, I'm not connected with Rocco or with Anthony's Pizzeria in any other way than as a local customer. Try the food, do your own quality-price calculation, take a few minutes to get acquainted with Rocco, and then you'll understand why I'm enthusiastic this restaurant and its chef.
