And yes there were a few calls I received from her where I said it was not a good time for them to enter because it was often last minute and I had a one year old who was napping. I absolutely would not allow them to enter when I wasn't home, because I had much distrust for the manager herself. Back before she arrived, I often would allow entry when we weren't home to fix something because I knew the maintenance staff. This time it was random and different people each time. We also had no working dishwasher from November 2020 until the day we moved out this past June. We were promised back in Nov/Dec we would be receiving a new one and never did. We had numerous issues that I won't go into detail about such as broken blinds, incomplete and different shades of paint on the same wall, fridge that caused mold quickly, cabinet doors that didn't fully close, dining room track light being out for almost a year, screens with rips and tears, mailbox key and lock that continuously stuck and wouldn't lock, stinky stagnant water backing up into the dishwasher just to name a few. The pool furniture was confiscated and chained up during summer 2020 As if, this furniture that was baking in the sun all day, was somehow harboring Covid and like children we could not sit on a pool chair that we were in essence paying for. The water bill in my small apartment was more than $200 a month! Now, I live in a 2500 sqft house and my water bill is $100. Not to mention the rent in this place is astronomical for the so called "luxury" you receive. So if a shabby, leaky apartment with greasy old appliances, amenities that you can only use when they say so, and a unprofessional manager who has the "how dare you bother me, you lowly resident" attitude is LUXURY in your eyes, then this is the place for you. If not, RUN as fast as you can to the Treetops next door.

I will be glad to change my review if they will either mail my photos or email me back. Spent 3 hours and $125 getting pictures done....not as much fun as my daughter imagined, but it was the whole experience, so that is OK. We live 45 min away, so were not too happy about being required to drive back on a week night to view photos. Well, the day of the viewing someone called and offered an online session...great! A number of nice photos. Well, we bought over $500 worth of photos and paid in full. We were told 2-3 weeks. All good.....until we had to contact customer service.....there's literally none. A month after, we had no photos, so I sent a quick email to enquire. No reply in a week. So, sent a second email.....included my order number....lady replied she needed my daughter's info/school......ok, sent that.....she replies back that she will check with production. Then I got an email saying the issue was closed and how did I like the customer service. HUH? Husband tried to call a few days later.....one hour on hold....no answer. Now over six weeks...still no photos, no one will email back.

Don't get the mussels, they are mostly empty shells or very small. Service was very good. 
Should never served the mussels, the kitchen should have caught that. They didn't do anything about it when I mentioned it.

Well it was really cold out today so I wanted to go walk around so antique mall is right around tge corner. Great place. Like a garage sale or fleamarket but higher end like antiques. I killed two hours in here feeling only lile 20mins. Theres so much I wanted to get. Great conversation pieces everywhere. Will be back no questions.

We are very pleased with Mesquite vet... our neighborhood spot... we are new to Catalina, and our pets were all up to date from the previous place we lived in. Then our kitty got into a rattlesnake den. Mesquite vet got us in immediately- and Prince, who would be better called Rambo is back to normal. Then I got five puppies... (I'm crazy)... and Dr. Whiting and Mesquite vet have helped us with our puppies too. We are happy, and grateful to have an awesome neighborhood vet.

Had a really nice meal here - their hummus w cauliflower is delicious;  lentil soup perfectly made and spiced;  and lamb chops on bed of roasted veggies that was perfect. Plus Jamal is quite a character and so funny. We'll definite be adding this to our short list of frequently visited. 

4-4-19
We've continued to eat regularly. Always great!  One of our favorite restaurants in NOLA. Tonite had the hummus with cauliflower, the fatoush salad and the Magazine burger. Boy - the cauliflower is so delish, and the burger is one of the best in town. Who would expect that?  I just added two pictures but we were too ready for the burger to pause for a shot of it!!

My neighbor buddy and I take turns picking up the tab once a week for lunch and we've found ourselves back at Red Robin quite often I love the  their Banzai Burger - incredible flavor.  The garlic fries with dippin sauce - so tasty.  We were seated in Lori's section the first visit and she made us feel like old friends so we've stuck with her. Something special about a person like her that knows your beverage of choice and almost has it on the table as you sit down. The manager is a heck of a nice fellow too. This is as upscale a restaurant specializing in burgers as you will find!

Awesome sweets and great service 

Donuts incomparable and TRUE comfort food 
Keep up the great work and efforts

Divine Designs has the most friendly, and courteous staff I have ever had the pleasure of meeting. All of the hair stylists are extremely knowledgeable and very skilled. My hair isn't exactly the easiest to handle, but it was no problem for them. I even purchased a gift card for my mother to the salon, she couldn't stop raving about her experience. My husband works two two jobs, both are hard on his back, so I send him to the spa regularly for messages. They keep very good records of past appointments, so if you don't remember the type of service you had previously or who provided that service, don't worry. They make it so easy! I won't go anywhere else for any of my beauty/pampering needs.

Quite a few variety of beers although not very impressive. Most of them taste similar (i.e. watered down). Also had brisket sandwich which had very thin slices of brisket topped of with cheddar which seemed a bit strange to me.

I didn't expect to give Han Dynasty 2 stars. I think it has a very good reputation but today's lunch was a big disappointment.  Our primary complaint was the poor service. My lunch partner asked our waiter for a fresh plate and didn't even mention it was because of the hair in his food.  The waiter took the plate with an annoyed look and never returned (we finally grabbed a plate from another table). Various other waitstaff walked by periodically and gave us funny looks but never asked us if we need anything and didn't bring the check until we asked twice, even though there were customers waited to be seated.

The food was fine, but really pretty greasy.  I'd eat it again if it were half the price.

For fried chicken this is as good as it gets in NOLA, yes it doesn't have massive pots of premade mashed potatos, or rice from last night either, and thats what I loved about it. 5 pieces (Half chicken) for less than $4, and it taste just like Grandma's.  No sit down dining but as fast as the service is you can pick up lunch and still have time to eat it in the park on your lunch break.
Love Wawa!  The deli bar and coffee are the best!  What's more?  The prices!  Very affordable!

I would recommend never coming to this place, but if you have to never let the woman Rosa touch your hair. I told her a two on the sides and an inch and half off the top, she takes the razor and cuts halfway up the top of my head. Literally an inch and a half of the top of my head she cut like it was the side. Sat through the rest of it to see if she could salvage it but the was no chance. Even the spots she shaved with the two were uneven. I went home and buzzed it all off right away, absolutely the worst haircut I've ever gotten in my life.

The worse hookah and service. Never again. Server had an attitude when we complained about the small orange head that they charged extra $6 for. Suppose to have a decent size orange to keep the hookah moist. Food is ok.

We are the 3rd tenants in the building since 2014.

Microwave shoots sparks catches fire occasionally.

Dishwasher broken (3 months and still no professional fix) and drywall repair staring at me for 2 months waiting to be painted.

Constant battle for the elevator between a food business, hotel next door sharing the elevator and rented common space to people whom don't live in the building and taking over the common space for renters.

This ones important: FIRE ALARM HAD GONE OFF AT ALL HOURS OF THE DAY, 6x in a year!!! With no FIRE OR EMERGENCY!!! The drill calls for all residents to exit the building no matter the weather or time of day/night. Up to 45 min to 1+ hour to re enter the building. Meanwhile, the alarm constantly beeps until the FD says it's clear.

NOT WORTH THE PRICE!!!!!

This place is terrible. The so-called Margaritas were basically lemonade and cheap tequila. I had a "beef" burrito which was 3/4 rice and a little beef. It was not fresh and had been heated on a grill.  The rice was over-cooked and the refried beans were soupy and had no flavor. The place has no atmosphere at all.  No decor.  Just a big room with tables.  Very disappointing.

Three stars mainly for the horrible service. I don't know if they're understaffed or just bad with service. Went here 2 nights in one weekend. The first night it literally took over an hour for our food to come out. It took 20 minutes to get drinks (water). The owner felt our frustration and comped the meal. Very stellar on his part and his wife, the chef personally came out to apologize. The food was simply wonderful with the exception of salty pork chops and bad gumbo! So, we overlooked that experience and returned a second time. The attitudes of the servers is beyond me...really callous. It may just be frustration with an overworked system but don't take it out on me! Again, we waited forever for our food. Again, the food was really good (except the gumbo, it tastes pre-packaged) but we were afraid to order anything else after dinner (like dessert) for fear that it would take forever to come out and we would be yelled at because the kitchen was closing. I'm from NOLA and even though I was visiting, I know this is not our form of true southern hospitality! They need to get together with their servers and work on improving service time and customer experience. Until then, I recommend you call ahead and order your food to go!!

Decent place for go karting...I mean, what's not to love about a place like this!

It was clean, and a fair amount of value, which is what you'll normally pay elsewhere...

Jerk chicken is one of those pleasures in life that will leave you hunched over in abdominal pain the next day from the amount of spice on it, but thats a price worth paying. The oxtail was good too, but the star for me was always the chicken with a side of candied yams and greens.

Definitely a tourist spot. We went right after watching fireworks for New Years in Jackson square. This place is right at bourbon street. The service was prompt and right on, Although the bathrooms are nasty there are water on the floor everywhere. The music rotates from country, hip hop, pop, rock etc. they make the stage as karaoke place. So you can test your how good your drunk self sing. They have male and female host. I like the male host, he make the crowd Cheer and hype without using excessive curse words. The female on the opposite curse every other word, it's almost she has little word bank in her brain except for profanity or curse words. The drinks were pretty decent and the price comes between $4-$7.
We had a really good time in this place.

I hate to be critical of the Food Co-op, because we really like it. We decided to try their café for lunch and were really disappointed. Service is non existent as apparently its common here to take 20 minutes to make one sandwich. Any more than three people in line and you wont be able eat during your lunch hour. Cost us 20 dollars for some oily soup and a French dip sandwich that smelled bad and tasted worse. Seats are uncomfortable, which is common these days, so who needs more of that? Sorry, but this place is on the never again list.
Consistently good service and food. There is a WH less than a mile from my house that I won't go to again. I may have to drive 3 miles to get to it, but Sidco Waffle House hasn't disappointed me yet.

I have to say the food is good and the people are always friendly. The only reason why I did not give them 5 starts is because someone from the back of the restaurant came to the counter with no mask. Also someone who worked there came in and went to the employee table with no mask. What the hell! There is a pandemic going on and the Governor had to make it official again to wear masks. I will be back after a vaccination.

Stone Soup Company was instantly inviting. I later realized that it was the owner that approached us outside and opened the door. But what I was immediately drawn in by was how good it smelled inside.

It was exhausting walking up and down 7th Ave in search for a good place to eat for lunch. We stopped at a few places here and there, and one restaurant in particular smelled so badly of burned oil, that I couldn't even stay a while to look at the menu. Shortly after, we happened across The Stone Soup Company. It was such a relief to be greeted the way we were.

Ilya Goldberg (the owner) has a heart for the community and good sense of what is quality food. It's really cool seeing someone take initiative in creating a solution for those who go hungry. For every cup of soup sold one is donated to the homeless. And all of it is made from scratch.

I usually hate the smell of seafood, but the lobster I sensed was so pleasing that I had to have whatever it was. So I had their Lobsta Chowda and it was the best seafood soup I've had in a while.

If you get a chance to eat here, definitely try their Cubemanti Sandwich. It's inspired by the Primanti Bros. You have the choice to put whatever freshly sliced meat you want, but just ask for the chef's choice. He'll hook you up. 

I'm definitely going back for more

This is probably one of my favorite dessert places in philly! The cafe is modern and cute. The desserts are beautifully presented and there's a huge variety. They are made in house and have both an European (think French or Italian) and an Asian flair. My go to is always chocolate so I've gotten something chocolate related every time. They have fruit based/tiramisu/panna cotta/cheesecakes/lava cakes/sizzling ice creams, so something for any type of dessert craving! They also have a full coffee/tea bar to fit any type of caffeine need as well as matcha drinks which seem to be a huge fad right now. My most recent visit, I tried the chocolate peanut butter mousse/cake. It was amazing! I don't tend to like green tea but I want to go back and try some of the matcha items. I also want to try the milk foam beverages! Perfect place to stop by after you've had a meal in the area and are craving something sweet. Will be back soon!
My husband and I got the crispy shrimp and it was okay. It was softer than crispy, but not bad. We just know we have had better.
Best place to stay in town!!!  Service is outstanding. The rooms are great. The spa suite you can't beat. Best value in town hands down!!!
Good food and good service. Lovely family owned restaurant! Wonton soup and bbq ribs are amazing! Best chili oil in town! Sesame beef is delicious.

You have to look past the copious amount of stuffed animals that are stapled to the celling and the sometimes uninvolved staff. They have a nice selection of men's clothing, which some shops tend to forget. However, I had a hard time finding anything that spoke to me in the women's wear. I feel as if similar options are available at Goodwill or Salvation Army.

Emm, $14 for an iced latte and avocado toast? And by avocado toast I mean a small bit of avocado on one toast. That wasn't really toasted. It was tasty, but come on. I get avocados are expensive, but this was a little pricey. The iced latte wasn't anything out of this world either, unfortunatly.

However, the vibe here is cool. They are roasting beans so the smell kicks you in the nostrils as you are walking in through the parking lot. A bunch of creative types with laptops open, chatting, or just hanging out. It's all windows, so the sun shines in and the place is nice and bright.

But just as I started working with my counterparts - within 4 minutes we all start groaning, huffing, puffing and sighing. The WiFi was SUPER slow. Like old school AOL internet slow. Pages took a lifetime to load, some having to be refreshed just to load. It was frustrating.

The staff was friendly enough. It's full of hip employees, with tats, colored hair - and most of them smiling. The gent that took my order was great - had some awesome energy and super friendly. The server/busser wasn't that nice. She just grabbed plates off the table without really saying much. She looks like she needed a cup of coffee, if only she had somewhere close by to perk her up.

Extremely disappointed with my experience at this Shari's location. When my family and I got to our table, it took a while for us to get our drinks. Then it took a while for us to even put our order in. After we ordered, we waited a good 20-30 minutes for our food (keep in mind, there was only three of us eating). When we received our food, it was downright awful. Mine and my wife's eggs were ice cold, our hash browns were ice cold, and our daughters pancakes were tough and over cooked. My family wouldn't have minded the wait if the food was enjoyable, but we couldn't even finish it. So, with our breakfast hardly even touched, we waited for the check to pay just so we could get out of that terrible diner. Our waitress never even brought the check. We asked for it twice and even stood at the front of the restaurant just trying to pay, but nobody gave one to us. So we dropped  $20 on the table and got out of there. We will never be returning to this Shari's location. If there was an option for it, our rate would be negative 5 stars.

This place doesnt equal a 3.5 star hotel. It's similar to a motel 6. It has the smallest bedroom and bathroom that I've ever seen. The towels appeared very old, and I had to pay $10 for parking. It's right next to the freeway and is very noisy.

Love their pizza I am from the east coast and this is the closest to philly pizza and New York  because   the  slices  are  big and the cheese is good quality they are expensive  but  you get what you pay for my lg pizza with  cheese is no more  than $20.00  and on 135 they always  let me use coupons  which makes it  cheaper  ty Luca pizza on 135  only
We ordered online and picked up sandwiches for our beach day. The veggie was delicious! Anything with the that bread and olive spread would be wonderful!!!

In the beginning, I must admit I think I was skeptical. Picture this: 3 20-30 something, reasonable attractive ladies loose in New Orleans for 3 days, stuffing Cajun delights, fried green beans, and crawfish pie, topped off with dark chocolate pecan pie down our snouts for 2.5 days, the last place you think about going is a place called the Green Goddess.
At least one of us had done some research, prior to the beginning, and she happens to be a vegetarian so this is how we came by this amazing work of art called a Restaurant. 
 
The place is very small with a few court yard seats if the weather is not sweltering or cold. It was, so we sat in side. It took about an hour and a half to get seated, so we went across the street and had some good wine prior to dinner. I would recommend the wait if you have time. The ambiance is not the greatest: Its funky and you feel like you're eating in the kitchen of a funky Portland diner, but again the food is SERIOUSLY the best meal I think I have ever eaten; mostly, because it was so unexpected. 

 I started with a grilled cheese made with Irish Porter Cheddar cheese, made with Guinness, and pear butter on thick wholegrain bread. When it came out, I thought it was burnt. I was a bit tipsy and asked the waiter (who happened to be the chef) if he could cook it again. He assured me it wasn't burnt (but by this time I would have eaten it if it was charred to a brick like state). It was amazing, and unique. 

Miss M ordered the Golden Beet Ravioli which is a Golden Beet "Ravioli" filled with cheese and pomegranate molasses. There were only 4 of these small, thin delicacies on a plate and served with a Borolo. I cannot tell you the explosion of flavor that occurred after having one of these things with a sip of the correctly paired wine. It was better than.....well you know. Really. And I am not joking. 

We soon got the run down from the chefs on their concept on the art of cooking, and simplicity. I cannot wait to go back the next time I head to the Big Easy. 

I would give it 5 stars but the wait and the seating, however worth the wait is still a little excessive when you are starving.

The char grilled oysters were just ok. They were not as "meaty" as others we have had. A few were not very fresh and they were not grilled enough. The shrimp bisque had potential to be good but it was a bit too salty. I had the Gulf Fish Amandine with poached crab meat on top. The crab meat was dry and the creole meunière was not very good. The fish was lightly breaded, which I wasn't expecting, and was overly salty. My husband had the Grilled Pork Chop with oyster french  bread dressing and ham-hock gravy. The chop itself was acceptable but the oyster dressing was fishy.  Our server took a very long time to acknowledge our presence. He was not friendly nor attentive. This was not the experience or meal we were hoping for.
We went to Charlie's and the food was delicious. Service was fast. Had a great dinner with friends.

This dollar tree is just ok. It usually very messy. Customer service is ok.  I have seen so many nice dollar trees on you tube! They carry crafts,books, and so much more name brand  items. Wish our stores would get same products!

The customer service is fantastic! 

The drivers know the city and are true professionals and I love the lady (Sharon) who answers the phone in the morning. Full disclosure-I've left my home twice since March 19th. Both times for medical appointments. One day I took four taxis and on another day I took two. All six times I called 215-666-6666 and a nice lady (Sharon) answered my calls. By the sound of her voice it's the same nice lady and she always treats me with kindness and dignity. She's very re-assuring and I've to admit that this pandemic has turned me into a nervous person who is easily rattled by what I've seen on the two occasions I've left home. The only place outside my home I felt safe was in this taxi services' cabs which are clean, sanitized and all of the drivers wear masks.

I know I just told you that the taxis are clean but they really are and they send a text message when they arrive and everyone is kind and patient. 

What more could you want?

I've been coming here for a year and it's probably my favorite "pizza" joint in all the land.

And not for the pizza. It's actually a half Indian, half pizza joint. And you know they're serving legit-ness, amazing, flavorful, spicy food when most of the customers are South Asian!

The grilled veggie sub is one of my favorite vegetarian meals of all-time. Potato based with shredded broccoli, peppers, and spices. And THE SPICES! Obviously south asian based with a kick. All served on a hoagie roll - super flavors drench the inside of the bread.

However, I feel that the signature dish is the spicy chicken sub. I haven't eaten it often enough but my family loves it.

Staff is friendly - constantly busy because of the demand. As a fellow immigrant family, we love seeing them succeed. It's a great local, unique pizza joint in an era where pizza joints are both ubiquitous and disappearing. Awesome spot and we'll be dropping in for years to come.

Bryce Carney is the best car salesperson I have ever worked with.  He worked hard to get the deal done and saw it through to the end.  I appreciate his hard work and dedication getting me into my dream car! Thank you Bryce and thank you Dolan Toyota!
The service was terrible here I waited 10 minutes for a coffee and.....it was wrong, such a disgusting disappointment. I know this isn't the best coffee, but it could at least be consistent

The food here is delicious but customer service is not great. My 85 year old Aunt got asked for her ID when she ordered a glass of wine.  85 years old!! I understand the need to be careful but this just seemed silly and awkward. Also, my Dad ordered the Roland seafood stew which he has ordered dozens of times. It came out with 0 crab claws which is normally included in the dish.  We asked our waiter, who was very polite, to inquire. He came back and stated the stew does indeed include crab claws and he was very sorry my Dad's dish didn't have any.  Not a one.  We asked if they could give him another dish of it then and the cook had told our waiter he would NOT. He wasn't asking for addition claws, just to have SOME.  For a table that spent close to $200 and would always take family from out of town there.... It seemed rude and unnecessary.   But I guess since people will go there anyway.... They don't need to please the patrons anymore.

Fresh & BEAUTIFUL flowers from this florist!!!!
The customer service was amazing & very personable.

Give them a try...YOU will not be disappointed!!!

I was so happy when a culvers opened in my neck of the woods!  What I like about Culvers is the selection.  Their butter burgers are delicious and my husband loves that they have fish.  It is also refreshing to have a fast food joint that offers mashed potatoes, cole slaw, green beans, and a side salad just to name a few.  It is also nice to have a fast food joint that offers burgers as well as chicken and fish.  I had my first sweet potato fries and they were fantastic!!!  Their frozen custard is also soooo good!  
I will have to try their root beer based on the reviews on here.  In addition the service is great - they are so friendly!
This is simply not your average fast food joint!!

Worst service ever. Disgusting bathrooms. Food items missing and food that was requested with no cheese, still had cheese. Their idea of brisket is ridiculous, worst I've ever had actually. I had to ask 4 times to finally get a refill on our drinks and even then, I asked the hostess and she had to bring us drinks because our server was no where to be found. We complained to the manager but nothing really changed. He offered us 1/2 off our bill. Not sure if even that was worth it. Stay clear of this particular location. This Chili's is poorly run.

Came here a couple of weeks ago to try this place out. This was around 7:30 on a Thursday and they were closed. Figured I should give it a second try, so I called them today to make sure they were open before driving over there again. They said, "well we might close early if it's not busy." Sorry but I don't support businesses that inconvenience customers by choosing to open or close when they feel like it and not stick to their normal hours of operation. There are plenty of other good Indian restaurants in the area. Don't waste your time.

Hands down one of the Best Philly Cheesesteak sandwiches i've ever had... one of thee BEST sandwiches i've ever had period!! The bar-b-q wings... to die for! My most favorite place in all of Philadelphia. MAN i can't stress enough, how Amazing the food is here. Especially the ones i've mentioned!! I love vegan/vegetarian food like this... So Good!
Excellent salads and breakfast foods. Duck gumbo was especially goid. Casual seating. Great service. Music and tvs playing. Easy parking.

Pretty good pizza, wings, and breadsticks. There's something about Pizza Hut's crust that makes me crave it every couple of years... that level of greasiness and crunch... mmm...

I ordered online for contactless curbside
The pizzahut.com website listed the wrong number to call, but the one here on yelp worked.

Chain resturants normally have the impact on me that garlic does on a vampire. I retreat with haste at the very idea.  Yet I have eaten in more chains in the six months since moving to this  area than in the sixteen years combined before.  I'm not kidding. 

Most of those experiences were woeful so I walked into Noodles & Company with low expectations.  Imagine my surprise to find myself a fan!  I found  friendly people, efficient order and service model, good food using fresh ingredients and served at the table in real dishes, not plastic, along with fair prices.  

THE GREETING:
My husband and I paused at the menu board.  An employee welcomed us warmly to ask if this was our first visit.  When we said yes, he went on, "I hope you'll let me take about 30 seconds and I'd like to explain how this works at Noodles and Company..."

My knee jerk thought was "I do not need a tutorial on ordering fast food" but then I realized I was being jerk.  Because this man was so engaging and as it turns out I really did find the overview useful!

HOW IT WORKS IN A NUTSHELL FOR "NOODLE-NEWBIES".

1.  Look at the menu board to choose your entree.  The focus is noodle bowls, but there are also three or four salads, and equal number of soups and also a few sandwiches plus a flatbread.  

There are dozen-ish items in noodle bowl options listed with photos in rows.  They are logically arranged so narrowing down  to answer, "What sounds good  today?" is pretty easy.

Each of the vertical rows is a regional / ethnic specialty.  First Row - Mediterranean / Italian.  Second Row - Asia / Chinese, Thai, Japanese.  Third Row - American / although with specialties on that list like Stroganoff or Spaghetti with meatballs.

The top item in each row is the best seller in that specialty.

Worth mentioning that all of the noodle dishes start out as vegetarian.   Not to get ahead of myself because in everything is connected to everything else mode, this will lead us to steps three through five.

2. Choose large or small bowl size.  The large is nearly twice as much food for only about a buck and a quarter more money.  Being lighter eaters, we thought the small was swell.  Being types to support the underdog, we chose from lower rows of options.  Being in the mood for SE Asian flavors, we chose rice noodle dishes, one with a bit of kick from a peanut sauce and the other with a slightly sweet coconut curry.

3. Mosey to the counter to place your order with a friendly staff person.  This is when you can order protein to add to your dish if you want to, from tofu to chicken, pork, beef, meatballs or shrimp to top it off.  You can also decide if you want soup or side salad added to your order of noodles for a pittance extra charge.  

4.  Pay for your meal and notice at how little it costs.  All the noodle dishes start out at the same price for small and then another for large.  It is the addition of proteins that makes the price go up.  A couple of the noodle bowls most typically ordered with a protein, like spaghetti and meatballs or beef stroganoff, are priced with the meat included.  But you can subtract that (mushroom stroganoff anyone) with cost deducted too.

5.  The friendly counter person will give you a number.  Take it a table in the clean, brightly lit space (or on the patio in nice weather) and wait on one of the nice service staff to bring you your meal on real dishes with real cutlery.  While you wait you can read the sign about the company's commitment to holding down waste by using dishes that can be rewashed and not end up in landfills.  (Read fast, the food is quick to arrive.)   I despise plastic containers and utensils in fast food places.  The real deal here was a lovely surprise. 

6.  Tuck into those noodles and enjoy fresh flavors and veggies cooked just so for pretty-darned-good food while you think about hatl you'll order next time, since you know there will be one.  And just when you thought it couldn't get better for a fast casual food model it does when you find you don't need to 'bus your own'.  Ta dum!

DIETS:
All items have calorie counts posted and that sure does give one pause about how super diet friendly some of these dishes are while others can bust the diet bank.  Also, gluten free items on menu.

FUN:
For entertainment, stand by the soda machine, which is also the water dispensary, and see how long it takes first timers to figure out how it works.  Which won't be long as it seems the been there before timers are eager to help others learn how the cool contraption functions.  Social bonding experience.

SERVICE:
It is worth saying that every employee here conveyed a sense they were glad we were there and they hoped we'd come back. Delightful.

THIS N THAT:

1) PARKING:  The lot is shared by a couple of other businesses, including Blaze pizza.  

2) ACCESSIBILITY:  Accessible parking:  Level in.  Standard height seating.  Ample aisleway

If I could give zero I would.
I made a service call for my sofa and I was set up for today between 10am and 2pm.
I called the store service department and they confirmed that I am on Chris's route today. Then the service guy(Chris) called and he said that the warehouse didn't put the part in his truck. I then called the store back and spoke to the warehouse and they told me that it was the service persons duty to get the product on his truck before they leave. (At least Chris is who they told me my techs name was.)

Not only am I out of another day of work because they can't place an item that was order months ago into his truck, which is covered under standard warranty but they won't even do anything to the tech because of his mistake.
I think some changes need to happen with the service department maybe not the other two service guys but Chris is definitely not someone I would keep. 
No telling how many other people this has been done to that hasn't came forward but my time is just as valuable as the next customers. This is of-coarse probably not going to happen on Thursday which is the day they rescheduled me to. We will see. 

The warehouse told me he couldn't go back to them to pick it up, even though we were the first stop and it was around 10am  but he lied and said that they left it off his truck and when I called him back about this. he denied everything.
I have been going here for the past few months and have had great success with haircuts.  Kathy and Ann have both done a great job.  I highly recommend them.

Confused my package for someone else's mine was not delivered because it was still in truck. The guy on customer care was really nice and Sid it would be fixed and will be delivered later in the day. Was right but when I got home my package was not even inside the mailbox nor was on my porch but out by the street next to my mailbox. Someone could have stolen this but thank god I have honest neighbors

I ate too fast to take a photo, but I had the veggie Somosa plate and the falafel plate. YUM! I have been vegetarian for 15 years and have eaten a lot of falafel-
This was seriously the best falafel I've ever had, and the owners of this market couldn't be nicer. I can't wait to be a regular here!!

Seriously, is there anything really to say about the co op?  I won't shop anywhere else in the SB area for groceries (unless I need something Japanese, in which case I hit up Nikka).  All of the organic, locally grown produce that I need is here.

The people who work here are also awesome.  They usually know what they're talking about and can give helpful suggestions about different products.

Maybe I'll get to work here someday, but for now, I'll just enjoy the great selection that the co op has.

May I ask why you bother to shop anywhere else for groceries?

We had our first visit to Elmwood Saturday night. I love the space, very open and loft like and the kitchen is glassed off so you can see the chefs in action. We started with 2 delicious cocktails and the WAGYU SHORT RIB BEEF JERKY SKEWERS. I almost didnt get them because of the "jerky" term (I don't like chewy meat) but so glad we did. There was nothing jerky about them. They were so tender and had a fantastic teriyaki sauce. Our main courses, I had the ELMWOOD BURGER. It was cooked perfectly with a spicy Korean bbq sauce and I had the twice cooked potatoes. They came with a wonderful dipping sauce that was a little curry, a little ketchupy and a little something else, not sure but it was really good. My friend had the SPICE-ROASTED POUSSIN which is actually roasted chicken. It comes in a sauce of muhammara, aleppo, cumin and coriander. Oh man, it was soooooo good and tender
 We could not stop talking about the flavors and spices. This is a gem in Maplewood and we are already planning a second trip.

Horrible!
I was in the area for a course. Had a hankering for Indian food. All the other local Indian restaurants were closed on a Monday. 
I took a chance on this place. 
The food was tasteless and extremely spicy. For appetizer there were vegetable spring rolls. Tasteless. I could have bought them in the freezer aisle of my grocery store. There were about 4 veg dishes, chicken tikka and a chicken biryani. All extremely tasteless and spicy. There were Gulab Jamun for dessert that were probably made from a Gits kit. Disgusting. 
It was $10.66 down the drain. 
Wish I could give it 0 stars. 
btw, No a la carte menu available for a weekday lunch.

As the name suggests you'll find quite the beer and wine selection here. I found myself visiting for the first time during a beer tasting. Picked-up a bottle Brooklyn Black Op and a growler of the Brooklyn Brew master special. 

Spacious liquor store that knows their stuff. A bit slow in growler pouring, but good beer takes time. Isn't cheap either. But the selection here is pretty deep.  Will look at the wine next time!

Just watch out for possible trains if you are approaching here from 99th. It always seems like those ones take forever!

This place used to be owned by a super sweet family. Then I go in one day, and I'm halfway through my pedi before I realize all the furniture and paint is different. Then other workers began showing up and I realized the place was being run by new people, mostly men. The man working on me was nice and did a decent job despite seeming very unsure of himself. As I was sitting at dryer--kicking myself for not being a more loyal patron to the nice family--the owner went out of his way to amusedly point out to me that their giant fish in the fish tank were eating one another. I was not amused. It was incredibly eerie.

Very enjoyable experience at Trax on a busy Saturday night.   They easily accommodated my party of 8 and provide great service.  The use of the old train station is very cool, but not many tables so reservations are probably needed on most nights.  Excellent menu with added specials that all sounded good.  My table tried almost all the appetizers with the Brussel sprouts and bacon stealing the show.  Tomatoes with the mozzarella appetizer were a bit disappointing but it's November so hard to find good ones, especially locally.
Main courses were solid.  The lamb chops were nicely cooked and the accompanying mashed potatoes were outstanding. Being a BYOB was a plus too.

ate here on Sat night - food is good here but the service was terrible.  15 minutes to get acknowledged and then at the end it took just as long to get a check. Waiter forgot he has already given us the bill.  Kinda weird and a darn shame because the place could be great.

The food and shopping are good but many of the people that work here are less than friendly. But my main gripe is terminal F.  There has to be a better way to get to and from this area.  The shuttles are horrible, the people that work in the shuttle areas are worse, and who wants to walk and have to go through security again!?  FIX IT!

I belong to this gym for its extreme convenience. It's awesome when I want to go do a quick cardio workout or get some machine work in. There are no real classes offered...just equipment. They are 24/7 so it's nice to know its there whenever I need it. 

It's kind of warehouse-y which I'm not the biggest fan of. It's not a very motivational atmosphere in my mind due to this, but like I said, it's an inexpensive convenience that I enjoy having.
This place is bomb!! And Whitney is the best server. Definitely recommend it! The French toast was the best I have ever had!!

I absolutely love this place. Hands down the best place in Tampa to get your nails done. The pedicures are amazing!! I drive all the way from Apollo Beach just to come here because it is so worth it!!

Why eat pizza when you visit New Orleans? Magazine Pizza is why. 

The only reasons this is not five stars​ were the long delivery time and communication. When you order online, an automated email receipt​ is sent along with a message delivery will be in 60 mins and maybe longer during peak times. That seemed unusually​ long for an estimate but it was true. The order​ took so long (1hr 20m) that the restaurant had closed. When the delivery man showed up I was putting on clothes to grab snacks from the lobby. It would be helpful it the restaurant could provide updates especially when it's near closing time so customers know the order is still coming.

TIme and communication aside, this pizza is very close to the best I've had, ever.  Fresh Mozzarella​ and Tomato base atop a near perfect crust was the last thing I expected from this "it's late I'll take whatever deliver​​ to my hotel" option. The quality and taste of the pizza coupled with their complimentary ranch dressing made the wait worthwhile.
Great food with great atmosphere. Staff were friendly and informative. Would check out fajita bowl with steak

I'm giving this place 4-star since I ate here once. I ordered a salad and it was good enough.
The service was not over the top great but I was fine.
Been there two times. First was good and wasn't overcharged. Second time, they charged me 6.00 for a bean burrito and said all the burritos are one price. No thank you!!!

I would happily eat here every day of my life. I went with a large group (10 people) that included a vegetarian, some very picky eaters and some food snobs (myself included) and we all found something we absolutely loved. Not one of us had a bad review of our food. I had the Dat Chick and that bacon cheddar ranch fries. Both were to die for. I love the large menu and the laid back atomsphere. Plus the staff was super nice and accommodating considering we were asking lots of questions and had so many orders. The only downside is that there isn't one in Miami!

I really am disappointed. Went through the drive through late nite. I was the only person in line. The food was cold. Cold fries. Cold nuggets. Cold burger. I wish there was something better closer to home. It was depressing

Delicious! Everything you want is on the menu. It's spacious. It's clean. The environment makes you feel like you're right at home with mamma cooking you food. You will wait a little to be seated but it's worth the wait.

The food is pretty good here - especially if you compare it to the new Los Patios location on Hwy 67 on the southwest side of Indy.   The service is much better, too.

Prices are about what you expect for this type of Americanized Mexican restaurant in Indiana.   $7-10 for an entree.    All the standards are here (tacos, burritos, enchiladas, quesadillas) with no frills (beans and rice come with everything).   The food is seasoned and cooked well.

I'm not really sure where the name Los Patios comes from, but I didn't see any outdoor seating at all.   My best guess is that the interior decor is supposed to recreate the feeling that you are dining outdoors somewhere in Mexico.

My family and I arrived for Sunday brunch here and were seated right away. The server was great and attentive, however the food served was horrific. My 8 year old daughter got sausage with her and eggs and they were completely raw inside. We let the server know and she removed it from our bill. My mother then found a giant black hair in her drink and when she told the server there was no sympathy and the drink was just removed from the table with no communication. We received our bill and went to pay and spoke with a manager who explained that the items that were wrong were removed from the bill and that was the end of the conversation. We've been regular customers at the mosaic cafe dos on la cholla for years and will never be going back to either restaurant due to their lack of empathy.
They told me $500 to replace my distributor. A buddy and I just did it with a $79 part from Amazon, a little research, and a couple beers. 30 minutes. I'm not kidding.

Fast and convenient.. They use milk powder for most of their drinks and has that Taiwanese taste (milk powder). They don't have much fruit options, but what they have is the BEST tapioca pearls in town. You can have lemonade, and still taste the pearls. 

People I've seen there: mostly asians and teenagers.
Not worth the price. Its a nice view but its a small space and you will probably be bored after 10 minutes.
Great company to work for - always has amazing collection of items to choose from, everyone will be satisfied! Also great for accommodating large parties, unlike most local restaurants

I rolled up to Reno in my Whip Black Beauty to see My Friend Big Mike the Teflon Don Of Spanish Springs. 


When I arrived I was famished!!! Hungry like a Hound Dawg LoL. 



Mike suggested Moreno's Mexican Restaurant .
So we jumped into his low key whip and rolled to Moreno's.


They are located in a Strip Mall so there's plenty of parking!!!



We parked in the lot and rolled  in. We were Greeted and Seated and presented with Menus.


We have Similar taste in Food so we both ordered the Steak Chaquilles .



They brought us our food in Ten Minutes .

Chaquilles  was basically Steak and Egg  Nachos with melted cheese on top!!!



It was Different!!! It was very Filling ,but a little bland!!!!



It was ok but hindsight being 20/20 I would order something different next time!!!


I would probably give Moreno's another try next time I'm in Reno!!!!

This place is absolutely gorgeous and stands out among all the other restaurants/venues in Downtown Nashville.. the staff, food , drinks EVERYTHING is top notch!! You feel like you are stepping into another city when you walk in. Nashville needed Nashville Underground

Sarcastic waiter... fish was spoiled on the seafood platter.. fries were old and turned, had a weird taste. This is my first review in life and I'm over 40. We seemed to be bothering the manager. However, he did take it off the bill. We can hear him loudly tell the other employees "the food was spoiled" and laughing it off. As we walked out, the manager stared us down and got quiet as if they were talking about us. The outside is littered with trash and debris. I expected more... I do understand the pandemic situation but that's still no excuse for not being hospitable towards customers. Hopefully they get it together. I won't go back anytime soon.
For a brand new restaurant in the first week there were minimum mistakes. The food was amazing along with the service. Will definitely be back soon for more

Have visited several times since my last review and things have improved. The music was not as loud during early dinner hours. They do several items very well, fantastic Calamari, tender and crispy, lightly breaded, fried peppers. The Pot Pie, Fish & Chips and the Shepard's Pie are really good. Good sandwiches and good beer selection. Also a really good bottled and rotating draft beer selection. The negative, the burgers are ok, thick and tasty but the meat doesn't even come close to covering the dried out bun, an inch or two of bun left after the meat is gone.

their steak n egg breakfast sandwich is the best. awesome hangover food and they delivery. not only do they deliver their deli food but they will also deliver anything they sell in the store, which is also like a mini convenient store.very little seating available though

Noah's Caring Hands Animal Hospital at Geist is my go to vets office for my cats. The location is great and the staff is always helpful and friendly. 

They have some of the best hours that allow for after work and Saturday appointments, which can be tough to get last minute depending on your appointment need. They offer the Science Diet Food. If they don't have what you need, they can order it for you and you can get it relatively fast. 

I also like the fact that they have the cats boarding area completely separated from the dogs. They offer two options for cats, a Kitty Condo or Townhouse which is a bit more. The townhouse allows for the cat to view the staff at all times, as it is a window that faces the checkin/checkout counter. So if you have a shy/timid cat like mine, the Condo is the way to go.

It terms for exam rooms, they do have two special rooms for cats. One of them has a window facing the wooded outside area where the cats can view the birds. They also have a small house where the cats can hide while they wait.

Overall, your pets are in good hands. One of the downsides to this office is that Amex is not accepted.

My dad and I have been coming to this Qdoba for years and never have I seen such a rude incompetent manager. Her name was Angie and she refused to serve me a beer when that was all we could have due to a water boil order.  I had two valid forms of ID including a military ID. She was unable to do simple math and refused to believe me and made a big deal and was utterly and entirely rude to me. Never have I been so disappointed with the customer service there.  The saving grace was the food and the newly renovated building that I hadn't seen yet. Was happy to be able to go now that I was finally home and she ruined this experience for not only me but the two friends I brought with me. Angie needs to be retrained on customer service and or stripped of her manager position for her lack of customer experience and simple competence. My birthday is 1/30/1996.
Wonderful service and wonderful cuisine. Left overs were still amazing for days after!

I love firehouse subs! They have so many varieties of sandwiches plus the bread is always so soft. I enjoy coming to the Castleton location because the staff is always so friendly. When I ask for suggestions you can best believe they will explain each sandwich and tell you about any likes or even dislikes.  (No lies). Never had a bad meal yet.  They will always get my vote for the best subs hands down! 

My only  is they don't have coupons. Lol. I love deals and feed quite a few people.

We found this place when we first moved to the oldsmar/plan harbor area and now it's our #1 go to when we have family and friends in town. It's nicely price, not expensive. Their beer menu is fabulous with several rotating taps.  and Cobb Salad, buffalo cauliflower, Mac & cheese and flat breads are our favorites. Eat in or carry out. Food and portions are always delicious. We've been here dozens of times and will keep going back.

Rose Tailor Shop has recently changed ownership. The previous owner, an Asian lady who retired, was good at her craft, reliable and her prices were reasonable. The new owners, a couple, don't seem as friendly but their craftsmanship is good and they seem reliable. Their prices however were a bit of a shock. For two pair of men's pants I was charged $143. That included taking in the waist 1", hemming the legs and attaching 9 belt loops to each pair of pants. Other than the price being a bit high everything else seemed fine.

Quality varies widely from one dish to another.
The margarita mix is awesome and I recommend bringing a good bottle of tequila to mix with it!
The BBQ pulled pork platter is delicious. Order it. Everything about it was incredible, and I wish that I was the one who had ordered it (instead of my wife).

The sweet potato burrito is supposedly a favorite here, but I was disappointed in it. When I first read the description I thought that it was an odd combination but then thought it could be "just crazy enough to work". I was right the first time though. It was just not a pleasant mixture of flavors and textures. Imagine what it sounds like; that's exactly what it tastes like. (FYI I am a huge fan of sweet potatoes normally)

The restaurant itself is very cramped. We had a very difficult time fitting our baby's stroller up the stairs(no ramp) and had to have the host store it in the basement. There was also barely any room for the high chair they provided. It was kind of a spectacle getting ourselves settled in because of this. I wouldn't recommend this place for kids at all, especially if you have any parenting equipment with you. Unless the place is slow at the moment, people will stare while you get situated.

A fabulous cafe. I'm sad that it took me until their one year anniversary to discover this gem in Kennett Square! The smoothie and specialty item I got this morning were delicious!! They are handling the curbside very nicely and I will definitely be back! It is absolutely worth a visit!

We have tried this place twice and both times the service was horrible. The waitress took too long to bring out our food, but we were patient. After 25 minutes, we asked if our rolls were coming out soon, and she gave us a complex look. She forgot to put them in and seems to be suspicious that we had actually eaten them and were lying to her. Up to the point that she started counting the half eaten rolls on the table, asking each of us how many we had eaten, and checking her booklet multiple times. In the end, she realized he had forgotten them and did not even apologize. The second time around the service was even worse. our rolls were brought out within 20-25 minute gaps. Our group could not share our rolls because of their horrendously slow service. In addition, the waitress was annoyed every time we had to ask for drink refills. the most annoying thing was when she was more concerned if we were paying together or separately as she sat us down. The miso soup and edamame were served cold. They took the edamame back and supposedly heat it up, yet it was still cold or even more cold than before. I would not recommend this place at all. You're better off at Sushi Garden.

I have been here two times now and both times was happy with my dining experience. The portion sizes are generous, the food is well prepared, and the menu is diverse. There is plenty to choose from to make everyone happy from the healthy eater to those looking to indulge. I have had the turkey burger and the spinach and blueberry salad. Both were good, although the salad was lacking on the protein component a bit; I would have enjoyed more chicken. My boyfriend got the Salmon BLT this time and while he enjoyed it, he felt it was a bit burnt. Others in our party got the pulled pork which they raved about and one got a cod sandwich which she declared was one of the best she had! She said it was not to heavily breaded and there was plenty of fish. 

As for the beer selection, you can't go wrong. They have an excellent selection that is on tap and rotate through a couple of seasonal beers. This time, my boyfriend and I took home a growler of the Jubilee Irish Red Ale and we can't wait to drink it! 

Overall a good place, I would recommend it to anyone and will definitely be back.

Amanda did an amazing job altering my sister's wedding gown and 5 bridesmaids dresses! She added cups and bustling and had to completely rework the top of her dress. She was super accommodating. She came to us and allowed us to have a little dress try on party while she fitted us. The fit was perfect for all and the turn around time was fast. I highly recommend her!!

Really missed it for me at this place.... I ordered tacos to go last night and was not impressed. The reason for two stars instead of 1 was the green salsa that comes with them is very good. I got the chicken avocado/verde tacos and steak tacos (6 total) I only ate 2 and threw the rest away unfortunately. The chicken was fatty and barely filled the tortilla at all (see photo) and the steak completely dry and lacked flavor. I really hate leaving bad reviews like this but I feel like I needed to share....

While it is inexpensive gas, there is one pump there (1&2) that regardless of cash or credit charges you credit card price.  I've tried both sides of the pump and found that it shows the credit price even after I pay cash inside and press the button.  I went inside and said - it's showing credit card price, she said, oh it will change over. NO it does not.  And what it is showing on the pump is what we are charged, regardless of the BS that they say, oh it changes over.  The other pumps work just fine, just the 1 & 2 are off.  Fix the pump.  I think it's actually illegal but I don't know who to report it to.

We ordered three things
Coconut shrimp: Amazing... A absolute must try
Lobster roll special: it was OK , a little on the dry side also not very flavourful.
Fried combo: really good and fresh seafood

This what the plates looked like after eating

The staff was nice. Looks family owned! The portion looked small but was actually huge as we couldn't even finish our regular sized bowls! The flavor was wonderful. Our favorite meats were the octopus and bbq eel. The salmon looked fresh but it didn't taste as fresh as I had hoped...nevertheless still good. Avocado was not extra which is a bonus! Also came with toppings Like crab salad and seaweed salad which are usually an additional cost!! However, the rice wasnt very good and didn't seem like the typical sushi rice.. it was kind of hard as opposed to soft and aromatic. Would come back again though.

I don't understand the reviews here. Give a rave review and then 4 stars?
Best Taqueria in Tucson, but we're blessed with many. (Karamelo King gets the silver). I'm not really a chkn guy, but their taco is the best. The place is spotlessly clean always. I don't understand why they can't serve a breakfast burrito after 10:30-- how hard can that be.

Want to feel good about where you live go north 2 blocks, then you'll want to stop at Lim Bong's across the street, while you pat yourself on the back. Back in the day Juanitos gave you half an avocado for $.75. Everything you put in your mouth is better if it includes lime, avocado, or mint. I'm done here.

We came here with a group of people on a dinner meeting.    Our group was going to Ruth Chris, but on learning I was vegan, chose this place.  And it was a good choice.  

Service was excellent.  We were promptly seated.  Noise level was not too bad, though the place was very lively.  One small unfortunate note, no vegan appetizers (there are vegetarian ones).  I do not downrate them for that, how I eat is my problem, not theirs!  But on the positive, they have some awesome bread served with a spicy oil.  Any place that serves bread without just butter being the only option, is awesome to me.

A good bar selection.  We tossed back a few.  

The options for a vegan are pretty limited.  As in very limited.  But as long as they have one thing I can eat that I want, I am happy.  And they did.  The grilled tofu was amazing.  You have to do things well, to just serve some grilled tofu and have it come off as well as it did.  The tofu is served with some grilled veggies and an amazing wellington made from butternut squash and wild mushrooms. Yum.  The house salad was excellent also.

So great place.  Great food.  Great service.  Three thumbs up from me.
We've been coming here about once a week for a smoothie recently, and I can't say enough about how much we love the smoothies and the service. They go above and beyond!

Been here twice, ordered the vegetarian spinach wrap both times. The first time we dined in the restaurant it was delicious and tasted very fresh and healthy. The second time we ordered online for pick-up and it didn't taste very fresh... They also didn't pay attention to the order as they put in ingredients we asked to omit. I think they made the food immediately and then just left it out to sit for a half hour, because the online ordering makes you have the pick-up time be at least a half hour later. Overall I would never do pick-up again here but I would totally dine in again.

Easily my new fave cupcake spot. Stopped here on the way to our hotel across the way. The owner was nice in letting us taste cakes and frosting. The margarita frosting was delicious. It had a key lime taste going that was a perfect balance of sweet with a little tang. I tasted the red velvet cupcake, but it was not as flavorful as I prefer. Still good and moist, though. The strawberry cupcake was so yummy!! I purchased the turtle cheesecake without having sampled it. I was not disappointed. The cheesecake was not overly sweet.  It had a creamy consistency that was not too dense. The turtle toppings were as expected and that is what gave it the sweet factor.

My son enjoyed the oatmeal cookie pie and my husband smashed the margarita mini cakes which included strawberry and lime flavors.

Service was great by all and great cakes. Hope the store in Illinois can live up to this high standard.

I came back home to the Philadelphia area for a long needed visit and had no idea what type of organic specialty grocery stores were nearby.  After an extensive Yelp search, looked like Martindale's was the clear winner for selection, price and variety.
     The produce section employees were extremely helpful and knowledgeable about origin, flavors, and recommendations.  Curious about an new apple type? Just ask and you shall receive a sample taste.  I even located my favorite Bulletproof Coffee, Cold Brew and Collagen Bars, WoW thought I would never find my local LA product line.  The vetting of each item is extensive and I instinctively trust their selections.  
     Prepare for higher prices than Whole Foods and Trader Joes.  Despite the additional cost, still recommend for one of the best local markets for  quality produce, meat, supplements and service with a smile.

We came by for our last hurricane treat as we finally have power. We had a coffee malt and Small cookies and cream. They were both pretty good. 

The staff was very friendly and it looked clean inside. It is a walk up ice cream shop and tables out side. Took ours to go and will be back by when in the area.

We got the reference from my parents who have been taking their dog here for years.  We wouldn't go anywhere else - the staff is wonderful!  They are very friendly and accommodating and do a great job every time and our dog always leaves with his tail wagging.  I also like the fact this place has the small home town feel and truly enjoy giving them our business!  Keep up the great work guys!
WOW! I am blown away with this place. It's SO GOOD. And Gino the Filipino was hilarious

I feel lucky to have a Filiberto's in Oro Valley. Bonus is they have a drive through. I think it will catch on in time because it is orders of magnitude better than the other drive through taco place nearby. I have been a few times and the food is delicious and consistently prepared. The salsa bar is kept clean and fresh which is a nice change from other places. The nice thing about this location is that everything in the kitchen and dining room is new and super clean. The staff is very professional and detail oriented. It still has the old weird restrooms from the location's prior duty as a Carl's Jr and I hope they manage the sewer odors better than Carl's Jr did.

We had our chimney rebuilt due to a leak coming inside the attic space from the chimney. Jamison stated we need a rebuilt chimney to be sure the leak would be resolved. After the work was done we noticed new water stains on the bathroom ceiling and saw that the chimney still leaked. Called Jamison and they stated it was the roof. However our roof was fine but we decided just in case to get the roof done. The chimney still leaked and they would not address it. They just would not take any responsibility for their work. We also got a chimney liner and was sent a letter a year later stating if we did not get chimney care yearly the warranty would be voided.

I almost don't want to review this place, because it's right around the corner from me and apparently hasn't yet been descended upon by the brunch legions.  But alas, praise is deserved.

My girlfriend and I arrived at noon on a sunny and unusually warm February Sunday to find a small, brightly colored, yet half-empty restaurant.  Our waiter was very polite and actually unusually formal for the neighborhood.  He asked if we had a reservation.  We did not, but were seated right away.

I started with a cappuccino, the lady with a chai latte.  My cappuccino was fantastic, the best I've had in Fishtown (I'll spare you my La Colombe rant). It was on par with Hub Bub and Parc.  The chai latte was a bit mildly seasoned, it smelled better than it tasted.

Wow, the menu was slightly intimidating.  The French Toast has a scoop of coffee ice cream on it. Two smoked salmon breakfast dishes.  There was a lot to take in, but fortunately I had a cappuccino to assist me.

I eventually went with a Croque Monsieur with fried egg, and she chose poached  eggs benedict topped with smoked salmon.  Both were served as open-faced sandwiches with a side of homemade potato chips.  The sandwiches were a bit difficult to hack into with the butter knives we were given.  My sandwich was pretty much what I expected, which is fine by me.  The chips were seasoned with herbs and caramelized onions which was a nice touch.  I will say I prefer smoked salmon cold, and when served atop eggs benedict it is not.  So I wasn't a big fan of the bite I stole from my girlfriend's dish.

Why not, we ponied up for a raspberry tart dessert.  It was large and seriously chocolatey.  I don't regret it.

Other tables near us had BYO champagne.  The waiter kept bottles in the back on ice and was attentive to return with said bottle to refill drained glasses.

I guess I must comment on the tipping thing.  Tipping is not required but yet not discouraged. Honestly I like the idea but when you go against cultural convention in such an ambiguous way it's hard to know what to do.  We enjoyed our meal and tipped 10% when I would ordinarily tip close to 20%.  Did we overtip? Undertip? Who knows.

Overall, a really nice Sunday brunch experience, and for the time being you don't have to wait an hour for a table.

Really great service and innovative menu. Tonight we had the black bean salad with Boston lettuce; delicious red fish entree with collard greens; fries; 2 cocktails: tail feather and something with lemon and st germain; and carrot cake with cinnamon ice cream. Outstanding food, and a beautiful second location for Toup's!

Horrible. My fiancée tried to go here for her bachelorette party, specifically the PBR bar. Even though her entire wedding party, and even me, tried to email every contact from EVERY bar on their website, they were turned away at the door. They had more than 6 women in one party and they were actually not just turned away, the bouncers were very disrespectful. I'm glad I wasn't actually with them. 

I used to go to company events here all the time, but you won't see me frequenting there again. The last time my company had the entire place rented out until 8:30 and they called "last call" at 8:10 and would give anyone waters, saying they were too busy.

It's a great concept with horrible service and poorly executed.

This is one of many restaurants around town run by the Cunningham Group (others: Bru, Stone Creek, Boulder Creek, Bru) so if you have been to any of the others you know what to expect.  Slick space, stone floor, dark and intimate.   Food is consistent across the board.  Beautifully presented and cooked well by the seasoned staff.   However, the last time I was here, the caesar salad disappointed me.   It tasted really bitter for some reason.   I'll give them a mulligan for that, though, as my chicken velvet soup was excellent.   Almost as good as the version the other, more famous, place in town serves.

The coffee (Americano) tasted bold but had a aftertaste of synthetic coffee. 
The bathroom was dirty and had no paper towels. Service was OK, just OK though. 
Nothing to write home about.

Surprisingly I really liked this place. We stumbled upon it last minute. We all ordered the corn and crab bisque, duck empanadas, fried green tomatoes, fried alligator, and the Taste of new Orleans plate. 

4/5 on the bisque and duck empanadas. The soup was creamy and well balanced, and it really hit the spot.

after six months of anticipation, we got to GREKO last night. I have five words :
under seasoned, over priced, and loud. 
1.  I had lamb pita and subbed the village salad for fries due to allergies.  Feta on salad was good.   Lamb was bland, pita was tough. 

2.  Restaurant was maybe 1/4 full, but the volume of music combined with low ceilings and cinderblock walls made conversation nearly impossible.   I guess this makes for good customer turnover, but I couldn't stand that noise level for a whole beer.  

Overall, we were all underwhelmed and more than a little disappointed.   Not a place to add to the regular rotation.

I came to St. Louis from Chicago for business and we were in dire need of good, strong and delicious coffee. I yelped Bosnian coffee and found this place. Although the name is not Bosnian by any means, the moment you walk in, you feel the Bosnian atmosphere and you most certainly hear the Bosnian chatter and music. 

This place was not difficult to find but if you're an outsider like myself, it may be unusual to pass through a number of side streets to come here from the Hilton at the Ballpark. Parking was accessible, available on the street next to the restaurant or a block away. The street was extremely quiet at that time but the neighborhood is well known for being a Bosnian neighborhood. 

Our server was Semir and he is absolutely wonderful!! We decided to sit outside and he welcomed us in very graciously, made sure that our seats had cushions and that the sun wasn't in our eyes. We all ordered cappuccinos but then decided to get some appetizers since we were expected to be at a bigger dinner later. 

We ordered: 
1. Goat Cheese Fritters- wow!! I didn't get a chance to take photos since our eyes were as hungry as our stomachs. It comes in a serving plate of four with tomatoes and balsamic seasoning at the bottom and the fried goat cheese fritters on the top. High recommend scooping some of the tomatoes and placing them over the fritters and allowing the balsamic to drip over the fritters before eating it, it is so delicious!! The balsamic really complimented the goat cheese, giving it that extra kick it needs. This was my favorite dish. 

2. Shrimp Neum- this was sooo good that I actually thought I was in Croatia for a second! The appetizer came with about six large shrimp but they are really large shrimp. The shrimp were cooked to perfection before being placed in with wine sauce and tomatoes and sprinkled with Parmesan. It was really good. I'm not crazy for heavy sauce but this sauce was so good that once the shrimp was gone, I scraped the remainder of the sauce with bread. The plate was literally wiped clean! If you're a seafood lover, highly recommend! 

3. Bosnian pastries: this dish is basically the Bosnian version of pierogi. It's triangle pieces of dough stuffed with beef. If you ask me, there could have been more beef because the heavy whipping really overpowers the beef. That or the beef needs to be seasoned better! You get about 6-7 of those homemade Bosnian beef pierogi's.

Semir was very attentive to us, he kept checking in with us and making sure other tables were being served as well. The prices are very decent but the quality of the food stands out above all. I haven't tasted quality food like that in a long time! My family and I cannot wait to return to St. Louis again and come back here for dinner!!

Great pizza and wings.  Relaxed comfortable environment.  Beer selection is perfect, not to many choices, six drafts with local selections and miscellaneous bottled craft beer like Stone and Rogue. 
I agree with the comments that the sauce could use a little kick, I felt like salting mine (but didn't!).  The crust is thin and crunchy, but still has some softness to it.  
We had the wings with the garlic knots and while each was really good alone, together it was something special.  The wing sauce had a kick to it and dragging the knots through the wing sauce was killer.  Reminded me of the old Semenzas  in Reno.
I'm looking forward to going back and trying some sandwiches.

FINALLY NW Tucson has a decent quality sushi joint.  Recently opened in 2011 sushi cortaro is already building a good name for itself.  They offer 2 menus, an all you can eat menu for twenty bucks or a traditional menu.  The all you can eat menu is one of the best deals going in Tucson.  The quality and selection is very good and Fei. The sushi chef doesn't skimp, cheat, or play any of the games that other all you can eat sushi restaurants do in Tucson.

While the place is still very new service on my visits has been outstanding.

I am sure ill be a regular.
Came from Houston to New Orleans for the first time with friends, read reviews about this place and went two nights in a row. Both times were a great turn out good music and right on Bourbon street.

This hotel sadly missed the mark on so many accounts. The lack of cleanliness, poor staff, and room smelling like pure cigarette smoke were the "highlights" of my stay. I would 100% never come here again. Two stars for the fact of the restaurant inside was good.

This place is fantastic! I went based on Yelp reviews and was not disappointed. The heel on my favorite pair of ankle boots snapped TOTALLY in half. Villa's not only fixed that heel, they fixed the other heel, which was chipped, and shined them and made the pair look almost brand new. All for $20, and in a day and a half. Amazing, and definitely recommended.

The takoyaki balls were one of my food adventures for the summer.  I first tried them in June and I loved them.  Went back in July with my wife and I continued to love them.  Went back a few days ago and probably had the best takoyaki in 3 visits.  I liked them all.  The octupus, spicey shrimp and the sweet and sour were my favorites.  The crab c ake and the barbecue were also done well.  I think the chef- owner works hard to please his customers.  His wife is very friendly, easy going and aims to please.
We also tried the yakosobi noodles, which were good.  The Japanese potato salad was very good.
I think it is an interesting place, small and quaint.  The food is very different from any other restaurant.  
Be adventuresome and take a trip to the streets of Japan.

I was in the neighborhood and hungry, the place looked nice so I walked in and sat down. It wasn't until I opened the menu was that I realized this place did not serve meat. Even though I'm not a vegetarian, I eat more vegetables than most vegans so this wasn't too much of a stretch for me. To play it safe, I let the waitress suggest my order. I got a club sandwich- it was great and I would come in again. Didn't miss meat at all during my meal. The place was hop and the service was very friendly. Good job!

Once upon a time, there was a time - a time long long (but actually not too long) ago, before moving to the NY area, I lived in a world in which I had not ever experienced Mister Softee.

My soft serve came from buildings that did not sit on wheels, often touting flashy promotions, a seemingly endless array of new ice cream type products, and a fixed address.

One day I came to NYC, a visitor.  Naive in demeanor yet confident in spirit, I ventured through the most populated of areas, experiencing a variety of food options, always (foolishly) engaging with anyone that looked my way, never pondering the motives behind the amazing tour bus deals, CDs with no labels, or very pointed "Hey, do you like Human Rights?" type questions, in which "no thank you" isn't really an answer that makes sense.

In one of those early visits, as if David Blane himself was working me with invisible strings, a soft serve twist cone with chocolate sprinkles presented itself to me.

It was amazing.  It was delicious.  It was my favorite.  

I now associate Mister Softee with all the good things about New York. 

It is a treat among treats; consistent no matter which truck you encounter, and no matter which way you order it...you have made the right decision.

If I didn't live in NJ I would probably indulge my fatty fatty lardo soft serve inner-brain cortex (that's the scientific name) and run outside to find one right now, given i've spent 20 minutes typing about it.

We love our Q7 and have had this dealership do all the checkups and maintenance.  They are so very accommodating and go the extra mile to give exceptional customer service.   Robert was our service coordinator and he is exceptional.  He kept us in the loop and was great at explaining all the details.  Thanks Robert.

I've only had the pizza a taglio but it's so good that it merits 5 stars. No where else in Philly can I get pizza a taglio done right. It tastes as close as it can to pizza a taglio picked up in the streets of Rome.

It's kind of funny for an SFBA native, but I'm really enjoying my work trips to Reno specifically because of the food.

Today, I was craving a bowl of 牛肉麵, and the cold, windy weather was amping that feeling into overdrive.  I walked the extra few blocks through the bitingly-freezing wind to come to 101 instead of just stopping at Kwok's like a sane person would have.

The soup broth had great depth and was full of both umami and various aromatics. I could taste orange peel, star anise, cinnamon, etc. The multiple large chunks of beef were chopstick tender and had very little fat. Noodles were nicely chewy.

I've been here a couple of times before and have generally stuck with the 三杯鸡. That's good too.

Only not bumping up to a five because the capsaicin levels are a bit tepid.

They refused to return a gift (cost of $18.99), even for store credit or an even exchange, because I did not have a receipt. I was told to get the credit card number of the gift giver so they could look up the transaction if I wanted to return the item. The manager in Brentwood was incredibly rude and snotty about it, including walking away from me while I was talking to her.

Really good. Quite humorous observing tourists getting insulted by the supervisor just trying to keep the line moving. Worst sin is holding the door open, OMG! Then the ridiculous questions....anyway. Just order a cheesesteak and be happy people, this isn't the second coming of a gourmet dinner. Do some online research beforehand.
The sandwich is awesome. Really. Roll is so soft, beef is excellent, hot, and cheese just right. I sat at the counter and enjoyed ticking this one off the list. Waitress was very polite and kept the counter spotless, which demonstrates her attention to detail.

Came to Nashville for a
