They didn't take my address or my cell number.  All they had was the caller ID when I called to set the appointment. I called at 5:15pm and was told he is almost finished and they would call me.  After 7 hours I went to pick up my baby.  They never called me and it was hitting 8pm!  I was told he wasn't ready yet.  I waited in their store and they finally said he was ready at 8:20pm.  He was given a bath and a little trim.  Groomer said it always takes 7 hours to groom a dog in her experience.  She also said no one told her I wanted a poodle cut.  She offered for him to come back the next day but no way would I ever let them groom him again.  They never apologized for running so late, or not calling me to keep me informed. I did pay and told them they lost my business.  Worst experience I ever had with a grooming salon.  With their customer service they most likely will be closing soon.

What can I say... that spicy honey changed my life. I wanna smother it over my every meal. Don't get me wrong, everything I've eaten from the Eagle was above par. And everything is served family style so expect leftovers if it's just you and a friend. Chopped salad, exactly how I like my salads: lots o' toppings and a little bit o' lettuce, not the other way around. Succotash, sweet potato crock, spoon bread (more like swoon bread, amirite?), fries (with aioli, try them!), collard greens, and Mac & cheese. All worth the money and the calories, I promise. Fried chicken is obviously bomb, but don't skimp on that honey! I'm telling ya, it's what keeps me coming back. 

Well, that AND the great service. This place is alwayyyys busy on the weekends, and most evenings as well so there is usually a wait for dinner. Ask for Aaron if you go! He's super helpful and attentive, we love having him as our server when we can. And he may have once or twice even snuck me an extra ramekin of spicy honey to go. ;) Okay, I'll stop rambling on about my honey obsession now. Go try it yourself and you'll see.

For an early Father's Day gift, my wife booked a paella class on Sunday, June 12.  We were the only diners to show for the class and we were afraid they'd cancel it or, worse yet, it wouldn't be fun since the chef and servers outnumbered us at least 2 to 1.  However, Chef Matt and his team were great.  Matt, Leah, Jill and the others were so friendly and professional and eager for us to enjoy our class.  The Paella was wonderful and so were the ciders that Leah provided. Within days we used the paella "kit" Matt provided us and we did a credible job reproducing his paella.
 I would recommend this class to anyone interested in Spanish cuisine.  Also, try the Catalonian Vermouth and a Pimm's Cup!  Great job, guys, thanks!

I came in to this shop concerning my phone vibrating in a peculiar way.  The man at the desk (I did not catch his name but he spoke with an eastern European accent) explained that a tiny screw was missing from my phone and he replaced it for free.  I will definitely come to this shop for phone repair again.  5 Stars.

My husband and I LOVE this place.
With Covid and having kids, it's harder for us to go out and enjoy a restaurant. With covid, they offer takeout and we were amazed by it every time.
With every roll you get, you get a free appetizer, a way for you to get "all you can eat" as take out.
It works so well for us.
Before covid, this was our favorite place to go into to eat. They are warm and welcoming every time you walk in the door. The service is on par and the food, to die for!
Dr. Gallinger has been our family dentist for over 20 years.  Great staff, fast & efficient office, and first class dental work.  Highly recommend.

The best Sushi in St. Louis. Hands down. Even when compared to places in the central west end. The staff is fantastic as well. The sushi is super fresh, and the rolls are delightful, and for sushi the prices are reasonable.

A really good place to taste south indian food.i will highly recommend it to people who love food.
The service and cleanliness..i will give full marks...must visit place.
Absolutely love the Sandbar! The people that work here are incredible and so nice! Love being able to come hangout with friends and have a drink and play volleyball!

This was touted as one of the best vegan/vegetarian restaurants in town, and I was a little disappointed. I had the sweet potato poor boy and was not impressed. My wife got a carrot smoothie earlier and was also not impressed. Not sure whether we would come back or not.

I love poutine so I was delighted to hear that this place was coming to Philly. I've gone once and I have to say - I was pretty disappointed. The poutine simply wasn't that great. I'm not sure I'll be back.

I stopped in with a friend last night for a quick dinner before Little Lebowski Festival.  I had heard (and read) lots of good things, so I was pretty pumped to try this place.  Unfortunately, even if I had gone into this with no preconceptions, I still would have been severely disappointed.  

I ordered a 1/2 chicken platter, with baked beans and mac and cheese.  I will say that the sides and corn bread were great.  The mac was NOT the creamy style you might be used to from WaWa, for example, but was a little on the dry, crumbly side.  I happen to like 'em that way.  The baked beans had a little bit of heat to them that added a nice dimension.  And the corn bread might have been the moistest I've ever tasted.  It literally melts in your mouth.  

Now for the "meat" of the review:  The chicken, which was a total "WTF" experience.  My first bite was from the drumstick, and it was dry.  When the dark meat on a chicken is dry, that's no bueno - it means the white meat is going to be wooden - which it was.  Seriously, if you tried to eat it with a fork, instead of being easily pierced by the tines and subsequently producing a little clear juice, this chicken offered substantial resistance, eventually splintering apart (like wood). My buddy also got the chicken, and before I said anything about mine I could tell, by the look on his face, that he was just as surprised/disappointed.  I tried, in vain, to help the chicken by slathering it with several of the sauces (which were pretty decent), but to no avail. The meat had just been overdone to the point where it was like a moisture black hole.  I know it doesn't have to be this way - I had the chicken at Abner's a few years ago and it was excellent.

If I hadn't had a movie to run off to, I would have taken the matter up with the staff, who were all very friendly.  The place has potential, and I'm thinking this may have just been an "off" day.  So I'll give them some time and try again.

My car got stuck in a flood and J&J saved me about $500 by just replacing the pad and cleaning the existing carpet, rather than pay $1,000 to get all of the carpet replaced. They were so quick and communicative during the entire process. In about two days the work was finished and you couldn't even tell my car had about 5 inches of water on the car floor. I had a great experience and would highly recommend this business!
God in heaven the pork rinds.  Amen pork rinds.  AMEN!  God fed baby Jesus these pork rinds. Snap crack and pop pop pop these pork rind rinds!!!
Great atmosphere and food selection. Brunch, lunch and dinner menu. Perfect for your next date night or brunch with friends.

I've been going to Dr. Citrin for going on 6 years and I love him and his staff.

The first time I called to make an appointment, I'd been living in Tucson for a few years and hadn't seen a dentist and was terrified to go in for a cleaning.

I called and the receptionist was SO sweet and got me right in (even though there can be a wait to see him- his practice is very popular!).

First off, his office is amazing- beautifully landscaped, water falls, greenery, etc.  On the inside?  It's apparent that Dr. Citrin loves basketball, especially U of A, but he's a fan of other teams as well.  I can't comment much on the waiting room because I've never really waited in there- they're that prompt!  

Each exam room has a big picture window that you get to look out (when you're not tilted back being worked on).  I've seen TONS of wildlife outside of those windows and it's very relaxing (for the nervous types like me!).

Their equipment is also state of the art, including digital x-rays!  They show up instantly on the computer screen in the room and there's no development wait time.  Fancy!  

Their hygienist is great, very friendly, and gentle.  Dr. Citrin (sometimes people call him Dr. Jay) is SO NICE.  He's funny, personable, and always has time to chat about bball or golf, or his kids.  He takes the time to get to know you as a person, not just a chart and a patient number.

Okay folks, time to come clean.  I've had a cavity or two and have had them filled by Dr. Jay.  Part II- I'm SUCH a wuss when it comes to dental work.  When he had to numb me up, I cried and he gave me tissues (I've seriously had other dentists tell me to "suck it up").  He's very sensitive and pays attention to the patients' comfort level in addition to doing a great job with the dental work.

At the end of each exam, you are given a toothbrush (and it's a nice one too, not just a one-use travel type)  that says "Dr. Jay Loves Me!", a travel tube of toothpaste and some floss.  Seriously, people.  I get WAY excited about that toothbrush.  

I highly recommend him- I can't say enough good things about the practice he has established in the Old Pueblo.
Yum, Yum and more Yum. Next time we are back in Santa Barbara, we will definitely stop by for another great meal.

Terrible.  Don't bother.  Waitress greets us with "we have no drink menu"....well that was super friendly.  Then brings us canned beer.  Are you kidding me????  We were there 5 minutes and pathetic singer comes over with bucket asking for a tip.  Why????   Place is a dump.   Don't spend your money here!!!!
Just had diner with my family and our waiter was fabulous!!! So attentive and friendly the food was good too. Thank you chan (:

Tony, the owner, hooked us up with a couple of really good quality rental bikes and even gave us choices if we were picky. He had the bikes adjusted for us and showed us how to use all the gears (yes, I'm a biking noob). I had a great two hour ride on the Katy Trail (across the pediastrian walk across from his shop). He made biking process easy and convenient! Would definitely come again soon! 

Not to mention, his shop has vegan speciality foods and non-vegan options on the other side with cozy seating areas indoor and outdoor. There were lots of folks with computers and books chilling and hanging. I got the chicken quesadilla with avocados, heck yes.

I can only comment on my lunch experience which has been excellent. I always order the No.1 special, Pad Thai. 

They start with a small mug of a broth soup (think Pho without the fixins). OUTSTANDING! Definitely left me wanting more.

I usually get the beef option for my Pad Thai. You know, it seems every Thai restaurant does their Pad Thai a little different from the others. This version is very good and always fresh tasting.  It includes a spring roll and a small salad with a spicy dressing. All this for $7.99!

Tough to beat this deal. Warning: after eating this big meal you may want to take a nap.

Julia child's fav restaurant? I can see why. 4 stars for great food and a menu full of variety. Most "street taco" vendors have a just a few options but here there were so many to choose from! 

Get the Super Rica special and the taco de cabacita. I wasn't a fan of the chile relleno since it was drenched in sauce. The tamales were also a hit!

The service was friendly but I gave it three stars because everything was overpriced for what it is. I ordered the shrimp and grits for lunch. Seafood and breakfast combined sounds amazing, but it was not worth the $26. They offer an ayce breakfast seafood buffet for $28 or $38 (didn't hear) but with just a little more it would be equivalent to a Vegas buffet. I mean the food wasn't horrible....just isn't worth it in my opinion.

A beautiful holiday light show every half hour accompanied by Christmas music and a beer garden! I was really excited to visit Franklin square during the holiday season because of those 2 things but I was slightly underwhelmed with both the light show and the seating provided in the beer garden. The light show was very beautiful and I loved the Christmas music that went along with it but I wished there were more colored lights, it was mostly all white lights. And the pictures of the beer garden make it seem like there's a bunch of Fire Pits with benches to sit around but there are only 2 fire pits. I'm glad we went to see the light show but probably won't be coming back.

I really enjoy coming here on my visits to the Franklin.  There pedi's are decent and the mani's are great.  I recently had acrylic applied to my nails and chose to have the natural pink and white look.  Johnny the nail tech did a great job.  

The atmosphere is nice and they offered a glass of wine during my appointment.

The only reason I did not give them 5 stars is because they are little more expensive then other nail salons.

Stopped in Saturday to pick up a cheesecake (which we've done before), only to be told slices only, no whole cheesecakes.  Maybe you should make more?  Settled on a key lime pie instead since we had company coming over.  It was fine and delicious until one of guests ended up with a piece of spatula in her mouth.  Fine, accidents happen and I'd normally just drop a review by a star or so.  However, this was not a small piece (an inch long) and I emailed them a photo 4 days ago and they haven't cared to respond.  So, maybe someone there will see this and remedy their process that would allow someone to lose a chunk of spatula and not notice it as this could easily have been a choking hazard.

The place is big and spacious,  but that's the only thing it had. The food is mediocre. The portions given doesn't match up to what you would expect to pay. I had to hold back my tongue and just eat cause I was there with my family.  . I had the bibim bop. And the bulgogi was half the size of my hands and I have small hands.  So basically that would be 2tbl spoonfuls.   I was really hopeful that this place was worth it.  For the quality and portions given for their meals, it was too pricey.

Stopped by this location to order a sandwich before getting onto a flight to head home and met this lady who provided great service.  Couldn't see her name as she was busy but still provide exceptional service.  I asked her help to taping my donut box and she didn't have to but was very helpful and made sure my donut was secure in the box.  Thanks.

Hands down best variety of flowers in all of nashville this place is a feast for the senses. 
Soo many choices! Things youve never seen. All the colors.fresh af. You will leave stoked.
Great food. Had the fried chicken. Juicy and moist. Made to order for sure. Hubby had seafood platter. . Bread pudding and sweets potato pie pure heaven.

I would give 1 star. After living here 13 months and several transitions in the leasing office. The current "community leader" is more like a dictator. Even sending our "unauthorized" letters to residents. What luxury rental community that you pay 2000$ a month for requires you to damage a car, ask for permission for guests "during business hours". The units themselves look beautiful however they are cheaply made. You head everything from gandy Blvd traffic to the neighbors above and below you. The walls are hollow thin. Save your money. Visit a property like Camden, hermitage, seazen, etc. This is luxury from a cover but managed poorly, constructed cheaply and not worth your time nor money. 

Hello- 


I would like to address a conflict with a particular security guard in the pool area. Today myself, along with my neighbors and guests. We're enjoying the pool. It is my birthday. We brought supplies to make drinks. A bottle of champagne and orange juice. The security guard approached our area and told us to remove the glass from the pool area. We put the glass outside the gate. He came back and told us we are not allowed to legally do so. Mind you, he just came right to us- check his body cam. I am gay and so are my neighbors and my guests. He did not approach anyone else or continue to walk through the pool area to "inspect" for violations by any of the heterosexual guests. Scumbag in the service center, Dave Z, told me since I "didn't buy my car at their location it would take longer." Bad attitude Dave! Arrived at 11:50 for a 12 apt. Said it would take maybe 20-30 min for state inspection. After an hour and a half I inquired why it was taking so long. After seeing other cars arrive after me and leave before me, finally had my jeep pulled in. 
Talked to the sales manager and he stated the service manager would come out to discuss with me. 15 minutes later I still did not see the service manager and jeep was done so I left.  2 hours for an inspection. 
Purchased a pre-owned certified jeep out of state which is why I brought it to the dealership. First and last time at this place. Instead of spending all hat money on the new showroom, they should have spent it on customer service training.

I've gotten my hair done here many times and am always happy with the results.  Everyone is so friendly and put me at ease.  My favorite stylist is Cindy.  She always listens to what I want and gives me great feedback.

What a great find! Loved this gem! Great location, super friendly staff, delicious food and wonderful beer selection! Family and pet friendly along with super cozy outdoor seating. Clean and Covid restrictions enforced.  We will definitely visit again when we are in the area.

I don't know what the fudge they're doing in Southampton. I've eaten at the newer Las Margaritas on Second Street Pike a few times, and was never satisfied with any of the food I sampled there. I was expecting tough meat, indifferently prepared veg, and too much cheese.

I don't know why, but the quality of food at this original location is far better. The salsa and chips are even fresher! It might be due to the huge turnover (20 minute wait on a MONDAY night), or maybe the owner keeps a closer eye on things over here. Regardless, at this location you will find properly prepared Tex-Mex food that relies on the quality of ingredients rather than adding a whole bunch of cheese and sour cream. This includes perfectly charred veggies with your fajitas, fantastic Mexican rice, well-seasoned beans, and burritos/tacos/what have you with good fillings. You'll also get fantastic margaritas (as the name implies) as well as other cocktails. Even though they're not made to order, I even recommend their house margaritas, as they're a perfect balance of sour, sweet, and tequila.

Everything about the meal wasn't great, the steak in my fajitas was overcooked (though still juicy), the guacamole tasted jarred, and service was slow. Still, this spot is likely the best Tex-Mex in the area, and worth a visit if you're in the mood for this kind of cuisine. It's not authentic, but it hits the spot well.
Really nice that they're dog friendly! Prompt service and FANTASTIC coffee, I got the cafe con leche. I actually plan on going back to try the food.

Terrible experience with Pennsylvania inspection on my 89 year old mother's car.  Bear in mind she drives 500 miles per year, the car was purchased here and serviced every year here.  This time round they told her she needed a part costing over $1300.00 so they would not give her a "pass inspection" sticker.  She took the car to another local mechanic who confirmed she did NOT need the part but had to charge her again $33.00 to apply the "pass" inspection sticker.  These people should be ashamed of trying to take advantage of an elderly woman.  Thankfully, it only cost her the additional $33.00 and also that my mother has her faculties and didn't fall for this.  Please do yourself a favor and service/inspect your car elsewhere. This type of deceitful behavior is what gives car dealerships a bad name.

I'm trying to add more photos to my reviews, but I ate my wings so fast that I didn't get a chance to take a picture. Let's start at the beginning, a waitress was at the door as we walked up only because she saw us walking up!  That never happens at a bar!  She was so polite and showed up to all available seating. Then, there's happy hour on Saturday! Whoa!  Now, back to where I started, we ordered the brussel sprouts, bone-in wings, boneless wings, mahi tacos and SOHA fries. Nothing disappointed!  How have I not known about this gem in my neighborhood?  Our drinks were made to order and while I needed more liquor (not the bartenders fault), they were still tasty. Looking for good wings last week, found them this week.

Today, after leaving CVS, which is right across the street from OCF, I entered the coffee house for the second time.  They always have specials on their wall, and for today, the special was hot Apple Cider with Carmel.  Extremely delicious!!!  Also, I picked up some banana bread as well.  It seemed to be homemade since it was neatly wrapped in saran wrap.  I prefer a 16oz cup then 8oz, so that is why I gave four stars.
Oh my goodness food quality off the charts and they actually listen to your special requests  They have to go orders pick up down ....I'm so thankful for Red Mesa very close to home too

5:30 reservation on a Friday afternoon...doors weren't opened until 5:30 promptly.  Small dining room filled up quickly - only 12 tables and it seemed everyone had reservations.  Our waiter (owner Tim?) was excellent - explained everything and gave recommendations.  It's a BYOB restaurant and he quickly uncorked our wine.  Antipasto was outstanding - small portions of A LOT of vegetables,meats and cheeses.  The spinach gnocchi was probably the best dish had at the table - melted in your mouth - outstanding!!  Roasted chicken was ordered - VERY tasty.  Seafood stew was an amazing assortment of ocean delicacies - shrimp, fish, mussels, etc in a tasty broth.  Our meal was simply amazing and will certainly go again.  My only complaint - and I feel awful mentioning this as our visit was great - was the sun shining in the window was right in my eyes for about 30-min.  There was no shade or curtain that could be drawn.

A friend recommended this place for us to take our parents for their Christmas dinner. Wow, was this place ever so amazing.  The food is authentic French food and very rich and vibrant.  They were offering a special for snapper that everyone ordered and absolutely loved it. The server told us their seafood is fresh everyday. The fresh oysters were from Canada (west coast) and Rhode Island and were great.I had the roasted chicken and it was so moist and tasty. This is a wonderful place to bring on a special occasion or date night.

Okay so I'm originally from the area and used to love this place before I moved away. So naturally I was excited to bring my family here for brunch. Needless to say, EXTREMELY disappointed. The only reason I'm giving it a 3 star is because the server was nice. 

First, came in and my husband ordered a coffee which he had to actually get up and get himself?!?! Really that's just weird but whatever. Second, I ordered a latte which tasted like booty. One would expect in a higher end place like this that they would know how to properly prepare a latte. Instead it came out with way too much milk that wasn't properly steamed and lacked espresso. Third, we both ordered the croque madame - they actually sent mine out using the end caps from the bread bag (who does that? ) needless to say my husband got stuck eating it bc IMO it tasted like shit. And lastly, although the fresh squeezed OJ I ordered for my kids tasted good, I'm not convinced it was actually fresh squeezed since there was absolutely no pulp in it. I guess they could have strained it but I doubt it. 

Needless to say we will not be back. So disappointed :(

Ok. This was honestly the worst pizza I've ever had. It was completely dry and cold by the time I got it, it was missing ingredients, and I think I was overcharged. I mean, I still ate the whole thing, but it was nowhere close to good...

The Burek is to D.I.E. for!!!

it is just like my mom used to make.It's awesome!

I agree that customer service was lacking. Walked in and was not really greeted, just more stared at with a 'Hey' as the guy sat in his chair. Kind of weird and awkward vibe from him. I would have thought he would have at least stood up and asked what he could do for us or what we might be interested in and/or needed. I wont go back because of the experience. I think the guys name was James maybe but Im not sure. The only plus was the prices were pretty good but I think I can find things at the same price elsewhere or find a place that might price match.

I REALLY wanted to like Clesi's crawfish because he's such a nice guy and I was happy to see the addition to the Mid City neighborhood, but...

I had some of their boiled crawfish from an event that they catered.  I gotta say...it just wasn't good.  The crawfish themselves just fell flat for me on flavor, and the potatoes and garlic were both undercooked.  I LOVE crawfish boil garlic.  That soft, mushy deliciousness smeared onto a potato.  Twas not to be.  I couldn't even smash the garlic between two fingers.

This was my first time in St. Louis so of course I wanted to try Sweetie Pies. I wanted to see if it is overrated and no different than your average soul food restaurant. I think the most honest statement I can make is this: If Sweetie Pies was never on TV and I happened to give this place a try, I would consider it a great soul food restaurant but believe the prices would be much lower. 

This location is the original and I purposely chose to make a visit here. What I loved is that it looks like a soul food restaurant I visited back in the day. There is nothing modern about the place so there is a sense of southern comfort that has been taken out of many establishments that pride themselves on "glitz and glamour." I was surprised to receive a token to give to my server in order to get my drink. The soft drinks are served in those wide mouth classic Coca-cola cups!

The staff were pleasant and navigated quickly so there wasn't much of a wait. This is a cafeteria style restaurant where you get your tray and silverware and move down the line identifying which food items you wanted. I ordered the fried chicken with sweet potato, mac n cheese, a drink and some peach cobbler. The food was really really good. The fried chicken was breaded and prepared perfectly. The mac n cheese was creamy, smooth, & cheesy. The portion sizes were great. I was stuffed by the time I left. 

Why the 3 star review you say? PRICES. We spent over $50 for two adult meals with two desserts. I didn't ask the price of the peach cobbler; however, when I sat at the table and looked the receipt I realized I paid over $4 for a SMALL container. A lot of people pay for "glitz and glamour" so maybe these would be acceptable prices elsewhere but being that this is a simple "hole in the wall" with good food, the price point should be lower. I am glad to say that I've tried it once; however, I do not think I would revisit if ever in St. Louis.

Where have you been all my life?! My friend suggested this and this was the first time I had an opportunity to visit. Went during lunch. Short wait and the hostess was nice and helpful. Our waitress, Charlotte was AWESOME: knowledgeable about the menu, accurate in her descriptions of the cocktails and just a sweet, smiling ray of sunshine. I had their seafood okra Gumbo! It was excellent! I will definitely be back and would recommend to anyone!

I recently had 2 Guys Handyman to my home to do a variety of things.  They were terrific!  They arrived ahead of schedule and were extremely personable.  They built furniture, hung pictures, moved furniture etc...  The guys made sure they did things right and never rushed through just to finish.  They left my home clean and me very happy!  The charge was more than reasonable and now I feel like I have a go to company that I can depend on.  I HIGHLY RECOMMEND Those 2 Guys Handyman!

Went today for lunch. Service and staff were okay. While we were sitting eating noticed two roaches climbing around on the wall next to us. We notified the waitress who proceeded to kill one. We could not finish our lunch because we were disgusted and totally lost our appetite. The waitress apologized and took the diet soda and beer off our bill. We should have had the whole bill paid especially since we couldn't eat it. Needless to say we will not be going back there again !

My daughter was raving about this chicken salad, so we made plans to go. The next day I couldn't believe when I received a generous flyer that included a free lunch AND $10 off a $25 order. I used both the same week. I've tried the "Fancy Nancy" and Basil chicken salad so far. I love the basil so much that I think I'll stick with it. The broccoli salad side was also amazing. The lunch meal also came with a small iced shortbread cookie. I literally thought to myself "who needs McDonalds fries?" when I tasted it. It was the perfect size to top off the amazing meal. I'm very thrifty, and expected this to be a place I'd rarely treat myself to. I was pleasantly surprised by how cheap it is. It will be my new go-to. I live off Dorsett with many lunch options, but this place is well worth the extra drive!
Food is delicious. A little on the salty side. Otherwise quality, value, service can't be beat. Thank you.

Romantic atmosphere indoors and out. Great place for a nice date night. Lots of options for seafood lovers. Not as many for pasta lovers. Good
Spot for yummy dessert, definitely share the tiramisu, it's a good portion and rich.

We were in Nashville and I wanted to treat my host to a special meal. After a few minutes on line I decided to try what others had called the best Brunch in Nashville TN. pretty big shoes to fill. No I didn't try the others but I did check out The Garden Brunch Cafe.  Had the food been okay the hospitality would have made it a terrific visit. We ordered Steak & Eggs and we not dissapointed. We really enjoyed our Brunch and would reccomend you give it a try. They also can help with your special events as they do weddings and other events. The boss and I travel and I like to choose one place where the locals  eat to tckle our taste buds this was an exceptional choice.

Wanted to give the new Tampa hotspot a try. Previously tried to go but wait was too long. As soon as you step inside you get a big city feel. Very urban decor. Wait staff was very friendly. Had the steamed pork bun and fried chicken snacks. The pork bun was ordinary but the fried chicken was very succulent! My only wish was that there was a second option for the dipping sauce as it is pretty spicy. Had the Champon ramen and was not disappointed. The pork was as tender as I've ever had and the mushrooms, corn and onions went really well together. Flavor in every bite! Will definitely come back to try the rest of the menu.

Great vibe, friendly service and delicious food! I enjoyed the crispy shrimp taco and duck taco. My son loved the roasted chicken off the kids menu and my husband enjoyed the hearty chicken soup that was loaded with carrots, potatoes and corn. Loved the open air dining.

I had order some hair and still haven't receive it I been trying to call the company no answer I tried email I still haven't got my shipping date I bought hair from them once before and it's good hair but as of right now I don't know what's going on and I'm pissed !!
Great meet up place for a few friends or sushi for two sat at bar saki shots and sushi all delicious and well prepared

I will give it two stars for the fact that I USED to have good times there back in the day. The service was inexperienced and unhelpful and most of all the food was terrible. Would never recommend this spot,

The setting for the Boathouse has such amazing potential with its picturesque views on a  beautiful day, why not? It was indeed a gorgeous day and many had the same idea as we did. We did have about  
a 20 minute wait which was fine. It was obvious as to just how busy they were. So, we took a paddleboat ride and truly enjoyed the serenity  it provided. Very nice to stop & take the time to enjoy just one of the many beautiful features in Forest Park. . If not had our name in I truly could have enjoyed staying in the boat across the lake and just inhaled off its beauty.
Lunch was quite good though I got a seafood salad. Tasty though not 5 stars being it sort of basic. My friend got a hot sandwich which  was very good. Our server was attentive and very polite. This is a great place to enjoy on a beautiful day. I will absolutely return with out of town 
friends. There's not many places that are kid friendly in addition to pet friendly. Though, we had neither. It has a diverse menu considering their location. After enjoying my meal I couldn't help but to notice just how extremely busy they had become even since we sat down. The servers are very busy though in all honesty I think we had one of the nicest, eager to please type servers in far too many restaurants. Manners' don't cost $$$. And, they go Along way. The Boathouse has a big dose of charm, good food and beautiful surroundings. For those with little ones: They do have a children's menu & you can buy food for them to feed the ducks.
Let's see we order curry veggie roti only one roti curry vegetables salty as hell rice & no peas customer service sucks

As I wrote in another review, I'm from Boston, so I don't know how this place compares with Reno, but I sure can tell you how it compares with Boston.  It compares favorably.  That is really an understatement.  This place is outstanding.

If I had to pick a place back home to equate this with, it would be Sel de la Terre.  Only here, I spent about half what I would spend back home.  The bread and olive oil that preceded the entrée were good, and to be honest, if a restaurant doesn't get that part right, it's usually a bad sign. For the entrée, I got the special for the evening, roasted pork on cabbage, and a nice glass of red wine.  My wife got the seafood primavera linguine, and it was simply packed with fresh seafood.  Coming from Massachusetts, and having grown accustomed to fresh seafood, I was a little uneasy with my wife's choice-- fresh seafood in Reno?!  My fears were unfounded.  Also a great dish.

I wish we had been able to fit dessert-- but we were both quite satisfied by the end of the meal.  I would call the portions tending toward generous, but by no means an ungodly pile of food.

I only have two suggestions: one, no espresso?  OK, my taste in coffee is perhaps a bit too snobby (in their defense, their coffee WAS good), but an espresso would have been the perfect end to the meal.  Second, the place is a little lacking in ambience... specifically, warmth.  It would benefit hugely from, say, a fireplace.  The New Englander in me is simply a sucker for a nice, warm fire.

Anyway, great place.  Highly recommended for a date, and while it was not cheap, it certainly did not break the bank either.  If I were to relocate permanently to Reno, I most definitely could see making this place our standard go-to for special occasions.

OH-- one last thing.  Sunday nights are burgers and pizza only.  While I would probably be happy with their Sunday food, my wife and I went back a second time hoping to have a meal like our first, and were a bit disappointed.  I can't say I blame them, Sunday nights are probably slow.

It had been over a year since I l had last chomped on an In-N-Out burger (in San Francisco).  I have fond memories of that burger, but the burgers we had in the desert today are not quite worth all the hype.

The hamburger meat is absolutely excellent in flavor, but the tomato on the burger was rock hard and there was way too much 1000-island dressing (at least that is what I think the sauce was). 

The bun was served at a temperature as blistering hot as the tarmac at Sky Harbor Airport on a July afternoon.  Ouch!!!

The onions were not grilled, but they were hot too.  Were they blasted in the microwave?  Cold crunchy onion would be better.

The fries, on the other hand, were good.  I also loved the strawberry shake with an incredibly natural flavor.

But really, the best part of In-N-Out is the cheap prices!

I've looked high and low and there just isn't a better nail salon in Philly! Nobody else comes close. I used to frequent the Northern Liberties location and my nails always turned out great, I work with my hands all day and my nails would never chip or peel.

When the Nolibs location closed I tried to find another salon close to home and none of them come close. I've been to this location three times and have not been disappointed. It's worth the trip!

Don't let name distract you..... I needed AC repaired and rear strut replaced. They saved me $400 over another national brand! Scheduling was prompt, Mgr Chris answered all my rather dumb questions. Everything completed on time. Only suggestion: paint the waiting area (it's dirty/shabby) and tape corner of counter so clothes won't tear. I'll return !

We weren't sure what to expect; we wanted a great dinner but were a little uneasy bc of some of the reviews on Yelp, but we loved it!  Ms Hays chicken wings are a little unusual by the description, but they were fabulous. We got the fried chicken and the shrimp&grits and both were tremendous. 
Service is essential to a great night, and our waiter, Travis Roberts made the evening really fun - not to mention he had some great recommendations. And Eddie Osberry is just fabulous.
Just stopped in for food and coffee. The falafel and latte were very good. We'll be sure to come back and try the games!

Oh such mixed emotions about this place.  I grew up nearby and remember when it was MGM with a real lion you could take pictures with.  Then Ballys and then I when I was old enough to gamble, Hilton.  Now it is Grand Sierra.  I have always liked that it was a little far off the beaten path and that the parking was vast and easy.  I am always glad that they kept the revolving doors.  I remember going through them when I was very little so I always make it a point to go through them every time I come.  We tried them out when they first changed to GS and liked them but now not so much.
The gaming floor is depleted little by little each time I come.  I find that I get bored very quickly here.  Poker room is barely alive with only one table going.  Comps are not great.  Food is a decent selection though and there is some family entertainment upstairs with the bowling alley and theater but as far as gambling goes it is lacking.  I will say waitress service is better than average.  They are plentiful and come fairly quick.
The rooms leave little to be desired.  Even stayed in the "newly remodeled" and it was still bleh.  Instead of gutting it out completely, I think they just put new linens and a coat of paint.  Still very dated with old thermostat.  
Lastly, there is a distinct strong soapy odor here that hits you in the face when you walk in that it gives me a headache.  I know they do it to mask the smoke but its like spraying a ton of Febreeze or something.  Our annual convention is going to be held here this year to my dismay and I will have a stay here a whole week.  Lord help me!
Closed - this place no longer exists.  Save yourself the mile walk from resorts and head towards Central street for food options.
Love coming to bourbon blue for happy hour! Always have great specials. Their brunch is also very good with a build your own Bloody Mary bar with anything you could imagine wanting in it!
Use to love this place.... But like most places over time, the prices went up and the quality went down. Sad

Jaime R. From The Bronx, New York. Upon Visiting Friends In New Orleans In June 2011, We Accidently Stumbled Upon This Cafe After Having Left Several So-Called Italian Restaurants Highly Disappointed With Their Menus And Knowledge Of Basic Dishes Which Are Offered At Home. Anyhow, We Entered And Found The Granada Pleasant And Comfortable To Be In. I Give A Rousing And Well Earned Five (5) Stars To The Chef And Staff For An Extraordinary Preparation Of The Dishes Served. Everything Tasted Above What We Expected, Especially The Fish Wrapped In Parchment Paper Which You Don,t Ordinarily Find Outside Of Spain. The Only Caveat I Can Give Is The So-Called Waitresses. They Were Pleasant Enough But Very Deficient In The Ordering And Timely Delivery Of Our Orders. I Will Give Them A Half Star Rating For Professionalism And That Is Being Charitable. I Am Usually Lay Back About Service As Long As It Is Fairly Steady. These Ladies Didn't Have A Clue. Disappointing Considering That Everything Else Was Above Board. I Would Recommend The Granada Cafe Heartily To My Jaded And Spoiled Culinary Acquaintances From " New Yawk" On Their Next Visit To The Crescent City. I Give A Big, "Well Done" To The Gracious Owner Of The Granada.

Most always a very nice meal, and we were able to get an outdoor table(a little rickety) near canal. (Not sure why they allow the guy standing in the middle of the street to act as a fake parking attendant, for the purpose of collecting tips...)
Server was nice, a little ditsy, had to be reminded to bring several items. Lamb kebabs delicious, but don't expect veggies on skewer, just lamb. Love the salad w/ the sumac dressing. Generous servings, great preparation, fair prices.

If I could put less than zero I put Less Than Zero. Second time in a row that we have been in this place sat for 5 minutes and no one acknowledged our existence. The last time we were here which is been a few years we left because no one waited on us. There were officially four people I repeat for people in this restaurant at the same booth with seven people walking around no one came to our table. We will never ever ever go back there again and I'm going to write letters to corporate because this place is an absolute joke and the manager had an attitude when we got up and left and save all the ladies coming right over we should have to wait we were ready

I had a nail in my tire and after checking Yelp I gave 11th Street Auto a call to see what could be done.  I was told to stop in and they would check it out.  I figured it may take a while so I put on all my gym clothes thinking I would run to the gym and work out while they did what needed to be done, what a waste of time changing was.  It literally took them five minutes.  I think I was in the parking lot and out in under 10 minutes and it cost next to nothing.  As long as I live in Philly I will be going to this place for all my car troubles.
Not worth your time. Food is completely disgusting and unflavored. It's more like bad texmex

Came here for a business lunch meeting and was greeted by amazing staff and the new owner. Food was fantastic - ordered the Halibut as well as the iced blueberry tea. Would highly recommend! I was expecting smaller portions being the higher-end class of restaurant that it is, but was pleasantly surprised when I was perfectly full after ordering just an Entree.

I use this Shell station because they have a US Post Office franchise inside, and they're close to my home. There are generally only one or two people in line ahead of me, so it's easy to buy stamps, mail letters, small packages, etc.

This Shell station is located on the corner of N. Dale Mabry and Linebuagh Avenue, right next to the Publix shopping center, and across the street from Starbucks.

It's a standard gas station / convenience store (with an automated car wash), although I am mostly there for the Post Office facilities.

First thing is first, the decor is a whimsical combo of Buffalo Bill (silence of the lambs) and Liberace. Blood red walls, roman busts, huge oil painting replicas encased in elaborate gold frames. It works here though. It was very busy and even with our reservation we waited a half an hour. I was pretty shocked to see patrons here in jeans or that the management allows it but I guess that's a Florida thing. The portions were out of control but I guess that can be a good thing. Included in our steak entrees were salads, baked potatoes, soup - the lobster bisque was amazing and then your steak dish has greens, carrots, and onion strings. The delmonico was very flavorful and my girlfriend had a great fillet. Our server was attentive and the meal was an overall success. The wine cellar tour was eye opening and we totally felt in the way w the kitchen tour during peak hours. 

On to the less than stellar moments.....we were out  for a romantic v day meal and we were sat in a room w a table of ten that were having fun but borderline obnoxious. When they finally left people clapped and the room dynamic became more fitting of fine dining. I think the staff could have grouped large parties separate from couples trying to have a nice date. 

The dessert room was also very nice. We had the king Midas carrot cake and macadamia nut ice cream. Both amazing. Total bill was around $30. I gave our waiter $100. The server brought me $48 in one dollar bills!!!! I lost my damn mind. He apologized in advance which means he knew it was wrong. He gave us all his shitty change instead of getting a few twenties or tens. The rest of the change was $5s. I would have made a bigger deal but we were already there for three hours. Overall a good experience but a shitty move by our server to give me all his ones was the last impression we were left with.

This is the closest McDonald's to me, which means I frequent it when I'm running low on time and can't have breakfast in the morning.  Every time I order a single sausage burrito, they give me 2!  Also, they are very friendly.

beef on weck and custom cocktails make this place a winner.


Wine on tap as well?

We got you

I ordered a dozen cupcakes for my daughter's birthday.  I don't live in Philly so I took a chance and called Whipped on a whim.  The person who answered the phone and who handled the order was delightful.  My daughter knew she was getting a delivery but didn't know what it was.  On the day of the delivery, she received a call letting her know the time frame for the delivery and they were on time - it was perfect!  Most of all, the cupcakes were fantastic - both in presentation and in taste.  She and her party guests loved them!  Would absolutely order from Whipped Bakeshop again!  Thank you for helping to make her birthday so special.

Greetings from Seattle!!
Need more stars so i can give Lorenzo's  5 more!!  
This is the home of the Best  Italian Hoagie that I ever had the pleasure of devouring!  10 days 12 hoagies and packed one for the plane ride home. 
You guy's are without a doubt  just hands down fucken awesome!!
As someone with a tree nut allergy, I get nervous about buffets. This place labels all their brunch buffet items NF and GF! When asked, staff talked to manager and folks changed gloves upon request.

The doctors are wonderful but, the office staff definitely needs work. Have had trouble many times getting appointments within 30 days for medication refills and either no response to messages I've left, or maybe get a call days later after leaving 2 or 3 messages. I almost changed doctors because of these issues.

We came here for the second time for a brewery beer dinner (Allagash) This was the first one they've done in this space and boy did they knock it outta the park! The Allagash beer was excellent and the food pairings were just spot-on and delicious. Ahi Crudo, Chicken Mole' on polenta cakes, Pork loin and Apple tart. All paired appropriately with delicious Allagash beers. The service was absolutely amazing and attentive, heck even the owner herself was running food. Clearly they were pulling out all the stops for their first beer dinner and it was very much appreciated. 

I realize this doesn't necessarily represent a day-to-day visit and I'll need to visit again to really assess that but I fell these folks are really working hard to make this project work and I do appreciate that. 40 great beers from around the world on tap, how much can you really complain about that :-)

Purchased a puppy from here about a year ago, was told that it was a poodle but ended up being a terrier mix.  The dog was inbred according to the veterinarian and had a laundry list of health issues including blind in one eye, testicles didn't descend, and serious allergies.  When I went back one day to talk to them witnessed a woman come in literally off the street with a laundry basket full of puppies and told the employee that her dog had the puppies and she didn't know what to do with them.  The employee took them from her and told her that they would sell them and took them from the woman and then placed them into a pen for sale - no questions asked!  Seems like the will take any puppies to sell without asking questions and knowing their history. Given my experience here and some that I have heard from others wouldn't trust a purchase from here.

Classic north end spot. Awesome ambiance. Never had a bad experience until recently. This post is just in regards to the fish tacos which I think they recently changed. Long story short they used to be pretty money. Borderline not edible last visit. True or false you should be able to pick up a taco? I say true. Not so much with these fish tacos. More like three tortillas with a big spread of creamy fish slathered all over them. Not a fan. Asked the waitress "how am I supposed to eat this?". She was busy but clearly not interested in engaging in any meaningful way. Fair enough but I say bring back the old fish tacos.

If you go to a Walmart expecting it to be a luxury shopping experience, then you are setting yourself up for disappointment.

I think this Walmart is great for exactly what it is- A Walmart. I have been here many times, and I find the aisles to always be cleaned and the shelves to be well stocked. The prices are amazing, and the clientele it a little classier than most other Walmarts.

Came in yesterday with a friend and the service was amazing. We came in an hour after they opened and the wait wasn't long. The people there took their time to explain everything and were really nice and informative. Our piercer was Zach and he was really fun, made the whole process less stressful (esp. since my friend was getting her nipples pierced) and we had a great time overall. Would highly recommend this place!

I've been eating here for 11 or 12 yrs and I've never had a bad experience. I usually get the oxtail or jerk chicken, both are delicious! They give you huge portions and they have 2 sizes which are both packed with food. I'll add pictures. I use to get the steamed snapper on Fridays but I'm not sure if they still sell that. I've been meaning to ask but each time I'm there to pick up I only want to get my food home to eat it. I've also had the brown stew fish, bananas.
Everytime I come here they always keep my credit card causing me to have to back over to get it they never call me

We went for an endless lunch on Saturday. The koizi restaurant was a nice restaurant. We were given a seat in the restaurant as soon as we reached. For starters we ordered Miso Soup and then we ordered Sesame Ball, Dancing Krab Roll, California Roll, Vegetable Roll, Philadelphia Roll, Tempura Roll and Koizi Roll. We loved each and every roll. The best among were Dancing Krab Roll and Koizi Roll. This restaurant has amazing sushi rolls and service is also fast. Covid-19 guidelines were followed and everything was safe. We loved the food.

My husband and I drank and ate at The Libertine for the first time last night.

First, the good:  the drinks are tasty and well balanced (we enjoyed the Screw and Bolt, the Piscou Sour, and one of the Cava cocktails), the food also very tasty (we had the Lobster Carpaccio, Artichoke Crostini, the Burger, and the Porcetta Sandwich), and the setting chic and transporting (such as to a larger more cosmopolitan city).  Based on these areas alone, my husband and I both agree they earned a solid four stars.

The bad (very bad): the service.  Specifically its lack of efficiency.  Our server was fine.  The time it took for us to get our cocktails was on the longer side of acceptable with the redeeming quality being the lovely taste of each of them.  The wait for the food, though, was absolutely ridiculous.  It heavily detracted from our overall experience.  To give you an idea we spent approximately an hour and forty-five minutes at our table during which we ordered a total of three cocktails, two appetizers, and two main dishes.  The food was all ordered at the beginning of our experience.  The vast majority of the time we spent at our table was waiting for food.  Though the desserts sounded tasty, we opted not to try any of them as we were not willing to invest any more time.  Another indication of the time it took: my two drink buzz had worn off by the time our main dishes arrived (I'm a small person).  

Overall we enjoyed the establishment and its offerings enough to consider returning in the future.  However, we would likely try it on a weeknight as the painfully slow food service detracted significantly from our overall experience.

We have been here several times.  The food is always great!  There have been some issues with service, but for the most part it has been good.

The only major issue was a few weeks ago when we went for brunch.  They seem to have an issue with it taking a long time to receive your food if you order something like French Toast or Pancakes.  If it would have said that on the menu, we would have ordered something else.  Instead, we watch others sit down after us, and leave after completing their meal... while we still did not have our food.  We spoke to the manager, and did receive vouchers for a free meal.  Glad to report that we took advantage of that this weekend, and everything was great!

I had such a great experience at Taco Mar the other night! The food was unbelievable and authentic Mexican. Everything was cooked perfectly! The chicken was savory and full of flavor, the refried beans were smooth and creamy, and the rice reminded me of my grandma's rice. 

The service was also amazing. The entire staff was very nice and accommodating! I'm not sure if we were being served by the owner or the manager, but he provided great service, and it was obvious that he cares about the customers and serving great food!

We were in desperate need of a new Mexican restaurant, and I'm so happy we found Taco Mar! I'm very excited to go back!

Pro Tip: it is BYOB so be sure to bring something with you. But, if you don't no need to worry! Bar Avalon right next door serves to-go margaritas that you can have with your dinner at Taco Mar! I suggest the Avalon margarita!

Love their salsa (spicy) and creamy jalapeno dip with warm fresh chips.
I have had their veggie enchilada and chile releno and both have been good. I love their Boom Boom sauce and always ask for it on my dish and it brings the flavor to another level!!
 Sometimes there is a wait but the service is fast. Good place to hangout with friends.

Overall my parking experience was pretty good considering it was a last minute reservation due to another parking service not having a shuttle due to covid (whimps).   Going there was fine checked in and followed a shuttle to show us where to park (it is a gravel lot).  No problem in getting to the airport process took about 20 minutes.

Going back was another story.  After you get your bags you have to walk up and take the train to the rental car center and down to the curbside pickup area pretty good 10 to 15 minutes to get there w the train and walk down.  After I called it took about 20 min for the shuttle to come for the return trip maybe longer than usual maybe not.   Their number doesn't always answer the first time I called their mailbox was full.    No other problems in delivering me back to my car.    I stayed an extra day hopefully they didn't overcharge me and signed up for their frequent parker program which a savory traveler should do no matter what.   Assuming they didn't overcharge me for the extra day I'll probably give them another shot.  

They are closed from 1 am to 4 am so do plan accordingly if you are departing or arriving near these hours.

A great Sunday brunch spot with a good mix of NY and southern options. The staff really works had to make sure you have everything you need. Kitchen could be faster, but with the volume of to-go orders they are clearly working hard and worth the wait.

Mmmm, this place makes my taste buds water! What an elegant, classy, simplistic restaurant in the Keystone area. Warm toasty bread is served with oil before your meal. Everything tried here made my insides very happy. Comforting, yet light food. Salmon was cooked perfectly, along with my vegetables. Both can be tricky to master. If you are a seafood fan, it's a go! They offer a few other options as well.

Seems to have all the books I could possibly need.
They sell starbucks brand coffee and cheesecake factory desserts in their cafe.
Yum

Wow! I'm glad that we have these kind of restaurants in town!

Whenever I think of a restaurant on mass all it comes to mind is bars that have restaurants with one or two special things that they are known for, I must say that I've passed by this restaurant many times and didn't call my attention; I guess the name doesn't tell you a lot about it or probably the outdoor part not calling my attention but if you're reading this and you want a nice fancy dinner in downtown please go inside!

I was there with a group of friends, we made a reservation for 9 people and following CDC guidelines and all we were given sanitizer, asked for face masks and given our own section which was very cozy, with a mid volume music and a screen showing some burning logs inside a chimney everything suited perfect to enjoy ourselves while being able to talk. The restaurant has a great design and with everyone wearing formal clothes makes it even better.

I apologize since I didn't grab quite well our waitress name but she did an awesome job, so thank you mid 30s, 5'5", blonde girl with eyeglasses. Even though the night was busy you managed to be very patient, got our orders right and our drinks fast; everything was awesome.

Now, getting to the food. I read many yelp reviews about this restaurant and from the most reviewed dishes, I picked the "Pan Roasted Chilean Sea Bass". I hesitated for a minute while reading a yelper saying that hers was overcooked but since it was repeated on the pictures it seemed a good choice so I took the risk.

Needless to say this was one of the best fishes I've tried. It was flawless, crispy on the outside (did you guys do it with those little torch lighters?) and the inside was very tender and tasty also the sauce that was around it was excellent.

As a side my gf picked the onion rings and thank god they ran out of them so we get to try the BWI Cauliflower which seemed to be cooked in the oven and placed on top of homemade hummus which was very smooth.

Our wine selection was a Kono - Pinot Noir from New Zealand that we enjoy, smooth with a strawberry taste.

Now my gf choice was the Seafood Pasta which was generous portion of marinara mixed with linguine pasta with shrimp, mussels and asparagus. Very good flavor but I believe adding cherry tomatoes makes it more acidic taste and I rather enjoy a hearty tomatoe sauce.

We couldn't reach the dessert section since we had appetizers at a bar but we will be back for sure!

Dan and the team are the best!  They are very knowledgeable and take the time to explain things clearly to you.  Our home-buying process went much smoother with the detailed informative reports we received.  We were able to use their reports to get the builder to remedy items on our home prior to delivery.  If you're looking for someone honest and knowledgeable, then Dan is your man!
I was craving Pho and decided to give Ha Long Bay a try. We were very satisfied! Food is great. Price is fair and portions large. Service is excellent.
Service was Great !!! Food was ok nothing special ! Burger was pretty tasty ; ) limited menu . Bar was nice !
Delicious food. Supremely accommodating chef (my wife has a strict diet because of health problems) and a kind staff. Grateful that we have this little gem in our neighborhood.

I was expecting greatness and got average. It was an expensive night for average. I would have given them 3 stars for food, 4.5 for beer and 1 for service so that's how I came up with two stars.
Food. I ordered the Shitaki and Gouda burger with onion straws. It was lacking in mositness and flavor but it was not awful. What saved this meal were the sweet potato fries. They were killer. What killed it was the fact that the order was wrong and I got the wrong fries. The redemption was I tried the regular fries and they were also amazing. 
Beer. I chose to do the 1.75 5 ounce samplers versus the larger beers seeing as I was not sure what I would like. First sample was the raspberry cider. Very sweet, nice good flavor. Not something I could drink more than a 5 ounce sampler but would do again. I also had a Pilsner, the name slips me, it was VERY good. I am a beer wimp and I really enjoyed the flavor.
Service. YIKES. Terrible, awful bad. Appetizers never came. Beers came sporadically. Order was wrong and server threw the kitchen under the bus. I think the kitchen was not the person taking the order.... Not to mention she had an excuse for everything instead of taking the blame. It was a Sunday so it was not even crowded. 
Will I go back...for the addicting sweet potato fries and beer, sure.

Casual. Casual is the best word to describe Angry Pepper Waterside. We started our venture into this restaurant by anchoring our boat at their very convenient dock by the restaurant. We were seated at a mediocre  deck and ended up moving from our original seat to the bar, which, for me was nice except the music was a bit too loud for conversation. The service by the waitress was great, she was very laid back and friendly. Overall the scenery and service was exceptional, but they lacked in tasteful food. I ordered blackened fish tacos, which I thought would be one of their better meals considering they are right by the Bay. As soon as I got the food I could tell it was not going to meet my standards as I could tell it was loaded with way too much cheese, and when I began to eat I noticed it lacked in flavor, I could not even taste the blackened fish inside the taco. All in all, this was a very relaxing and casual bar that I would recommend going to for a relaxing night out.

Guy showed up and claimed he could not even put gauges on my unit, told me I needed to replace unit without even a test if system. Says he was walking away. Got a company out, was low on Freon and he was able to get his gauges on and fixed unit. 

Rip off trying to sell new unit when mine is only 6 years old.

Stay away

Tacos at Buena Onda are good. There's not much in the neighborhood like it. Vibe and decor are cool. There are still some ordering/kitchen/pickup issues that need ironing out, but overall worth a visit.

Verti Mart, you are excellent and just what I need at basically all hours of the day (except from 4-6 am since that is when you close your kitchen for cleaning....ppffttt, who needs "cleaning"?). 

I wish you weren't cash only, but your awesomeness helps me overlook that part of you that I dislike. 

Your food : exactly what I want and need. Fried, greasy, straightforward, cheap, and tasty. I believe it's a "til supplies last" kind of place, and from what I've seen, your jambalaya and cheesy noodles seem to be quite popular. My cheeseburger killed. Po Boy was a little salty, but what do I know. 

Your location: convenient for where I stayed and easy to find

Your merchandise: you're a convenience store with a food counter in the back. Vitamin water?  Electrolytes from a night/day of drinks?  Chips?  Cat food?  Smokes?  You got it all and you've got it good.  Not much space to move around, but whatever - not there to hang out, I'm there to get my food and get back outside/my place with AC. 

Oh!  And you deliver!  How awesome is that!  I wish we had a Verti Mart in the Twin Cities.
I order the family platter almost weekly for my construction crew. The portions are large and very filling. The food is great, the ribs are my favorite. Give this place a try.

Food was okay. Drinks were good. Service was awful! Waiter took drinks from us before we were finished. Rushed our meal. Then put the bill on the table, face up. So our guest saw the amount. After we paid, another waiter came & put the same exact bill back on the table, face up again! Probably wouldn't recommend or return. Too many other great places to choose from.

This place had a decent amount of good reviews so I went twice to have chips "repaired". However the second time I went, the "repair" looked questionable to me so I asked the technician if it was repaired and he said yes. A few weeks later my windshield appears like this in my pictures. I called and went back in. I'm guessing it was the manager/owner who examined it. Whoever mentioned management is rude and has poor customer service in another review is spot on. The manager tried to avoid blame by saying there was another chip but you can clearly see in my photos the one repaired had grown and is the largest chip on my windshield. Closer, you would be able to see that it wasn't filled properly. I told him that the technician had informed me it was repaired and the manager/owner tried arguing with me forever while talking down/mansplaining to me what a repair is as if I don't know. He stated that repairs weren't always guaranteed & his offer/warranty to fix the problem was to deduct the cost of repair from a new windshield so it's still hundreds, oh and right before Christmas during a pandemic. If it had been fixed properly the first time, I wouldn't be upset about that offer, however I don't believe that was the case and management was unwilling to take any blame for their poor quality. Then his quote with that discount was equal to what another place quoted me WITHOUT a discount so they are overpriced as well. I informed him that he lost my business and I would not be giving a good review and he didn't seem to care at all.
Update: I also find it this odd and, quite frankly chauvinistic after the way I was talked to there, that my review is the only one this company has responded to. Nor did I ever demand anything, I pointed out the obvious that the "repair" was not repaired correctly.
Been to Hyde Park several times: drinks, dinner, reception and brunch. Always have had great experience, service and food. Decor is contemporary elegance.
價格跟一般美國拉麵差不多，但比其他拉麵豐富許多，甚至比日本區的拉麵還棒 平時吃拉麵都要加麵 第一次吃拉麵還沒加麵就超級飽 重點是他的麵是在美國很少可以吃到的波浪型拉麵 炸雞個人覺得也不錯 唐揚炸雞講究薑的味道 他的炸雞薑味很濃厚 餃子也還蠻好吃的 可以說是目前在LA西北邊的拉麵可以排名第一名

Radcliffe Painting always come by quickly to look at the job and give you a bid. They do great work, easy to book with them. Either by the job or by the hour. Rachel gave me some of her best guys to do a high contrast room (new crown molding putty and fill, paint white with super dark walls). Exacting work and paint to cover, which was a lot of coats on our thirsty contractor quality (I.e. Watered down, low quality) painted walls. Used them again and again for things that come up. Booking them soon for more crown molding work. More expensive then doing it yourself, but with so much less hassle and headache. Check out some detailed pics along with review.

If you enjoy store bought pasta drenched in store bought sauce and overcooked check then you have hit the jackpot. If you want a real Italian meal cooked with fresh ingredients then I caution you. After barely touching my entree they brought out another box with the same entree. I figured my son or dog might eat it so I brought it with me. Upon walking to the car i dropped it in the bag from knee height (I am about six feet, not ten feet tall). The container busted open. Needless to say the raccoon's might have a decent meal tonight (for a raccoon used to trash).
Good variety of interesting dishes.  Maybe a little pricey but probably not for for the location.  Good portion sizes (large).

I've ate here a few times.And I've never had a bad experience. The service has always been friendly and prompt.We were a party of 11 on Christmas eve day. The waiter was awesome.The food was great and I like their menu.Well Done "Q"

The Mixed Grill Cafe recently opened in my area, I heard of it only because a random man came tromping through my yard and handed me a menu of theirs that contains Greek and American traditional cafe food. It's actually pretty good he did because if he didn't, I would never have run across the place.

Situated on Grandview Ave, which runs parallel to Nolensville Road, it's basically situated right where nobody is ever going to see it (unless they work for Red Bull, which has trucks back there - who'dathunkit). Its entrance is on Woodbine, which is the street next to La Hacienda, Phonoluxe, etc.

It's got a pretty nice dining area, the aesthetic is sort of marred by iron bars on the windows, but I think those were there before they moved in so can't fault them for that at only being open a month.

They advertise they accept major credit cards, but evidently American Express is not one of the major ones they accept ;)

The fries here are great, I;m told the cheeseburger is acceptable, and the veggie burger is pretty good. They have a fairly extensive sandwich menu. I thought about listing off what they have and then thought "everything" looks like it encompasses it. Maybe not everything, but they have cow, chicken, turkey, fish, veggie... so if it walked, flew, or grew it looks like they have a sandwich of it.

They do deliver. I do not know what their radius is, and they're not "it's 2am OMG I need a snack NOW" capable, but that's pretty cool.

Wow...what an amazing blend of flavors, and at great happy hour prices!  I'm impressed and will return often.  The bacon dates were more meat than date, and very filling.  The mole negra sauce was yummy.  I also had the stuffed peppers and fried potatoes which were ample sized.

Peter the bartender was helpful as this was my first time here.  All of the sauces were just soooo good.  There is also a nice happy hour drink list which includes two good house wines.

I cannot wait to return and try the brunch and the rooftop bar.
Absolutely horrible completely burnt pizza called the restaurant and was told they were super busy and could not help me.

An online visit with Doctor On Demand on Labor Day led me to my most recent visit to this Walgreens.  

I called the pharmacy first to check on the price of my prescription.  The friendly pharmacy tech answered right away and identified herself, though I don't recall her name.  She told me the price and transferred me to the pharmacist for a question I had about the medicine.

It took a bit longer for the pharmacist to pick up, but he answered my question.  I was also grateful that he offered to apply a discount card of some type to my prescription when I said I had no insurance.  The price went from over $75 down to $41 and change.  It turned out he didn't tell me the exact amount, but I am grateful for the price reduction nonetheless.

The Walgreens closest to me was closed permanently in July and the next closest to me is not a 24 hour store or pharmacy.  We also discovered that the 24 hour CVS down the street is a 24 hour STORE, but there is no longer a pharmacist late at night.  This Walgreens is a bit of a jaunt from where I live, but still relatively close at 5.5 miles away.  On the trip over, I saw another CVS that was locked up and must have closed before 9, though I wouldn't use it no matter what time of day because of the neighborhood.  It's irritating that there are no longer any other 24 hour pharmacies closer to me, but I was happy with the service at this one.

I once again used the drive-thru.  It isn't the best neighborhood, especially at night, but I didn't feel like going inside anyway.  They had a button to push for service that rang a phone.  A lady came on quickly to say she would be right with us.  She was pleasant and we were in and out after no longer than five minutes total.  I prefer their drive-thru compared to another I have used and reviewed.  This one has two lanes, has relatively bright lighting and is adjacent to a lot in the open rather than being in a tight alley-like single lane backed up to a building.  I feel the setup of this drive-thru is safer, despite the neighborhood.

I had my aunt and uncle and their Beauceron with me so I felt safe, but if you aren't packing a police-type dog, I do think there is a security guard stationed at this store from what I have read in other reviews, should you have any issues.  When I have been inside in the past, it was a clean and nice store.  I just often see sketchy people lurking about the area outside, sometimes in the parking lot, but usually closeby on the sidewalk and the corner.  

Good store with what is probably the only 24 hour pharmacy for a lot of people.  I just want to stress to be aware of your surroundings outside, no matter what time of day it is.  At the very least, it is often a busy and packed parking lot with erratic drivers from time to time.

Baja Cafe is a great hole in the wall breakfast place! My husband and I go there almost every weekend. Each time, we have had fast service and absolutely delicious food! Plus, every week they have new specials, which is what really keeps us coming. They have hearty eggs Benedict choices and lots of sweet breakfast items.

Was there on a Friday night sometime ago and they had line dancing there and was very interrested but I met the line dance instructor and her friend and was extremely upset at the way it was run and very unhappy with there attitudes very mean and unpleasant people will never go there again

Amazing taco truck, the menu ranges from beef brisket, carnitas, and chorizo tacos. You'll usually find him at Dos Jeffes and the Kingpin, and is currently scouting out spots in the downtown area. Alex is super nice and I was lucky enough to get a special meatpie on my birthday.
Love this place. The frozen margaritas are to die for. Great food and great bartenders. Noah was very nice and helpful.

I recently went to Franco and I don't think it lived up to the yelp hype...

Food was decent, but definitely nothing special. For starters, I had the french onion soup which was rather salty. I had the pork chop as the main course and was not very memorable. It was the sides that were actually exciting (fried brussel sprouts and beets gratin). However, I just can't justify paying for the meal simply for eating the sides.

The decor and restaurant itself is actually quite nice. Would be good for drinks on a date. The service could be better, but it was a Friday night and there was a large 15-20 ppl party that probably slowed things down. The bread did come continuously which was good. For any popular nights, I would definitely recommend reservations. Parking is fairly easy; be sure to remember to read the signs since you may not need to pay for parking on the street or even in the lot.

I had heard so much about McCormicks and Schmick's reputation that I was very excited to go there for the first time this evening, 4/12/2013.  The atmosphere was very nice.  Both the bar area and the dining room were comfortable and nicely decorated.  We were greeted very promptly an shown to our table.  Given the option between white or black cloth napkin, was a nice touch. But I was quite surprised with the ripped plastic place mat on the table.  If you've ever been here, then you know the menu is kind of pricey, so since we were ordering appetizers averaging $15-19 each and meals ranging from @9 to 54.99, I expected them to be perfect in both tastes and presentation.  

I was wrong

The coconut shrimp arrive cold and over fried and the calamari platter had a not so fresh taste and was also cold.  The assistant manager promptly replaced our appetizers and you could immediately see and taste the difference. 

Now it's time for our meals.  One order was shrimp scampi with garlic, linguini and herbs and the other was McCormick and Schmicks Trio (salmon, grilled shrimp and stuffed shrimp).

The linguini and the shrimps were over cooked, but I decided to work my way through it, until......I noticed that some of the shrimp were not deveined!!!  How can this be?  How can they not wash and clean their shrimp. I could not eat any more.

The McCormick and Schmidt trio was a little better.  The plate contained 2 grilled shrimp, 2 stuffed shrimp and a 2 oz size, string beans and squash,  The beans and the cheddar squash were very cold.  As a matter of fact we were able to move the squash across the plate as one unit.  When we asked the assistant manager if he could tell us how was the food plated, he didn't know what that meant. But he did promptly go to the kitchen and bring out some fresh cheddar squash.  We then showed he how different they looked and asked him to taste it to prove the point.

All this trouble for a $106.32 + tax +tip for dinner for 2.

Definitely not worth the HYPE!!!!!
Their service has really gone downhill. The pedicures now look like my two year old did it.  Stay away.

I've always enjoyed hitting up Tenno on West End.  I was excited to see they moved to Brentwood and took over Miyako... This from someone who's been going to Miyako since they opened 20 years ago.

Tenno has some great sushi hand rolls.  I'm a big fan of the spicy scallop hand roll.  They have a pretty wide selection of specialty rolls.  They even still make Miyako's old specialty rolls. The service was decent and we got soup and salad with our meal... Not sure what Chelsea is talking about in her "tip" that she posted.

Tenno is on pace with Hanabi and both are better than Peter's.  Also, they have a fountain Coke machine now!  I always hate when places like this give you a can of Coke.

Great breakfast joint.  Love the scrapple and pork roll with pancakes.  My wife always has a ham and cheese omelet and loves it.  Very local type place and down to earth.  Don't expect total fancyness.

The bubble tea at Tsaocaa is amazing! I got the brown sugar and it was super yummy. I took my niece there and she loved it too! It was sweet and such a fun drink thanks to the chewy tapioca bubbles. You can get tired of the bubbles after a while, but the drink is still great and refreshing. 

We also got honey garlic wings and fries. All was very good and fresh. Get the combo, it's a better deal than a la carte. I wish we did. Any who, check them out. They were friendly as well.

Great sandwiches and pastries, totally worth the price PLUS the folks working were incredibly friendly. We sampled several of the pastries and bought the lemon bar (the bread pudding with divine as well). We bought the turkey pesto and turkey avocado-they were both quite delicious! I will definitely be back again! :)

Its a charmer. We heard that the fee to ride across the Mississippi River to Algiers was $2.00 adults, $1.00 seniors. A $6.00 round trip with bragging rights we'd technically boated Old Man River.
