Love love love BLFT!!! The cutest boutique with the friendliest owners in town. Try to catch them at our local events around town :)

I absolutely LOVE this place. Food is always delicious and service is good. They are never overly busy or crowded so you can enjoy your meal and never have to wait. Great for take out or catering too. They are happy to sub things for you and the owner often stops by to make sure you're enjoying yourself
Great food great service I have such a great time every time I go their chicken and waffles are amazing
Just had some of the best bar service we've ever had in Reno. Serena took such good care of us, I couldn't tip her enough.

5 of us dined here this evening & the food was delicious, the portions more than ample & the service was polite & quick.  Lily was our fine waitress! I had the lo-carb lamb kebobs & enough leftovers for another hearty meal. We dined on their patio & we all enjoyed the experience.

I'm beyond angry!!! I went to Target to pick up Purina Tidy Cats Non-Clumping 24/7 Performance Multiple Cats Litter. And let me tell you I had a heck of a time trying to find it. And when I asked a young man to help me find it, he was very rude and didn't not help at all he, he just kept walking.... like what are his parents teaching him. And I couldn't find MiraLax, as an older woman I have trouble in the restroom and to not have one of my basic needs is ridiculous!!! Let's just say I'm never coming back here ever again. If I could give zero stars I would.

I had walked past a few times, now that I've finally tried it - my mouth waters every time I go by. 

Fresh sandwich and soups at an affordable price. Retro contemporary atmosphere. Good for families, groups and lunch dates. 

We had a chicken sandwich and tomato soup. Fantastic!
Great little place. Gumbo was amazing. Crawfish etouffee tasty. Crawfish boudin delicious and a little different. The woman at the counter, Sunshine, and the owner super friendly and helpful
Had the cinnamon brown sugar hot doughnut... so much flavor in one bite! Can't wait to head back and try the fried chicken!

Very friendly staff! Called in and got a better rate than advertised online. Room is clean and spacious enough for the two of us. We were surprised that the room had a microwave and mini fridge. A small happy hour is from 4-5.
Absolutely wonderful!! Color by Alex F. Cut from Nicolette! Love the environment, love the service. I hate salons, but this place is a dream.  :-)

Outstanding service! Raymond, the installer, could not have been nicer, and he did a great job.
I had to reschedule twice, and it still was a breeze.
I checked with my insurance company at the last minute and only had to pay a $50 deductible for a $340 job. 
Awesome! 
I highly recommend.

The food was wonderful. We had the "surf & turf" enchiladas Banderas and T-bone steak. The enchiladas were amazing. The three different sauces for the steak, lobster, and shrimp complimented each enchilada nicely. The steak had a great crust and practically melted in my husbands mouth. We found this place just walking down the broadway and we are amazed at the quality of the food. They even gave us free chips and salsa, and let me tell you it's just as delicious as all the other food. I don't usually like beans or rice but they were equally amazing!
Stiffest drinks in the district, prices are always lowest in town. Good friends and great times, always!

Great fresh sushi. I ordered the udon noddles and a sashimi bowl and were both delicious! My friend got 3 rolls and they were large and came with miso soup. I will definitely be going back. They also have some grab n go food if you're in a rush. The only issue is the limited seating during lunch. It would be great if they separated some of the 4 ppl chairs so more people can sit.

My girlfriends and I came here for some coffee and tea because our boyfriends were watching sports across the street. I love the open concept of this place, it's very comforting! 

I ordered an iced tea and it was less than $2.00. They had a large menu of seasonal drinks that sounded delicious. 

There were a lot of people playing board games which is a fun concept in general. Great coffee spot!

So glad this popped up to be reviewed.   Looks like I am not alone in my thoughts 

Gossipy girls behind the counter. Phone just rings trying to place order in advance.  Rude counter help when you finally do get to order.   Slow service with an illiterate behind the grill that can't read the orders.  More than once my order was wrong but not waiting in line to get it corrected.  The dirty interior, filthy ceiling tiles and limited seating makes this more of a take out joint.  The all kid crew makes it perfect for the young crowd but as for us working folk - maybe not.  Perfect stop just before the 95 entrance is the only reason I kept coming back. I have tried to give this place a 2nd, 3rd and 4th try because wawa across the street and the DD are the only other options before I jump on 95 for work.  Have to find a new morning stop.

The only reason this is two instead of one star is because at least the bagels are good. Not round, but good.

I had no idea Pearl was SO trendy.  Dark, loud DJ, and a very hands on staff.  

Definition of "hands on staff":  hugged me the second I walked through the door and continued to put an arm around me while the menu was discussed.

The food wasn't terrible, it certainly wasn't fantastic either.  As a fellow diner accurately put it, it would be easy to spend a lot of money at Pearl for sushi that is less than stellar.  Several specialty rolls can cost around $19.  

Prices aside...  Pearl's menu has sushi, but only rolls.  No nigiri to be found.  There is "Asian" fare, including such inoffensive dishes as Beef and Broccoli and Teriyaki Chicken.  But then there are steaks, salads and fish entrees as well.  Otherwise known as... American fare.  I understand once you drop the term "fusion" in a restaurant name, your bracket tends to loosen up a bit.  

But really.  If you want really good sushi... you know what to do.

P.S.  I really like hot sake.  I understand that one usually heats sake because that sake is in fact considered the "crappy", or lesser sake.  Well, the hot sake at Pearl was less than lesser.  It probably would have disinfected the cut I have on my finger, though.

We used Red Spirits and Wine for our daughters wedding last week. They were great to work with, reasonably priced and had good recommendations for us. They were able to deliver the beverages which sealed the deal when we were trying to juggle so many details. Highly recommend!

This is the closest library to our home and we have young kids, so we go A LOT! The kids area is nicely appointed with tables, computers, puzzles and the occasional toy. My kids adore it and could spend all day here. The book and DVD selection are great.
We've had really great experiences with the public programs they run geared toward kids. The staff that works the educational programs and reading time are always so kind, but the staff behind the counter could learn a few lessons from the eduction staff. They tend to be VERY grumpy, which is a major turn off.

The Foodery is such a hidden gem. I have been once for SIPS, and again today for lunch with coworkers. I absolutely love the "serve yourself" style- it is so much more enjoyable than being waited on. After ordering at the counter, you can seat yourself with your food number, and then serve yourself from three "types" of water (very cool)! Even though I am not a beer drinker, I was very impressed with their selection.

Today I tried the Kale Caesar, which was absolutely delicious. The portion was huge, and it was not drowned in dressing. I also tried the fried chicken wings, but was not impressed. I would not order again.

This beer spot is an atmospheric haunt with a nice selection of craft beer and some pretty good grub to go with it. The space inside is bigger than it looks if you manage to get past the narrow entranceway near the bar. There is a ton of local craft beer on tap, so it's a great spot to take a tour of the area's breweries without having to walk. The food is also good, especially the pub fare offered for brunch or dinner. Service is pretty friendly and fast too and makes it feel like a nice neighborhood spot.

Wide selection of beers on tap and generous pours on flights make this a excellent stop to grab a pint with your friends.  Live music on Tuesdays is a fun early-week break from the same old weeknight routine.  A sports jersey or t-shirt are not out of place here if you want a casual place to hang out.
Best Pizza in Tampa,Lagza is very good,every time I go to downtown Eddie & Sam's is a must-eat place

yelp has a 5% off coupon for here when you check in.  I went for happy hour and asked to use the coupon.  The waiter had to check with mgmt, came back and said they didn't think it applied to HH prices but that they'd honor it anyway....which was the tip of the iceburg on great service we got all night!  Very impressed!

the food was incredible!  we had the goat cheese, calamari, and mussels appetizers along with many rounds of drinks.  The food came out of the kitchen very quickly, was all very hot, and incredibly flavorful!  we loved everything!  I really liked that the calamari had hot/sweet peppers mixed in with them - nice flavor addition. 

My only small criticism is the seating.  the chairs aren't comfortable.  most are metal without cushions and some don't even have backs (like the barstools).  I suppose that helps them to turn the tables over more quickly.

Its an upscale version of chinese fast food. I don't get it. No frog? The signature sichuan dish in my opinion. Weird menu..... why the taiwanese, hunan, and shanghai thrown in at random. (Sausage, 3 cup chicken, lions head, tea smoked duck are all not sichuan dishes...) 4 rivers is much better and much more authentic in terms of no frills sichuan food, not as spicy, but better overall. 

dan dan and cukes are way overpriced (well everything is really) and really not that special. I've had better dan dan in a can.

PS - as an aside. Whoever wrote that most US chinese cuisine is either cantonese or mandarin and that this is something else is a bit wrong. mandarin and cantonese are 2 speech dialects .... not cooking styles. Chinese cooking has 8 styles. Cantonese is the most popular in US. However, "mandarin" does not exist as a cooking style. Sichuan (or szechwan) is also one and is one outta two that use spiciness as a main flavor the other being hunan. Hopefully this will unconfuse some people...

food, service and atmosphere were all excellent.  we had the brisket lunch with macaroni & cheese and potato salad and the pulled pork lunch with fries and apple sauce - all were very good. the apple pie desert was to-die for. we will definitely visit again.
Excellent museum.  My friends and I got in with our college ids, for a discounted rate and were blown away at all there was to see! Phenomenal experience , and so much to see!

Classic for all the right reasons. The service, ambiance, food, and drink are all too good to be true. I don't know how the butter that comes with the french bread is even so good, but every detail is perfect.

The coffee cake foie gras was outstanding, and very rich with flavor.

I had the "pig and the peach,"whose peach galette paired perfectly with the roasted pork belly. 

The watermelon and peach salad with honeycomb and goat cheese was unique and definitely worth trying, too.

The only downside to the meal was the soup sampler, all of which we found to be too salty.

I would wildly recommend the Louisiana white shrimp (only an option under the three course menu when we visited) which came in an astoundingly creamy sauce with artichoke and roasted tomatoes.

Desserts are uncanny. Try all of them if you can.

I've been to a few different vets in Philly due to being heavily involved in animal rescue and let me say, I trust everybody at WCVH. The staff are so friendly and positive, especially Kayla and Brenda and the vet techs are kind and loving to my fur babies. I trust each and every vet here, Dr. Springs, Dr. Petronis, and Dr. Yard. They listen to my concerns and help my babies feel better in no time! I love everyone there and trust them completely, and I don't trust many people. Thank you everyone at WCVH for everything you do!

So, this is the next in what I'm calling my series of "pandemic" updates...when I went to Costco on 3/12/20 which was just when things were starting to ramp up, it was full-on Panic at the Costco...it was worse by far than right before the holidays, they were out of all paper products and the chicken case was completely empty.   It was packed, stressful, and just generally awful...and I swore I wasn't going back until after this was all over.

So why did I go back today?  I heard they were metering people into the store to promote social distancing and that they were largely stocked now that people had settled down on the panic buying.

They have a very organized line system to get in that is set up in a way that does permit social distancing.   Basically, they have a series of parallel lines along the side of the store separated by piles of wooden pallets.  Line 1 is on the sidewalk (closest to the store).  When enough people come out, line 1 goes in, and line 2 (closer to the parking area) moves into the line 1 position, and if there is a line 3, they move into the line 2 position.   It only took about 10-15 minutes to get in on a Friday afternoon.   

This system makes for an uncrowded store and fast checkout.   They were stocked with everything except Lysol wipes and hand sanitizer.   They put the things they're out of on a white board up front.  I was able to get hand soap, latex gloves, boneless chicken, a rotisserie chicken, lots of fresh produce, frozen berries, milk, eggs, frozen fish, cheese, and...drumroll please...TP!!!   

They've put tape on the floor by the checkouts to remind people to stay 6 feet apart and have re-arranged some areas with tighter aisles to make it easier to stay far enough away from folks.    They are also handing out wipes after you grab carts, and have installed plexiglass shields to protect the checkout workers including the person checking receipts.   

Heads up that they have shortened their hours and so are no longer open in the evenings.

The two girl working the counter seemed overwhelmed, but needlessly so. When I approached the cashier, she told me to wait. I was nice, didn't mind. Eventually ordered our stuff - two coffee drinks and breakfast sandwiches. Not hard.

Firstly, they don't call out your drinks, so if you sit down, you won't know they're ready. The girls will not yell out for you or come find you, either. Secondly, it took them twenty five - 2 5 - minutes to make a bacon-sausage-cheese bagel with 3 ingredients pre-cooked, AND they just assumed somebody made my burrito and forgot about it. Thirdly, we were not the only ones in there, no, but everyone received the same crap service. No smiles, no help, and everything was the customer's fault.

I'm a barista at a coffee shop on Magazine. I know how this works. These people need better training and a serious overhaul in customer service.

I used to live central and ate at OPG tons for their firecracker shrimp. I was extremely happy when I moved across the street from this place and found out they have them in the bar area too. Only tried the bar menu from the 3-4 times we have been there, but all the bar food is delicious and priced incredibly well. We usually order like 5 different appetizers and make that our meal. Add in some drinks, and you are in for a good time. Love the zucchini bread they give you! This is my hidden spot to go watch a game at, because the bar area doesn't usually get packed, and has enough TV's to make it enjoyable. Would like to see them upgrade the bar area to be better to watch games at, ie bigger and more TV's. But then that might attract too many people and ruin my hidden game-time spot!

Don't forget to try the pizza! It is excellent. We have even ordered it to go before, as we like it so much.

Removed 1 star, as their cocktail menu isn't anything to write about, but at least they usually have a couple of decent microbrews.

I've been to both the West End & Galleria location multiple times. You can NOT get a bad meal here. Period.  The decor alone screams it loud and the service compliments it.  This is the perfect business lunch to take clients.  They don't rush you, the staff is knowledgeable about the menu, and the fish is always fresh. 

The kicker is the freaking coffee; wow brings a tear to my eyes - a press. I made the mistake of ordering an espresso one visit.......not good. I ordered it short but it came full to the brim and room temperature; they would hang them for that in Sicily.

Their new system for customer service sucks and they're @$$holes about it.

They ask you to place an order, then call your name when it's ready, and then you're allowed to stand in line for 20 minutes to actually get it.

Ok, fine. I get it, protecting your staff should take priority, even if this is a bit convoluted.

So I call in an order, get told "30 minutes or so", get there in 20 to make it easy on them, and stand under the speaker to be sure.

15 minutes go by, no name. So I ask, "Nope, not on the list, give it a few minutes.

10 more... again, nope.

Finally, 10 more... "Let me look. Oh, it's been out for a while, go get in line"

I look over: 15 people in line... "ok, fine, but no one called my name" "you must have missed it."

I wait another 20 minutes in line. Get handed a cold cheesesteak, and I'm just like "yea, forget it."

Again, I understand and support wanting to keep your staff safe, but if you can't find a way to offer the most basic customer service, then do that by SHUTTING DOWN FOR THE DURATION.

Or at least take responsibility and apologize when you screw up.

Anyway, once I cool off I'll be back.

Just annoying as heck.
Nice environment but only the first floor is wheelchair accessible. It's also very pricey. They have the book making machine, which is cool, I'll admit.

Schmear It is my fav bagel place outside of center city. The bagels have the right texture with a chewy inside and nice crusty exterior. The ability to mix your own cream cheese creations is a big bonus - but be careful because the cost can really add up at $0.50 each. I also wish they used fresh jalapeño instead of pickled because it has no kick to it and a briny flavor that I find to be less enjoyable compared to fresh. There is plenty of seating inside if you need to eat there. Also the employees are always very nice, they always greet you and say goodbye, and they are smiling even when it takes you an hour to decide what you want!

Culpeppers has a little bit of everything and while I can honestly say I have not ever had anything I absolutely hated here I have also never suggested that we eat at Culpeppers.
The wait staff at Culpeppers has always been very nice and extremely accommodating. I feel like management likes running a lean ship though as the wait staff always seems to be running around like a chicken with its head cut off.
I think the three best items on their menu is the Buffalo Chicken Wrap, the Culpepper Burger, and the Waffle Fries.
This company used to be all over Saint Louis and unfortunately, I think I understand why they only have a single location left.
Great food, great beer. Over 100+! A little loud but tolerable because it was worth it. Look forward to coming back here again. Never knew Carmel had such a. Great night life.

So much fun! We did the art gallery room for my birthday. The room had us guessing with 7 1/2 minutes left but we got out. I recommend to do it with a group of your friends, but with strangers it works fine as well.

First time at this restaurant for President's Day weekend.

Overall, I enjoyed dining here. I ordered the duck breast which was pretty good, but not amazing (a little chewy and thick). My partner ordered their popular salmon with thai curry dish, which I enjoyed more after sampling.

Good location, good ambiance, great staff and service, and good for any occasion really.
The employees are hustling and attentive to the movement of the line.   I love the drinks.

This is our neighborhood fresh fish/hot boiled crawfish place to shop. The catfish , trout and redfish are always beautiful and great to cook. The prepared foods are classic local favorites. Take them home and warm them up... You won't be disappointed... Except maybe because you wish you'd bought more!

Pleasant surprise for a local pub in the area. Have been here before a long time ago. Nice for them to have our local feline rescue in for the night. Had the Texas Tender appetizer which was half price on happy hour. This was a meal! Perhaps the finest local chicken fingers/tenders. Heard their entire menu Was A Cut Above So we will be back. Nice to see people we knew in there that were not there for the cat rescue. Managers and owner are very attentive to customers.

I am a huge fan of Cigar City and was excited over a year ago (the last time I was at a southwest terminal) that one was being put in.  

They have their own beer selections (And wine) and mainly sandwiches to choose from.  Their food was good but the reason I am giving 3 stars is mainly due to the service.

When we walked into the seating area, we took a seat and it got our waters and put in our drink orders.  We got our drinks fairly quickly, but when we asked our server to put in our food order, she acted like we were a burden to her.  We weren't rude or pushy, but she acted like we were acting so.  I noticed other tables were getting frustrated as well.  There were other employees that were coming around making sure we had refills on or water and asked if we wanted another beer, but it wasn't our server.

Despite the poor service, I would order again next time I am in the southwest terminal.

I dropped my iPad mini on its screen and I thought that finding a place to fix it would be easy. There were very few places so Ballard computes is who I chose. They did a great job with my iPad and it works great it was done in a day. It's run by Marvin and he was nice and new what he was doing. He also gives you a nice case when you come in for a screen repair. Beats Apple's ludicrous price to fix it.

Great experience overall!

Food: We loved garlic nan bread but not too much of onion one. There's nothing wrong with the taste. Maybe it's just my preference on onion texture. Fried rice with medium hot shrimp was tasty. However even though we ordered mild on all other dishes, it had some kicks. It's not really good for kids if they can't eat spicy food.

Parking: Restaurant is located in a strip mall so plenty of parking space and convenient. 

Service: There's nothing bad about service because you will get whatever you order in decent time. However they are not too friendly but it's ok with me as long as I get my food in time. 

I haven't tried a buffet yet but I'm looking forward to it. I was told that weekend buffet is little bit upgraded than the weekday buffet.

Stopped into Montecito mid-road trip with a bunch of friends and we got rave review recommendations from friends to try Jeannines. 

We were SO glad that we tried it. We got there and it was the most popping place on the road. Even though there was a long line, it was super super efficient and we were seated and eating within 30 minutes. It was super efficient, as we ordered at the counter and then as we were in line, our table was prepared for us.

Now to get to the AMAZING food. 

Norwegian Benedict: incredible. I didn't even know that smoked salmon on a Benedict was a thing, let alone the MASTERPIECE that was this dish. 10/10 and the Hollandaise sauce was muahhhhh (chefs kiss)

Kahlua Bananas Foster French Toast: hands down the STAR of the show. Every single person in the group who tried this dish was blown away. We literally still talk about this dish and the sweet sweet bananas 

The egg white omelet: now bear with me, I know it doesn't "sound good" because it sounds healthy, but it was actually SUPER delicious, especially if you're feeling health conscious 

Last but NOT least: the SCONES!!! I'm not even a scone person but the scones here were highly recommended. And let me tell you, these scones were absolutely out of this world. I couldn't stop eating them! We got the blueberry and the raspberry. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. These and the banana French toast are MUST TRYS here

In regards to Matt R's post, I don't know that I would say that Jester's caters to the bar crowd, however, this is the "Cheers" of Bordentown, and I think that the bar business supports the restaurant just as much as the restaurant does.  My recommendation if you do not want to hear the bar crowd, is to request a table in the back room, separated from the bar, and then the problem is solved.

Regardless, this is the meeting place for the "townies," whether staying there for the entire evening, or just meeting up for cocktails before heading elsewhere.  Mike and his staff do a good job, but you will get some vagrants that hang out there that I can do without.

The bar pie is good, and the rest of the food is ok, but somewhat inconsistent.  Menu needs some revamping, but with a new chef in the kitchen now, it could be happening.  Look forward to finding out soon.

Best pizza in town. Staff is always friendly, especially Jordan. The pizza is good priced, less than $9 and a good size. There is a variety of toppings and its unlimited toppings. It's easy and is pretty fast, only 5 minutes for a pizza. I recommend herb butter for the oil and barbecue for the sauce. Welcome to the neighborhood.

2 stars for effort... We have ordered take out several times with the quality and accuracy of the order going downhill each time. While they try hard, the quality and consistency is just not there. The tomato pies are good; the wraps and entrees could stand improvement. With such a large amount of competition locally and a location that is a proven loser; the over/under says vacant by July

Went last Sunday for the first time. We are instant fans.. Don't go for any atmosphere, go for the food.
The place is small so keep that in mind.
We will be back many times for sure.

Once you try Gigi's cupcakes, you will never again be satisfied with any other cupcakes. They are so delicious and the variety of flavors is phenomenal with cupcakes like Kentucky Bourbon Pie and Candy Bar Crunch as well as traditional flavors.The only make certain flavors on certain days of the week and will not modify that schedule by any means so plan accordingly if you are after a specific cupcake.  They are always looking for ways to meet customers needs by offering sugar-free and gluten-free cupcakes. The only drawback to those is that they will not mix mini boxes with regular, sugar-free, and gluten-free. So it can be frustrating when trying to accomodate a large variety of needs.They are pricey, so if you are serving a big crowd the minis are the way to go. In addition to cupcakes, Gigi's offers baked breads, cheesecakes, cookies, and event cakes. I ordered a whole cake for my birthday last year and while it was good, they used a lot of fondant that was pretty bland. I highly recommend getting an iced cake over the fondant option.

First time here. I had the bbq pulled chicken. It's a perfect blend of bbq sauce and tangy. The chicken tender and melts in your mouth, all that on their own fresh baked bread. Yumyum. Not a fan of coleslaw with vinegar, this was not overpowering. Get a beer and chow down on the bbq pulled chicken.

So our first big restaurant stop in New Orleans was lunch at the iconic Commander's Palace and though I could rattle off five better places that we ate at, I still have to give this place its props... or some love... or whatever the kids are calling "compliments" are today.

The ambiance had a classic, southern charm and the wait staff was extremely polite and attentive. I had a sparkly, fruity rum drink which was as light and refreshing as I was hoping while Jeannene had a Cosmo Martini (25 cents). Yeah, you read that right, that's one of the menu items this place is known for.

We then moved on to something we can't get up in Cleveland -- Turtle Soup. The brown sauce was full of black-peppery goodness with crumbly pieces of chewy meat. I'd definitely order it again.

For main course, I had the Cast Iron Seared Gulf Fish ($23), in this case that would be Sheepshead. Always intrigued by a fish I've never had before, it had a bland, meaty taste. I was also intrigued by the "Louisiana crab boiled peanuts pureed with brown butter." It was the first peanut puree I've ever had and I kind of liked it but the problem was it did not not complement the fish at all and neither did the accompanying farro or eggplant. Everything cooked well but some acid or spice was needed.

Jeannene, working on her second 25-cent martini, had the Garlic Seared Gulf Shrimp ($22) and found it thoroughly enjoyable.

We passed on dessert and made our way to the cool cemetery across the street.
Agree with another reviewer, this is a well run location, clean and they have a good crew. I've never been disappointed at this store.
